articleTitle: Arc Fault Detection and Line Selection in DC Multi-branch Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage power supply systems have developed rapidly in direct current (DC) microgrid, construction industry, and commerial fields. In these DC multi-branch scenarios, altered arc fault characteristics would challenge existing detection methods. In this paper, a feature-driven long short-term memory (LSTM) method is proposed for arc fault diagnosis in DC multi-branch situations.Firstly, an arc fault experimental platform is constructed for studying arc fault characteristics in DC multi-branch systems. Next, the characteristics of arc fault current signals are studied using different time-frequency transformation technologies. By setting the lifting ratio Z for bus-level DC arc faults and MZ for branch-level arc faults, it is found that the lifting ratio Z and MZ between the fault state and the normal state are relatively small for the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), which may cause a mistaken system state judgment. Therefore, the wavelet transform method is more suitable to detect arc faults and select their occurrence line. Then a DC arc fault detection and line selection method is proposed based on LSTM network. Compared with the data-driven mode, the feature-driven mode achieves higher accuracy. Finally, viewed from the verification of various experimental data, the LSTM-based algorithm displays 13.36% higher detection accuracy on average than a random forest (RF) diagnosis model.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Power Internet of Things Based on 5G Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power system is crucial to the economy, but traditional inspections are inefficient and risky. Therefore, this system combines 5G and drone technology to enhance inspection efficiency and accuracy. The system design includes an image transmission and diagnosis module. The image transmission module utilizes specific chips and 5G modules to achieve efficient video acquisition, encoding, and transmission. The image diagnosis module, through preprocessing and edge detection steps, accurately detects power line faults and uploads the diagnostic results in real-time to the cloud. This system improves inspection efficiency and accuracy, saves labor costs, reduces safety hazards, and has significant economic and social benefits.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Dispatch of Community Integrated Energy System via the Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy storage is an indispensable component in the community integrated energy system (CIES), offering numerous benefits such as reducing energy consumption and emissions and optimizing system operations. However, energy storage safety issues such as energy leakage, fire, and explosion have not received sufficient attention in energy storage applications. This paper proposes a scheduling strategy for CIES via a safe storage technology namely the liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHC). First, a mathematical model of the CIES containing P2H (power to hydrogen) and the hydrogenation reaction model is established. A dual-objective model is then established to optimize the scheduling cost and carbon emissions. The relaxed non-convex product term is transformed into a convex optimization problem by setting different state variables and their corresponding outputs. Finally, the case study results demonstrate that the proposed model can effectively reduce carbon emissions and costs through P2H and hydrogen storage. The comparison results show that the LOHC exhibits significant advantages in terms of safety, hydrogen storage density, and scheduling costs.

articleTitle: Flexibility Retrofit Time Series Planning for Multiple Generation Resources Considering Complementary Wind-PV-Coal-Storage Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The synergistic development of coal power with new energy and energy storage is an important path for the low-carbon transformation of China's energy and power industry. In order to achieve the optimization path of coal power retrofit and new energy and storage planning, this paper proposes a method of multi-resources flexibility retrofit time series model based on the complementary characteristics of wind-PV-coal-storage to achieve the improvement of system’s operation flexibility. Firstly, a multi-resources flexibility supply model on the power generation side and system flexibility evaluation indicators is constructed. Secondly, based on the complementary characteristic of wind, PV, coal and storage, a multi-resources collaborative planning and retrofit time series model is built. The case simulation is based according to the actual scene of the Ningxia region, and obtains the collaborative optimization results of the multi-resource retrofit time series. The proposed method is verified to be effective, and a planning scheme that considers system’s flexibility and economy is obtained.

articleTitle: The Development of Power Transformer Noise Optimization Calculation Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: On the basis of the theory calculation of power transformer noise, this work design and develop a program for optimizing the noise of transformer with Python program. Though the comparison with the noise measurement of the transformer actual products, the accuracy and practicality of the procedure are verified. This is significant for the optimization of product design and the improvement of economic efficiency.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Assessment of Power System Flexibility Based on Bayesian Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the share of renewable energy sources grows, it becomes essential to develop effective management strategies to handle the associated variability and uncertainty. This paper presents a novel approach to rolling optimization modeling aimed at enhancing data collection and developing flexibility indicators for power systems. These data and indicators are utilized as inputs and outputs for Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs), enabling regression-based predictions of power system flexibility. By leveraging historical operational data and advanced predictive modeling techniques, the study facilitates rapid assessments crucial for effective management of renewable energy integration and overall system flexibility. The findings reveal significant fluctuations in flexibility driven by the variability of renewable energy sources, underscoring the model's high predictive accuracy as demonstrated through a case study of the IEEE-33 node system. Ultimately, by integrating rolling optimization with data-driven predictive models, this research contributes to the ongoing discourse on achieving a sustainable energy transition while ensuring the reliable and efficient operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Active Noise Reduction Technology of Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: a variety of substation power equipment represented by power transformer will produce significant noise in operation. As noise is one of the typical environmental pollution sources and may harm people's health, the noise reduction technology of power equipment is worth in-depth exploration. This paper takes the noise of power transformer as the main research object, analyzes the noise generation mechanism of power transformer, constructs the simulation model of noise source of power transformer, and discusses the principle of active noise reduction technology based on the principle of reverse superposition of secondary sound source. The specific control algorithm and the detailed implementation path are proposed, and the field verification effect of the prototype is given. Field measurement results show that the 220kV transformer noise is mainly concentrated within 500Hz, and 100Hz, 200Hz, 300Hz and other integer multiples of 100Hz. The use of active noise reduction has a obvious noise reduction effect on most of the noise frequency band. This work can provide reference for specific noise reduction technology researchers and substation green operation and maintenance technology popularization.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction Based on Multidimensional Power Technical Indicators and LSTNet Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A wind power prediction method combining multidimensional technical indicators and the LSTNet algorithm is proposed to address volatility in wind power time series. Using financial time series analysis, K-lines and technical indicators are integrated into the framework. A sliding time window creates a power K-line, followed by feature extraction and model building. Case study results from an Inner Mongolia wind farm show the model improves Mean Squared Error (MSE) by 24.2% over the benchmark.

articleTitle: Typical Model of Virtual Power Plant Participation in the Market and Relevant Suggestions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale new energy access, the demand for balancing capabilities within power systems is expected to rise significantly. As a high-quality flexible regulation resource that aligns with the standards of the power grid, virtual power plants are emerging as a crucial component in the regulation and control of future power systems. In light of this, the article reviews typical models of virtual power plants participating in the market in Europe and China. It further summarizes the key challenges faced by these VPP in market transactions and proposes targeted solutions to address these issues.

articleTitle: Multi-ports Modular Frequency-Domain Modeling Method of Wind Power Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The wind power converter is always accompanied by multiple frequency harmonics when participating in the oscillation. The multi-harmonic interaction leads to the coupling between wind power generation equipment or its internal power electronic converters, which makes the frequency domain modeling of large-scale wind power generation system (WPGS) difficult. To address this issue, this paper develops a multi-port modeling (MPM) method. The multi-port model not only can accurately embody the multi-harmonic characteristic of power electronic devices or systems through extending the single frequency port variable of the classical two-port model (CTPM) to the multi-frequency harmonic port variable, but also realize the modular aggregation. Besides, a network function-based stability analysis technique is then put forward to study oscillation. Finally, the effectiveness of multi-port impedance model and analysis method are validated against the MATLAB/ Simulink testbed of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind power system.

articleTitle: A Fault Detection Method for Wind Turbine Using the Dynamic K-Nearest Neighbor and Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing importance of wind energy utilization and the high costs of maintenance, effective fault warning is crucial for ensuring the long-term stability of wind turbines. This paper addresses the issue of fault detection in wind turbines by proposing a novel detection method based on the dynamic k-Nearest neighbor (DKNN) and Autoencoder models. This study first employs Zero-Component Analysis Whitening (ZCA) for the preprocessing of SCADA data, reducing feature correlations and enhancing the performance of subsequent machine learning models. By utilizing the DKNN algorithm, we can identify pattern features under both normal and abnormal conditions, while the Autoencoder model detects anomalies through reconstruction errors. Experimental results demonstrate that our method effectively identifies potential faults in wind power systems and successfully achieves a two-day advance warning, significantly improving the timeliness of fault detection. This approach provides a new pathway for the reliability and intelligent management of wind energy systems, showcasing the potential for further optimization of detection performance across broader datasets.

articleTitle: Study on local discharge type identification based on acoustic signal processing and PCA-BP method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Acoustic detection technology is a technology capable of detecting and pinpointing the origins of abnormal acoustic signals stemming from localized discharges in power equipment. Nevertheless, the current iteration of this technology primarily locates the sources but struggles to elucidate their fundamental origins. As such, a comprehensive composition analysis of these detected acoustic signals is imperative. To tackle this challenge, this paper introduces a methodology for identifying distinct types of localized discharge, alongside the construction of an experimental apparatus simulating various local discharge scenarios. The apparatus employs an acoustic sensor array to capture these sounds. Considering the inherent noise within the experimental setting, we apply a noise reduction strategy to purify the acquired acoustic signals before proceeding with their extraction and identification. We then convert the signals from the time domain to the frequency domain using FFT and wavelet transforms, subsequently extracting their characteristic features via the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) algorithm. Finally, the Back Propagation (BP) neural network ingests these condensed feature vectors, enabling the accurate classification of various local discharge types.

articleTitle: Assessment of Vulnerability Severity in Power Monitoring System Based on Text Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Power Monitoring Systems (PMS) are essential for ensuring national energy security and societal stability. Remediation of vulnerabilities is labor-intensive due to the increasing severity of cybersecurity threats, which highlights the importance of effective severity assessments to prioritize. The standard method for assessing and prioritizing vulnerabilities uses the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). However, the internal vulnerabilities specific to PMS do not have CVSS scores, making it difficult to assess their severity accurately. To remedy this problem, we present a text mining approach that achieves vulnerability severity predictions in PMS. The method conducts semantic analysis of vulnerability descriptions to extract key features and uses similarity analysis to rank vulnerabilities. Experimental results on real vulnerability data demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in prioritizing vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: A Method for Predicting the Ownership of Electric Vehicles Based on a Comprehensive Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The rise in the number of electric-powered vehicles has a greater effect on the composition of the power system load. This paper initially presents the predictive methods for electric vehicle ownership, including the grey prediction model, Bass diffusion model and elastic coefficient prediction model. Subsequently, the different weights of the grey prediction model, Bass diffusion model and elastic coefficient prediction model are allocated by the entropy weight method, which can realize the comprehensive prediction of electric vehicle ownership. Finally, this paper proves the method has better accuracy compared with the single method. The final calculation of the representation of the variance proves that the comprehensive prediction method has better reliability.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Optimization Operation Method of Flexible Distribution Network Based on Carbon Emission Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Clarifying responsibility for carbon emissions is a crucial step in establishing a low-carbon electricity system. Current carbon emission analysis techniques can deduce the distribution of carbon emissions within the power system. However, because of the varying operational states of the soft open point integrated with an energy storage system (ESOP) and the intricacy of the model, few studies incorporate this aspect into the calculation of carbon emission flow in the power grid. To tackle this challenge, this paper presents a low-carbon optimized operation method for flexible distribution networks equipped with ESOP. A case study using the enhanced IEEE 33-bus system is conducted to illustrate the distribution of carbon emission flow and the low-carbon optimization operation method for a flexible distribution network, taking into account ESOP.

Author Keywords: soft open point with energy storage system

articleTitle: Online Monitoring Method for Reactive Power Support Performance of Reactive Power Compensation Devices Based on Active Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: There is currently a lack of online performance monitoring methods for the reactive power compensation devices in renewable energy power stations. To address this, an online monitoring method based on active injection for reactive power compensation devices is proposed in this paper. Field test results show that it can test the reactive power support performance of reactive power compensation devices under different control modes in grid-connected conditions.

articleTitle: Resilience Assessment of Power System for Extreme Ice disasters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Extreme ice disasters have a serious impact on the power system. It is particularly important to assess the resilience of the power system under extreme disasters. This article models ice and snow disasters, constructs a probability model of line failures affected by ice disasters, and then constructs a resilience assessment index to reflect the resilience level of the power system. The results indicate that the proposed system level resilience assessment method is satisfied.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Assessing Vulnerable Lines in Offshore Wind-containing power Systems Considering the Impact of Typhoons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the impact of typhoons on offshore wind power system lines, this paper is devoted to researching and proposing a method for assessing vulnerable lines of offshore wind power systems containing offshore wind power systems that can consider the impact of typhoons. First, this paper establishes the Batts typhoon model and proposes a line failure rate model directly caused by typhoon wind speed. Next, this paper proposes an assessment process for vulnerable lines. Considering the volatility of wind power output caused by typhoon wind speed and the temporal sequence of typhoon impacts, this paper introduces the wind power output model and establishes a model for the risk of line current overruns in the power system by combining with Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN). Then, this paper proposes two lines vulnerability indicators, the direct failure rate and the tidal current overrun rate of the line. Finally, this paper analyzes the examples to verify the rationality and practicality of the vulnerable line assessment method studied in this paper.

articleTitle: A Distributed Fixed-time Economic Dispatch Strategy for Smart Grids Over Switching Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This brief investigates the collaborative economic dispatch (ED) problems for smart grids. In order to minimize the generation cost, a consensus-based distributed strategy is proposed to optimally assign the energy demand among distributed generators. Different from the existing distributed ED methods, the proposed strategy achieves fixed-time convergence, which satisfies the fast response requirements and various user preferences. Moreover, the proposed strategy supports switching communication networks and is fully distributed, thus it is more flexible, and robust to communication failures. Finally, two simulation examples on the IEEE 30-Bus systems are presented to validate the effectiveness and fast calculation speed of the presented method.

articleTitle: Data-driven Bad Data Detection and Identification in Power System State Estimation Considering Partitioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The existence of multiple interacting and consistent bad data is a major obstacle to the application of power system state estimation. In this paper, we propose a multi-label classifier based on a spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (STGCN) to detect and identify bad data in power systems, including gross errors, topology errors, and parameter errors. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of detection and identification, we propose to divide the entire system into multiple subareas and applying the classifier to each subarea. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other machine learning and model-driven methods, offering superior accuracy, robustness, and reliability in detecting and identifying bad data.

articleTitle: Motor control technology based on integrated meta-heuristic algorithm optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This document addresses the speed-torque problem in motor control technology by proposing an optimizer based on a comprehensive meta-heuristic algorithm. This optimizer effectively mitigates the issue of heuristic optimization algorithms frequently becoming trapped in local optima. By monitoring the state of the "active particles," it provides real-time insights into the optimization process of the meta-heuristic algorithm. Additionally, the presence of the "active particle archive" facilitates the exploration of new optimization landscapes. The incorporation of other heuristic algorithms enables quicker and more accurate identification of suitable solutions. Furthermore, comprehensive performance evaluations using relevant motor model test functions have validated the feasibility of the optimizer. Ultimately, the results demonstrate that the optimizer significantly enhances the adjustment of control parameters for motors, leading to superior control outcomes.

articleTitle: Real-time Optimal Dispatch of Source-Grid-Load-Storage based on Graph Database
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to fluctuations of renewable energy, it is necessary to coordinately dispatch source-grid-load-storage. However, it takes long time to solve large scale optimization model and may not satisfy real-time requirement. This paper proposes a real-time optimal dispatch of source-grid-load-storage based on graph database. A spatiotemporal graph model of power system is established using a graph database, introducing adjustable loads and energy storage. A real-time optimal dispatch model is developed to minimize the cost of generation units and adjustable resources. Case studies on IEEE118 and IEEE1354 test systems indicate that the application of graph database can reduce the computation time to satisfy real-time dispatch requirement.

articleTitle: Overvoltage Risk Assessment for Renewable Energy Based on Active Control Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of new power systems, the integration of renewable energy has raised concerns about overvoltage and system security. Rotor angle swings predominantly influence voltage fluctuations, while the characteristics of active current become less pronounced, complicating overvoltage prediction. This paper proposes a fitting regression prediction method based on statistical analysis, comparing it with two approaches: active current value based on empirical analysis and the LSTM (long short-term memory) algorithm respectively. Each method has distinct advantages and limitations, contributing to voltage prediction and security assessment.

articleTitle: Low-carbon and Economic Operation of Integrated Electricity-HCNG Distribution System Considering Flexible Utilization of P2G Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of distributed renewable generators (DRGs) into the distribution network has brought about serious power balance issues. Power-to-gas (P2G) technology can effectively promote the consumption of the DRGs’ power generation and enable the active distribution network (ADN) and natural gas distribution network (GDN) to be closely connected. In addition, the hydrogen and methane produced by P2G facilities can be blended into the GDN and utilized as hydrogen-enriched compressed gas (HCNG), which effectively increases the flexibility and economy of the GDN. This work proposes an integrated electricity-HCNG distribution system (IEHDS) that includes the ADN and GDN, interconnected through the P2G facility and hydrogen-mixed gas turbines (HMGT). The production and methanation of green hydrogen of the P2G facilities can effectively reduce the carbon emissions of the IEHDS. A low-carbon economic operation model of the IEHDS is proposed in this work to realize the flexible, economical, and low-carbon operation of the IEHDS. Case studies on the proposed operation model are performed on a typical day in the IEEE 33-bus ADN and 10-node GDN test system. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed operation model in improving the low-carbon and economic operation of the IEHDS.

articleTitle: Multi-Switching-Cycle Modulation for Power Dispatching of Bipolar DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To meet the requirement of bipolar power dispatching of a bipolar DC-DC converter, a multi-switching-cycle (MSC) modulation strategy is proposed. The proposed multi-switching-cycle modulation strategy ensures the consistency of soft switching conditions for all switches under different working conditions of the power difference between the positive and negative poles, thereby expanding the high-efficiency operating range of the converter. The bipolar power dispatching performance of the proposed multi-switching-cycle modulation strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Optimization of Local Energy Internet Based on a Multi-objective Linear Weighted Sum Salp Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Based on the Energy Internet system model, this paper establishes different types of independent energy hub optimization models, and uses the Salp Swarm Intelligent Optimization Algorithm to solve this type of model. In this paper, the traditional Intelligent Optimization Algorithm for Salp Swarm population is improved, and this paper proposes a novel multi-objective linear weighted sum Salp Swarm algorithm for solving the optimization problem. The new algorithm have the advantages of fast speed and high accuracy in solving energy management problems.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Maintenance Strategy Based on Multidimensional Risk Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the expansion of the power system, the maintenance management of transmission lines has become increasingly complex. Effective maintenance strategies are essential to ensure the reliability and economy of the power system. This paper first summarizes the importance of risk assessment, and introduces the composition of risk assessment technology in detail, and puts forward the assessment methods including equipment loss risk, personal environment risk, social loss risk and system risk factors. On this basis, a transmission line maintenance strategy based on multi-dimensional risk analysis is proposed. By quantifying the system risk of transmission lines, a maintenance decision-making process based on fuzzy set theory and interval analysis method is proposed, and the maintenance decision is made by combining economic risk indicators. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by an example analysis. The results show that the method can effectively reduce the maintenance cost and improve the operation efficiency of the power system under the limited maintenance budget.

articleTitle: Topology Analysis and Parameter Calculation of a Novel MMC Sub-module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, a Damped Series Double Sub-Module (D-SDSM) topology with DC fault damping capability is proposed. The topology adds a damping resistor inside the series double sub-module and replaces the IGBT on the internal series branch with a lower-cost IGCT. Compared with other sub-modules with fault current blocking ability, D-SDSM can clear DC fault current faster; and has the advantages of high economy and simple control. The blocking MMC with DC fault clearing ability is built by using D-SDSM and HBSM. Under the background of actual engineering parameters, the blocking MMC can realize the selection of various internal devices, which verifies the feasibility of its application in practical engineering.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Fault Ride-Through Parameters of Energy Storage to Reduce Short-Term Power Impacts Under Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In high-penetration renewable energy systems, voltage dips during short-circuit faults can trigger a large number of renewable energy sources to enter (Low Voltage Ride Through, LVRT) control, causing significant short-term power impacts in the system. The commissioning of new energy storage introduces additional regulation resources to the system. This paper proposes an optimization method for energy storage fault ride-through parameters to reduce short-term power impacts during faults. Based on PV output power and the charge/discharge state of energy storage, the voltage threshold for energy storage entering LVRT is optimized. Additionally, based on the voltage threshold for energy storage stations entering LVRT control and the equivalent impedance between each energy storage station and PV station, the control strategy for energy storage exiting LVRT control is optimized.

articleTitle: Optimized Operation of the Integrated Energy System Based on the Node Carbon Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The uncertainty of wind energy output makes it difficult to accurately track and quantify the carbon emissions on the power side, and the participation of the schedulable load will further increase the complexity of carbon emission optimization. For this purpose, this paper proposes a two-layer optimization scheduling strategy based on the demand response under source-load interaction. First of all, combined with the operation characteristics of wind power, hydro power and schedulable load, the proportional sharing principle is used to track carbon emissions, build a carbon flow model based on the dimension of time and space, perceive the carbon potential change of each node from its dimension, and efficiently and reasonably aggregate the random output scene set of the power grid under the random environment; Secondly, the carbon reduction potential of the load side is finely quantified, and the carbon flow analysis is introduced to construct the demand response model for carbon emission based on the node carbon potential. Finally, the pre-scheduling-re-dispatching of coordinated carbon reduction can realize the change of the carbon flow in the process of economic cost, solve the optimal economic scheduling of the system, and verify the effectiveness of the IEEE14 node system.

Author Keywords: double response of supply and demand

articleTitle: Non-Communication Based Coordinated Control Approach to Improve Commutation Failure Recovery of Hybrid Multi-Infeed HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A novel non-communication coordinated control approach is proposed. It utilizes the MMC-HVDC system to monitor variations in phase angle, enabling the identification of commutation failure (CF). In response, the system shifts from constant power control to an AC voltage control mode that actively provides reactive power support. This enhanced reactive power support alleviates continuous commutation failure in line-commutated converters (LCC). Case studies conducted using PSCAD/EMTDC demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and its ability to enhance performance during fault and recovery periods.

articleTitle: Risk-Informed Vulnerability Identification for Transmission Systems under High Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The high uncertainty arising from the volatility of renewable energy sources and the stochastic occurrences of component failures poses significant challenges to transmission systems. This paper explores a novel approach to quantitatively characterize the vulnerability of transmission systems under uncertainty by evaluating the associated risk and identifying the vulnerable link within the system. A vulnerability analysis framework is firstly proposed. The uncertainty in terms of RES output and random component failure is modeled, based on which a risk evaluation method for transmission systems is proposed. Then, a risk-informed vulnerability identification method is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed method is tested in the IEEE 39-bus system, and the result shows that the research contributes to the resilience enhancement of transmission systems under high uncertainty.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Decision Support for Optimized Carbon Quota Allocation Across Industrial Sectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, governments allocate carbon quotas to industries under Emission Trading Systems. Allocating these quotas involves complex modeling challenges that require effective distribution strategies, which traditional Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) methods struggle to address comprehensively. These methods often fall short of encapsulating the preferences of policymakers and the distinct characteristics of different industries. In response, this paper proposes a novel framework termed the Large Language Model Carbon Quota Allocation Assistant (QAA). The QAA framework combines classical decision-making approaches with a robust expert knowledge base, enhancing the adaptability of allocation schemes to meet specific user demands and industry-specific characteristics. We validate this model through an empirical study involving the allocation of carbon quotas among six major emitting industries in Guangdong, China. The results are analyzed and compared against those derived from conventional linear combination weighting methods. Our findings substantiate the superior efficacy of the QAA, demonstrating its capability to optimize the monetary value of carbon quotas by harmoniously integrating user requirements and expert insights. This study not only underscores the potential of large language models in environmental policymaking but also sets a precedent for future research in this domain.

articleTitle: Adaptive Decoupling Control Strategy for Improving Inertia Support Capability of MMC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of gradually reduced inertia and more and more prominently frequency stability of receiving-end AC grid caused by large-scale wind power connected to the grid through MMC-HVDC transmission, an active support control strategy based on adaptive decoupling of DC voltage and submodule capacitor voltage is proposed for improving inertia support ability of MMC-HVDC. Established a coupling relationship between receiving-end AC grid frequency and DC voltage, which makes MMC-HVDC can actively restrain the frequency change of receiving-end AC grid, and reveals the key factors affecting its inertia support ability; based on the above analysis, an adaptive decoupling modulation strategy based on local measurement information is designed respectively for receiving-end and sending-end MMC, which adaptively adjusts inserted number of submodules without communication to realize the effective decoupling of DC voltage and submodule capacitor voltage, fully utilize the energy margin of capacitors and improve inertia support ability for MMC-HVDC. Considering the safety constraints of frequency, DC voltage and capacitor voltage, a control parameter design method is proposed, and an adaptive recovery strategy is designed to maintain the safe and stable operation of MMC-HVDC while improving the inertia level of receiving-end AC grid. Finally, based on the RTLAB OP5600 real-time digital simulation platform, the simulation model of offshore wind farms connected to the grid through MMC-HVDC transmission is built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Wind Farm Coordinated Control Method Based on Wind Turbine Frequency Regulation Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the low-carbon transition of energy systems and the increase in wind turbine installed capacity, significant challenges have arisen for the frequency stability of power systems. Therefore, integrating renewable energy sources into power system frequency regulation is crucial for improving the system's frequency characteristics. However, current frequency regulation (FR) control methods for renewable energy sources mainly focus on enhancing the frequency regulation capabilities of individual units, while lacking good adaptability for coordinated distribution between wind farms (WFs) and individual units. Based on the analysis of general frequency regulation control for wind power, this paper establishes a unit-level adaptive control strategy with rotor protection mechanisms. Then, a station-level parameter coordination control strategy is proposed, considering the differences in frequency regulation energy sources at different wind speeds. Finally, simulation verification based on the MATLAB/Simulink platform demonstrates that the proposed method can adaptively adjust the wind power frequency regulation parameters according to the grid frequency requirements, ensuring system frequency security while effectively enhancing wind power frequency regulation capabilities.

articleTitle: Low-carbon Optimization Scheduling of an Urban Integrated Energy System Considering Energy Complementarity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, China's urbanization process has accelerated rapidly, with various industries forming clusters. Due to their geographical proximity, these industries have developed into closely connected multifunctional urban regions. The electric and thermal loads, along with the energy consumption characteristics of different functional areas, exhibit significant differences. The deployment of generation units with varying capacities among them provides favorable conditions for the development of energy complementarity in multi-energy systems. In the planning and construction of urban integrated energy systems, the transmission and coordination of information between different subsystems should be considered, and appropriate control strategies should be introduced to enable the orderly flow and collaborative transformation of multiple energy forms—such as electricity, heat, and gas—among the subnetworks. This chapter proposes an urban multi-energy complementarity system structure incorporating an upper-level energy supply center (UESC). Based on the objective function and constraints of the UESC and integrated energy systems (IES), a hierarchical energy complementarity optimization scheduling model is established, considering tiered carbon trading. The ADMM algorithm is employed for distributed iterative solving. Through comparative analysis of five simulation scenarios, the proposed method is demonstrated to effectively enhance the economic, low-carbon, and resilient performance of urban multi-energy systems.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Impedance Trajectory-Based Adaptive Distance Protection for Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Considering the significant risk of malfunction or non-operation in single-phase faults with fault resistance occurring in renewable energy transmission lines, this paper proposes a novel distance protection scheme based on modified impedance trajectory, using transient component. Firstly, multiple fault characteristics of the entire frequency band are extracted utilizing synchronous squeezing S-transform (SST) and S-transform (ST)methods. On this basis, a classifier based on artificial neural networks (ANN) for identifying low-resistance and high-resistance grounding faults is constructed. Then, attenuation coefficients and delayed coefficients are derived by utilizing ST coefficient matrix, and the expression for the fault resistance is deduced. Finally, the impedance trajectory is modified that compensates for additional impedance. The proposed protection is validated on the RTDS platform, the results show that it is unaffected by the weak infeed and strongly withstand the fault resistance, operates rapidly and reliably without communication and delay, and has anti-interference performance.

articleTitle: A Method of Abnormal Detection for Power Grid Control System Metrics Based on AI Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the intelligent maintenance of power grid control system, a real-time anomaly detection algorithm for metrics based on sliding windows is proposed. Then, short-term prediction and dynamic threshold are distributed constructed based on AI platform. Finally, multi-dimensional correlation analysis are achieved. Based on the metric of a system, a case study was conducted to verify that the method proposed in this paper is significantly superior of timeliness, accuracy and efficient.

articleTitle: Dissipating Energy Flow Analysis of a Constant Power-controlled MMC for Sub-synchronous Oscillation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: When a modular multilevel converter (MMC) is connected to a weak grid or wind turbine, there’s a risk of sub-synchronous oscillation. Due to the complexity of MMC topology, conventional time/frequency-domain methods may have drawbacks in studying MMC sub-synchronous oscillation. This paper proposed a dissipating energy-based method for sub-synchronous oscillation analysis of MMC. First, considering the role of PLL and constant power control loop, the AC terminal dynamic of MMC is studied. Then, the expression of the average slope of MMC dissipating energy flow is derived, which reflects the source/sink characteristic associated with the damping level of MMC. Finally, simulations are made on a MMC-integrated system. Simulation results demonstrate the relationship between system parameters and sub-synchronous oscillations from the perspective of dissipating energy flow.

articleTitle: Short-term Charging Load Forecasting for Electric Vehicles with a Multilayer LSTM Model Considering Sliding Windows and Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the large-scale development of electric vehicles (EVs), accurate short-term charging load forecasting for EVs is the basis of vehicle to grid (V2G) interaction. In this paper, considering the uncertainties of EV users' charging behavior, a multi-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model considering sliding windows and online learning is proposed for short-term forecasting. Several typical features including peak and valley tariffs, environment temperature, charging date, charging time, historical average charging load are extracted considering their correlations with charging load. A multilayer LSTM model considering sliding window is proposed by inputting the typical feature matrix, and an online learning method is added to the model to improve the processing speed of the model for fast and accurate short-term charging load prediction. Finally, the proposed multilayer LSTM model considering sliding window and online learning is demonstrated to have unique advantages in terms of robustness, processing speed and prediction accuracy through practical examples.

articleTitle: A Fast Power Distribution Strategy for Overspeed Deloading Control of Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Overspeed deloading control (ODC) is an important technical approach for wind farm (WF) to participate in system frequency regulation. Due to the stochastic variation of wind resources over time, ODC needs to adjust rapidly in response to real-time wind speeds. Optimization-based methods can enhance ODC control, achieving optimal control effects. To allocate the power command of each wind turbine generator (WTG) within a WF efficiently, a complex non-convex optimization problem that maximizes the stored rotor kinetic energy needs to be solved. However, slow solution speed limits the application of this technology. This paper proposes a fast power distribution strategy for ODC of WF. First, the complex non-convex optimization problem is converted into a quadratic programming (QP) through linear approximation. Then, the distribution characteristic of the QP’s optimal solution is analyzed and proven. Based on the characteristic, the optimal solution is adjusted to eliminate the error introduced by the linear approximation in the power equality constraint. Finally, a WF model comprising thirty doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs) is established. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Innovative V2G Control Strategy for Isolated AC-DC Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To enhance the safety and stability of Vehicle-to-Grid interactions within new power systems, and to improve the seamless integration of a large number of electric vehicles with the power grid, this paper introduces a novel V2G control strategy for electric vehicles utilizing Isolated AC-DC Matrix Converters. An advanced Virtual Synchronous Generator control strategy, which engages in coordinated modulation, has been developed. This approach not only ensures safer charging and discharging processes for electric vehicles but also simulates the inertial and damping characteristics of synchronous generators. It effectively mitigates the grid impacts associated with mass electric vehicle integration, thereby enhancing the overall stability of modern power systems. A simulation of the electric vehicle charging and discharging process was conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, confirming the validity and feasibility of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Analysis of Internal Discharge and Burn in 750kV HGIS Disconnector Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: HGIS is a new type of integrated electrical equipment, structurally similar to GIS but without the inclusion of bus equipment. It has the advantage of having the bus not installed in an SF6 gas chamber but exposed, thus offering clear and concise connections, convenient installation and maintenance, flexible modular design, and high operational reliability. This paper deeply analyzes an internal fault of a 750kV HGIS disconnector switch that led to the tripping of related protection within the station. Through rigorous analysis, the root cause of the fault was accurately identified, and effective solutions and preventive measures were proposed to significantly enhance the operational reliability of the HGIS equipment within the station.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Online Monitoring Methods for Inertia in New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the decrease of inertia caused by the grid-connected large-scale new energy in the new power system, the demand to evaluate the inertia of power system has become urgent, and the on-line monitoring of inertia based on PMU measurement data is considered as an effective method at present. Three typical online monitoring methods are discussed respectively which are ordinary calculation method, integral calculation method and differential calculation method. The theoretical calculation of these three typical methods is presented. Simulation analysis is carried out by IEEE39 nodes with load increase and cutting off of generator respectively, and the characteristics of each inertia calculation method are compared and analyzed, and a conclusion that the error of ordinary calculation method is smallest and most stable among these three methods, which is recommended. It can provide reference for online calculation and analysis of inertia in the future.

articleTitle: Fault analysis of AC power supply cables in power plants affected by low voltage ride through device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The article proposes a fault traveling wave characteristic analysis method about AC power supply cables fault in power supply system of power plant key auxiliary motor. First, a small step simulation model including VVVF(Variable voltage and variable frequency) and low voltage ride through(LVRT) device is constructed. Then, the fault characteristics of voltage and current signal about key auxiliary AC power supply cable faults are derived. Furthermore, the signals are analyzed by wavelet methods, to achieve accurate fault location based on the traveling wave principle. Simulation shows that under disturbances or faults, there will be sudden changes and noise caused by electronic components in AC power supply system to the plant motor. By applying wavelet analysis methods, the sudden changes can be accurately identified. Compared with current signals, voltage signals have more significant amplitude changes and less noise impact. Due to the presence of power electronic switching devices, the three-phase power signal switches are not synchronized, and symmetrical faults also have zero sequence components in the sudden changes caused by faults. Therefore, fault analysis can use phase components or zero sequence components. At the same time, the load side current also needs to consider the sudden changes caused by noise and electronic devices. In the simulation case, the main energy of most of the voltage and current signal sudden changes is concentrated in the frequency band of 12.5-18.75kHz, which can be used to set the sampling parameters for accurate fault location equipment.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of LCC-MMC Cascaded Hybrid HVDC for Receiving-End Fault Overcurrent Limiting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Receiving-end short circuit fault will lead to the DC voltage reduction in the LCC-MMC cascaded hybrid HVDC system. It can cause the active power surplus of the renewable energy and reactive power changes of the sending-end LCC, which both contribute to overcurrent of the sending-end MMC. To address this issue, a coordinated control consisting an active power control and an improved voltage dependent current order limit (VDCOL) is firstly proposed. The former control aims to achieve DC current regulation and active power balance between AC/DC sides of the sending-end MMC. Based on the reactive power variation characteristics analysis during the DC voltage recovery, the latter control is proposed to prevent overcurrent of sending-end MMC via defining the operation region. Finally, the effectiveness of the coordinated fault current limiting control is validated by simulation in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Analysis of Performance Improvement in Multi-Frequency and Multi-System Integrated Positioning Based on the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the maturity of the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) and the deployment of the BeiDou-3 system (BDS-3), more abundant frequency resources are now available for positioning. In recent years, the construction of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite internet has also become a national priority. Combined with the future requirements for a more ubiquitous Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) network, the integration of these two systems can provide rich multi-frequency signal data and diverse observation measurements, thereby enhancing the accuracy and reliability of positioning services. However, most current studies on multi-frequency and multi-system observation combinations in positioning focus on simulation results at the phenomenological level, without deeply analyzing the underlying mathematical principles. This paper, based on the definition of the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB), provides a detailed derivation and analysis of how multi-frequency and multi-system observation combinations can improve positioning accuracy. This analysis offers theoretical support for the future construction and application of a more ubiquitous PNT network.

articleTitle: Research on Protection Configuration Method for Low Voltage Flexible DC Interconnection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Flexible interconnection devices are mostly voltage source converters composed of fully controlled power electronic devices. When a single pole grounding fault or inter pole short circuit fault occurs on the DC side of the interconnection system, the fully controlled devices inside the interconnection device will quickly lock, and the diodes in anti-parallel with the fully controlled devices may burn out due to overcurrent. This article proposes a protection device for flexible interconnection devices, which can quickly block short-circuit current or limit short-circuit interruption within a certain range when a fault occurs on the DC side, thereby protecting the power electronic components inside the device from damage. At the same time, with the line protection and equipment protection of the grid, accurate fault location can be achieved, effectively reducing the range of power outages caused by faults and improving the reliability of system operation.

articleTitle: Wind Speed Forecasting Based on Denoising Diffusion Model and Multivariate-Aware Spatiotemporal Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As a renewable resource with significant potential, wind energy presents considerable challenges for its integration into the energy grid due to its inherent randomness. Therefore, accurate wind speed forecasting is crucial for effectively utilizing wind energy. Existing wind speed forecasting methods still fall short in modeling spatiotemporal correlations and lack sufficient consideration of the relationships between wind speed and other auxiliary variables, such as temperature and pressure. This limitation affects their performance in complex wind speed forecasting scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a multivariate-aware spatiotemporal diffusion model (MASTDM) for wind speed forecasting. This model is a probabilistic forecasting approach based on Diffusion Denoising Probabilistic Models (DDPM), which effectively models temporal and spatial correlations using the self-attention mechanism of transformers. Furthermore, it explicitly models the multivariate correlations and the interdependencies between wind speed and auxiliary temporal information. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves comprehensive and significant performance improvements over various baseline methods.

articleTitle: Wildfire Detection and Localization in Power Transmission Corridors using the DETR Algorithm: A Critical Component for the Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wildfires near power transmission lines pose serious threats to energy infrastructure and can disrupt energy distribution. In the context of the energy internet, where real-time monitoring is essential, timely wildfire detection is critical. However, traditional detection methods face challenges such as environmental noise and the difficulty of identifying small-scale fires. In this context, this paper proposes using the DEtection TRansformer (DETR) algorithm for wildfire detection and localization around transmission lines, which leverages the powerful Transformer architecture for object detection. DETR's end-to-end design simplifies the process, offering enhanced accuracy by utilizing global context understanding. Experimental results on real-world wildfire datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional CNN-based methods in terms of detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved CBBA Algorithm for Task Allocation in Multi-UAV Inspections of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The technology of multi-UAV coordination and formation flight has a broad prospect in the field of power system inspection. Aiming at the collaborative operation of multiple UAVs in foreign object removal tasks during power inspection, this paper proposes an improved CBBA algorithm to address the task allocation problem of heterogeneous UAVs in dynamic and time-sensitive environments. The algorithm integrates the distributed structure of market mechanisms and the convergence idea of consensus strategies, which is particularly suitable for dealing with time-varying and dynamic task allocation scenarios. This paper proposes an optimized CBBA algorithm that improves the communication structure and reward function, introduces and optimizes the CBBA-LR algorithm to handle task conflicts, and uses a grouped multithreading pre-treatment mechanism to reduce computational load. These improvements enable the algorithm to ensure the reasonableness of task allocation while guaranteeing the efficiency of search and rescue, and can quickly provide effective task allocation schemes for large-scale UAV swarms. Simulation results verify the advantages of the improved CBBA algorithm in improving task allocation efficiency and reducing computational pressure.

articleTitle: A Method of Calculating the Cost of Energy Storage Providing Primary Frequency Regulation for Power Systems with Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy storage participation in frequency regulation is emerging as a crucial aspect of building a new-type power system. However, there is a lack of a comprehensive evaluation mechanism for the cost of energy storage in frequency regulation, which significantly hinders its further promotion. To address this issue, this paper starts from the framework of the power system dispatching model. Firstly, models for energy storage participation in frequency regulation and system frequency regulation are established. These models are then integrated into system dispatch to construct a power system dispatching model that includes energy storage providing frequency regulation services. By solving the power system dispatching model, dual multipliers corresponding to the frequency regulation constraints are obtained. Leveraging marginal cost pricing theory, the cost of energy storage providing frequency regulation services is derived from these dual multipliers. Finally, simulations are conducted using an improved IEEE 14-bus system.

articleTitle: Study on CO Detection Based on Wavelength Modulated Cantilever Enhanced Photoacoustic Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to its excellent insulation and arc extinguishing properties, SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> is widely used in gas insulated equipment. When it comes to organic insulating materials, CO will be generated under faults such as partial discharge or overheating in SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas insulated equipment. In this paper, based on the cantilever enhanced photoacoustic spectroscopy technology, a CO near infrared detection platform is built, the optimal modulation frequency and modulation depth of the system are studied, and the detection effect of the first four harmonics is studied. Finally, the second harmonic detection with the highest signal-to-noise ratio and good stability is adopted, and the results show that the lower detection limit of the system is 13.7ppm, and the linearity of the response of multi-concentration CO is verified. This work can provide a reference for the monitoring of the insulation status of gas insulated equipment and the safe and stable operation of the power system.

Index Terms: Energy In The Form Of Heat

articleTitle: Rationality Analysis on the Location of Distributed Generation Access based on Load Moment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Based on the large demand of distributed photovoltaic access in the new power system planning, this paper realizes the rapid computation of the node voltage. Based on the threshold of the maximum allowable voltage drop of 10kV of 7%, considering the difference of the distributed power distribution lines, the feeder access, lateral access, single-node access and multi-node access simulation scenarios are provided to estimate the complexity of the distributed generation access according to the reasonable range of voltage drop.

articleTitle: Research on the Multi Modal Adaptability of Adjustable Load Resources in Spot and Peak Shaving Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid development of China's spot market construction, the demand for stimulating large-scale adjustable loads through market means is becoming increasingly urgent. This article first establishes a declaration model for the regulatory capacity of market entities. The sequential clearing mode and the joint clearing mode for adjustable load participation in spot and peak shaving markets are proposed. Then adaptability analysis of different modes based on case simulations and are conducted. At last, Finally, according to the development of China's electricity market, suggestions are provided to explore a more suitable trading model for adjustable loads participating in the spot market that meets the needs of China's power grid.

articleTitle: Carbon emission index calculation and influencing factors analysis of coal-fired power plants considering distributed photovoltaic and integrated energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Coal power is the main source of carbon emission of electricity and its unit carbon emission index is the basic basis for implementing low-carbon planning and operation. Considering the availability of data of coal-fired power plants, a calculation method of carbon emission index of coal-fired units based on material balance is proposed. This method takes into account the easy operability of macro statistics and the accuracy of technical application, and integrates the compilation of macro GHG inventories with the operation indicators of micro planning, which can improve the accuracy of the compilation of departmental GHG inventories and provide basic data for the implementation of emission reduction indicators in the planning and operation of low-carbon power systems. At the same time, the peak load capacity of cogeneration units can be improved and the load level of power system can be increased by the technology of electric heating and heat storage. The correctness and practicality of the proposed method are verified by case study of an actual coal-fired power plant, and the analysis on its influencing factors shows that the order of carbon emission intensity of coal-fired generation units is not independent on their coal consumption.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Internal Electric Field of the Transformer Under Overvoltage Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Reasonable insulation structure of transformer can ensure its safe and stable operation. However, the internal structure of transformer is complicated, and its electric field distribution is often difficult to calculate. This paper presents a model based on finite element analysis which can accurately calculate the electric field distribution inside the transformer. The model provides a theoretical basis for ensuring the safety of transformer operation under the condition of overvoltage. In addition, a two-dimensional model of the main insulation structure of 110kV transformer is established. The electric field distribution can be analyzed by the above model, which provides theoretical support for designing transformer insulation under overvoltage condition.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Optimization Scheduling Strategy for Photovoltaic-Storage-Load Virtual Power Plant Considering Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the dual carbon goals and the increasing penetration of renewable energy, the volatility of photovoltaic (PV) output generation poses significant challenges to the stable operation of the power systems. In this context, the PV-storage-load Virtual Power Plant (VPP), which integrates PV, energy storage system (ESS), electric vehicles (EVs) and flexible loads, has become an important method to enhance flexibility of the power systems. Therefore, a day-ahead optimization scheduling strategy for a PV-storage-load VPP considering EVs is proposed. First, the important role of the PV-storage-load VPP in enhancing the flexibility of the power system under a high proportion of renewable energy is analyzed. Then, with the objective of minimizing the total operational cost of the VPP’s day-ahead scheduling, a day-ahead optimization scheduling model for the PV-storage-load VPP considering EV constraints is constructed. Finally, a case study is conducted on a PV-storage-load VPP in a certain region of Zhejiang province of China. The simulation results show that the proposed model is applicable to day-ahead scheduling scenarios of the VPP in different seasons and can effectively promote the consumption of renewable energy and reduce the operational costs of the VPP.

articleTitle: Supply Function Equilibrium-based Generation Capacity Expansion Planning for Capacity Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents a generation capacity expansion planning method for the capacity markets with generation companies’ market power. The strategies of the system operator and generation companies in the capacity market are formulated as a bi-level optimization model. The model is solved by analyzing the competition of generation companies as a non-cooperative game and employing Supply Function Equilibrium to obtain the capacity prices. The case studies verified the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing the capacity payment and mitigating the abuse of market power possessed by generation companies.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control Strategy of DFIG Wind Farm for Transient Reactive Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to enhance the LVRT capability of wind farm, the transient reactive power characteristics of wind farms needs to be improved. In this paper, a transient reactive power control strategy of GSC cooperate with multiple reactive power sources in the wind farm is proposed. Firstly, a DFIG wind farm model with SVG reactive power compensation device is established. The influence of SVG transient reactive power characteristics on the reactive voltage characteristics of the wind farm during the voltage fault recovery stage is analyzed, and the SVG transient response time constant is parameterized. Then the cooperative control strategy is carried out. This control strategy improves the transient reactive power response speed of the wind farm, enables the wind farm to quickly retract reactive power during the fault recovery stage, suppresses overvoltage at the wind farm's PCC, and the control strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Attention Mechanism Based Calculation of Pseudo-measurements of Key Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of insufficient real-time measurements in the system after access to large-scale distributed re-sources, low system redundancy, poor efficiency of traditional model training, and limited accuracy of pseudo-measurements, a key node pseudo-measurement modelling and calculation method based on an attention mechanism is proposed. First, a node comprehensive importance index is constructed using the weighted sum of three indicators: node connectivity, node density, and node power intermediation. A key node screening method based on comprehensive importance is proposed to measure the importance of nodes in the network from three perspectives: structure, state, and frequency. Second, the key nodes are taken as the research object, and a CNN-GRU pseudo-measurement generation model based on the attention mechanism is established to compute and deduce the pseudo-measurement of the injected power at the key nodes. Finally, simulation tests are carried out on an IEEE 33-node standard distribution network. The results show that the proposed method can correctly identify key nodes in the network and significantly improve the accuracy of the pseudo-measurement data.

articleTitle: Using the Multi-head Self-attention Mechanism to Analyze and Extract Key Features from Power Grids with Complex Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the proportion of distributed renewable energy generation rises, the structure of regional power grids is becoming more intricate and varied. Representing the spatial characteristics of the power grid accurately is crucial for dispatchers to gather essential feature information. Traditional methods, like graph convolutional neural networks, are limited to capturing information only from neighboring nodes. This paper, referencing Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), proposes a power grid representation learning method based on the Multi-head Self-Attention (MSA) for feature extraction of power grids. The proposed method’s effectiveness in addressing the challenge of power grid feature extraction is demonstrated through an improved IEEE 9-bus test system case study.

articleTitle: A Further Performance Improvement of Distributed Photovoltaic Location Planning and Hosting Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The large-scale integration of distributed photovoltaics (PV) into the distribution network has introduced challenges such as voltage over-limit, voltage fluctuation, and branch capacity over-limit, which pose risks to the safe and stable operation of the power grid. This paper addresses the urgent need to plan the location of distributed PV installations effectively and enhance their hosting capacity by leveraging flexible resources. Specifically, we consider two types of flexible resources: network reconfiguration and mobile energy storage, and propose a coordinated approach for PV installation location planning. Taking into account the spatial-temporal characteristics of flexible resources and aiming to achieve a balance between economic viability and hosting capacity, we establish and solve a two-stage stochastic optimization model. This model enables us to determine the optimal installation location for PV systems and devise an operation strategy for flexible resources. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed method, we conduct a case study in a specific region of northwest China. The results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in improving the hosting capacity of distributed PV systems, as well as optimizing the utilization of flexible resources.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy of Wind-Solar-Hydrogen-Storage Integrated Energy System Based on P2G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this study, three different operating modes are calculated and analyzed by constructing multi-objective functions and applying dynamic differential evolution algorithm for the integrated energy system of industrial parks, and the results show that the optimization method effectively improves the efficiency of wind power consumption and energy utilization, enhances the environmental protection and flexibility of the system, and reduces the total cost of the system.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Energy Storage System Considering the Risk of Insufficient Flexibility in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To solve the problem of insufficient flexibility caused by high proportion of wind and solar resources accessing to distribution network, an energy storage system (ESS) allocation model considering the risk of insufficient flexibility is constructed. Firstly, the traditional confidence interval calculation method is improved by the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), and the conditional confidence interval of net load power is proposed. Secondly, the flexibility boundary of distribution network is constructed, and the risk cost caused by the over-limit of net load fluctuation is calculated to form the risk cost model of insufficient flexibility. Thirdly, the bi-level optimal allocation model of ESS considering flexibility, economy and reliability is constructed by fully calling the flexible resources. The upper layer is the ESS allocation decision layer, and the lower layer is operation optimization layer. Finally, case study is analyzed based on IEEE33 system to verify the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: A Two-layer Optimal Scheduling Model for Wind-Photovoltaic-Thermal-Storage System Considering Synergistic Application Value of Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Existing works on multi-energy complementary optimization scheduling primarily concentrate on the role of energy storage peak load reduction and off-peak load compensation to assist thermal power units with peak regulation. However, the broader application value of it remains to be fully explored in the wind-photovoltaic-thermal-storage combined system. To address this issue, we propose a two-layer optimal scheduling model that considers the synergistic application values of two scenarios. Energy storage can concurrently participate in the electricity energy market to obtain economic benefits. The upper layer concentrates on collaboratively optimizing the change/discharge power of the energy storage station. In the lower layer, the model cooperatively optimizes the output power of thermal power units. Simulation results of a typical day in the Xinjiang region demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other optimal scheduling models, lowering the total operating costs of the combined system.

articleTitle: Research on Stepless On-load Voltage Regulation Method Based on Auxiliary Potential Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the output voltage of the on-load tap changer is poor and the real-time performance is poor, a stepless on-load voltage regulation method based on auxiliary potential transformer is proposed. In this method, the power is absorbed from the power grid by the rectifier circuit, and the inverter is controlled by the SHE-PWM technology through the DSP to generate the required voltage, which is connected to the power grid in series through the auxiliary potential transformer, so as to realize the stepless on-load voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Random Matrix Theory-Based Data-Driven Framework for Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy, microgrids face challenges in maintaining grid stability due to variability and uncertainty in energy supply. Enhancing microgrid flexibility through demand response is essential, but accurately assessing demand response potential is complex due to high-dimensional and noisy data.
