This paper proposes a framework combining Random Matrix Theory (RMT) for high-dimensional data analysis and a Deep Auto-Encoder Network (DAE) for feature extraction and visualization. RMT identifies hidden correlations between microgrid users and environmental factors, optimizing demand response strategies. The DAE reduces data dimensionality, providing clear visual insights into user behavior and demand response potential. A case study based on data from a southern city in China demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method. Results show seasonal variations in demand response potential, highlighting the need for tailored strategies. This approach enhances situational awareness and supports renewable energy integration in microgrids.

articleTitle: Collaborative Demand Response of Distribution Networks and Microgrids Based on Edge Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the dual carbon goals, the construction of a new power system is progressing steadily, and the large-scale integration of renewable energy has brought significant challenges to the operation of the power system. Based on the coupling between distribution networks and microgrids in terms of physical connection and information interaction, a coordinated demand response model between the two is gradually taking shape. Meanwhile, the introduction of the concept of edge IoT provides solutions for power system dispatching. This paper designs a distribution-microgrid coordinated interaction framework based on edge agents, where the distribution network is divided into multiple sub-regions, each with an edge agent acting as a distributed control center. These sub-regions communicate with the centralized control center to achieve coordinated demand response based on edge agents. Finally, case studies are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Temperature Field Simulation of A Six-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor With Stator Water-Cooling Pipe Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The effective heat dissipation structure is very critical for large power multiphase permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) driving. In this paper, a water-cooling pipe structure placed in the stator core yoke of a six-phase PMSM is adopted. To accurately analyze the cooling effect of the pipe structure, the multi-physics coupling method is used to calculate the temperature field. Firstly, the impact of the stator pipe structure on the electromagnetic performance is analyzed, and the copper and iron losses are calculated. Secondly, a three-dimensional fluid-solid coupling simulation model is established for the calculation of fluid and temperature field. Temperature distribution of the six-phase PMSM is analyzed. Finally, experimental verification is conducted to confirm the effectiveness of the stator water-cooling pipe structure.

articleTitle: Minimizing Age-of-Information for Multisystem Energy IoT System with Multiple Subsystems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Age of Information (AoI), an important measure of information timeliness, plays a critical role in energy Internet of Things (IoT) systems. Maintaining a low AoI means that energy systems have access to up-to-date information to make more accurate and reliable decisions and ensure safe, efficient and reliable system operation.Focusing on a wireless networked energy IoT system with multiple subsystems, this paper analyzes the lower limit value of the average AoI of the system under unreliable wireless transmission, and verifies the accuracy of the theoretical analysis results through simulation experiments. Meanwhile, the experiments also reveal the effects of the number of channels, channel state (transmission success rate) and data sampling rate on the average AoI, which provides an important theoretical basis for optimizing the timeliness of energy IoT information.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Spectral Characteristics of the Interface Defects between the Conductor Insert and Tri-post Insulator of 550 kV GIL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper explores the ultrasonic transmission characteristics within the interface bonding region of epoxy resin and metal inserts in epoxy resin insulators. A specialized ultrasonic flaw detection platform was constructed specifically to analyze the epoxy resin/metal insert interface bonding region. To improve measurement accuracy, the probe structure was optimized, enhancing both the interfacial bonding and the ultrasonic signal transmission between the probe and the test area. The study examined the ultrasonic transmission properties across the metal inserts and the epoxy resin/metal interface regions, providing valuable insights into the effectiveness of interface bonding. The findings of this research contribute to the development of ultrasonic testing methods for evaluating the integrity of epoxy resin insulator bonding interfaces, offering a basis for further advancements in insulator reliability assessment and maintenance.

articleTitle: Network-Constrained Energy Trading for Integrated Energy Microgrid Clusters with Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As prosumers, data centers can achieve multi-energy coupling through the scheduling of computational tasks. Establishing a rational framework for energy and information trading in integrated energy systems that include data centers is crucial for enhancing renewable energy utilization and reducing energy costs. This paper proposes an energy trading model for integrated energy microgrids (IEMs) with data centers, considering both information flow and energy flow within multienergy networks. First, an IEM operation model is developed, consisting of a data center, photovoltaic generation system, small diesel generator, heat pump, and energy storage. The model also includes an electric-thermal network that connects the IEMs at various nodes. Compared to previous IEM cluster models, this model improves energy coupling through waste heat recovery from the data center and enhances the flexibility of energy transmission by establishing connections between IEMs and the network. Additionally, a mechanism is adopted that enables simultaneous peer-to-peer energy trading between IEMs and energy transactions between IEMs and the multi-energy networks. Finally, alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm is employed to optimize the dispatch strategies for each time period. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces energy costs and increases the consumption of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Analysis on Difference of Dynamic Characteristics and Stability Between Synchronous Generator and Virtual Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of the power system, new energy generation equipment is gradually replacing traditional synchronous generators, and the regulation resources are becoming increasingly scarce. Using virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control technology to control the grid-connected converter of new energy generation equipment is an effective method to address this challenge. VSG simulates the rotor dynamics equation of the generator in the controller, so it is considered to be able to provide inertia and damping for the system. However, existing research results lack analysis of the differences between VSG and synchronous power generation, resulting in inaccurate evaluation of VSG stability and dynamic characteristics. This paper takes VSG based photovoltaic system connected to microgrids and distribution system as the research object, and analysis the differences between VSG and synchronous generators from several dimensions such as the characteristics of the prime mover, the implementation method of the rotor motion equation, and influence of the line impedance of the connected system. Theoretical analysis and simulation have shown that the above differences will lead to differences in stability and parameter security domain between VSG and synchronous generators.

articleTitle: Cooperative Yaw and Induction Control for Wind Farm and Its Effectiveness in Providing Secondary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dual point gradient descent method specifically designed to tackle the challenge of local optima in wind farm power optimization problems. Unlike conventional approaches that frequently get trapped in suboptimal solutions, this method enhances the likelihood of achieving global optimality. We extensively test the proposed approach through a series of case studies, focusing on its convergence speed and capability to maintain global optimality, particularly for wind farms operating in Automatic Generation Control (AGC) mode. The results confirm the method’s effectiveness, showcasing its potential as a robust solution for optimizing wind farm power output under varying operational conditions.

articleTitle: Transient Performance Analysis of Aggregated VSG Models in Photovoltaic Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the significant increase in the proportion of new energy power generation, power electronic devices represented by voltage source converters have been rapidly adopted in power systems, profoundly changing the structure of modern power systems. However, high-penetration renewable energy power systems face stability challenges. To address this issue, Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) technology has emerged. VSG technology virtualizes grid-connected inverters as synchronous generators, automatically regulating their active and reactive power output in response to fluctuations in grid voltage, frequency, and amplitude, providing crucial support to the grid. In the simulation analysis of photovoltaic power stations, current aggregation methods do not take into account the consistency of transient performance before and after aggregation. This paper modifies the voltage and current dual-loop control structure to achieve equivalent aggregation. Ten parallel-operated VSGs are equivalent to a single VSG with the same power rating. This achieves an equivalent aggregation method that does not affect transient response. The accuracy of the conclusion is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: Evaluate the Performance of New Power System: A Multi-criteria Decision-making Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: One significant step China has taken to address climate change is the implementation of the new power system (NPS). Due to its unique characteristics, it differs significantly from traditional power systems. Thus, this research builds a comprehensive performance evaluation framework for NPS based on the multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) method. First, a thorough performance evaluation index system was built from four aspects based on the NPS's characteristics. Next, the CRITIC and TOPSIS methodologies are used to form the comprehensive evaluation model. Lastly, a case study is used to verify the efficacy and applicability of the suggested approach using actual data from 2021 to 2023 collected in China. The outcome demonstrates that: in comparison to infrastructure construction, emission reduction performance is the most significant NPS evaluation factor. Moreover, China’s NPS performance has been greatly improved during 2021-2022, while declined slightly in 2023.

articleTitle: A Multi-Time Scale Optimization Dispatch Model for Virtual Power Plants Based on Master-Slave Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the issues of high demand response costs and low renewable energy utilization in traditional virtual power plants (VPPs), this paper proposes a multi-time-scale optimal dispatch model for VPPs based on leader-follower game theory. Firstly, a day-ahead game model for VPPs is established by leveraging the leader-follower relationship between load aggregators and loads from electric vehicles and air conditioners. Based on this, combined with the forecasting information of wind power, photovoltaic power, and loads, a rolling optimization model for intra-day scheduling is adopted to proactively optimize and adjust the output plan of renewable energy sources. The feasibility of the proposed method is verified through case studies, and the experimental results show that the proposed framework can help VPPs reduce demand response costs and improve the consumption rate of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Research on Rotor Protection Scheme for Variable Speed Pumped Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Variable speed pumped storage units utilize three-phase low-frequency AC excitation, and the probability of internal failure in rotor windings is high. However, the existing rotor protection systems do not adequately meet safety and sensitivity requirements. This paper analyzes the rotor low frequency signal acquisition technology because of the low frequency signal transformation problem of the electromagnetic instrument transformer. This paper simulates and analyzes the fault characteristics of rotor single phase grounding and short circuiting between phases via resistance under power generation, pumping and startup conditions, puts forward the protection criterion that reacts to changes in the amplitude of three phase voltage of the rotor, and based on this, puts forward a comprehensive rotor protection scheme that is effective in reflecting the weak faults of rotor faults.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Enabled Green Energy Recycling System: An Example of Fine Disassembly and Regeneration of Automotive Lithium Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy Internet and system integration promote the development of green energy, but the battery recycling problem is becoming increasingly serious, especially the proliferation of used lithium batteries for electric vehicles. The traditional crushing method of recycling has problems such as low purity, limited economic value and environmental pollution. Fine disassembly, as an emerging technology, enhances the efficiency and value of resource recovery through flexible deconstruction and graded fine disassembly of pole pieces. In the face of complex working conditions, the combination of deep learning and machine vision detection technology provides intelligent and stable solutions for battery core pack dismantling, ensures the safety and efficiency of the dismantling process, promotes the upgrading of the green energy recycling system, and realizes the efficient recycling of resources and sustainable development of the environment.

articleTitle: Distributed PV Power Anomaly Detection Based on LSTM-Informer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic power plants cover a wide range of areas, and due to the unpredictability of meteorological factors and the diverse and complex installation environments, interference factors are difficult to eliminate completely. Under such a background, it is particularly difficult to accurately determine the power abnormality of distributed PV equipment. Therefore, how to accurately identify the power abnormality of distributed PV systems with the help of limited metering data has become an urgent problem for the industry. In this paper, a distributed PV power anomaly detection model based on LSTM-Informer is proposed, which is able to identify the three weather conditions of sunny, cloudy and rainy days by calculating the kurtosis of the power curve according to the characteristics of the PV power curve of different weather types, and use the Monte Carlo method based on LSTM-Informer to train the normal output interval, and determine whether the distributed PV system is operating abnormally by calculating the coverage of the time-series power data to be detected in the normal output interval. In this paper, simulation experiments are carried out using PV data from a power station in Australia, and the results show that the model can effectively detect power anomalies in distributed PV systems, with high detection rate, accuracy rate and low false alarm rate.

articleTitle: Data Engineering and ML for Real-Time Fraud Detection in Financial Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Fraud detection remains a critical challenge for financial institutions, especially in high-frequency transaction environments. This study proposes a real-time, AI-driven fraud detection system utilizing XGBoost and optimized data engineering to process up to 10,000 transactions per second with minimal latency of 7ms. The system addresses the issue of data imbalance in fraudulent transactions while ensuring transparency through Explainable AI (XAI), utilizing SHAP values to make model predictions interpretable. Experimental results on real-world financial transaction datasets show that the proposed system achieves 99.2% accuracy, with precision and recall scores exceeding 95% and 93%, respectively. When compared to baseline models and existing literature. our approach demonstrates superior scalability, speed, and accuracy. This solution offers a robust and efficient framework for real-time fraud detection, ensuring both performance and transparency, while maintaining low prediction latency, making it ideal for modern financial services.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Modulation Strategy for Fractional Level MMC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) applied in medium-voltage field features a smaller quantity of submodules (SMs) and relatively lower voltage quality. The fractional level MMC (FLMMC) adopting fractional level modulation (FLM) can effectively enhance the voltage quality of the MMC with fewer SMs. By introducing the square wave output mode into the working modes of the fractional level SMs, a hybrid modulation strategy for FLMMC based on FLM and square wave pulse width modulation, namely fractional level square wave pulse width modulation (FL-SWPWM) strategy, is proposed in this paper, which can further improve the voltage quality. The proposed FL-SWPWM is characterized by simple control and good scalability, and equivalently can increase the number of ac output voltage levels. Simulation results based on Matlab/Simulink reveal that under the proposed FL-SWPWM, the low-order harmonic content of the ac output voltage is significantly reduced, the voltage quality of the MMC with fewer SMs is greatly enhanced and the degree of current distortion is considerably decreased.

articleTitle: Research on a Comprehensive Optimization Modeling Method for Power Transfer of Substation Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of energy internet, high elastic distribution network can improve the economy and reliability of the system by configuring various sources, loads and storage resources. For the high-elastic distribution network with controllable distributed micro-sources, demand-side management resources and energy storage resources connected to the microgrid, the optimal load transfer model under fault conditions is established considering the call of source-load-storage resources. The established model takes into account the call cost of source-load-storage resources and takes the minimization of the comprehensive loss of power load during the fault period as the objective function. At the same time, the establishment of the model also takes into account the necessary constraints such as Branch circuit capacity constraints, system power balance constraints, node voltage constraints, and Unit output power constraints. Finally, the validity and correctness of the model are verified by formulating the load transfer scheme for a high-elastic distribution network based on IEEE33 standard node system under fault conditions.

articleTitle: Comparison of Active Power Response Rapidity Between Small-Scale and Large-Scale Pumped Storage Plants under Power Control Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Pumped storage plays an important role for regulating emerging power systems. However, large-scale pumped storage plants (LPSPs) encounter several challenges, including site selection constraints, high construction costs, and stringent head height requirements, which hinder their sustainable development. In contrast, small-scale pumped storage plants (SPSPs) offer greater flexibility and potential for integration with distributed renewable energy sources, positioning them as a promising direction for future developments in energy storage. This study aims to compare the active power response rapidity of small-scale and large-scale pumped storage plants. First, numerical models for both small-scale and large-scale pumped storage plants were established using MATLAB/Simulink. Next, the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) was utilized to weight indicators associated with regulation rapidity, thereby establishing an evaluation framework. Finally, the differences in active power response rapidity were assessed through time-domain simulations and quantitative analyses. The results indicate that, under the operating conditions analyzed in this study, the active power response rapidity of small-scale pumped storage plants exceeds that of large-scale plants, showing a 9.49% improvement under normalized conditions. This performance difference is primarily attributed to the influence of the surge tank on the regulation capabilities of large-scale plants. The findings highlight the advantages of small-scale pumped storage plants in terms of response rapidity, providing significant support for the optimal operation of pumped storage systems.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Configuration of Pumped Storage Energy in Power Grid Considering Voltage Transient Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy into the power system has solved energy shortages and environmental problems. In response to the problem of renewable energy units being disconnected from the grid due to excessive transient overvoltage after faults, this paper proposes a location selection method based on transient voltage safety indicators. Under the premise of meeting voltage safety crossing requirements, the configuration capacity of pumped storage is minimized, then established an optimized configuration model for pumped storage that takes into account voltage transient stability, and solved it using an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm; Simulations were conducted on the modified Nordic system in the northern region and equivalent external systems to determine the optimal configuration nodes and capacity of pumped storage power stations. In response to three-phase short circuit faults, the changes in the bus voltage and transmission channel power of wind turbines before and after the configuration of pumped storage were investigated. The simulation results verified that the optimized configuration method of pumped storage proposed in this paper can effectively improve the transient voltage safety level of the power grid at the sending end and reduce the deviation between the external transmission channel power and the arranged transmission power after faults.

articleTitle: Wind Power Forecasting Research Based on Autoformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the complexity and uncertainty in wind power forecasting and to enhance prediction accuracy and stability, this study proposes a wind power forecasting model based on Autoformer. By leveraging its self-attention mechanism, the model effectively captures the trend and periodic characteristics inherent in wind power data. The model's performance was validated using data from Wind Farm A in Liaoning Province, comparing its forecasting accuracy against LSTM, Informer, Transformer, and Autoformer models. Prediction outcomes were evaluated using mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) as metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that the Autoformer model outperformed others across all evaluation metrics, with the predicted curve closely aligning with actual values. Compared to other models, Autoformer achieved significantly lower MSE, MAE, and MAPE values, and a higher R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value, proving its substantial advantage in capturing dynamic power fluctuations and enhancing prediction precision in wind power forecasting. Future research may explore multi-model integration to further improve forecast stability and applicability.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Energy Management System for Based on Microservice Architecture and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As software architecture continues to evolve and system scales expand, microservices architecture has gradually become the mainstream paradigm in software development, particularly well-suited for addressing increasingly complex business logic and the need for rapid feature iteration. The scalability, flexibility, and fault tolerance of microservices provide new solutions for traditional Energy Management Systems (EMS) in handling complex energy demands and supply management. However, challenges persist in areas such as resource scheduling in dynamic and complex environments, load balancing, and fault recovery mechanisms, making it difficult to meet the requirements of distributed energy and rapidly changing market conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes an EMS architecture optimization design based on a combination of microservices architecture and reinforcement learning techniques. By decoupling the system through microservices, the scalability and flexibility of the EMS are enhanced. Furthermore, leveraging the advantages of reinforcement learning algorithms in complex decision-making and adaptability to dynamic environments, the proposed system achieves intelligent decision-making and control. Based on this approach, a web-based microservice EMS for process industries has been developed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves system performance and exhibits strong adaptability to complex business demands.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of switching overvoltage waveform measuring in a 500kV substation using electro-optical E-field sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Electro-optical E-field sensors show great potential for substation voltage detection due to their wide frequency bandwidth and easy maintenance. However, in substations of 500kV and below, the coupling signals of adjacent conductors cannot be ignored due to the large number of outgoing lines and compact electrical structure. The existing decoupling method often results in a high transient overvoltage amplitude, making it challenging to provide engineering application. Therefore, a new overvoltage decoupling method has been developed to consider the influence of neighboring equipment and line operating voltages. This method utilizes the sensor waveform of the line to be measured before closing to calculate the matrix of coupling coefficients of the adjacent conductors in order to isolate their influence. Measurements of voltage waveforms during breaking and closing were conducted in a 500kV substation. The decoupled waveforms were compared with voltage measured by CVT and existing decoupling methods. The results demonstrate that electro-optical sensors have a wider frequency bandwidth than CVTs. Furthermore, the background signals of adjacent conductors can reach up to 30% of the steady-state amplitude of the measured signal, causing a decoupling error exceeding 100% in traditional methods. Compared with existing decoupling methods, the proposed method more effectively eliminates the influence of coupling signals from adjacent wires, resulting in more accurate reconstruction of transient voltages.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Voltage Balancing Control for MMC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The voltage balancing control of submodules’ (SM) capacitors is the key in modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct-current (MMC-HVDC) transmission system, where the sorting link for the SMs’ capacitor voltage has relatively high time and space complexity. According to the principle of the bitonic sorting algorithm, parallelism and pipeline technique, a parallel sorting network suitable for field programmable gate array (FPGA) is designed in this paper based on the idea of staged-calculation, which can reduce the time complexity of the voltage balancing control. Secondly, according to the characteristics for the voltage data of SMs’ capacitors and the sorting network, the data format input into the sorting network is designed. And the sorting network is designed to adapt to changes in the number of SMs and can be time-sharing reused, based on the ideas of redundant calculation and logical reuse, which can reduce the space complexity of the voltage balancing control. Finally, the proposed voltage balancing control is implemented based on FPGA, and its effectiveness is verified through in-the-loop simulation experiments based on RTDS.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of an Integrated Energy System by Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increase of global energy demand and the aggravation of environmental problems, the limitations of traditional energy in remote regions and isolated regions are becoming more and more obvious. These regions often face the challenges related to energy shortage and unstable supply, and single energy systems are difficult to meet their economic and reliability needs. Therefore, the development of hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) that combine multiple energy sources has become an effective way to solve these problems. In this study, we simultaneously consider the indicators of economy, environmental protection and reliability. The multi-objective optimization design and simulation of an off-grid wind-solar-diesel-storage hybrid renewable energy system in an island region are carried out using a genetic algorithm. To verify the validity of the constructed model, we use the power supply demand of a strategic island as an example. Energy management decision-making schemes with different emphases are obtained using the constructed renewable energy planning system to assist in the optimization of equipment combinations. In order to visualize the model constructed in this study and facilitate the operation in engineering applications, we developed a hybrid renewable energy management software platform based on the energy planning model, which has important theoretical reference significance and engineering practical value for the construction and deployment of energy systems.

articleTitle: The Cluster Partitioning and Autonomous Optimization Control Based on the Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the voltage limit issues caused by the large-scale integration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems into current distribution networks, this paper proposes a voltage control strategy based on cluster-based autonomous optimization. The strategy aims to minimize PV generation loss and line active power loss by optimizing the active and reactive power output of PV inverters. Using k-means clustering, the paper introduces an improved K-means clustering method based on the Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO) algorithm, considering the silhouette coefficient as the evaluation metric for network partitioning. The cluster autonomous optimization control rapidly adjusts the voltage within the cluster by updating the optimal solution and virtual balance node within the group, achieving voltage control through active power reduction. The proposed method is applied to a 10.5kV line in China to verify its effectiveness and feasibility.

articleTitle: Interval Forecast based on Markov Chain Monte Carlo with Autoregressive Recurrent Networks for Natural Gas Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Natural gas plays an important role in both modern life and national carbon neutral policies. In the case of companies, for example, being able to generate probabilistic forecast with confidence intervals is critical for procurement, storage and supply of natural gas. In this paper, a novel forecast method based on an autoregression recurrent network and Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm is proposed for natural gas consumption prediction. The application of Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm contributes to the implementation of deep learning techniques in decision making. The forecast accuracy of the proposed method is improved by about 5.87% compared to the state-of-the-art method through extensive empirical evaluation on the real gas dataset.

articleTitle: Dynamic and Adaptive Synchronization Analysis of a new Five-dimension Hyperchaotic System for Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power system is a typical nonlinear system, and its rich dynamic behavior can be regarded as a high-dimensional chaotic system, which is a mathematical theoretical direction for the study of power system excitation and response. The dynamic characteristics and adaptive synchronization of a new five-dimension hyper chaotic system is analyzed. Its dynamic characteristics from the aspects of dissipation, Lyapunov exponent diagram, and stability of equilibrium points are examined. A passive based adaptive synchronization problem between systems is considered by combining the theory of passivity and adaptive control methods. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted in MATLAB, and time-domain waveforms of state variables and error variables are plotted. The results show that adaptive hybrid synchronization is achieved between systems. The numerical simulation results indicate the correctness of the synchronization theory analysis and the effectiveness of the synchronization method.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Pseudo-Measurement Generation Based on Power Forecasting in Active Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of photovoltaic (PV) generation, state estimation in Active Distribution Systems (ADS) faces challenges due to insufficient real-time measurements. This paper proposes a comprehensive solution that combines PV power forecasting with Gaussian pseudo-measurement generation. First, an advanced spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN) algorithm is employed to achieve high-precision short-term forecasting of PV power, ensuring accurate predictions across various time periods and weather conditions. Then, based on the forecasted results and the topology of the distribution system, Gaussian-distributed pseudo-measurement data is generated to supplement areas with insufficient measurements, enhancing the completeness and reliability of state estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves robust estimation performance across different scenarios, significantly improving the situational awareness of ADS and providing critical support for the intelligent dispatch and optimized operation of the distribution network.

Author Keywords: Dual three-phase permanent magnet brushless AC machines

articleTitle: Generation method of anti-misoperation locking logic rules for substations based on typical wiring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At present, substations usually use electrical blocking facilities to achieve the function of anti-fault blocking, but new stations and new reconstruction and expansion stations have the problem of low efficiency in the compilation and review of anti-fault blocking logic rules, and also need a lot of manual debugging and checking time. In this paper, based on the typical substation wiring and anti-false blocking logic rules, the typical substation wiring library and the corresponding blocking logic library are constructed; then, the graphic editing module and graphic analysis module are constructed by combining the substation modelling method with the topology and other technologies. Finally, the automatic generation of anti-error latching logic rules is realised, which solves the problems of low efficiency and lack of reliability in the writing and checking of the corresponding substation anti-misoperation locking logic rules.

articleTitle: Modeling the equivalent of doubly fed wind turbine clusters using the K-means algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the swift growth in renewable energy sources, wind energy now constitutes a significant component of the worldwide energy framework. Incorporating wind farms into the existing power grid introduces novel difficulties concerning the grid's stability and dependability. In this paper, Wind velocity serves as the key parameter for categorizing wind patterns, combined with the pitch angle control, the K-means clustering algorithm is used to divide the wind field into three categories, and then the three types of wind fields are modeled with equivalent values, and finally the parameters of the equivalent wind turbines are identified, the discrepancy between the outcomes derived and the actual measured data is minimal, indicating that the equivalent model can better simulate the operation state of the actual wind farm. As the scale of new energy sources continues to grow, wind turbines have become increasingly important within the power grid.

articleTitle: SF6 Gas Leak Detector Based on Photoacoustic Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: SF6 is a synthetic gas with a potent greenhouse effect and is extensively used in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). This paper presents the design of a highly sensitive, miniaturized photoacoustic gas sensor specifically for SF6 leakage monitoring. Experimental results demonstrate that the sensor achieves a response of 14.47 μV/ppm within the concentration range of 0-100 ppm. Based on variance analysis, the detection limit for SF6 gas reaches 1.04 ppm with an integration time of just 1 second.

articleTitle: Study on Micro-mechanism of Protective Effect of Metal Passivator Against Multiple Sulfides in Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At present, there are few studies on the optimal additive concentration of passivator and the protective effectiveness of oil-paper insulation system containing multiple sulfides. Therefore, the passivator Methylbenzotriazole (TTA), which is widely used, and three typical sulfides, dibenzyl disulfide, hexadecanethiol and benzothiophene, are selected in this paper and simulated by reaction molecular dynamics. By measuring the van der Waals energy, molecular chain movement (MSD), elastic modulus and hydrogen bond number, the protective effect of TTA with different mass fractions on multiple sulfides was studied. The results show that TTA passivator can effectively protect the transformer oil-paper insulation system containing multiple sulfides. By reacting with oxygen to inhibit the lead substances required for the formation of corrosive sulfur and transferring from oil to insulating paper to form a protective film on the surface of copper windings, TTA passivator can hinder the reaction of sulfide and copper to a certain extent, and thus effectively delay the aging rate of oil-paper insulation. For insulating oil, before the mass fraction of passivator TTA was 150 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, the protective effect increased with the increase of passivator content. However, after 150 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, the aging of insulating oil was accelerated to a certain extent due to the solubility of TTA, but the aging rate was still lower than that of the blank control group. For insulating paper, the protective effect increases with the increase of passivator content, and TTA has no effect on the mechanical properties of insulating paper. From the perspective of comprehensive economy and protective effect, the best protective mass fraction of TTA is 50×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>.

articleTitle: Prediction and Analysis of Shared Bicycle Rental Demand Based on Feature Engineering and Regression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper utilizes machine learning algorithms to analyze various types of data of shared bicycles and predict the rental demand. It conducts a correlation analysis based on the influence of factors such as time, holidays, weather, season, and humidity on the demand for shared bicycles. Feature data is screened according to the correlation coefficient and a feature dataset is constructed. By comparing the real values with the predicted values after model training, it is found that the random forest regression model has better prediction performance in this study.

articleTitle: Power System Simulation Intelligent Assistant: A Chatbot Integrating Large Language Models and Domain Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Simulations are crucial for secure and economical operation of power systems. Recently, with the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 have demonstrated impressive capabilities in natural language processing tasks and their applications are being widely explored in many fields. However, directly applying LLMs in power system simulations is challenging due to their limitations in specialized domain knowledge. Despite this, LLMs offer significant flexibility in interactions, making them promising candidates for collaboration with existing power system domain models (PSDMs). To facilitate this integration, a collaboration framework between LLMs with PSDMs is proposed and a power system simulation intelligent assistant is developed based on this framework. The assistant guides users through power system simulations in a logical sequence with an interaction-driven exception-handling mechanism to improve robustness. Furthermore, the assistants based on different LLMs are compared.

articleTitle: The Group Acceleration Technology of Power Grid Mode Calculation Adapted to Power Generation Production Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A grouping acceleration principle is proposed to address the challenge of using traditional serial and parallel computing structures to significantly improve computational efficiency in production simulation calculations. This principle is used to process massive power grid calculations after production simulation. Firstly, the existing power generation production simulation is used to transform the ground state method based on the hourly output of power generation load balance data throughout the year, forming a task queue. Based on the computing resource capacity, it is divided into multiple subgroups to form a task matrix. Secondly, a bidirectional matrix parallel computing structure is constructed using multiple computing tasks within each subgroup and the split subgroups as units. Finally, parallel computing in both directions was initiated and completed, achieving a significant improvement in the computational efficiency of production simulation methods.

articleTitle: Distributionally robust scheduling of electric-thermal-hydrogen microgrid based on comprehensive norm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The electric-thermal-hydrogen microgrid provides a promising choice for hydrogen utilization and energy transition towards low carbon. However, the economic operation of microgrids is impeded by source uncertainties, thus, a distributionally robust scheduling model considering security constraints of hydrogen equipment is proposed. First, the electric-thermal-hydrogen microgrid structure and equipment models are established. Secondly, the economic objective function for minimizing system operating cost is proposed. Furthermore, in the first stage, constraints are introduced based on deterministic scheduling model. In the second stage, the supporting set that represents the source uncertainties is considered. Then, in order to reschedule the flexible resources, further constraints based on the comprehensive norm are introduced. Finally, the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm is adopted to solve the proposed two-stage scheduling model. Simulation is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model. It is confirmed that the proposed scheduling model appropriately strikes a balance between robustness and economic operation.

articleTitle: Probability Assessment of Power System Resilience Based on Stochastic Dynamics Under Sandstorms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Frequent extreme sandstorm disasters have led to power system failures and significant losses, drawing widespread international attention. Considering the impact of stochastic disturbances is crucial for assessing system resilience. This paper proposes a resilience probabilistic assessment method based on stochastic dynamics specifically for extreme sandstorm events. First, the effects of sandstorms on various aspects of the power system are examined, and a system failure model is developed. Next, a fast generative adversarial network (Fast GAN) is introduced to extract relevant features from historical sandstorm disaster data, enabling the generation of extreme disaster scenarios. Then, the Itô process from stochastic dynamics is applied to describe the system’s stochastic disturbances, and resilience metrics are constructed to obtain the probabilistic distribution of system resilience indicators. Finally, a modified IEEE 14-bus system is used in a case study to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method in generating extreme scenarios and assessing resilience probabilities.

articleTitle: Effects of Surface Treatment on the Flashover Characteristics of the GIL Tri-post Insulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Because of its excellent insulation, thermal and mechanical properties, anhydride cured bisphenol-A epoxy resin is widely used in the support, insulation and packaging of electrical equipment and other key components. Surface defects of various sizes and orientations can occur on the tri-post insulator surface during molding due to clamping lines, die wear, and impurities. So, polishing is essential to remove these irregularities and foreign matters. This paper examines the influence of surface treatment on the flashover characteristics of gas-insulated metal-enclosed lines (GIL) tri-post insulators. The results indicate that the presence of metal dust, even in small quantities, significantly reduces the flashover voltage of the insulators regardless of the surface polishing, highlighting the detrimental effect of environmental contaminants on insulating performance.

articleTitle: An Optimization-Based Development Path Planning Approach Considering Coal Power and New Energy Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: We consider the problem of determining transforming quantities of coal power and new energy at different developing stages in China. We predict regulation demands of power systems, contributions of transforming technologies to those demands, and transforming costs. Subsequently, we establish the optimization model of path planning and solve it to obtain quantities of different transforming technologies. Marginal costs at different developing stages are calculated. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization-based path planning approach.

articleTitle: Frequency-Coupled Admittance Modeling Of Converter-Interfaced Generators Using Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Oscillation is becoming one of the most critical issue in a power system with large-scale renewable integration. Frequency-coupled admittance model (FCAM) is widely used in the analysis of oscillations. The operating conditions of converter-interfaced generators (CIGs) are variable in the evaluation of oscillation risk. Therefore, it is necessary to construct the functions of FCAM on the operating conditions. However, the existing modeling methods for FCAM has not taken variable conditions into account. The state-space modeling method is unable to establish accurate models for CIGs with unknown structures and parameters. The impedance measurement method can only obtain the impedance under a specific operating condition once at a time. Moreover, the measured model cannot represent the dynamics under other operating situations. To fill this gap, a linear regression-based modeling method is proposed in this paper. The FCAMs of the CIG are measured under several operating conditions. Linear regression is then used to obtain FCAM as a function of operating conditions. The effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method is verified by comparing the theoretical model and the regression model.

articleTitle: Fast Soft Startup Strategy for DAB-SRC ISOP Hybrid Modular DC Transformers based on SRC Resonant Tank State Observing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The input-series-output-parallel (ISOP) hybrid modular dc transformer (HMDCT) consisting of series resonant converter (SRC) and dual-active bridge (DAB) converters combining the advantages of both the superior regulating capability of the DAB and the extremely high efficiency of the SRC. However, the soft start strategy of ISOP HMDCT is quite challenging due to differences in SRC and DAB submodule modulation methods and power transfer characteristics. To address this problem, this paper proposed a soft startup strategy based on SRC resonant capacitor voltage observing which can accurately limit the peak current of SRC and DAB as well as maintain the input voltage balance among different submodules during the startup procedure. Besides, using the proposed observation method, the use of any resonant tank current or voltage sensors can be avoided, and it can also be applied to the startup control of a single SRC converter. The proposed strategy is experimentally verified on a 500 W prototype.

articleTitle: A Multi-regional Implementation Strategy for Economic Dispatch of Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To improve the efficiency of distributed energy use, a comprehensive optimization strategy for sub-regional virtual power stations is proposed. Firstly, the traditional single virtual power plant model and its application are analysed; Secondly, a multi-region virtual power plant structure map is constructed to finely manage wind energy, photovoltaic and other resources in different geographical areas through virtual power plant partitioning; Moreover, efficient integration of regional energy sources and inter-regional power complementation are achieved through the interconnection of integrated energy systems in each region; After that, by aggregating the joint operation among the sub-virtual power plants, the capacity of renewable energy consumption is improved in order to achieve the goal of maximising the operational efficiency. Next, a complementary strategy for parallel partitioning of virtual power plants based on molecular differential evolution is proposed for high-dimensional nonlinear objective functions, to address the shortcomings of ordinary optimisation algorithms in terms of long computation time and slow convergence. Finally, three regions within the VPP are simulated as examples to verify the effectiveness of the strategy proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Industry Economic Monitoring and Forecasting Model Based on Electrical Energy Use Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This article investigates the relationship between electrical energy use data and industrial economic data over the period from 2013 to 2023. To quantify this relationship, an economic growth sentiment index calculation model based on electrical energy use data is developed. The article then applies this model to an eastern province of China, using empirical data to assess the economic prosperity of the electricity industry. The analysis applies the time difference correlation coefficient method to explore the relationship between electrical energy use and various industrial economic indicators, including those specific to the manufacturing sector. Based on this analysis, the study identifies leading, consistent, and lagging indicators within industrial economic data. Subsequently, based on the composite index method, a calculation model for the industrial economic growth sentiment index is constructed to analyze and study the industrial development trend of the province. The research results indicate a significant correlation between electricity data and industrial economic data, and the calculation model of the industrial economic growth sentiment index based on electrical energy use data can effectively reflect the changing trend of industrial economic indicators. The leading group indicators selected based on the time difference correlation coefficient method can predict economic growth or decline in advance, providing decision-makers with forward-looking warning signals and better supporting policy formulation and economic forecasting.

articleTitle: Design of Chemical Water pH Control System in Thermal Power Plant Based on Fuzzy PID
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the country continues to progress and electricity demand increases, thermal power plants are subject to heightened requirements for power generation. Consequently, power plant equipment demands higher standards of water quality. Maintaining an appropriate pH value in boiler water is crucial as it protects equipment, enhances thermal efficiency, and ensures safe and stable operation. Therefore, controlling the pH of boiler water is of significant importance in the operation of thermal power plants. This paper investigates the pH dosing control component within the water treatment systems of thermal power plants and analyzes and designs the associated control process. Initially, the research background and current state are examined. Subsequently, the furnace water treatment process is analyzed, and an overall control method is designed. The control system for the internal water of thermal power plants is developed using PLC and HMI software, with Siemens S7-1200 PLC selected as the main controller. Its hardware configuration is determined by writing control programs in PLC and integrating HMI software for signal acquisition and processing to achieve system control and status monitoring. The control system employs PID control to adjust the frequency converter’s output, regulating the valve opening of the electric dosing valve, and the dosing flow rate to manage the boiler water’ s pH. Two control schemes, conventional PID and fuzzy PID, are evaluated. A control simulation model is established in Simulink with MATLAB for comparative analysis, confirming the feasibility of fuzzy PID control. Fuzzy PID control demonstrates enhanced adaptability and superior performance compared to traditional PID control.

articleTitle: Research on Robust Generation Scheduling with Large-Scale Wind Power Integration considering Forecast Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Integration of large-scale wind power increased the uncertainty of power grid significantly. It brings new challenge to traditional optimization model of generation scheduling. Robust optimization has recently gained substantial popularity as a modeling framework for optimization problem under parameter uncertainty. In this paper, we propose an adjustable robust optimization formulation to solve generation scheduling problems under uncertainty. Unlike stochastic programming or chance constrained approaches, the robust optimization formulation does not require information on the exact probability distributions. This method protects power systems against all possible scenarios within a deterministic uncertainty set. Furthermore, a novel model that incorporates the forecast scenario into the robust generation scheduling problem are also proposed in this paper, thereby reducing the conservatism of robust optimization. Analysis shows that robust optimization models considering prediction scenarios are very flexible and can be applied in various forms. Case studies on IEEE RTS-1996 test system show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Lightweight Digital Twin of Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents a method for constructing a lightweight digital twin of power electronic devices based on data-driven approaches. Initially, a data-driven model of the power electronic device is developed using data collected from the device. The predictive capabilities of this data-driven model are then utilized to digitally enhance model predictive control (MPC), thereby creating an MPC strategy based on the data-driven model. Finally, the offline model is trained and updated online, enabling the construction of the lightweight digital twin of the power electronic device. The effectiveness of the data-driven model predictive control is validated through experiments, with frequency stability adjustment of virtual synchronous generator (VSG) used as a case study.

articleTitle: Mechanism of High-frequency Oscillations Induced by the Measurement Link of Voltage Transformer in an Islanded Converter Station Connected to the VSC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) is widely used in islanded networks. The application of high-ratio power electronic equipment makes the islanded network in VSC-HVDC present nonlinearity, which leads to the phenomenon of high-frequency oscillation occurring many times in the VSC-HVDC. In order to study the causes of high-frequency oscillations, this paper proposes the mechanism of high-frequency oscillations in MMC-type islanded networks due to the measurement link of voltage transformers. First, a mathematical model of the islanded network containing the voltage transformer measurement link under light load is established based on the π-equivalent circuit. Second, the stability of the islanded network under light load is theoretically analyzed, and the mechanism of high-frequency oscillation of the islanded network induced by the voltage transformer measurement link under light load is proposed. Finally, the simulation verification in PSCAD/EMTDC shows the accuracy of the mechanism of high-frequency oscillation of islanded network induced by the voltage transformer measurement link proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimization of regional net load prediction based on integrated algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increase of national electricity consumption year by year and the continuous development of electrical equipment, a large number of new power loads are connected to the grid, which puts forward higher requirements for the carrying capacity of the power system. Distributed generation has penetrated into every part of the power system. Compared with traditional load changes, today's user-side load becomes more difficult to predict and involves more influencing factors. When forecasting the net load power of a certain region, the influence of distributed generation on the net load of the region should be considered. In this paper, the Adaboost ensemble learning method is adopted to introduce the influence factors of distributed generation into the prediction of regional netload, and Adaboost processes each LSTM neural network learner by assigning weights, etc., to form a strong learner for regional net load power prediction. There are more factors involved, and the predictions are more accurate.

articleTitle: Analysis on Interaction of Wind Farms with UHVDC under Commutation Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To achieve the strategic goals of "carbon peak" and "carbon neutrality," large-scale clean energy, primarily from wind power, is transmitted via ultra-high voltage direct current (UHVDC) systems, leading to significant changes in the power grid structure. A DC phase-change fault can cause transient overvoltage at the DC sending end, a critical issue that needs addressing. This paper investigates the complex interactions between the wind power base and the UHVDC transmission system during fault conditions. An electromagnetic transient model of the wind power base connected to the UHVDC system is developed using PSCAD/EMTDC software. The study analyzes the impacts of the wind power base on the UHVDC transmission system and vice versa while exploring the effects of varying wind power penetration rates, fault ride-through capabilities of wind turbines, and turbine faults. The system's response characteristics under different wind power penetration levels, fault ride-through parameters, and DC control settings are also discussed.

articleTitle: A Reactive Power Optimization Method Based on SOCP Relaxation with Feasibility Guarantee
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to build a new power system dominated by renewable energy, a high proportion of power electronic devices are gradually being integrated into the power system. The static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) can enhance the voltage stability of the grid, while the doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) can also provide reactive power support to the grid. Therefore, considering reactive power optimization with multiple reactive power sources is of significant importance. This paper proposes a reactive power optimization method for multiple reactive power sources based on the Generalized Benders Decomposition (GBD) algorithm, which decomposes the mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) original problem into a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) master problem and several nonlinear programming (NLP) subproblems. This approach guarantees the AC power flow feasibility of the solutions obtained from MISOCP, allowing for the reasonable allocation of reactive power outputs from various sources. Case study based on the modified IEEE 14-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed GBD method.

articleTitle: Identifying Market Power for Potential Collusions in Electricity Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Market power identification is an important issue for spot electricity market analysis and operation. Market power is more complicated than that in other market to identify due to the specific properties and mechanisms of electric market. This paper proposes a method to identify different type of market power, such as generation dominance, transmission congestion and collusion between electricity suppliers. Structural indices and indices base on market simulation method are presented to identify three type of market power. A three-bus test system is presented to verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Key Fault Screening of AC/DC Receiving Power Grid Based on Super Efficiency Data Envelopment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A key fault screening method method based on super efficiency data envelopment analysis is proposed to address the challenge of evaluating the stability of AC/DC receiving end power grids. Firstly, comprehensive evaluation indicators are constructed; Then, complete the screening and sorting of key faults in the receiving power grid through data-driven methods; Finally, the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method were verified through a practical system example.

articleTitle: A Control and Switching Method for Photovoltaic Inverter in Grid-Connected and Off-Grid Modes without Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing application of renewable energy sources (RES), the randomness and volatility of RES power leads to severe power balancing issues, which may cause power quality issues like voltage deviation. Currently, the photovoltaic inverter may directly disconnect from the grid to solve the problem, which results in serious waste of power. Especially, in distributed networks, this may result in conflicts among different users. To address these issues, this paper proposes a control method and switching strategy for photovoltaic (PV) inverters under different operating conditions. The control method achieves the current-controlled operation when PV inverters connect to the grid, ensuring stable power output. When power quality issues arise on the grid side, the PV inverters operate in voltage-controlled mode, running in island mode to power the loads even without energy storage. Besides, a switching control strategy has been formulated to reduce the power impact and oscillations caused by the mode transition. Experimental verification has shown that the photovoltaic inverter can operate stably under both operating modes, with minimal power fluctuations during the switching process, proving the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: GIS Electrical Contact Characteristics Simulation Based on Electric-Magnetic-Force Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is difficult to observe because of its closed and compact structure. Therefore, the study of GIS touch electrode electrical contact characteristics becomes significantly more challenging. The article is based on the coupling of electric field, magnetic field, and structural mechanics. Calculate the magnetic field strength of GIS, and based on the simulation of structural field, establish a three-dimensional simulation model of moving and static contacts, thus obtaining the influencing conditions on the electrical contact characteristics of GIS contacts. The factors affecting electrical contact of GIS contacts include radial deformation, contact pressure and bending stress of contact fingers. The results show that: the magnetic field strength dominated by the outer diameter of the conductor is significantly greater than the magnetic field strength inside the pipe, and the direction of the magnetic vector is along the tangent of the outer diameter of the conductor. The current and the magnetic field are concentrated on the inner surface, with the magnetic induction intensity inside the shell being higher than that outside the shell. Based on the relationship between contact pressure and contact resistance, the calculation of factors affecting the electrical contact of GIS contacts is carried out. According to the theory of electrical contact, each contact finger in the circuit is in a parallel relationship, which allows the determination of the contact resistance. Through the contact resistance, the electrical contact state of the GIS contacts can be identified.

articleTitle: Three-Subject Game Based Economic Optimization of Integrated Energy System for Carbon-Green Certificate Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To reduce the carbon emission level and improve the operation economy of the system, an integrated energy system (IES) optimization operation model is proposed. First, combined with the green certificate trading mechanism, the model of the stepped carbon trading mechanism and the stepped green certificate trading mechanism is constructed. Second, three-subject game model of the integrated energy retailer (IER) as the leader, energy producer (EP) and load aggregator (LA) as the followers is constructed. Finally, three-subject game-based economic optimization of integrated energy system in carbon-green certificate trading markets mechanism is verified by an example, and the benefits of objective functions IER, EP and LA are maximized. Simulations are presented to validate the reasonableness and effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Identification system of key communication nodes of cyber physical power system based on line impedance and power flow information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The inaccuracy of key communication node identification on the information side causes the defense strategy of cyber-physical power systems (CPPS) against cyber-attacks to have loopholes, which leads to the expansion of the impact caused by intentional attacks, and the information transmission efficiency on the information side decreases dramatically, which is prone to cause large-scale blackout accidents. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes a CPPS information-side key communication node identification system that comprehensively considers communication line power flow and impedance information. First, based on the centrality theory of complex networks, CPPS information-side key communication node identification indices are proposed to ensure the accuracy and validity of the identification results. Second, the numerical values of the identification indexes of the information-side impedance information matrix, active loss information matrix, and reactive loss information matrix are computed. The computation results of the three types of information matrices are synthesized to rank the importance of the communication nodes to propose a key communication node identification system to ensure the comprehensiveness and accuracy of the key communication node identification system. A node identification system is proposed to ensure the comprehensiveness and reliability of the key node identification results. Finally, the CPPS information network transmission efficiency index is proposed, and deliberate attacks are simulated to quantitatively assess the changes in the network transmission efficiency of the key communication nodes after they are attacked. The effectiveness of the system is verified by comparing the simulation example IEEE 118 node system with the entropy weight method and entropy weight TOPSIS method.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Multi-step Prediction of Wind Power based on iHHT and TSLANet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of renewable energy sources such as wind power in the energy structure, high penetration of wind power has become crucial for the normal operation of the power system. In order to improve the accuracy of wind power prediction, this study proposes a wind speed correction algorithm based on improved Hilbert-Huang Transform (iHHT), and introduces TSLANet network for multi-step prediction of ultra short term wind power. Firstly, the improved HHT method was used to decompose and analyze the wind speed in Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP), effectively solving the mode mixing problem in Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD). Next, model the model through linear network layers and determine the weight coefficients. Finally, the corrected wind speed data is input into the TSLANet network for feature learning and ultra short term multi-step wind power prediction. The experimental results indicate that the method proposed in this study can effectively improve the accuracy of power prediction.

Author Keywords: Ultra short term prediction of wind power

articleTitle: A Numeric Study of the Impacts of Energy Storage Cost on the Energy and Capacity Markets’ Revenue
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the integration and impact of energy storage systems (ESS) on energy and capacity markets. With the rapid integration of renewable energy sources (RES), the intermittent nature of RES necessitates robust energy storage solutions to ensure grid stability and reliability. This study leverages a market model that combines energy and capacity clearing, factoring in the influence of ESS. Our findings highlight the critical role of ESS in shifting energy costs and demand profiles, thus influencing market clearing prices across both markets. By simulating various scenarios of energy storage costs, this paper quantifies the impact on market outcomes.

articleTitle: A Flexible Load Precision Control Device’s Autonomous Method for Station Areas Based on Edge-Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the advancement of new power system construction, the large-scale integration of renewable energy has significantly increased the demand for distributed regulation. This paper proposes a flexible load precision control device’s autonomous method for station areas based on edge-computing. The primary objectives are to control the maximum load rate of the distribution area, reduce reverse power flow from the area to the grid, and provide reserve capacity for the grid. An optimized operation model for autonomous management is developed to generate an optimal operation plan for the distribution area. Additionally, a real-time control model is established to dynamically adjust the operation when the planned operation results in heavy loads or reverse power flow to the grid. Both models, along with a CBC solver for optimization, are deployed within the flexible load control device. This method mitigates the impact of errors in load and renewable energy power forecasts, enhances the safety of both the distribution area and the grid, and reduces the need for capacity upgrades or replacements of station areas.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Ransomware Defense Strategy through Behavior-Based Detection using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the topic of Ransomware Defense Strategy through Behavior-Based Detection (BBD) using Machine Learning (ML) and propose a novel solution to the limitation of the existing approaches which were previously proposed for ransomware detection however they are facing challenges of high false positives during detection and cannot detect zero-day attacks or unknown threats. The importance of ransomware defence strategy using the BBD approach provides a proactive, adaptive, and comprehensive solution to the evolving threat of ransomware. The research aims to bridge the gap in current knowledge by proposing a Ransomware Defense Strategy through BBD using ML algorithm approach. By combining these techniques, the paper aims to reduce high false positive rates and improves real-time detection and response capabilities, ensuring rapid identification and containment of threats and address the issue of zero day attacks. The research methodology will involve conducting a simulations to evaluate enhanced ransomware defense strategy using BBD and ML algorithms within a hypervisor environment approach. A relative analysis will be put forward to prove how the proposed solution is unparalleled and superior to the existing methods. The results of the simulations will provide empirical evidence of the effectiveness of the Ransomware Defense Strategy through BBD using ML in improving ransomware detection. The findings of this paper will be suitable for any network analyst and researcher to determine the appropriate set of handover techniques for ransomware detection under various circumstances, such as feasibility and cost

articleTitle: Improved LSTM Network Wind Speed Second-level Forecast Based on Error Modal Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The capability of frequency active support in wind power is essential for maintaining the frequency stability of systems with a high proportion of wind energy. However, the output of wind power is subject to stochastic fluctuations.
