Accurately estimating the current output and forecasting future regulation capabilities are critical for ensuring efficient and safe participation in active grid frequency regulation. To address this issue, this paper introduces a method for second-level wind speed forecasting using an improved Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, which is based on the modal decomposition of forecast errors. This approach enhances the accuracy of wind speed predictions for the next few seconds by extracting valuable information from the errors and correcting the forecasted wind speed in real time. Ultimately, a second-level wind speed forecasting model is developed in MATLAB/Simulink, and the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated using actual operational data from wind power systems. This research holds practical significance for the efficient and safe active frequency regulation of large-scale wind power installations.

articleTitle: Influence of Interval Between Successive Power-Offs on Extreme Value of Hydraulic Parameters in a Pumped Storage System with Fixed and Variable Speed Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Focusing on the complex hydraulic transient problems caused by successive power-offs in the pump mode of variable speed pumped storage units, the study takes a pumped storage system with a hybrid layout of fixed and variable speed units (FVSU) as the research subject. The objective is to investigate the impact of initial speed and the interval between successive power-offs on the extreme values of dynamic hydraulic parameters, such as speed, pressure, and discharge. The results indicate initial speed exhibits a negative correlation with some dynamic response parameters, such as the duration in the pump zone, the maximum speed reversal rate. Specifically, at 96% nr (rated speed), the unit that loses power later exhibits the maximum speed reversal rate of 63.07%. When the interval between power-offs is 4s and the initial speed is at 96% nr, the first power-off unit experiences the maximum spiral case pressure of 615.5 meters. The results indicate that a lower initial speed is more likely to lead to unsafe operating conditions. When successive power outages occur while the first power-off unit is close to the pump braking zone, it is more likely to generate unsafe extreme values of hydraulic parameters. The research results can provide reference for the safe and stable operation of variable speed pumped storage unit (VSPSU).

articleTitle: A Robust Optimization Method for Dynamic Operating Envelope Coordination in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Dynamic Operating Envelope (DOE) coordination method for aggregators in distribution networks (DNs). While the DOE acts as a time-varying power export limit to ensure the DN’s integrity, existing aggregator-agnostic allocation overlooks the surplus of aggregators. To address this limitation, our approach allows aggregators to cooperatively adjust DOEs by solving a two-stage robust optimization and settling payments between themselves. The coordination problem is solved by the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm, ensuring that any power injection within the adjusted DOE maintains the network integrity. Consequently, the aggregators’ total surplus increases. A 4-bus system case study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Transient Voltage-Based Fast Auto-Reclosing Scheme for Renewable Energy Outgoing Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Considering the widespread utilization of conventional auto-reclosing strategies in renewable energy outgoing lines, the inability to distinguish fault characteristics before reclosing poses risks to the safe operation of renewable energy systems, particularly in cases of permanent faults causing severe secondary impacts. Therefore, a fast adaptive auto-reclosing scheme for renewable energy outgoing lines based on transient voltage without shunt reactors on 220kV is proposed. Firstly, the equivalent circuit models for transient and permanent faulty phase voltages are established, expressions for faulty phase voltages are derived. Secondly, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis methods are employed to extract data features from each simulated fault and faulty phase fundamental frequency voltage under different fault characteristics is investigated. Finally, a fast adaptive auto-reclosing scheme based on fundamental frequency voltage amplitude is proposed. Theoretical derivations and real-time simulations on the RTDS platform confirmed that the proposed adaptive reclosing scheme can prevent system overvoltage, achieve fault location even in the case of permanent faults, and provide immunity to fault resistance up to 100Ω.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy for High Proportion of Electric Vehicles and Wind Turbine Participation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to fully tap the flexible interactive resources in the regional energy network and improve the operation economy of the system, the unit combination optimization strategy of considering high proportion of electric vehicles ( EVs ) and wind power access is studied. When a high proportion of EVs are connected to the power grid, the conventional quantitative model is difficult to solve the problem of low computational efficiency caused by large-scale decision variables. A bottom-up method is proposed to describe the flexibility of cluster EVs. Firstly, the physical characteristics of EV battery are analyzed, and the feasible region model of unit EV power is established by depicting the boundary of power and electric energy. Then, a storage battery model is established to characterize the power feasible region of the cluster EV. Finally, the proposed model is applied to the unit commitment problem, and the example results verify its effectiveness. It shows that the optimization strategy of wind/vehicle collaborative participation in unit commitment considering the scheduling flexibility of EV can effectively promote wind power consumption and reduce system operating costs.

articleTitle: Optimization and Economic Analysis of Multi-Park Microgrids Based on Wind-Solar-Storage Complementarity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the optimal configuration of the wind-solar-storage complementary system of the multi-park microgrid, a multi-park joint operation model of wind-solar-storage complementary is established. The hybrid variable global optimization algorithm based on multi-dimensional and multi-scale is used to analyze the performance difference of the system after the energy storage is configured under the independent operation and joint operation modes of the park. According to the comparative analysis of the purchase power, abandonment power, power supply cost, power supply cost per unit power and average power supply cost under the two modes of independent operation and joint operation, it shows that the utilization rate of renewable energy under the joint operation mode is improved, the total cost is reduced, and the capacity demand of battery energy storage equipment is reduced, and the economy of system operation is improved.

articleTitle: Design of Five-Level Full-Bridge LLC Converter Based on Switching Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to meet the needs of electric vehicle chargers and High-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission for LLC converter, a new five-level LLC resonant converter is proposed in this paper. The performance of the LLC converter is significantly enhanced by achieving double gain and reducing the voltage stress on the switching tube. The double gain is achieved, the voltage stress of the switching tube is reduced, and the capacitor voltage is self-balanced, and the efficiency is up to 98.33% under the modulation strategy. In order to verify the accuracy of the proposed converter, a 100kHZ, 200V converter was built in PSIM simulation for verification.

articleTitle: Resilience enhancement of port power systems through integration of multi-energy systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Port power systems relies on external power systems. In order to cope with the blackout in ports due to failure of the external power system, this paper proposes a two-layer resilience enhancement framework through integrated multi-energy systems, which considers the optimization of both the energy side and the load side. On the power supply side, wind and solar power are used as energy input, and the optimal economic operation of the energy system is taken as the goal, and a control strategy is formulated for the related equipment of the integrated energy system in the off-grid state. On the demand side, the loads in the port area are classified according to their importance. When the external power grid cannot supply electricity, the load is restored according to the importance, and the important load of the port is restored to the maximum extent. At the same time, the average load recovery rate of the port at each time node is increased by 18.94%.

articleTitle: Research on Offshore Wind Power Collection and High Voltage Direct Current Transmission System Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Offshore wind power is characterized by being clean, renewable, abundant, and highly stable. Offshore wind development gradually advances toward deeper and farther waters. This paper first compares and analyzes the technical characteristics of typical offshore wind farm collection system topologies. Then multiple high voltage direct current transmission system topologies for offshore wind are proposed, with a summary of their respective technical features. Finally, an investment cost analysis and comparison of key equipment in offshore converter stations for typical topologies are conducted. The conclusion shows that offshore stations using full-power diode rectifiers or hybrid converters offer significant technical and economic advantages. This paper provides theoretical support for developing low-cost offshore wind collection and transmission system.

articleTitle: Research on Application Value and Business Model of Distributed Photovoltaic and Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the state has attached great importance to the development of distributed energy and energy storage, and the development potential of the photovoltaic and energy storage industry is huge. On this basis, it conducts a comprehensive and detailed analysis of its application value from three aspects economic value, social value, and management value, and conducts research on business models and economic benefits based on specific examples. The research conclusions show that under the same boundary conditions in the same province, the financial benefits of photovoltaic projects under the mode of " spontaneous self-use and surplus power on Grid" are the best, followed by solar storage projects. In provinces with a large peak-to-valley price difference, energy storage projects can be developed according to local conditions. In the future development process, the industry development trend and regional characteristics should be fully studied and judged, and distributed photovoltaic and energy storage project planning should be steadily carried out to improve the economics of the project.

articleTitle: Distributed Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling with Considering Preventive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This research is centered around the exploration of a distributed hybrid flow shop scheduling problem (DHFSP), which incorporates flexible periodic preventive maintenance (PM) for equipment. The maintenance strategy adopts a mixed mode for single and dual workers, while also considering equipment speed variation. A mathematical optimization model is constructed with the objective of minimizing the maximum completion time and the maintenance cost of workers. A four-layer encoding structure is designed, containing five essential factors: factory, job, machine, speed, and worker. In this study, a multi-objective honey badger algorithm (MOHBA) is designed. Considering capabilities of global optimization, MOHBA also exhibits good robustness for solving optimization problems. Comparative algorithms of the fast non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II) and the multi-objective seagull optimizer (MOSOA) are designed. From the Pareto front distribution and the quality of solutions, the results confirm MOHBA’s effectiveness. It can effectively solve the distributed hybrid flow shop scheduling and preventive maintenance with variable speeds.

Author Keywords: distributed hybrid flow shop scheduling problem

articleTitle: Investigation on Steady-state Performance of 500 kV Single-core AC Submarine Cables under Different Grounding Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The investigation of grounding methods for long-distance AC submarine cables is of great importance for the safe operation of the cable system. This paper uses the multi-conductor analysis method to establish a computational model of a 500 kV AC submarine cable system with solid bonding grounding and multiple intermediate shorting point grounding. Subsequently, a matrix cascading algorithm is used to calculate and analyze the steady-state characteristics of the submarine cable system. The results show that the core current under the solid bonding method gradually decreases with the distance increase while the sheath current and armor current remain unchanged. Under the multiple intermediate short-circuit grounding method, the sheath-induced voltage significantly reduces, and the sheath current and armor current exhibit a jagged and staircase-like decrease, respectively.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power Coordination Optimization under High Photovoltaic Penetration for Distribution Station Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As energy reform progresses, the number of distributed generation units, energy storage systems, and other elements within distribution station areas continues to increase, transforming them from passive systems into active systems. This paper proposes a coordination optimization strategy for energy storage and reactive power compensation devices in distribution station areas, utilizing the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The constraints and safe operating boundaries of various elements within the distribution station area are analyzed. The problem of maximizing the renewable energy absorption capacity is converted into minimizing renewable energy overflow power. A coordination optimization model is established with the objectives of minimizing the total network loss and the total renewable energy overflow over the course of a day. Case studies confirm that this strategy reduces both network losses and renewable energy overflow, ensuring the safe and stable operation of the distribution station area.

articleTitle: Framework for Zero-Carbon Park Pathway Development: Integrating Subsystem Synergies through Energy and Carbon Flow Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The global shift towards carbon neutrality has underscored the importance of transforming industrial parks, which significantly contribute to greenhouse gas emissions. This study presents the Integrated Subsystem Synergistic Pathway (ISSP) Framework, a systematic model tailored to guide the zero-carbon transition of industrial parks. Structured in three stages—Energy and Carbon Flow Analysis, Subsystem Synergy Planning, and Pathway Development — the ISSP Framework provides a comprehensive approach to mapping, analyzing, and optimizing energy and carbon flows across diverse subsystems in the park. By leveraging advanced data management, econometric modeling, and dynamic carbon accounting, the ISSP Framework offers an adaptable, actionable pathway that supports national and global carbon reduction targets. This framework not only addresses short-term emission reduction targets but also provides a strategic roadmap for sustainable, long-term growth in industrial parks.

articleTitle: Modeling Method for Dynamic Dispatchable Region of Flexible Regulation Resources and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of large-scale distributed energy resources (DERs) presents significant challenges for operation and control of next-generation power system. While these resources enhance grid flexibility and provide emergency support, their inherent uncertainty complicates the accurate quantification of their regulation capacities. This paper proposes a dynamic dispatchable region modeling method for DERs, utilizing a vertex enumeration approach by solving an optimal power flow problem under specified power factor to generate a vertex set, whose convex hull defines the boundaries of the dispatchable region. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through the modeling of the dynamic dispatchable region in an IEEE 33-bus distribution system, and its applicability is further verified in the coordinated optimal dispatch of integrated transmission and distribution systems (IT&Ds).

articleTitle: DQ Admittance Modeling of SVG Considering DC Voltage Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Because the static var generator (SVG) has the characteristics of flexible and rapid compensation of reactive power, it is widely used in new energy power stations. Through dynamic reactive power regulation, the power quality of the regional system is improved. Since the output power of SVG is close to pure reactive power, its admittance characteristics are significantly different from those of ordinary inverters. Therefore, considering the influence of DC side voltage fluctuation on AC side current, as well as the dynamic characteristics of phase-locked loop (PLL), current inner loop, voltage loop and power outer loop, the dq axis admittance model of SVG is established in detail. The correctness of the admittance calculation results is verified by frequency sweep measurement. In addition, this paper analyzes the small signal admittance characteristics of SVG from the two perspectives of dq subsystem coupling characteristics and negative conductance characteristics.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Control Technology for Motor Operating Mechanism Applied to Vacuum Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to improve the mechanical impact caused by contact collision and spring bounce during the closing process of circuit breakers, a segmented fixed duty cycle control strategy based on PWM control is proposed to segment control the motion process of the moving contacts of the circuit breaker. This article focuses on the design of a control device for the motor operating mechanism of a 126kV vacuum circuit breaker. A segmented duty cycle control strategy is adopted to complete the closing operation of the circuit breaker. Four control strategies are developed through theoretical analysis, and the response time and opening and closing time are compared through simulation verification and online testing. The experimental results show that during the open distance stage, the control strategy of strategy 3, which adopts full voltage starting, reduces the duty cycle before the close point and increases the duty cycle after contact, can shorten the response time and improve the closing speed, and alleviate the mechanical collision problem between contacts.

articleTitle: Research on the Protection Action Strategy for Multi-Terminal AC/DC Converter with Fault Blocking Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The multi-terminal AC/DC converter with fault blocking capability is widely used in the power system. In this paper, based on the topology of the multi-terminal AC/DC converter using clamp double sub-module (CDSM), the principle of blocking DC fault current is analyzed under the high-voltage DC bipolar short-circuit fault. The impact of the protection action strategy on the discharge path of the submodule capacitors of AC/DC converter is discussed. Different exit sequences and the locking time of the dual active bridge (DAB) converter and DC/AC inverter are discussed, and the protection action strategy is provided for multi-terminal AC/DC converter. Finally, simulation results are provided for the different protection action strategies.

articleTitle: Calculus Accumulation-Based Inspection Reading Method for Substation Pointer Meter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Outdoor pointer-type instrument working conditions are complex, the dial is susceptible to environmental pollution, and the readings are difficult to identify accurately online. A two-dimensional convolution and calculus accumulation-based instrument reading recognition scheme is proposed, and a weighted multi-feature matching algorithm is adopted to accurately obtain the center coordinates of the rotating axis, to improve the success rate of the instrument image recognition. The target pointer position is obtained by polar coordinate transformation and calculus accumulation of the dial image, and automatic readings are realized. Through the experimental comparative analysis of outdoor dust blocking, liquid droplet blocking, leaf blocking, and different lighting conditions, the results show that the algorithm has good robustness, almost independent of the external environment, and the recognition success rate reaches more than 98%. It provides a good reference for the unattended pointer instrument.

articleTitle: Low-carbon Economic Optimization of Smart Distribution Networks Based on Seasonal Carbon Trading Method and Refined Demand Response Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increase of carbon emissions and global warming, it is essential to implement low-carbon economic optimization strategies for smart distribution networks. This paper proposes a seasonal carbon trading method (SCTM) and a refined demand response model for low-carbon optimization in smart distribution networks. Firstly, this study introduces a SCTM to reduce carbon emissions from the generation side. Secondly, a demand response model that incorporates industrial processes is established to enhance the demand response potential on the consumption side. Finally, the numerical examples show that the method proposed in this paper can successfully reduce carbon emissions on the source-load sides of the system and improve economic benefits in the improved IEEE 33-bus system.

articleTitle: Study on the MMC-HVDC System Stability Impacted by Feedforward Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The high frequency resonance occurring in the initial stage of operation of Yu to E project is analyzed. The suppression method of high frequency resonance by additional filter control in the feedforward voltage loop is analyzed, and the effect of additional filter control on the system stability and the change of the impedance characteristic of the converter is simulated and calculated. The simulation is used to verify the correctness of the proposed method suppressed high frequency resonance.

articleTitle: Resilient Distributed Control for DC Microgrids Under Unbounded FDI Attacks and Stochastic Noise Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Distributed control technology has been widely used in DC microgrids for its scalability and flexibility. Nevertheless, the information exchange between distributed generators (DGs) may be affected by various types of stochastic noises and cyber attacks. To ensure the stability of the microgrid systems under stochastic noise and unbounded FDI attacks, we develop a hidden cyber layer that is integrated with the original cyber layer in the cyber system and then design a resilient distributed controller. By utilizing the hidden network layer, the controller can introduce a compensation term in the feedback loop to compensate for the unbounded FDI attack signal. Furthermore, a consensus gain function is introduced to make the microgrid systems robust to noise disturbances. The system stability is rigorously analysed using stochastic stability theory and Lyapunov function. The performance and the effectiveness of the proposed resilient distributed controller are verified by MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Evolution Characteristics of Typhoon Disaster Chain in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In disaster science, the study of disaster chains is crucial for understanding the propagation characteristics of disasters, improving system resilience, and reducing disaster-related losses. However, existing research has not given sufficient attention to the dynamic evolution characteristics of disaster chains within distribution systems, which limits the broader application of disaster chain analysis in distribution systems. In this paper, the disaster chain is constructed from the disaster mechanism of typhoon disaster. And the spatio-temporal characteristics of typhoon are established through the joint distribution of wind speed and rainfall. Finally, the evolution trend of typhoon disaster chain is described by dynamic Bayesian networks, which provides a foundation for applying disaster chain analysis to enhance the resilience of distribution systems.

articleTitle: Optimization Model for Combined Capacity, Electricity Energy and Ancillary Service Markets Considering Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The electricity market typically comprises several interrelated submarkets, including the electricity energy market, the ancillary service market, and the capacity market. However, most prior studies have focused on only one or two of these markets in isolation. This paper proposes a coordinated operational mechanism for the three markets, incorporating multi-energy participation, and develops a joint clearing model that integrates the capacity, energy, and ancillary service markets. By adjusting the capacity curve based on net energy and ancillary service revenues (NET E&AS), the model influences the generation mix and facilitates coordinated market clearing across all three submarkets. A case study using the IEEE 30-bus system is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Multi-energy Load Short-term Forecasting for Integrated Energy System based on Time Convolutional Networks and Multi-task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate multi-energy load forecasting is the premise of ensuring economic scheduling and optimal operation of integrated energy systems (IES). Aiming at the characteristics of large load fluctuation and complex energy coupling, a short-term multi-energy load forecasting method based on time convolutional networks (TCN) and multi-task learning is proposed for IES. Firstly, the maximum information coefficient (MIC) is used to consider the multi-energy interaction mechanism, multi-load coupling characteristics and the correlation of meteorological factors. Secondly, A multi-task hybrid A-TCN model based on Attention mechanism combined with TCN is proposed. Then, the A-TCN method was validated using the actual data of IES of Arizona State University. Experimental results show that compared with traditional model and single-task learning, the proposed model can accurately predict IES short-term load and has excellent performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Partial Discharge Characteristics in Power Cables with Different Defects Under Power Frequency Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between partial discharge (PD) behavior and applied voltage for different defect types in power cable insulation systems. A series of power frequency partial discharge tests were conducted. The study revealed that the partial discharge characteristics vary significantly based on the defect type and the applied voltage. For the main insulation knife-cut defect, both the magnitude and number of PD pulses increased steadily with rising voltage. Conversely, the sharp protrusion defect exhibited a decrease in PD activity at higher voltages due to a self-recovery phenomenon, while the conductive residue defect showed irregular PD behavior, reflecting the randomness of the discharge mechanism. These findings contribute to a better understanding of PD mechanisms in cable systems and provide insights for improving defect detection techniques and insulation material development.

articleTitle: Optimized Operation of Integrated Energy System in Zero-Carbon Park Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the multi-energy coupling and zero-carbon emission operation challenges of the integrated energy system in the park, this study adopts the deep reinforcement learning method and optimizes its operation based on the flexible actor-critic framework. Firstly, we construct a deep reinforcement learning model framework for optimal scheduling of integrated energy system in the park. Secondly, in order to interact with the agent, we designed the environmental model of the integrated energy system in the zero-carbon park, and planned in detail the core elements of deep reinforcement learning, such as action space, state representation and reward function. Finally, we set two scenarios for analysis : one is the traditional scenario without considering the carbon neutralization constraint, and the other is the carbon neutralization scenario integrated with the joint operation mechanism of carbon capture and power-to-gas. In these two scenarios, we combine the time-of-use electricity price strategy to conduct an in-depth analysis of the optimal scheduling results of deep reinforcement learning. The research results show that the proposed model and method are significantly effective. The zero-carbon park integrated energy system using deep reinforcement learning not only improves the utilization rate of clean energy, but also reduces the overall cost of system operation, and successfully achieves the carbon neutrality goal of the park.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Graph-Based Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring Method Combining Transformer and Graph Laplacian Smoothing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of smart meters and the advancement of smart grid technologies, demand-side management—exemplified by real-time monitoring and load management—has been playing an increasingly vital role in maintaining grid stability. Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), which can estimate the power usage of individual appliances based solely on whole-house power readings without additional equipment, serves as a low-cost and highly sensitive monitoring method. It provides data support for demand-side management in load management and has attracted significant attention in recent years. Machine learning methods based on graph signal processing (GSP) concepts have been widely applied to low-sampling-rate NILM tasks. However, the original aggregate power sequence features are difficult to separate, and enhancing feature selection can improve GSP performance in NILM tasks. This paper proposes a new semi-supervised GSP-based NILM approach by integrating neural network feature extraction with GSP. A transformer-based encoder-decoder is trained in a supervised manner to extract high-dimensional features from the encoder outputs, which are then used to generate graphs. After calculating graph weights using a Gaussian kernel function, graph Laplacian learning is applied to smooth the signals and infer unknown labels in a semi-supervised way. This yields the operational states of each appliance for load disaggregation. This method leverages the strong feature extraction capabilities of neural networks to enhance graph signal processing performance. The approach is validated on public datasets, outperforming traditional machine learning methods and two other GSP algorithms across multiple evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Multi Energy Microgrid Operation Considering Carbon Emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of the "dual carbon" goal and the construction of a new power system, the development of microgrid with multi-energy has been promoted. However, considering the poor anti-interference ability of new energy and the uncertainty of source load, the quality of energy supply is reduced, which makes the safety risk of multi-energy microgrid and the economy of microgrid difficult to guarantee. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes a multi-energy microgrid optimization method considering carbon trading. Firstly, this paper analyzes the energy supply, conversion and storage characteristics of each main body in the microgrid. Then, a low- carbon economic optimization operation model of multi-energy microgrid is established. On this basis, the research on multi-energy microgrid cluster is carried out according to the bi-level optimal operation system, and a multi-objective optimization algorithm of NC-MOPSO is used to solve the multi-energy collaborative interactive optimization objectives at the microgrid cluster level and the single microgrid level. Finally, the feasibility of the multi-energy microgrid optimization method proposed in this paper is verified by an example simulation.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization for Low-Carbon Dispatch in a Combined Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: While wind and solar power contribute to sustainability, their intermittent nature poses challenges when integrated into the grid. To mitigate these issues, renewable energy can be combined with coal-fired power and hydropower sources to stabilize the energy system, with battery storage serving as a backup source to smooth the total output. This study develops a low-carbon dispatch model for a combined energy system using a two-stage stochastic optimization approach. The model incorporates a carbon trading mechanism to regulate emissions and addresses the uncertainty in wind and solar outputs by clustering output curves into typical scenarios to derive a joint distribution. In the initial stage of scheduling, decisions are made regarding the unit commitment for coal-fired power plants. The second stage optimizes the expected operation cost of other energy generation sources. The feasibility of the model is demonstrated by comparing the results of stochastic and deterministic scenarios through simulation. Analysis of different carbon prices further explores the impact of the carbon trading mechanism on the system’s operation cost.

articleTitle: Study on Thermal Aging Test of 500kV Three-core XLPE Insulated Submarine Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Because of its compact structure, 500kV three-core XLPE insulated submarine cables usually heat more seriously than single-core cables of the same section, so the heat resistance of XLPE insulation and outer sheath materials is higher. In this paper, according to the standards GB/T22078.1-2008 and IEC 62067-2006, mechanical performance tests of XLPE and outer sheath of 500kV three-core XLPE insulated submarine cable prefabricated by manufacturers are carried out. thermal extension tests, and high-temperature pressure tests. The results show that the crystallinity and wafer thickness of the trial-made cable sample increase slightly at 100 °C, indicating that the proportion of antioxidants and crosslinking agents added is reasonable. At the same time, in the above experiments, the performance of XLPE sample, outer sheath sample, and cable segment sample is higher than the standard value, meeting the requirements of long-term operation.

articleTitle: Research on photovoltaic power generation prediction method based on improved Bagging model integration method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale application of clean energy such as photovoltaic in the new power system, the security problems brought by it are becoming increasingly prominent. Improving the prediction accuracy of photovoltaic power generation output is conducive to ensuring the safe operation of the power grid. Based on this, a prediction method of photovoltaic power generation based on improved Bagging model integration method is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the photovoltaic historical data is processed, then base learner is trained by K-nearest neighbor algorithm, artificial neural network and decision tree algorithm, and then a single photovoltaic power prediction data set is obtained. The weight method is selected to integrate the data, the genetic algorithm is improved to speed up the search for the optimal weight ratio, and the final prediction data is obtained according to the optimal weight ratio. The experimental results show that all the evaluation indexes of the model constructed in this paper are better than that of the single prediction model, which can effectively improve the prediction effect of photovoltaic output.

articleTitle: Short-term PV power forecasting system Based on GraphCast Weather Forecasting Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the inability to accurately predict photovoltaic (PV) output under extreme weather conditions, this paper proposes a novel method for predicting PV output based on the GraphCast weather forecasting model. By utilizing the predictive capabilities of the GraphCast model to forecast future weather data and integrating it with a deep learning model to predict PV output, simulations have demonstrated that this method offers higher accuracy, especially under extreme weather conditions.

articleTitle: SiC/Epoxy Coating with Graded Conductivity for Surface Charge Inhibition Based on Electric Field-Induced Assistant Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Applying a SiC/Epoxy composite coating on the surface of DC insulators is an effective method to restrain surface charge accumulation and to homogenize the electric field distribution along the surface. However, the limited and constant nonlinear conductivity coefficient of a uniform coating makes it difficult to match the regional differences in surface charge distribution and spatial electric field variations. Therefore, in this paper, a nonlinear conductivity gradient coating is constructed by using electric field-induced assistant technology (EFIA) to arrange SiC in a gradient within the SiC/Epoxy coating. Optical microscopy was used to determine the gradient configuration of SiC in the EFIA-coating, and the surface charge accumulation characteristics of both the ordinary coating and the EFIA-coating were tested and analyzed. The results indicate that the conductivity of the EFIA-coating in regions with originally strong electric fields is obviously improved, effectively homogenizing the surface resistive electric field distribution of the insulator. Additionally, the high-density charge accumulation area near the high-voltage electrode is suppressed under high applied voltage. At 15kV, the EFIA-coating reduced maximum surface charge density by 30.43% and increased the uniformity of the electric field by 45.58%.

articleTitle: Novel Diagnostic Method for GIS Mechanical Defects Based on Energy Entropy and Improved Probabilistic Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The mechanical defects of gas insulated switchgear (GIS) equipment are one of the important causes of equipment failures, and conducting research on mechanical defect diagnosis methods is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of equipment. This paper proposes a novel diagnostic method for GIS mechanical defects based on energy entropy and improved probabilistic neural network. Firstly, based on the true GIS mechanical vibration simulation platform, the defect vibration signals were decomposed into multiple components using the variational mode decomposition algorithm; Then, based on the cross-correlation coefficient, the main components were selected to extract energy entropy feature values; Finally, the sine cosine algorithm was used to optimize the probabilistic neural network and constructed a GIS mechanical defect diagnosis model, and its effectiveness was verified. The results show that the diagnostic accuracy of this method can reach 98% or above, and the diagnostic accuracy is improved by more than 11% compared to the unoptimized model, which can achieve accurate classification of mechanical defects.

articleTitle: Linearization and Acceleration Strategy of Unit Commitment Model Incorporating Cascade Hydropower
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper establishes a hydro-thermal unit commitment model incorporating cascaded hydropower stations. Due to the characteristics of high dimensionality and strong coupling between constraints, this paper adopts linearization methods for nonlinear objectives and constraints after considering the requirements of solving efficiency and calculation accuracy. It proposes corresponding Benders decomposition and heuristic solving methods, and solves the model using IEEE 118 and 300-bus systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy for an Independent Island Integrated Energy System with a Renewable Power-to-Ammonia System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Power-to-Ammonia (P2A) is recognized as an effective method for scaling up renewable energy integration and providing a new solution for island development and utilization. To fully utilize island renewable resources, an optimal scheduling strategy for an independent island integrated energy system with a renewable P2A system is proposed to explore innovative P2A application scenarios. Firstly, considering the island's resource characteristics and the advantages of ammonia energy, the P2A system is added to establish an independent island integrated energy system. The P2A system is then modularized and refined to fully exploit its flexible scheduling potential. Secondly, the objective is to minimize the total operational cost of the system. The problem is solved by the commercial solver GUROBI. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation examples. The results demonstrate that renewable energy is effectively consumed by the P2A system. Its flexible regulation capability further enhances the system's ability to integrate renewable energy while maintaining significant profit, thereby supporting the system's economic operation.

articleTitle: An Incentive Mechanism for Motivating Industrial Loads to Participate in the Power Guarantee Supply-Coordinated Operation of Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the surge in industrial load and renewable energy, the power grid is facing a huge pressure to ensure power supply. Since the industrial loads have a certain flexibility, how to motivate them to participate in the coordinated operation of power grid is essential to the power guarantee supply. In this paper, an incentive mechanism and a power source-load coordinated model are proposed to motivate the industrial loads to participate in the coordinated operation of power grid. The incentive mechanism and coordinated operation is proposed based on the Nash bargaining method, which can be equivalent to the total operation cost minimization operation sub-problem and the profit allocation sub-problem. Simulation results have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed model in power guarantee supply, and motivating the industrial loads to participate the coordinated operation, the operation cost of industrial load can be significantly reduced by 22.37%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Affecting the Performance of O-rings of 110kV Transformer Bushing Conservator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: O-ring failure is a primary cause of moisture intrusion in transformer bushings. In order to investigate the failure mechanism of the O-ring and the factors affecting its performance, ABAQUS software is employed to simulate the sealing structure of a typical 110kV bushing conservator. Equivalent stress and contact stress distribution of the O-rings under varying structural parameters and temperatures are botained by simulation and the impact of each influencing factor on sealing performance deterioration are analyzed. Furthermore, a plane seal structure test model is designed, and a thin-film pressure sensor is utilized to measure the contact stress of the sealing surface, thereby the accuracy of the simulation method is verified. The results indicate that the relative error between the test and simulation is within 10%. Additionally, it is found that the compression amount and the contact surface friction factor significantly affect the sealing performance of O-rings. Simulation shows on onehand under normal operation conditions, the temperature distribution of the sealing structure in the bushing conservator is relatively uniform, on the other hand thermal expansion exerting a notable influence on sealing performance. These findings contribute to the identification of key factors leading to the deterioration and failure of bushing O-rings.

articleTitle: Application of COA-HKELM in Photovoltaic Array Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of photovoltaic array fault diagnosis, a hybrid kernel extreme learning machine (HKELM) fault diagnosis model based on coati optimization algorithm (COA) was proposed. Firstly, the parameters of the HKELM model are optimized using COA algorithm, and the COA-HKELM fault diagnosis model is established. Then, the simulation model is built and the operating characteristics of photovoltaic arrays under different operating states are analyzed, and a 5-dimensional fault feature vector is proposed as the input of data. Finally, the different operating states of PV arrays are classified and compared with PSO-HKELM, WOA-HKELM and HKELM fault diagnosis models. The results show that the proposed fault diagnosis model can accurately detect the abnormal state of photovoltaic modules with an accuracy of 93.74%, which verifies the validity and feasibility of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Study on Operation Strategy of Islanded Microgrid Cluster Voltage Recovery Based on Distributed Hierarchical Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wind and solar energy storage as a microgrid cluster, usually large scale, a single control technology is difficult to perfectly adapt to large-scale power generation system, and it faces the risk of frequency and bus voltage overruns under heavy load access, so it is often used to be able to flexibly adapt to the large-scale power generation of hierarchical control strategy. To address the above problems, a distributed hierarchical control strategy with a multi-intelligent body consistency algorithm is proposed. The primary control adopts the VSG control as the basis of the whole system, and for the voltage offset, frequency offset and uneven power distribution problems generated by the primary control, the secondary control based on the distributed consistency algorithm is adopted for regulating the VSG parameters to realize the cooperative control of the microgrid system, and for the economy of the microgrid operation, the optimal economic dispatch control strategy is adopted in the tertiary control to realize the stable operation and economic optimization of the microgrid system as a whole. Finally, the proposed control strategy is validated in MATLAB.

articleTitle: A Generation and Transmission Expansion Planning Method Considering Carbon Quotas and Tax
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Driven by global carbon emission reduction targets, the planning of power systems faces significant challenges in transition to decarbonization. This study proposes a transmission system expansion planning considering carbon quotas and tax, in which the generation side include carbon capture power plants, conventional coal-fired units and gas units. By incorporating carbon quotas, economic factors, and other comprehensive elements, the optimization of generation units and transmission network expansion is achieved. Case studies based on a 30-bus transmission system validate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The study reveals that integrating carbon quotas into transmission planning effectively shifts the power supply mix toward cleaner energy sources and enhances the economic feasibility of low-carbon technologies in high carbon tax environments.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization of Multi-Energy Flow System Based on Energy Circuit Theory and PINN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the widespread application of renewable energy, traditional centralized energy systems are transitioning to decentralized and diversified renewable energy structures. This paper establishes a coupled dynamic model of electricity, heat, and gas based on Energy Circuit Theory (ECT), investigating the operational characteristics of devices such as heat pumps and water pumps. It explores optimization modeling and simulation methods for regional multi-energy flow systems based on ECT and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Through practical case analyses, the study validates the effectiveness of PINN for energy flow solutions and demonstrates the efficacy of dynamic modeling in smoothing and suppressing energy consumption fluctuations.

articleTitle: Imaging-Based Super-Resolution Reconstruction of Volatile Photovoltaic Generation Curves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: High-resolution electrical data is a foundational element of data-driven analytics in smart grids. Currently, due to constraints related to measurement frequency, communication costs, and data storage, high-resolution data is often subjected to compression, leading to the loss of high-frequency details. This paper proposes a super-resolution scenario generation method for electrical data to enhance low-resolution photovoltaic (PV) data to high-resolution. First, the one-dimensional electrical data is converted into a two-dimensional electrical image using the Gramian Angular Field (GAF). Then, the low resolution images is enhanced to a high resolution images using a generative adversarial network (GAN). To capture the dependency between PV data and weather conditions, weather data is incorporated into the GAN-based model alongside the low-resolution image. The proposed method has been evaluated using public datasets and compared with traditional data reconstruction methods. The results show that the proposed method not only recovers the high-frequency details of the data with smaller errors, but also generalizes well to different datasets in the same region, yielding satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Risk-Averse Optimal Scheduling Model of a Virtual Power Plant Considering Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A risk-averse optimal scheduling model is introduced to manage the virtual power plant (VPP). This optimization problem models energy transactions between market participants and VPP operator, aiming to minimize VPP’s operational costs. Considering various uncertainties, a multistage stochastic programming approach is formulated. Nonanticipativity constraints are applied to capture the stochastic nature of uncertainties, ensuring that decisions made at each stage rely only on the information available up to that point, without foresight into future data. The proposed scheme operates over a rolling-window horizon divided into intervals, producing sequential decisions as uncertainties unfold, rather than determining them all at once. By incorporating conditional-value-at-risk (CVaR) metric, scheduling goal is modified to minimize a risk-averse function linked to VPP operating costs.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Line Break Fault Detection Method Based on Phase Voltage Difference Across Disconnection Points
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Single-phase line break faults are among the common faults in distribution networks, often leading to hazards such as fires and electric shocks. To address the problem of line break fault detection, a mathematical model of single-phase line break is established for systems with neutral grounding through a small resistor. The mathematical expressions for the neutral point voltage of the power source and the phase voltages across the disconnection point are derived. A detailed analysis is performed on the changes in amplitude, phase, and sequence of the three-phase voltages on both sides of the disconnection point before and after the fault. It is observed that the fault phase voltage significantly differs before and after the occurrence of the fault. Based on these characteristics, a line break fault detection method utilizing the phase voltage differences across disconnection points is proposed and validated through digital simulations. The simulation results confirm the correctness of the identified characteristics of the line break fault and demonstrate that the proposed detection method effectively detects single-phase line breaks.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Supply Chain and Demand Response Strategy of Stadiums under Smart Grid Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of Smart Grid technology, the traditional energy supply chain and its management mode are facing great challenges. Especially in high energy consumption places such as sports stadiums, how to effectively use smart grid technology to optimize the energy supply chain and implement demand response strategies has become an urgent problem. The purpose of this study is to explore how to optimize the energy supply chain and demand response strategy to achieve efficient energy use and management in sports stadiums under the background of smart grid. Through the analysis of the current situation, combined with case studies, corresponding optimization suggestions are put forward, with a view to providing a theoretical basis and practical guidance for the sustainable development of sports venues.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment of Successive Commutation Failure in Multi-infeed LCC-HVDC Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The paper focuses on the subsequent commutation failure risk assessment in LCC-HVDC. Firstly, the critical commutation voltage (CCV) is selected as the index of commutation failure risk, then an improved calculation method of CCV is analyzed to improve its rationality and accuracy. Secondly, the probability of subsequent commutation failure risk is calculated based on the upper and lower thresholds of CCV. Finally, the simulation results verifies the correctness of the assessment method.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Adaptive-Indexed Scanning Vision Mamba Guided Lighten YOLO-v5 for Coal Gangue Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the different sizes, complex backgrounds, variable lighting, and severe occlusion, the detection of small coal gangue targets is a challenging task. Traditional YOLO-v5 based methods exhibit low accuracy in such scenarios. Therefore, we propose an improved YOLO-v5-based model that incorporates the RepNCSPELAN4 architecture from YOLO-v9 and the enhanced Vision-Mamba architecture with multi-scale adaptive position indexing. This approach is designed to better localize coal gangue targets of varying sizes. Experimental results indicate that our model reduces the parameter count to 0.64M and decreases the number of floating-point operations while achieving a detection accuracy of 98.8%. This demonstrates significant practical value for real-world applications, particularly in the context of detecting small targets under complex conditions.

articleTitle: The Optimization Design and Performance Analysis of the Accumulator Lifting System for 500kV Oil-Filled Submarine Cable Pumping Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the issues of high labor costs, difficulty safety risks associated with the installation and high safety risks associated with the installation and disassembly of pressure accumulators in 500kV submarine cable oil pumping stations, this paper proposes a specialized design scheme for a pressure accumulator handling and installation auxiliary device. This device integrates a robotic arm and guide rail system, specialized fixtures, and an intelligent control system to achieve precise movement and positioning of the pressure accumulator through remote control, reducing reliance on manual labor and minimizing direct contact risks with the pressure accumulator.

articleTitle: Research on Three-Dimensional Safety Technology of Power Monitoring System for New Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the core infrastructure of the new energy power station, the monitoring system undertakes the important tasks of information collection, real-time monitoring and operation control. This paper studies the three-dimensional security protection technology of the monitoring system from three dimensions of autonomous control of software and hardware, endogenous security of the system and core business process supervision to ensure the long-term stable operation of the monitoring system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control Method of Grid-Forming SVG under Non-Ideal Power Grid Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The parameter design of the current inner-loop proportional-integral (PI) controller is difficult to take into account the stability margin and control performance of the grid-forming static VAR generator (SVG). Meanwhile, due to the high proportion of power electronic devices connected to the grid, DC components and harmonic disturbances are introduced in the grid. In order to address the above problems, the grid-forming SVG adaptive control method and system is proposed. Firstly, the new PR controller based on generalized integration and specific harmonic compensation is designed and used to construct the current control inner loop of the grid-forming SVG. Then, the bidirectional long short-term memory (BDLSTM) network is used to construct the functional mapping relationship between the overshoot and response time of the current inner loop control with respect to the short-circuit ratio and the internal parameters of the controller. Finally, taking the stability margin, overshoot and response time of the current inner loop control as the optimization objectives, the adaptive new proportional resonance (PR) controller parameter solution method that can adapt to changes in the short-circuit ratio is constructed. The variable weighted crossover particle swarm algorithm is used to generate the optimized new PR controller parameters. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through the CloudPSS simulation platform.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration and Operation of DC Distribution Network Integrated with Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: DC distribution networks exhibit substantial advantages in integrating renewable energy sources, reducing operational losses, and facilitating the plug-and-play capability of electrical devices. However, the inherent uncertainty of renewable energy generation significantly compromises the safe and stable operation of DC distribution networks. Hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) are pivotal in enhancing power quality and ensuring operational stability in DC distribution. This paper presents a bi-level optimization model for the configuration of HESS. The upper-level model addresses the optimal siting and sizing of the HESS, while the lower-level model focuses on the optimal operation of the DC distribution network. Simulation results demonstrate the validity of the proposed model, showing notable improvements in power quality within the DC distribution network. The bi-level optimization framework developed in this study offers valuable insights and serves as a reference for other systems incorporating HESS.

articleTitle: Propagation of Partial Discharge Ultrasonic Signal on the Surface of Cable Cold Shrinkable Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the application of cables becomes more and more widespread, the number of cable joints gradually increases. It is of great significance to detect the ultrasonic signals generated by partial discharge of cable joints to prevent damage to the cable joints and affect the normal operation of the system. This paper measures the response of R15a type PZT at various places on the surface of the cable cold shrink joint, and then calculates the attenuation speed of the ultrasonic signal on the surface of the cable cold shrink joint and the axial distance required for the amplitude to attenuate to 90% of the peak value. The research results provide an important reference for ultrasonic non-destructive testing of cable joints and can provide support for joint surface defect detection and evaluation.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Scheduling for Microgrid Considering the V2G Mode of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the number of electric vehicles (EVs) has been steadily increasing. Integrating EVs into the power system through microgrids is becoming a trend. However, the charging and discharging behaviors of EVs exhibit significant randomness. The vehicle-to-grid (V2G) mode of EVs can fully utilize the energy storage capabilities of their batteries, enhancing stability of power system and reducing the operating costs of microgrids. This paper establishes a day-ahead scheduling model for microgrids with V2G-enabled EVs and uses the Shapley value method zto allocate the profits generated from EVs’ participation in the scheduling. Simulation result shows that EVs participating in microgrid dispatch under the V2G mode can significantly reduce operating costs while increasing their own profits.

articleTitle: Impact of the PLL’s Phase Delay Effect on the Stability of the Weak-Grid-Tied Grid-following VSCs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper develops a simplified model to analyze the impact of the PLL’s phase delay effect on the active power control stability. The novel simplified single-input single-output (SISO) model is developed and used to analyse the impact of the PLL and the non-minimum phase zeros on the stability margin of the active power control. We find that the PLL produces a phase delay effect due to the right half plane non-minimum phase zeros in weak grids, which decrease the stability and the damping. Time domain simulation results validate the analysis in this paper.

articleTitle: Research on Reactive Power Optimization Strategy for Voltage Regulation Involving Large-Scale Distributed Photovoltaics in Multi-Time Scales
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous increase in large-scale distributed photovoltaic (PV) integration, issues related to voltage stability and power quality in distribution networks have become increasingly prominent. To address this problem, this paper proposes a multi-time-scale reactive power optimization strategy for voltage regulation based on distributed photovoltaics. The strategy combines day-ahead and intra-day optimization: day-ahead optimization primarily focuses on coordinating the control of capacitors (CB), static var generators (SVG), and on-load tap changers (OLTC), while intra-day optimization dynamically adjusts the reactive power outputs of distributed PVs and SVGs. By constructing multi-objective functions that include network loss minimization, voltage deviation, and PV accommodation, and by balancing these objectives using contribution-based approaches, the overall operational efficiency of PV-integrated distribution networks is improved. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses voltage fluctuations, reduces network losses, and enhances the accommodation of distributed PV resources. Meanwhile, it ensures voltage quality in the distribution network and facilitates efficient utilization of distributed PV resources, contributing to the stability and reliable operation of the distribution system.

articleTitle: Distributed Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on GAT-TST
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) power stations are characterized by their dispersed layout, small equipment investment, and relatively poor quality of historical data, along with a general lack of meteorological data collection devices. This makes it challenging to improve the accuracy of power forecasting. To address this, this paper proposes a method for improving prediction accuracy by leveraging the spatiotemporal correlation of distributed PV stations. First, each distributed PV station is defined as a graph node, and the Graph Attention Network (GAT) is used to extract spatial features from the historical power data between stations. Then, taking advantage of the Time Series Transformer(TST) model's ability to efficiently capture temporal features, the dependencies between different time points in the historical PV data are captured, and the final prediction result is output through a fully connected layer. Finally, based on real PV station data, the model is validated for ultra-short-term power forecasting using only historical power data, even in the absence of meteorological data collection devices.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Energy Storage System Participating in Primary Frequency Regulation Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, a control strategy of energy storage system (ESS) participating in primary frequency regulation based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed. The control strategy aims to improve the system frequency dynamics and ensure the long-term performance of ESS during primary frequency regulation. The frequency deviation and state of charge (SOC) are used as the inputs of the model predictive controller to obtain the control signal for ESS. The frequency regulation demand and the SOC recovery are both taken into consideration. The control strategy is divided into different stages based on the frequency deviation. Then, the output power of ESS in each phase is determined based on MPC. Finally, the strategy is simulated and verified in a typical regional power system. The cases under step load disturbance and continuous load disturbance are simulated. The frequency regulation index and the SOC maintenance index are analyzed. The simulation results show that compared to the droop control strategy, the MPC proposed in this paper can obtain a good frequency regulation effect while ensuring its SOC maintenance effect.

articleTitle: Flower Pollination Algorithm Based on Adaptive Dual Differential Evolution and its application in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Flower pollination algorithm is widely applied for optimization problem in smart power industry. It is easy to fall into local optimum that lead to the shortcoming performance of convergence speed and searching accuracy. Flower Pollination Algorithm Based on Adaptive Dual Differential Evolution (FPA-DE) is designed to enhance the searching ability in local and global process. Two differential evolution strategy is used to improve the exploration and development of optimization ability. Meanwhile, two type adaptive searching weight to decrease the deviation of random value of scaling factors. Benchmark functions are applied to evaluate the performance of FPA-DE, the simulation verifies that proposed algorithm can maintain higher performance and convergence speed. And FPA-DE is used to demonstrate the optimization in clustering for smart grid, and it can performs better in clustering index.

articleTitle: Modeling and Low Frequency Oscillation Analysis of PMSG-based Wind Turbine Controlled by Virtual Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At present, the penetration of new energy represented by wind power has increased significantly and virtual synchronous generator (VSG) has been widely concerned because it can simulate the rotor motion equation to overcome the disadvantages of low inertia and weak damping caused by the grid connection of distributed energy. However, the low frequency oscillation threatens the safe and stable operation of PMSG-based (Permanent magnet synchronous generator) wind turbine controlled by VSG. To solve this problem, this paper takes the PMSG-based wind turbine system controlled by VSG as the research object, studies the interaction of different control links and their effects on the system dynamic characteristics and grid-connected stability. Based on the model, the eigenvalue of the system and their corresponding oscillation modes are solved and the key parameters affecting the oscillation modes are analyzed. Finally, the electromagnetic transient simulation model of PMSG-based wind farm controlled by VSG was built on MATLAB/Simulink platform to verify the accuracy of the analysis results.

articleTitle: User Satisfaction-Focused Scheduling Strategies for Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal scheduling of cogeneration virtual power plants taking into account customer satisfaction, aiming to improve the system operation efficiency, meet customer demand, reduce energy consumption, and promote the optimization of energy structure and sustainable development. The study includes the establishment of a customer satisfaction model, the introduction of a carbon emission trading mechanism, and the construction of an optimal scheduling model for a CHP virtual power plant, and the effectiveness of the methodology is verified through case analysis. The results show that the simultaneous consideration of customer satisfaction and carbon trading mechanism can effectively improve the economic efficiency of virtual power plants and reduce carbon emissions, the carbon emission allocation quota has an important impact on the operating cost, and there is a complex non-linear relationship between customer satisfaction and carbon trading price.

articleTitle: Scenario Generation of Renewable Energy power Considering Identification of Meteorological Risk Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Conventional scenario generation for renewable energy power systems primarily relies on historical output data, often neglecting critical meteorological factors. This oversight can result in an underestimation of risks in power system analysis. Key meteorological risks—such as extreme temperature fluctuations, prolonged periods of low wind or solar irradiance, and severe storms—directly impact the availability and stability of renewable energy sources. As renewable energy, characterized by its inherent volatility and intermittency, increasingly contributes to the energy mix, these factors become vital. To address this gap, this paper proposes a novel scenario generation method that integrates meteorological risk factors into the modeling process. By utilizing historical data on meteorological characteristics, including wind speed, solar irradiance, and precipitation, the proposed approach constructs probability models to simulate potential output scenarios. Incorporating these risk factors offers a more comprehensive framework for managing uncertainties in power system operations. Case studies validate the effectiveness of this approach, demonstrating improved scenario accuracy and enhanced support for reliable power system planning under varying weather conditions.

articleTitle: Transmission and Distribution Coordinated Blocking Scheduling Strategy with Dynamic Integration of Distribution Network Flexibility Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the excessive branch power exceeding the transmission line capacity limit, transmission bottlenecks may occur in certain periods for transmission networks. With the large-scale integration of demand-side resources and distributed energy into distribution networks, it has become possible to solve transmission bottleneck issues through coordinated dispatch of controllable resources in both transmission and distribution networks. Addressing the challenge of scattered demand-side response resources and the difficulty in negotiating compensation prices, this paper proposes a dual-layer optimization blocking dispatch strategy based on the dynamic integration of flexible distribution network resources. Under this strategy, the transmission network layer aims to minimize blocking costs, obtaining generator adjustment plans and node prices through optimization. The active distribution network layer then dynamically integrates the flexibility of distribution network resources based on load characteristics and node prices, collaboratively resolving bottlenecking issues. The effectiveness of the strategy proposed in this paper has been verified by modifying the IEEE-39 test system.

articleTitle: Iterative Clearing Model and Method for Electricity Spot Market with Embedded Direct Current Power Flow Security Check
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The effective operation of the electricity spot market relies on efficient market clearing methodologies. The Security-Constrained Unit Commitment (SCUC) program is the core of the clearing process. With the gradual increase in the number of market participants in the spot market and the consideration of more grid sections, the extremely dense matrix formed by transmission constraints and a large number of market participants poses significant challenges to the spot market clearing. To address this, an iterative clearing mechanism incorporating embedded Direct Current (DC) power flow security check and linearized Alternating Current (AC) power flow constraints has been established. This mechanism includes an optimization phase without network constraints and a DC power flow security check based on full data sensitivity, which rapidly provides initial schedules and grid power flows for optimized clearing. On the basis of security check result, the market clearing employs an incremental power flow method based on filtered sensitivity, improving iterative efficiency and the accuracy of power flow calculations during clearing. Through simulation analysis, the effectiveness of the proposed iterative clearing method has been validated, and this clearing method has already been implemented in practical provincial-level spot markets in China.

articleTitle: Forward Scheduling Optimization Decision-making Method for Power Grid Transmission Channels based on Graph Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: After replacing the dominant position of deterministic controllable power sources such as coal-fired power with intermittent and fluctuating power sources such as wind power and photovoltaics, the operational characteristics, safety control, and production mode of the power grid have fundamentally changed, resulting in complex and variable power flow in the power system.
