This poses great challenges to the scheduling and flexible adjustment of the power grid, especially affecting the operation and control of key transmission channels in the power grid. At present, the dispatching system mainly adopts the technical means of sensitivity adjustment and global optimization calculation of physical model. Based on the graph reinforcement learning technology, this paper breaks through the dependence of existing methods on model and prediction data, fully excavates historical data, and combines dispatching experience data to learn and generate a global disposal strategy considering time series characteristics, which effectively reduces the difficulty of solving risk disposal strategies for key transmission channels of the power grid, and improves the online practicality of power grid daily dispatching.

articleTitle: Simulation of thyristor single event burnout due to neutron irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, based on the thyristor model used in the converter valve of the Ultra-High Voltage Direct Current (UHVDC) transmission project, the single event burnout (SEB) caused by atmospheric neutron irradiation is simulated and analyzed. In the simulation, the energy distribution of secondary particles and the change of device parameters caused by neutron incidence are obtained by GEANT4 and Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) simulation platforms with reference to the real atmospheric neutron energy spectrum. By changing the Linear energy transfer (LET) value, incident depth and incident position of the incident high-energy particles in the thyristor model, the change of the leakage current of the device is obtained. The simulation results show that the LET value of the incident particles has the greatest influence on the leakage current of the device, and in some cases, it will directly cause the device to burn down.

articleTitle: A New Type of Capacity Market Dispatch Model Considering the Available Capacity of Electrochemical Energy Storage Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid growth of wind and photovoltaic power generation capacity, the system suffers from insufficient power generation capacity. To ensure sufficient power generation capacity in the power system, a capacity market mechanism is introduced. Compared with long construction cycle and high investment cost of large thermal power units, the electrochemical energy storage station has the advantages of short construction cycle, low investment and quick effect, which is an effective resource to provide power capacity for the system. This paper proposes a new type of capacity market dispatch model considering the available capacity of electrochemical energy storage station. The capacity market dispatch model not only considers power generating side of wind power, photovoltaic and traditional power units, but also increases the market participation of electrochemical energy storage stations on the power consuming side. The capacity market dispatch model considers peak capacity demand, basic capacity demand, power demand, valley load demand, climbing power demand and other system constraints. Finally, through analysis the impact of the available capacity of electrochemical energy storage station, total market capacity demand and installed capacity of renewable energy on the market dispatch results, the effectiveness of the new type of capacity market dispatch model considering the available capacity of electrochemical energy storage power station is verified.

articleTitle: Research on Hierarchical Regulation and Control Technology for Power Grids in High Penetration Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, especially in regions with high penetration levels, power grids are facing unprecedented challenges. This study proposes a hierarchical regulation and control technology aimed at improving the operational efficiency and safety of power grids through refined management in high-penetration areas. The study constructs a multi-level collaborative regulation and control framework that includes the main distribution collaborative regulation and control layer, the micro-grid mutual aid layer, and the distribution area autonomy layer. Based on the strong coupling indicators for micro-grid internal autonomous balance, the reserve degree indicators within the micro-grid considering risk prevention and control needs, and the node peak-valley difference indicators, a micro-grid partitioning indicator system was established. Through the analysis of actual power grid case studies, the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method have been verified. The results show that this hierarchical regulation and control method can significantly reduce the amount of information exchange, improve control efficiency and accuracy, solve over-voltage issues, and enhance the safety and economy of power grid operations. The research in this paper provides new ideas and solutions for power grid regulation and control in areas with high penetration rates, holding significant theoretical and practical value.

articleTitle: Research on Switching Capacitor of Vacuum Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, vacuum circuit breakers have been widely used in distribution networks and medium-voltage systems, especially in frequent operations. Therefore, vacuum circuit breakers are usually used to switch capacitors in shunt capacitor compensation devices. After a lot of research, it is pointed out that the vacuum circuit breaker has the phenomenon of delayed re-breakdown after arc, which may lead to re-ignition, and then produce high-amplitude re-ignition overvoltage. Especially in the case of multi-phase re-ignition, it seriously threatens the safety of the compensation device and the system, and damages the service life of the capacitor, and may even endanger the insulation performance of the equipment. This paper discusses the basic mechanism and working principle of vacuum circuit breaker, focusing on the analysis of the mechanism and harm of cut-off overvoltage, reburning overvoltage and closing inrush current. The theoretical and simulation analysis of vacuum circuit breaker switching 35 kV capacitor is carried out. In this paper, six groups of 5MW capacitor banks are used, and PSCAD simulation software is used to simulate the inrush current and overvoltage transient process of different capacitor banks ( synchronous input and asynchronous input ).

articleTitle: Research on Virtual Inertia Frequency Regulation Control Strategy for New Energy Grid Based on Adaptive SOC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of the control ability of the energy storage battery (ESB) when it participates in the primary frequency regulation (PFR) of thermal power generating sets, an adaptive integrated control method is proposed to optimize the output of the ESB based on the PFR characteristics and the state of charge (SOC) of the ESB . The virtual inertia control (VIC) is improved to obtain the virtual negative inertia control by analyzing the grid FR characteristics. In the early stage of FR, the power output of storage battery is mainly controlled by sag control and supplemented by inertia control; in the frequency recovery period, inertia control is mainly controlled by droop control and supplemented by inertia control. In order to optimize the storage battery power output, the adaptive output coefficient adjustment strategy is set based on the logistic function to maintain a good SOC. Taking a single-area power grid as an example, a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model is constructed, and the proposed adaptive integrated control method is simulated and verified, which proves that the control strategy can quickly reduce the frequency deviation, so that the power system (PWS) rapidly The control strategy is proved to be able to quickly and effectively reduce the frequency deviation, so that the PWS can quickly recover to the steady-state value of PFR frequency.

articleTitle: Personalized Short-Term Load Forecasting for Building Clusters Based on Federated Learning and Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Buildings are the main power consumers on the load side of power systems, and accurately forecasting building loads is crucial for proactive decision-making and maintaining stable operation of power systems. In the context of building cluster load forecasting, data is distributed across multiple building clients, making centralized model training a risk to data privacy. Additionally, building load data often exhibits randomness, volatility, and nonlinearity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a method that combines federated learning and the Transformer model. The aim is to establish a personalized load forecasting model for building clusters that preserves data privacy while capturing the complex temporal dependencies and nonlinear features of building energy data, thereby enhancing the accuracy of energy consumption forecasting for building clusters. First, a federated learning framework is utilized to aggregate local model parameters from each building, resulting in a global forecasting model. Throughout the process, the Transformer model is employed to extract features from building load data. To further enhance the model's personalization, local data from each building is used to fine-tune specific Transformer layers, thereby reducing computational costs and improving both the model's generalization and predictive accuracy. Experimental results show that this approach effectively balances building load data privacy with forecasting model accuracy.

articleTitle: An Automatic Analysis System for Loading Program of Emergency Generator in Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The research on the emergency loading procedure of emergency diesel generator sets in the nuclear power plant is an important guarantee for the equipment selection and power execution function of diesel generator sets. In this paper, the automatic analysis system of the diesel generator set loading program is constructed, through which the corresponding connection relationship in the auxiliary power topology is automatically identified, and the correct load object is selected; Then the load data information is classified to form the selection process of the utilization factor required for load capacity calculation; Then, according to the demand of load outage time and power supply reliability time of power supply system, under the premise of meeting the initial conditions of load step time assignment, the load time and load step are matched. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Modelling and Optimization of Park Integrated Energy System with Biogas Considering Dynamic Adjustment of Thermoelectric Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Park Integrated energy system (PIES) changes the traditional mode of independent energy supply, achieves multi energy synergy and mutual assistance, and improves energy utilization efficiency. Biogas, as a renewable energy source, has advantages of promoting wind and solar energy consumption and reducing natural gas supply pressure. However, there are limitations in the research on biogas utilization in PIES, and its carbon reduction attributes cannot be effectively utilized. The potential of energy-saving regulation by optimized scheduling strategies urgently need to be explored. To solve the above problems, this article establish the system structure of PIES with combined heat and power (CHP) units considering dynamic adjustment of thermoelectric ratio. Through simulation verification, compared with traditional PIES, the model proposed in this article can promote the output of renewable energy units, reduce system carbon emissions, and achieve more economical operation of PIES.

articleTitle: An LLM-Based Modeling and Decision Optimization for User-Centric Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Rapid adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has significantly increased the demand for user-centric and personalized EV charging solutions. Existing charging decisions primarily rely on static optimization, involving complicated modeling and algorithms. This, however, poses a high communicative and technical barrier between users and machines, leading to a poor quality-of-experience. To this end, this paper proposes a novel large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent framework, acting as a mediator between users and devices to deliver a direct language-to-solution service. Our framework consists of three specialized agents, i.e., Agent-I, M, and -C, with each responsible for information querying, model construction, and code generation, separately. First, Agent-I extracts vehicle information and user preferences through interactive dialogues with users, and retrieves comprehensive brand and model parameters from external databases. Next, Agent-M filters out key modeling parameters, and grabs real-time electricity prices for charging. Finally, Agent-C generates the professional codes for commercial solvers, e.g., Gurobi, subsequently obtaining optimal charging solutions. Two cases with different EV brands and user preferences have then been tested to demonstrate that our framework can significantly improve user experience while maintaining the accuracy and optimality of charging decisions through a direct language-to-solution mode. This study showcases the potential of LLMs in smart charging systems and pave a way for user-centric resource optimization and scheduling.

articleTitle: Demagnetization Fault Detection of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Continuous Variational Mode Decomposition and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of slow speed and low diagnostic accuracy of uniform demagnetization fault diagnosis of permanent magnet synchronous motor, a uniform demagnetization fault diagnosis method based on continuous variational mode decomposition and random forest is proposed. Firstly, the uniform de magnetization fault model of the motor is established to obtain the stator current fault signal of the motor. Secondly, the Successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD) is used to decompose the current signal. Compared with the traditional variational mode decomposition method, SVMD improves the decomposition speed and can obtain the modal component faster. The random forest algorithm is introduced to train and test the algorithm based on the decomposed data, which reduces the correlation between the vectors, ensures that the random forest model can achieve high accuracy prediction in the multi-feature classification problem, and realizes the diagnosis of uniform demagnetization fault. Compared with the traditional support vector machine and other classification methods, the diagnosis accuracy is improved. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed uniform demagnetization fault diagnosis method.

articleTitle: Optimizing Configuration of Mobile Power Sources to Enhance Distribution System Resilience
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, frequent extreme weather events have highlighted the vulnerability of distribution systems. In response to distribution system damages caused by natural disasters such as hurricanes, allocating defense resources in the prevention response stage can effectively improve distribution systems’ ability to respond to extreme weather events. Mobile power sources (MPSs) are gradually becoming key resources for pre-disaster configuration due to their flexibility and fast response capability. However, existing configuration strategies rarely consider the mobile features of MPSs. To this end, this paper proposes a DAD (defender-attacker-defender) model that introduces movement constraints of MPSs to effectively address the impact of transportation times in MPSs movement scheduling. The model is solved by the C&CG (Column Constraint Generation) algorithm. Its effectiveness is verified on the IEEE-33 bus test system, which significantly improves the resilience of distribution systems.

articleTitle: Deadbeat Nearest Current Modulation Strategy of MMC-based SAB Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To tackle the high harmonic content and losses in traditional step wave modulation for medium voltage DC distribution networks using MMC-based single active bridge (SAB) converters, a deadbeat nearest current modulation (D-NCM) strategy has been proposed. This strategy converts the single-phase system into a two-phase system through virtual orthogonal components and calculates the AC side current reference value using decoupling control. By comparing the measured current with the reference, the number of activated submodules is dynamically adjusted, allowing precise AC side current control. MATLAB/Simulink simulations show that D-NCM effectively reduces harmonic content and minimizes switching losses, enhancing overall system performance. This research suggests that D-NCM is a viable solution for improving electrical energy quality and operational efficiency in medium volt-age DC distribution networks.

articleTitle: Characterization of Spatial Electromagnetic Parameters and Propagation Properties of Overhead Transmission Lines Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to better utilize the information of magnetic field during transmission line faults and improve contact-free measuring and fault monitoring methods, this paper investigates the impact of fault current on the magnetic field characteristics of overhead transmission lines. The study is achieved through an analysis of simulation results, putting forward the identification of magnetic field distribution characteristics of the overhead transmission line under fault conditions. The study demonstrates that overhead transmission lines exhibit clear characteristics in their magnetic fields in different fault cases, utilizing a research method that combines numerical and finite element simulation. Additionally, the paper discusses the magnetic field traveling waves generated by fault currents, and provides some relevant insights. In the final, the simulation results prove spatial distribution, diapason characteristics and traveling waves of the magnetic field to be available to identify the occurrence and type of faults. This provides new research ideas and solutions for real-time monitoring of long-distance transmission lines, consequently useful for digitized energy internet construction.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Thermal Ageing of 500 kV EHVDC XLPE Cables Based on Molecular Structure Changes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the thermal ageing mechanism of 500 kV extra high voltage direct current (EHVDC) cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables, focusing on molecular structural changes. In this study, a self-constructed multi-field ageing experimental setup was utilized to conduct combined multi-physical field ageing experiments on ring-cut XLPE cable samples. Electrical properties such as DC conductivity, resistivity, and DC breakdown strength were analyzed. Simulation using molecular dynamics illuminated the thermal decomposition process of polyethylene, revealing a three-stage ageing mechanism. Experimental results indicated that conductivity initially decreased then increased with ageing time, while the breakdown strength decreased after 144 hours of thermal stress. Molecular chain scission and crosslinking reactions during ageing contributed to the alteration of electrical properties, which was supported by free volume theory analysis. The findings provide essential insights into improving the transmission efficiency and durability of high performance submarine cables.

articleTitle: Short-term photovoltaic power prediction based on KAN model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation has developed rapidly as a promising clean energy application in recent years. Reliable PV prediction contributes to the stable operation of the power system and promotes the widespread application of PV power. In this paper, a hybrid model, which combines a new deep learning framework Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) with traditional models (such as long short-term memory(LSTM), gate recurrent unit (GRU), and bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM)), is proposed. The hybrid model not only combines the advantages of LSTM, GUR, and BiLSTM in processing time-series data, but also incorporates the faster neural scaling features of KAN networks, which result in faster performance improvement along with increasing the model size. To verify the prediction performance of the hybrid model, three evaluation indices are applied: mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error(RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error(MAPE). The case study demonstrates that compared to non-improved benchmark models including long short-term memory (LSTM), forecasting errors of the LSTM-KAN-V2 model decrease by 33.45% (MAE), 21.65% (MAPE), and 37.23% (RMSE), respectively.

articleTitle: Research on the Penetration Testing Model in the Vertical Field Using Generative AI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Traditional penetration testing relies deeply on high technical requirements for testers, thus limiting the breadth of popularization. Automated pen-testing with artificial intelligence reduces the barrier. This article introduces the application of generative artificial intelligence in the field of pen-testing, introduces machine learning modeling techniques for vulnerability intelligence, constructs a large language model for experimental analysis, and looks forward to future research.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery Internal Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis by Joint Estimation of Internal Short Circuit Current and State of Charge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of internal short circuits (ISC) is essential for ensuring lithium-ion battery (LIB) safety, given the severe risks of thermal runaway associated with ISC. Addressing this, the present study introduces a novel ISC diagnostic approach with strong robustness against measurement disturbances. Specifically, the ISC faulty battery is represented through an enhanced first-order RC model, with ISC current incorporated as an additional state variable within the model. By employing the extended Kalman filter, the ISC current is estimated jointly with other battery states, significantly enhancing estimation robustness in the face of voltage and current measurement fluctuations. Furthermore, a recursive least squares method is developed to determine the ISC resistance, directly reflecting the ISC fault severity. The proposed diagnostic approach is validated for accuracy and robustness, maintaining ISC current and resistance estimation errors within 5 mA and 3 Ω, respectively, even under substantial electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: Load Resource Investigation and Model Construction Methods for Typical Industries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper studies the process overview, main process composition and internal process composition of enterprises in key industries, covers the mainstream subdivision processes within the industry, finds out the process equipment adjustment, start-stop characteristics and maintenance cycle, etc., and analyses the production and load regulation characteristics of the industry. Relying on the results of load resource investigation, the typical commonalities of the industry are extracted, the mechanism model of key industries is established, and the adjustable capacity evaluation method under complex adjustment methods such as multi-process joint adjustment is studied, so as to support the development of guided load investigation tools. Establish load resource data verification standards, study industry and historical data verification methods, explore hierarchical and classified load resource check data verification strategies, continue to improve the load management data check rule base, support the development and launch of automatic data verification tools, study data governance strategies and closed-loop management processes, and ensure the normalisation of load check data quality management.

articleTitle: Modeling and Response Characterization of Wind Turbines under Frequency-Voltage Coupled Disturbance Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the growing share of renewable energy and the rapid deployment of HVDC, the new power system increasingly exhibits characteristics of high power electronics integration. In this context, the frequency-voltage coupling characteristics of the system during disturbances become increasingly prominent, making the traditional approach of addressing frequency and voltage issues separately less effective. The high/low voltage ride-through (H/LVRT) and frequency regulation (FR) characteristics of renewable energy units are key factors influencing the system's frequency-voltage coupling behavior. This paper initially establishes a generalized electromagnetic transient model for wind turbine generators (WTGs), incorporating high and low-voltage ride-through control along with frequency regulation control. Subsequently, by analyzing the active and reactive responses of WTGs during coupled system frequency-voltage disturbances, the influence of wind turbines on system frequency-voltage under typical control strategies is clarified. Finally, a test system is set up on the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform to validate the accuracy of the proposed generalized model for WTGs and their frequency-voltage coupled response characteristics. The simulation results indicate that the coupling between the active and reactive power of the WTG is most pronounced during simultaneous frequency and voltage dips, which can potentially cause a further decline in system frequency.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis on Optimal Preventive Maintenance Policies for the Electrical Control System of Offshore Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For offshore wind turbines (OWTs), the electrical control system (ECS) is identified as one of the critical components with a relatively high failure rate. To delve into the aging process of this system and determine the optimal preventive maintenance (PM) interval, this study develops an aging model based on a non-homogeneous continuous-time Markov process (NHCTMP). The model segments the entire lifecycle of the ECS into five distinct states, to simulate the behavior and performance degradation across various stages of usage. The Chapman-Kolmogorov’s (C-K) forward equation is solved to determine the reliability of each state. Many factors are considered including the effective age and the cost of different operation and maintenance (O&M) activities. A numerical example is presented to verify our results. Moreover, we assessed the impact of data accuracy through a sensitivity analysis on key parameters, the results show that the shape parameter has a significant impact on the PM scheme.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term multi-step power load forecasting based on generative adversarial framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, in the process of carrying out power load forecasting, the accuracy of multi-step forecasting is usually much lower than that of single-step forecasting due to the limitation of the model's feature extraction ability and the impact of error accumulation. Therefore, a multi-step forecasting method for ultra-short-term power load based on the generative adversarial framework is proposed in this paper. Compared with the traditional methods, the feature extraction and learning capability of the forecasting model is further enhanced by introducing the training mechanism of generator and discriminator playing with each other in the generative adversarial framework. Specifically, the convolutional-long short term memory neural network (CNN-LSTM) is introduced into the generator to learn complex nonlinear relationship in the time series and generate the load forecast values for multiple future time steps; the multi-layer perceptron is used as the basic structure of the discriminator to judge whether the forecast value is close to the true load value. The analysis results of practical cases show that the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy of ultra-short-term power load multi-step prediction.

Author Keywords: convolutional-long short term memory neural network

articleTitle: Power Prediction Model of Wind-solar Combined Power Generation Based on Cluster Scene Reduction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale construction of wind power and photovoltaic units, the output prediction of such generating units has become a significant research trend, considering that the distribution of natural resources is relatively concentrated and geographically close to the wind power units and photovoltaic units have a great correlation. Therefore, in this paper, considering the ideal fitting degree, the Frank-Copula function is chosen as the combined probability distribution of wind and solar power, and the joint output scenario of wind and light considering the spatial correlation is generated. Based on this, the K-means clustering technique is enhanced to produce five large-scale output scenes, and the uncertain output curve of the scenery is obtained by combining the generation probability of different scenes with the output curve of the scene. Compared with the traditional method without cutting scenes, the power prediction curve obtained by this method reduces the influence of accidental scenes on the overall curve. It improves the rationality and accuracy of prediction.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Optimal Price Strategy of Virtual Power Plant to Coordinate Multi Integrated Energy Systems Dispatched by EFIS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The current trend is to achieve regionalized energy control through an integrated energy system and utilize virtual power plants for power regulation support. This paper proposes a day-ahead optimal price strategy of virtual power plant to coordinate multi integrated energy systems dispatched by evolution fuzzy inference system. The mathematical model of the integrated energy system and virtual power plant is first established, followed by an analysis of the scheduling using evolutionary fuzzy inference system and the feasibility of obtaining real-time electricity prices through a master-slave game. Finally, the proposed solution is evaluated through simulation experiments, resulting in an 8.4% optimization of economic indices for the integrated energy system and enabling peak cutting and valley filling. These results confirm its effectiveness and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Transient Synchronous Stability for Grid-Forming Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources into the power grid, the issue of voltage control in inverters has gained significant attention. The transient synchronous stability of the grid during major disturbance events has also become a focal point of research. Traditional analyses of the transient synchronous stability of grid-forming (GFM) inverters often overlook the contributions of damping and the reactive power-voltage control loops. To accurately investigate the transient stability mechanisms of inverters under large disturbances, this paper establishes a large-signal mathematical model that examines the specific roles of damping and reactive power control loops. Furthermore, a simulation model is developed to compare the solutions of the differential equations with the simulation results, which validates the accuracy of the proposed model and lays the foundation for future quantitative analysis and control strategy design.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis Model Study of Harmonic Losses in Converter Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The losses of converter transformers are relatively high, which have a significant impact on the stability and economic operation of the equipment. Currently, the losses measured by different methods vary greatly. It is necessary to conduct relevant research on the losses of converter transformers in order to provide a basis for the design and manufacturing of converter transformers. During the factory test of the converter transformer, it is necessary to measure the load loss. At present, the measurement methods for harmonic losses mainly rely on the calculation methods recommended by IEC 61378-2 and GB/T 18494.2 for estimation, which makes it difficult to obtain accurate frequency characteristics of harmonic losses in converter transformers. Research on measuring harmonic losses in converter transformers at near rated harmonic currents has not been carried out yet. Based on this research, a method for measuring harmonic losses in converter transformers using highpower harmonic power sources is proposed. The improvement of the design, manufacturing, and operation maintenance of converter transformers is of great significance.

articleTitle: Research on Magnetic Levitation Control System of Large Inertia Rotor of Energy Storage Flywheel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: By modeling the dynamic characteristics of maglev flywheel rotor, the shortcomings of the traditional distributed PD control method are analyzed by the root locus method. It is found that the gyro effect of large inertia rotor is the main reason for its instability at high speed. To solve this problem, a centralized control method of decoupling the translational mode and the conical mode is proposed. In the process of flywheel speed increase, the translational mode is not affected by the flywheel speed, and the control law is set separately for the cone mode, which can fundamentally suppress the influence of the rotor gyro effect. Due to the limited bandwidth of the actual control system, a control method combining modal decoupling and cross-feedback is proposed, which can effectively reduce the influence of gyro effect on the maglev system.

articleTitle: Testing Method for Frequency Support Performance of Renewable Energy Power Stations Based on Mechanism Model and Predictive Data-Driven
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The current testing signals for fast frequency response (FFR) control of renewable energy power stations are formulated from historical frequency disturbance characteristics, difficult to guarantee the frequency support capability of stations in response to unknown power disturbance events. To address it, a testing method based on mechanism model and predictive data driven is proposed. The test results demonstrated that it can effectively ensure their support capability responding to power disturbance events.

articleTitle: Improved Optimization Method for Dispatch of Shared Energy Storage Power Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the advancement of energy storage technology and the development of the sharing economy, the service model of shared energy storage power station will become a new form of energy storage application at the customer end. The article proposes to optimize the economic dispatch of shared energy storage power station for industrial users. Using improved particle swarm optimization (IPSO) algorithm to solve the optimal dispatch model, According to the simulation results, by coordinating the charging and discharging power of user group who use the shared energy storage power station, the optimal operation cost of the user group can be realized.

articleTitle: Demand-side Flexible Resource Intelligent Dispatch Strategy Embedded with Domain Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Demand-side flexible resource dispatching is an indispensable part of improving the balance regulation ability of new power systems. However, due to the unclear understanding of the mechanism of flexible resources, power dispatchers still face the problem of fast optimal decision caused by the high dimensional random response of massive objects. Therefore, this paper introduces the dispatch domain knowledge into the modeling and decision-making process of flexible resources, establishes a data-driven model of flexible resource decision-making behavior based on knowledge such as the historical response confidence of resources, and proposes an optimal grid scheduling strategy that takes into account multiple flexible resource groups after embedding the domain knowledge. From the two dimensions of flexible resource cognition enhancement and decision enhancement, the flexible resource intelligent dispatching decision based on domain knowledge fusion is realized. A numerical example of IEEE39 system verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Electric Power Load Forecasting Based on Fractional PID Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Load forecasting is one of the important work of the power system management. Increased load forecasting skills, conducive to saving coal and oil, and reduce cost of power generation, will help improve economic and social benefits of power system. In order to improve the accuracy of load forecasting, we designed a fractional order PID neural network model. Adjust parameters through using BP neural network, you can achieve a five-dimensional variable predictive model of self-learning. Fractional PID controller digitizes regulate synaptic weights of the network by BP algorithm adjustment of the neural network output as the parameter of fractional order PID controller. The simulation concluded that the accuracy of fractional PID neural network model is higher than the traditional neural network forecasting model. To improve the accuracy of load forecasting provides a reference program.

articleTitle: By Regulating the Flow of Hydrogen-electricity in the Microgrid Internet to Coordinate the Operation of the Distribution Network and Transportation Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles are rapidly increasing in urban transportation networks. However, the large-scale charging of new energy vehicles poses significant challenges to the coupled system of distribution networks and transportation networks. On one hand, the charging demand of new energy vehicles (including electricity and hydrogen) brings peak loads to the distribution network operations. On the other hand, uncoordinated charging behavior of new energy vehicles causes congestion in the transportation network. Therefore, how to effectively regulate the operation of the distribution network and transportation network within a safe domain is an urgent problem. This paper proposes achieving coordinated regulation of the coupled system by regulating the flow of hydrogen-electricity in the microgrid internet. Firstly, a model for the flow of hydrogen-electricity in the microgrid internet is constructed. Secondly, a collaborative regulation method based on price mechanisms is established. Inside the microgrid internet, electricity-hydrogen transactions are made based on electricity and hydrogen prices; between the microgrid and the distribution network, electricity transactions are based on electricity prices; and the microgrid guides the charging of new energy vehicles through charging prices. Finally, simulation verifies the effectiveness of the price mechanism in regulating the flow of electricity-hydrogen within the microgrid internet. Results show that regulating the flow of hydrogen-electricity in the microgrid internet based on price mechanisms can significantly adjust voltage fluctuations in the distribution network and improve traffic efficiency in the transportation network.

articleTitle: Research on the charging and discharging scheduling of electric vehicles driven by the carbon flow of the power system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the urgent global need to address climate change, the issue of carbon emissions has garnered increasing attention. To effectively address the carbon reduction issue in the charging and discharging scheduling model of electric vehicles, this paper proposes an optimization model for the charging and discharging scheduling of electric vehicles driven by the carbon flow of the power system. Firstly, an optimal power flow calculation model with generation cost as the objective function is constructed at the upper level. Based on the optimal power flow results, carbon flow is calculated and used to determine carbon prices. Then, at the lower level, an electric vehicle (EV) charging and discharging dispatch optimization model is established with the charging and discharging cost of EV users as the objective function. Finally, the optimized results from the lower level are input as parameters into the upper-level model to update the power flow and carbon flow results. The model is applied to a 6node system for case analysis. The results demonstrate that the proposed model in this paper has significant effects in reducing and quantifying carbon emissions in the charging and discharging scheduling of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Electricity Prices Prediction Method Based on Spatial-temporal Transformer with Variable-Specific Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Electricity price predictions occupy an important position in the electricity market and are a key to the healthy operation. in order to solve the problem that the past prediction models can only capture the average characteristic due to the variables sharing the same parameters, this paper proposes a spatial-temporal Transformer prediction model based on variable-specific modeling, by designing specific temporal projection matrices and spatial projection matrices that enable specific modeling of each variable and correlations between variables so that this prediction model captures the unique spatial-temporal characteristic of day-ahead electricity prices. Taking electricity price data from Australia as an example, verified the effectiveness of the prediction model by comparing it with six mainstream prediction models.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Optimal Dispatch for Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System Based on Minimum Inertia Evaluation of GFMS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The high proportion of wind power and photovoltaic (PV) brings many new challenges to the frequency stability and operation scheduling of power systems. In order to realize the day-ahead scheduling of Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System considering frequency stability, this paper proposes a day-ahead optimal scheduling method of Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System based on the minimum inertia evaluation of grid-forming storage (GFMS). Firstly, the system frequency response （SFR） model of Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System is constructed by considering the frequency response characteristics of the grid-following (GFL) control and the grid-forming (GFM) control. Then, the minimum inertia that needs to be provided by GFMS is evaluated by the optimization method, and the maximum response power of GFMS in the frequency response is obtained as the power reserve. Finally, the optimal scheduling model of Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System day-ahead that smoothes the fluctuation of system power output and reduces the peak-to-valley range of system power output is constructed by combining the above standby boundary conditions. The feasibility and effectiveness of the method are verified through the simulation analysis of the Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System for the evaluation of the minimum inertia of GFMS and the day-ahead optimal dispatch.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control for Multi-machine Power Systems under External Data Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the adaptive output feedback cooperative control for multi-machine power systems under external data arbitrary injection (EDAI). To circumvent this negative impact of EDAI, an observer is constructed based on the output information of each machine to obtain state information required for control design under EDAI, and two adaptive update laws relying on external data signals are designed based on backstepping technique. Moreover, the Nussbaum function is introduced to deal with the difficulty of unknown time-varying gain caused by EDAI. The results show that the proposed adaptive backstepping output feedback cooperative controller can effectively handle the adverse effects of EDAI in multi-machine power systems. Finally, simulation is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Data Aggregation of Flexible Resources Based on Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasing imbalance between power supply and demand in new electricity system, alongside the integration of a high proportion of renewable energy sources, has led to a significantly increased demand for flexible resources. To more accurately evaluate the role of flexibility resources in power scheduling, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving data aggregation scheme for multidimensional flexibility resource aggregation. By incorporating the Paillier homomorphic encryption algorithm, superincreasing sequences, and blind factors, this approach enables multidimensional data transmission while ensuring data privacy. Additionally, a signature authentication method based on the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem is employed to ensure data integrity and verify data sources. The introduction of Horner rules reduces data transmission volume, enhancing system efficiency by providing a parsable structure that enables the system to obtain aggregate data based on load classification across all users. Security and performance analysis demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only ensures data privacy for grid users but also achieves superior computational and communication efficiency compared to existing schemes.

articleTitle: Detection Method of Leakage Holes in Long-Distance Natural Gas Pipelines Based on Permanent Magnetic Perturbation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A detection method based on permanent magnetic perturbation is proposed to solve the problem of leakage hole detection in long-distance natural gas pipelines. The spatial field changes caused by defects are analyzed by combining the magnetic perturbation equation with Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. Simulation calculation of the coil cascade flux and the magnetic induction intensity under the permanent magnet is carried out by the finite element method, and the change rule of magnetic perturbation in the permanent magnet is further analyzed. The permanent magnetic perturbation detection system of pipeline leakage holes is designed and developed, and the experimental platform of leakage hole detection is built. The experiments verify the detection ability of permanent magnetic perturbation technology on hole defects. The results show that, when the sensor is located directly above the defects, the magnetic perturbation generated is the most intense, and the detection voltage signal is the largest; with the increase of the hole diameter, the amplitude of the detection voltage signal gradually increases. The method provides a reference for further engineering applications of pipeline leakage hole detection.

articleTitle: Research on Data Integration Technology of Large Power Grid Operation Mode for Unconventional Event Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The operating laws and characteristics of the new power system have undergone fundamental changes, and are intertwined with the impact of unconventional events such as natural disasters, resulting in a significant increase in safety risks. Firstly, based on the online analysis requirements of unconventional events, a data integration framework for the operation mode of the power grid was constructed, covering both online and offline data generation. Secondly, a standardized integration method for online data to simulation calculation data was proposed, which combines processes such as operational data parsing, topology correlation analysis, and flow convergence adjustment based on reactive power configuration. Finally, based on the characteristics of the impact of unconventional events, a predictive and clustered set of power grid faults is dynamically formed, providing basic data for the study of the evolution law of unconventional event modes. The multi-stage power grid operation mode data integration platform based on the above principles is of great significance for realizing the full cycle analysis of unconventional events and the application of emergency support technology.

articleTitle: Improved Kepler Algorithm Based Maximum Power Point Tracking for Distributed Photovoltaic under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Affected by buildings, clouds, and dust, the power-voltage characteristic curve of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation system exists multi peaks, which will lead to traditional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms failing to track the global maximum power point and affect the power generation efficiency of distributed PV. To solve this problem, a MPPT control algorithm based on improved Kepler optimization algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a new convergence factor and mutation strategy are introduced into the Kepler algorithm to improve the search accuracy and tracking speed of the original Kepler algorithm. Accordingly, it can track near the global maximum power point quickly and accurately. Then, it switched to the perturb and observe method to continue tracking the determined global maximum power point, and reduces power oscillations of distributed PV. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm in this paper has faster tracking speed and higher tracking accuracy in various working conditions compared to other existing algorithms. Finally, a hardware in the loop platform is built. It further verifies that the proposed algorithm has fast tracking speed and high tracking accuracy, and can greatly improve the power generation efficiency of distributed PV.

articleTitle: Transient Overvoltage Analysis in Large-Scale Wind Power Sending End Systems with Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As China pursues its "carbon peak" and "carbon neutrality" goals, the rapid growth of renewable energy has raised concerns about grid stability due to transient overvoltage. The overvoltage can exceed protective settings, leading to disconnections of renewable sources. This paper investigates the mechanisms behind transient overvoltage in a large-scale radial wind power integration system following a three-phase short-circuit fault. By modeling a large-scale wind power sending end system with both grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) converters, the study analyzes turbine dynamics and quantifies transient overvoltage. The research also examines the factors influencing overvoltage, providing a theoretical foundation for overvoltage protection in wind power systems.

articleTitle: Coordinated Optimization Scheduling for Power Transmission and Distribution Considering Wind Power Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of large amounts of new energy sources has given the distribution network more proactive capabilities, but traditional centralized scheduling methods with fragmented transmission and distribution cannot fully utilize the flexibility resources of the distribution network. Additionally, these methods are not conducive to protecting the privacy of the participating entities. Therefore, a model for coordinated optimization of transmission and distribution economic dispatch is proposed, and the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is used for distributed solving to protect the privacy of each entity. Case studies show that the coordinated optimization economic dispatch model can fully utilize various resources of the transmission and distribution networks, promote renewable energy integration, and achieve optimal system economy.

articleTitle: Design of New Energy Generation Full-Time Domain Evaluation and Application Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing share of new energy in power systems, the volatility and randomness of new energy generation impose higher requirements on the stable operation of these systems. This paper focuses on the design of a full-time domain evaluation and application software system for new energy generation characteristics, aiming to construct an efficient and intelligent system framework that provides comprehensive support for full-time domain evaluation of new energy generation characteristics, power and energy balance, and prediction of critical operational modes.

articleTitle: Thermal Unit Output Condition Recognition Based on Coal Blending Strategy: A Pre-trained Model Enhanced Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Thermal power units, primarily coal-based, act as the "ballast" in China’s power system, supplying over 60% of total electricity generation even amid the accelerated construction of a new power system. However, as renewable energy integration introduces increased grid dispatch volatility, the operational flexibility of coal-fired units faces new challenges. This paper proposes a unit output condition recognition method using coal blending strategy as input to assist managers in quickly and accurately adjusting the coal blending strategy. We designed the Imitator to enable effective feature extraction and expansion of the CBS and supplementary unit parameters into a format suitable for pre-trained image classification models. Subsequently, a pre-trained image classification model is used to complete the unit output condition recognition task. A case study was conducted using real operational data from a coal-fired unit, and results show that all ResNet models achieved training accuracy above 95%, indicating high feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modelling of DFIG Based Wind Turbines with Inertia Control for Frequency Response Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: An analytical linearized model of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) based wind turbines (WTs) with synthetic inertia control for studying frequency response is developed with high accuracy and low computational cost. The simplified DFIG model are firstly derived according to stator flux orientation, as well as the active power control framework including frequency-related signals. In order to fully take dynamic process of rotor into account, the speed regulator which integrates the aerodynamics expression, power tracking curve and swing equation, is further embedded in power control block, such that the physical properties and frequency response of DFIG based WT could be clarified. The simulated results of a generic two-machine system verify that the proposed model is effective for analyzing system frequency dynamics, and the accuracy and efficiency could still be guaranteed in cases of different control parameters.

articleTitle: Exploring Security Communication Tactics for Intelligent Substations Grounded on Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the challenge of simultaneously achieving high-quality security and low-latency response in smart substation communication services, this paper proposes a security communication strategy based on edge computing. Firstly, a security protection mechanism meeting the communication service security requirements is formulated based on the national cryptographic system. Secondly, a real-time acceleration strategy for the security protection mechanism based on edge computing is proposed, which provides shared proxy computing services for resource-constrained terminal devices through the deployment of edge servers. Finally, taking various operating states of the D2-1 type substation's unified star network as an example, quantitative calculations and OPNET simulations are conducted to evaluate the latency of the proposed strategy. The results demonstrate that while meeting the security requirements of smart substation communication services, this communication strategy effectively improves the real-time response speed of communication services.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Wireless Charging Power System for Intelligent Patrol Robot Based on 500kV Submarine Cable Unattended Terminal Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The design of this paper starts from the non-iron core disk motor. Different from the traditional motor, the motor design does not use silicon steel sheet, but uses special wound armature winding and permanent magnet. Therefore, eddy current loss and copper loss mainly exist in the disk motor. The circuit in the motor is connected by Y-type connection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Renewable Energy Forecasting: A Novel Approach Integrating Satellite Imagery with Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: One of the priorities in addressing the serious challenge of integrating renewable energy into the power system is to improve the accuracy and robustness of forecasts for renewable energy generation. Deep learning models, utilizing historical power generation and meteorological forecasts, have become central in predicting renewable energy outputs. Based on that, this study introduces an innovative approach of incorporating satellite cloud imagery as an alternative, robust data source for forecasting. This paper proposed a novel framework integrating three types of data: historical power generation, traditional meteorological forecasts, and image-based satellite data. The integration not only improves forecast precision but also fortifies the prediction system against data manipulation and external threats. Numerical studies reveal that this approach not only addresses the technical needs of accurately predicting power generation in an increasingly renewable-dependent energy system but also fortifies the forecasting process against potential vulnerabilities, ensuring a more stable and secure transition towards sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Strategy of Time-of-Use Tariff for Electricity Sales Considering the Two-Side Linkage Mechanism of Supply and Demand
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of new energy, the time slot division is affected by the uncertainty of new energy generation output, and optimizing the time slot division to form a reasonable tariff strategy becomes a key task to ensure the safe and stable operation of the new power system. To this end, this paper investigates the time-sharing tariff strategy for selling electricity under the two-side linkage mechanism of supply and demand. It constructs a tariff optimization model to minimize the peak-to-valley difference by dividing the net load curve into time slots through the K-Medoids clustering and partitioning method. The example results show that the proposed model significantly improves the load factor, reduces the peak-to-valley difference, and results in a reduction of electricity costs for large industrial users.

articleTitle: A Novel LambdaRank-Based Method for Assessing the Cost-Effectiveness of Power Enterprise Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The current evaluation methods for assessing the cost-effectiveness of the power grid projects predominantly focus on large-scale main grid initiatives that require significant investments. Nonetheless, an important deficiency exists in thorough analyses specifically addressing distribution network projects, which generally entail more modest investments. Existing evaluation systems face challenges: limited applicability of evaluation indices, complex mathematical models, and outcomes that lack rationality and scientific rigor. This research employs the LambdaRank algorithm to construct a project optimization model to address these issues. The model utilizes unsupervised learning techniques to select relevant project features, followed by applying the AHP-EMW method and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation to analyze and assess high-quality projects. A generalized post-evaluation system is subsequently established, tailored to the specific characteristics of these projects. By leveraging the LambdaRank ranking algorithm to prioritize power grid projects, the model provides a scientific reflection of both professional and economic impacts, thereby addressing the shortcomings in power grid enterprises' input-output evaluations of distribution network projects. The findings show that the proposed method enhances scientific rigor and transparency in project prioritization, leading to a more rational and systematic evaluation process.

articleTitle: An Integrated Grid Planning Approach Considering System Adequacy: A Case Study of Shanxi Province
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Maintaining the reliability and adequacy of the electricity system is critical in the transition to a low-carbon economy. Ensuring a stable energy supply can meet fluctuations in load demand, facilitate a successful transition to cleaner energy sources and effectively reduce carbon emissions. In this paper, a framework for analyzing the supply and demand of generalized adequacy at multiple time scales is proposed, and a collaborative planning model considering generalized adequacy is established based on the framework. Then the resource allocation in Shanxi under the low-carbon transition scenario is calculated with the Shanxi power grid as the measurement object, and the sufficiency situation of the planning results of the Shanxi power grid is analyzed. The results show that the system adequacy can be improved in the process of realizing the low-carbon transition in Shanxi Province through the effective allocation of multiple types of flexible resources.

articleTitle: Temporal and Spatial Characteristics of Energy Saving and Emission Reduction of Electric Energy Replacing Civil Coal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Civil coal is the main energy source in rural areas of China and a key factor for substituting electricity. It is essential to clarify the patterns of energy consumption and carbon emissions from civil coal use in order to achieve carbon reduction in rural areas. This paper quantifies the energy savings and reduction in carbon emissions, considering the incomplete combustion characteristics of civil coal, different sources of electricity, and grid line loss rate. It also builds an energy substitution model for reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions from the perspective of the entire energy consumption process. Using Tangshan City as an example, the paper uses a distribution coefficient to depict the characteristics of energy consumption and carbon emissions before and after substitution. The results show that after substitution, there is about 88% reduction in both energy consumption and emissions, with the most significant effects observed in Yutian County, Fengrun District, and Zunhua City. The peak value of hourly distribution coefficient for energy consumption and carbon emissions after substitution decreases due to differences in operating characteristics of electrical equipment during reporting period, resulting in a relatively flat trend.

articleTitle: Oscillation Risk Assessment for a Dual-infeed MMC-HVDC System Using Impedance Network Modeling and Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) technology is increasingly applied, the inverter buses of multiple MMC-HVDC links may be in close proximity, complicating the system oscillation issues. Conventional methods may fail to adequately assess the stability of such complex AC-DC systems. To fill this gap, this paper develops an oscillation risk assessment method for dual-infeed MMC-HVDC systems. An impedance network model including AC/DC networks’ impedances and MMCs’ three-port impedances is established, reflecting the AC and DC side dynamics and their coupling interactions. Besides, a calculation method for MMC's DC/AC-port equivalent impedances is proposed. Further, the impedance model aggregation and oscillatory mode analysis are presented. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Optimization for Microgrids with Electricity-CCER Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The paper proposes an electricity-carbon credit coupling trading mechanism designed to simplify market operations and optimize the low-carbon scheduling strategies of microgrid clusters. The model includes three types of microgrids: industrial, commercial, and residential, which participate in electricity and China Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) market trading. By constructing a two-layer model between the distribution system operator (DSO) and the microgrid clusters, this paper explores the coupling of electricity prices, carbon credit prices, and electricity quantities. The research model is divided into two-layer: the upper layer, where the DSO optimizes electricity and CCER prices to maximize its own benefits while balancing the lower layer microgrids' needs; and the lower layer, where the microgrid clusters, after meeting their own load, integrate and sell surplus electricity and CCERs to the DSO. To fairly allocate the profits within the microgrid consortium, this paper uses the Shapley value method to address the distribution issues arising from the electricity-carbon credit coupling. Case studies show that this mechanism not only effectively optimizes electricity and CCER trading and increases the benefits for both parties, but also promotes the development and maturity of the carbon market, providing new insights for future carbon trading mechanisms.

articleTitle: Study on the Topological Transformation of Electromagnetic Transient Models in PSCAD and ADPSS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: PSCAD, as an early power system analysis software, has accumulated a large number of simulation cases, while ADPSS is an independently developed all-digital real-time simulation system in China, characterized by high cost-effectiveness and good scalability. With the expanding application range of ADPSS, the demand for modeling is increasing. However, manually converting existing PSCAD models to ADPSS models is inefficient and prone to errors. To address this issue, this paper proposes an automatic topological conversion method for electromagnetic transient models from PSCAD to ADPSS. This method utilizes the topological relationships of PSCAD projects to establish connections between primary and secondary components in ADPSS, employing a depth-first search algorithm to construct electrical islands and resolve the reference voltage of busbars. Finally, the correctness of the proposed method is verified through standard test cases from Cigre.

articleTitle: Simulation and Design Optimization of Electric Field in Ultra-high Voltage Flexible DC Valve Hall
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Preventing corona discharge in flexible DC converter stations is an important foundation for ensuring their safe and stable operation. Through the simulation analysis and reasonable structure optimization design, the electric field distribution on the electrode surface can be effectively improved, and the phenomenon of corona discharge can be suppressed. This paper uses finite element simulation software to establish a simulation model of the ultra-high voltage flexible DC valve hall. The overall electric field distribution characteristic is calculated and it is found that the shielding ring on the low-voltage side of the suspension insulator has serious electric field distortion, which is previously overlooked. Based on this, the influence of the shielding ring diameter, ring diameter and insulator length on electric field distribution is studied. An improved method is proposed to reduce the electric field strength from 2630 V/mm to 1800W/mm, meeting the requirements of the design. The research results can provide valuable reference and support for the design and structural optimization of similar projects.

articleTitle: A Multi-index Comprehensive Analysis Method for Waveform Consistency of Single-phase Ground Fault of Power Source Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A multi-index comprehensive analysis method is proposed for the consistency of the output signal and the input signal of the power source about single-phase ground fault. Compared with the traditional single-index waveform similarity comparison method, this method combines the time-domain characteristics of the steady-state waveform, the time-domain ,frequency-domain and time-frequency domain characteristics of the transient state.The consistency of power source grounding fault waveform is comprehensively evaluated. On the basis of investigation and analysis of the field identification method of short-circuit and grounding faults in distribution network, the key characteristic parameters including the voltage amplitude changes of steady-state signals , harmonic distortion rate and amplitude of transient zero-sequence voltage, or the other characteristic parameters that cover the essential characteristics of transient signal waveform.All the parameters are divided into their importance grades. At the same time, the weight rank of each parameter is determined by the combination of the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and the correlation coefficient method. Finally, the waveforms of field grounding fault from the power grid and a power source are extracted, and a comprehensive evaluation model of transient signal output consistency is established.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Small Sample Voiceprint Recognition Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As an important equipment in power system, it is very important to ensure the safe and stable operation of power transformer. The diagnosis effect of the fault is significantly affected by the quantity and quality of the fault voiceprint samples. However, the occurrence of transformer faults is a small probability event, the sample of abnormal state of equipment is scarce, and the density of data value is low, which makes it difficult for intelligent diagnosis algorithm to realize the effective diagnosis of transformer operation state under the condition of less data. Therefore, a transformer fault diagnosis method based on small sample voiceprint recognition technology is proposed, which has the advantage of not needing a lot of training data set. Firstly, according to the principle of voiceprint recognition technology, the Mel cepstrum features of transformer operation are extracted. Then, the fault voiceprint of the transformer is compared and classified by the small sample voiceprint recognition method. Finally, the analysis and verification are carried out under the measured data of a transformer factory. Compared with the traditional deep learning algorithm, the results show that the method has higher recognition accuracy, which is of great significance to engineering practice.

articleTitle: Performance study of the acoustic detection algorithm for the local discharge model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper designs a set of acoustic detection system based on high-performance 80-channel multi-arm spiral microphone array based on the application of acoustic imaging technology in local discharge detection of power equipment. Through the combination of theoretical analysis, simulation and experimental verification, DAMAS2 (CBF), DAMAS2 and OMP-DAMS. The results show that although CBF algorithm can achieve basic discharge position positioning, its spatial resolution is relatively poor; DAMAS2 algorithm has improved resolution, but still has low computational efficiency. In contrast, OMP-DAMAS algorithm performs excellent in terms of resolution, positioning accuracy and calculation efficiency. Especially in the context of complex environment, it can more accurately identify the local discharge position, and the calculation speed is fast, which is suitable for real-time detection system. The research results of this paper provide an effective acoustic imaging algorithm and its practical scheme for the accurate detection of local discharge of power equipment, which has high application value and promotion prospect.

articleTitle: Research on Source-Load-Storage Collaborative Control Strategy for Novel Distribution Networks under Non-Ideal Communication Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to address the issues of complex and variable economic and security control, as well as the difficulties of centralized computing in novel distribution networks under non-ideal communication environments, a highly scalable and reliable distributed control strategy is proposed. Initially, a global sampling method is employed to enhance the optimization of the state transition matrix, thereby accelerating the algorithmic convergence. Subsequently, a self-switching control strategy for node communication states is introduced to enhance the flexibility of the control strategy. Then, based on the consensus principle of multi-agent systems, the incremental cost of source-load-storage agent nodes is used as the consensus variable to achieve optimal economic operation of the distribution network. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated through simulation case studies.

articleTitle: Research on Flexible Load Aggregation Modeling and Coordinated Control Method in Distribution Substation Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At the present stage, the load-side equipment in the distribution substation area is more diversified, and the large number of temperature-controlled loads, electric vehicles, distributed energy storage and other resources make the load-side flexibility and controllability enhanced, providing abundant adjustable resources for the power grid. How the large-scale adjustable load-side resources participate in the operation and control of the power system has become a new challenge for the power grid, however, there is a lack of in-depth research on cooperative control and optimal scheduling methods for massive heterogeneous loads. Therefore, this paper takes the flexible loads in the distribution substation area as the main research object. Firstly, defines the common controllable energy state margin index for flexible loads, and establishes the aggregation model of flexible loads with the controllable energy state margin index as the state variable. Secondly, in order to solve the problem of cooperative control of heterogeneous loads, a system of controllable margin indexes of heterogeneous loads characterizing the load regulation ability is established, and a flexible load state sequence control method based on the controllable margin indexes is proposed to realize the joint regulation of loads.
