Tianjin has achieved remarkable results in constructing a low-carbon city.

articleTitle: Reverse Overload Mitigation for Rural Low-Voltage Distribution Areas Based on PV Power Forecasting and Energy Storage Operation Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the advancement of new energy technologies and a progressive increase in new energy penetration, the quantity and installed capacity of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation in rural low-voltage distribution areas are increasing. Excessive PV power generation readily leads to reverse overloading of the distribution transformers, affecting the power supply quality and transformer longevity. Energy storage systems can regulate energy’s spatial and temporal distribution and have become a significant means of addressing this issue. However, the energy storage scheduling strategy must consider economic factors while mitigating reverse overload. Consequently, this paper initially proposes the XGBoost-Informer-based forecasting method to enhance the forecasting accuracy of PV and loads, thereby obtaining PV forecasting data for the subsequent day. Subsequently, based on the adaptive particle swarm algorithm, an optimization model of the storage charging and discharging power is established to minimize the degrees of reverse overload and ensure the economic viability of the storage operation. Finally, the model was implemented and simulation experiments were conducted for verification. Simulation results show that the proposed method has high prediction accuracy and can effectively reduce the hazardous degree of reverse heavy overload while ensuring the economic benefits of energy storage operation.

articleTitle: Position Optimization of Non-contact Current Measurement Array for Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Given the existing challenges in the measurement of overhead transmission lines, achieving flexible collection and visualization of power information within the energy internet is essential. In this context, non-contact measurement of power data emerges as a critical solution to enhance efficiency and reliability in power monitoring systems. This paper proposes an effective approach for the non-contact current measurement using magnetic sensor array. The array is installed on the towers to collect the spatial magnetic field generated by the three-phase conductors and deduce the electrical information of the overhead conductors. In practical installation, the sensor array should be installed within the safe working area. Moreover, the installation location needs to be optimized to ensure the normal operation of the sensors and reduce measurement errors. This paper optimizes the installation location using a PSO algorithm. Case studies demonstrate that the sensor array at this optimized location improves the accuracy and stability of the inversion process significantly.

articleTitle: Transient Over-voltage Assessment for Renewable Powered Systems with Practical Case Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In a power system with high proportion of renewables, transient over-voltage after faults may lead to unplanned drop off of generation and threaten system stability. To address this issue, the paper develops a comprehensive procedure of transient over-voltage assessment for renewable powered systems. The procedure consists of such key steps as parameter collection, model development, and detailed simulation studies. Focuses are placed on the critical factors that would affect the accuracy of assessment. To validate the feasibility and efficiency of the procedure, a typical test system is modelled and analyzed, including an exploration of the impact of SVG control strategies. Studies indicate that transient over-voltage induced by severe faults would not be affected too much by the type of faults due to the converter current limit. Case studies have demonstrated that the assessment procedure can be practically used for large renewable powered systems.

articleTitle: Undirected Graph Description and Dimensionality Reduction Deconstruction of Complex Microgrid Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to its complex architecture, modeling microgrids is challenging. This article focuses on proposing a downscaling strategy via the Louvain Community Clustering (LCC) algorithm. An undirected graph modeling method for microgrids is proposed. The algorithm divides the undirected graph into different functional domains, identifies and aggregates nodes within divided domains, and uses node clusters as the smallest modeling units, effectively reducing the difficulty of microgrid modeling.

articleTitle: Impedance Characteristics Comparison of Different Grid-Forming Control Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper firstly establishes the self-impedance and accompany-impedance models of Droop control, VSG control, and VSG control with virtual impedance in grid-forming control, and further derives their equivalent impedances. Subsequently, a detailed comparative analysis of these three control strategies is conducted. It is found that Droop control can essentially be regarded as a special case of VSG control. By comparing the output impedance, it can be found that the equivalent impedance of the three control strategies has little difference in high frequency characteristics, but the difference is significant in the middle and low frequency range. Particularly noteworthy is the sub-super synchronous frequency band (within 100Hz) , where both the magnitude and phase of VSG output impedance are lower than those of Droop control, indicating a weaker damping characteristic. At the same time, VSG controls have a larger phase jump near 50Hz, indicating a greater risk of synchronous frequency oscillations. In addition, the introduction of a positive virtual resistance leads to an increase in the resistance component of the equivalent impedance and a decrease in the inductance component, which increases the stability margin by raising the intersection of the impedance curve, indicating that a positive virtual impedance reduces the risk of oscillation generated by interaction with the grid by enhancing the positive damping of the system.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Strategy involving Load Restoration and Pavement De-icing for Intelligent Connected Highways after Snow-Ice Disasters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Ice-snow disasters can damage the power lines of intelligent connected highways (ICHs), causing power loss for critical devices. Besides, accumulated ice and snow on the road can lead to traffic accidents and hinder the repair teams and mobile resources from restoring the system. To address these issues, this paper proposes a comprehensive strategy concerning load restoration and pavement de-icing for ICHs, which considers the coordinated operation of compressed air energy storage (CAES) and mobile energy storage system (MESS). Before the repair of devices and power line faults, CAES and MESS function as temporary power sources to establish microgrids that supply important loads. Meanwhile, the thermal storage system of CAES provides heat to the Hydraulic Heated Pavement System (HHPS) to clear accumulated ice and snow, facilitating the rapid movement of repair teams and MESS, thus accelerating the system recovery process. The proposed strategy is established as an MILP model. Through a case study conducted on a real ICH segment, the effectiveness and superiority of the strategy are validated.

articleTitle: An Improved Extreme Learning Machine Approach to Real-Time Electricity Price Forecasting in Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Responding to the problem that the high volatility of electricity price data and the complexity of influencing factors in the electricity market led to the low stability and prediction accuracy of the existing prediction models, an improved extreme learning machine method for real-time electricity price predication in the electricity market is proposed. An empirical wavelet transform-based decompose of the electricity price data is designed to decompose the electricity price sequence into low-frequency signals that are closely aligned with the price and high-frequency signals that are influenced by noise. An enhanced random forest-based feature extraction price is proposed to identify the optimal feature combinations of electricity price influencing factors based on prediction importance. The kernel function replaces the hidden layer of the extreme leaning machine to construct the electricity price prediction model. The result, based on the real-time electricity price data of an electricity market, demonstrates the accuracy and stability of the proposed prediction method.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of DC Control Parameter Coupling Characteristics in Interconnected Emerging Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The DC project isolates the AC fault propagation and weakens the power mutual support between regional grids. Meanwhile, the frequency fluctuations caused by larger power imbalance events in regional grids are more significant. To solve the above problems, this paper adopts the measure of optimizing key control parameters. Firstly, correlation analysis is conducted on the frequency limit control (FLC) parameters that need to be tuned and qualitatively analyzes the coupling effects between various control parameters under the same indicator. Secondly, according to the results of the coupling correlation analysis, the objective function under the constraints of the DC regional grid is proposed to be taken into account. Finally, an intelligent optimization algorithm is selected to find the optimal for the objective function and constraints, and Python is used to call BPA to tune the parameters of FLC.

articleTitle: Improved Risk Analysis for Micro-grids based on Multi-Parametric Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous change of the world's energy structure, the safe and efficient operation of distribution system and microgrids is becoming increasingly important and challenging. This paper proposes an improved risk analysis algorithm for microgrids based on multi-parametric programming considering the integration of large-scale renewable energy. First, the risk analysis system for microgrids is established, including wind power curtailment risk, distribution line heavy load risk, and integrated risk. Then, the linear mapping relationship from uncertain factors like renewable energy output to value of each risk indicator is established through the multi-parametric programming method. The redundant optimization problem solving steps are omitted cause calculation is executed based on the divided critical domains. In the end, the risk analysis efficiency of microgrids is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Research on Dual optimization control method of DAB converter considering current stress and return power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As a key device for energy conversion and transmission in the Energy Internet, the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter will cause higher current stress and return power when its input and output voltages do not match, which affects transmission efficiency. So, a dual objective coordination optimization control method for current stress and return power of DAB converter based on Dual Phase Shift control (DPS) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the phase shift control characteristics of DAB converter are analyzed, and the mathematical model of DAB converter under dual phase shift control is derived, to analyze the generation mechanism of current stress and return power in the converter. An optimization control model with the minimum current stress and return power as the objective function is established, and an internal and external phase shift ratio coefficient is introduced to ensure that the phase shift ratio value is within the constraint range. Secondly, the gradient descent algorithm is used to obtain the optimal phase shift ratio, and the output voltage feedback compensation control method is introduced to realize the dual optimization control. Finally, the simulation and experimental platform is built by Matlab/Simulink software and TMS320F controller. The results validate that the proposed optimization control method significantly reduces the current stress and return power.

articleTitle: Analysis of Small Signal Stability and Optimization of Control Strategy for Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Weak grids are typically characterized by high impedance and low short-circuit ratios, which can result in system instability and reduced power transmission capacity. This paper develops a small-signal perturbation state-space model and an impedance model for a grid-connected inverter operating under weak grid conditions. It proposes a method to calculate the steady-state operating point and conducts a stability analysis by determining the eigenvalue positions of the state-space matrix, thereby defining stability boundaries. Under conventional vector current control, the system’s maximum output power is limited, losing stability when it exceeds 0.6 p.u. The primary cause of instability is the negative resistance behavior of the phase-locked loop. To enhance the inverter's output power, this paper introduces an improved control strategy known as impedance reshaping. This approach not only preserves a fast dynamic response but also extends the dynamic power limit to nearly match the static power limit, enabling the system to remain stable at around 0.9 p.u. Finally, a simulation comparison between the conventional and improved control strategies validates the effectiveness of the impedance reshaping approach.

articleTitle: Prediction of Dynamic Carbon Emission Factors Based on the Informer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous promotion of the dual carbon strategic goal, how to accurately predict the dynamic carbon emission factors in real time has become a key problem. Based on this, this paper proposed a dynamic carbon emission prediction based on Informer model. Firstly, the differences of dynamic carbon emission factors of different power equipment were analyzed, and thermal power units with the largest contribution to carbon emission among traditional energy sources represented by fossil energy were selected for study. Secondly, the Informer model used for long time series forecasting tasks was transferred to the fitting model of dynamic carbon emission factor in unit operation. The nonlinear relationship between the unit operation climb power and carbon emission factor was extracted by using the efficient extraction ability of the encoder's time series features, and the dynamic carbon emission factor in the future was predicted. Finally, based on the data collected by a regional power grid company, error evaluation metrics and correlation evaluation metrics are used to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Characterization of Flexible Region of Multisource District Heating System for the Electrical Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Multisource district heating systems (MS-DHSs) can provide flexibility to electrical power system (EPSs) via multiple coupling units. This paper quantifies power and energy flexibility of the MS-DHS based on the concept of flexible region (FR). An optimization-based iterative approximation method is proposed to explore the FR. Case studies illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method to characterize FRs of the MS-DHS. Impacts of the duration of flexibility and supply temperature on the MS-DHS flexibility are quantified.

articleTitle: Impact of Energy Storage Lifespan on System Operation Strategy in Full-Horizon Operation Simulation by Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the penetration rate of renewable energy sources in the power grid increases, it is essential to conduct an in-depth study on the scenarios where energy storage systems are used in conjunction with renewable energy sources to mitigate the uncertainty of renewable energy output and enhance the availability and economic viability of renewable energy generation within the system. During the operation of energy storage systems, there is a cost associated with their lifespan. Therefore, it is worth investigating how to improve the economic performance of hybrid wind-storage power stations during their operation. Conducting continuous operation simulations over the entire year would result in excessively high computational costs; however, machine learning methods can effectively extract typical scenarios, reducing computational load while retaining the characteristics of system operation status. In this paper, machine learning techniques are employed to extract typical scenarios and analyze the impact of considering the lifespan cost of energy storage on the dispatch strategy of an improved IEEE 6-bus system.

articleTitle: Multi-state Interval Optimization Strategy of Energy Storage Cluster Considering Frequency Regulation Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the challenges encountered in the secondary frequency regulation process of distributed energy storage clusters, this paper proposes a multi-state interval optimization strategy for energy storage clusters that considers frequency regulation capabilities. The simulation results show that this strategy significantly reduces the computational complexity of the control center and effectively improves the secondary frequency modulation capability of the energy storage cluster.

articleTitle: An Improved SiC MOSFET Analytical Model for Multi-timescale Simulation and Loss Analysis of Power Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC)-based power electronic systems have demonstrated significant potential in modern power grids and motor drives. While traditional physical models provide high accuracy for simulating the switching transients, they often encounter convergence issues in complex systems. The recently proposed piecewise analytical transient (PAT) model enhances computational efficiency while maintaining good accuracy. However, despite its validation on a 1.2kV/300A SiC module from Fuji Electric, further refinement is required for other SiC modules. This paper proposes a numerical-analysis-driven method and improves the transient stage segmentation and model expressions of the previous PAT model. Experimental validation on three different 1.2kV/300A SiC modules with 62mm packaging demonstrates that the improved model delivers greater accuracy and broader generalizability. A loss analysis of a solid-state transformer (SST) converter is also performed to showcase the proposed method’s effectiveness in simulating complex systems.

articleTitle: A Rapid Self-Healing Method Enhancing Resilience and Adaptability in Overhead Distribution Networks Against Failure Occurrence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper focuses on the issue of short-term power outages in distribution networks. Based on existing feeder automation technology and traditional fault section identification algorithms for distribution networks, it studies a fast fault self-healing algorithm for intelligent distribution networks to improve the self-healing speed to the millisecond level. Building on traditional distribution automation, a control system architecture for fast fault self-healing in intelligent distribution networks, based on overhead and cable lines, is proposed. This architecture can be considered a generic primitive framework for intelligent distribution networks, providing a basis for future simulation studies on rapid self-healing. Through detailed research and analysis of traditional feeder automation technology, a fast fault self-healing algorithm based on the intelligent distribution network model is proposed. Given the limited research on fast self-healing algorithms for intelligent distribution networks, the proposed algorithm has been validated through PSCAD simulations, demonstrating its correctness and reliability, and offering valuable insights for future research on fast self-healing algorithms for intelligent distribution networks.

articleTitle: Pollution Level Detection of Insulators based on Hyperspectral Imaging and Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Pollution flashover continues to pose a major threat to the safe and reliable operation of power systems, particularly in environments where insulators accumulate contamination. Traditional detection methods have struggled to achieve non-contact, precise evaluations of insulator pollution levels. Hyperspectral imaging offers a nondestructive testing solution by combining image and spectral data, making it a promising approach for assessing external insulation. However, conventional machine learning techniques often fall short in achieving high detection accuracy. In this paper, we propose using a Transformer model to determine insulator pollution levels from HSI data. Through extensive experimentation, the proposed model outperforms traditional machine learning methods, achieving a detection accuracy of [insert specific percentage] on real-world datasets. These results demonstrate the Transformer model's ability to significantly improve the precision and reliability of pollution degree detection, paving the way for enhanced maintenance strategies for power system insulators.

articleTitle: Long-Term Power and Energy Balance Optimization for Interconnected Multi-Region Systems with Pumped Hydro Storage Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Long-term power and energy balance analysis is commonly used to assess resource allocation scales in regional power systems or the adequacy of annual power generation resources. With the continuous increase in the installed capacity and generation proportion of renewable energy sources, the uncertainty and volatility of their outputs may lead to mismatches between supply and demand. Recently, the role of pumped storage in interconnected multi-region systems has become increasingly significant, and the potential for cluster development is becoming more evident. In the future, pumped hydro storage is poised to become a critical factor that cannot be overlooked in long-term power and energy balance analyses. This paper proposes a power and energy balance optimization model that considers pumped storage clusters. The model ensures that the hydraulic coupling relationships among pumped hydro storage units within the same cluster are satisfied, enabling the simulation of supply and demand behaviors of interconnected power grids containing pumped hydro storage clusters over several consecutive months. Finally, the proposed model is validated using data from interconnected power systems to demonstrate its analytical utility.

articleTitle: A New Energy-efficient Distribution Transformer Evaluation System Based on CensNet Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As one of the core equipments of the new power distribution system, the quality of its products has a direct impact on the reliable access to distributed power sources and the supply and distribution of electricity to users. In order to improve the quality of distribution transformer products, a new energy-efficient distribution transformer evaluation system based on CensNet graph neural network is proposed. For the new energy-efficient distribution transformer, the component material and process evaluation system is firstly established from the physical level to obtain quantitative indexes; then the Neo4j graph database is used to establish a directed graph of the supply chain, to analyse the supplier roles and to obtain the graph features; finally, the CensNet graph neural network is used to evaluate the suppliers by considering the node features and edge features together.

articleTitle: GIS Switch Contact Fault Simulation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the widespread use of GIS equipment, the eccentricity failure of GIS switch contacts due to equipment assembly has also increased. In view of this fault phenomenon, the finite element software was used to build an eccentric fault model, and the overall acceleration of the switch model was analyzed, and the acceleration was mainly concentrated at the top of the shell and the contact. A point probe was added to the top of the shell to observe the dynamic response characteristics of the top of the shell under different current conditions, and it was found that the vibration acceleration under the contact eccentric fault increased from 0.01 m/s2 to 0.307 m/s2 with the increase of current, and the frequency domain was mainly 50Hz and 100Hz, which was consistent with the frequency domain characteristics of the actual faulty equipment, which further verified the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Research on Active Defense Strategies for Asynchronous Interconnected Power Grids Based on Two-Stage Robust Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address potential natural disasters or man-made attacks on asynchronous interconnected power grids, this paper proposes an active defense strategy based on game theory. A two-stage robust optimization model for a three-layer sequential game of DAD is established, and is solved using C&CG. The results indicate that a pre-allocation of defense resources can significantly reduce system losses after a fault, with a notable enhancement in system robustness, especially in DC back-to-back grids.

articleTitle: A Two-stage Optimal Bidding and Dispatch Strategy for Integrated Energy Producers Considering Uncertainties in Electricity Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the development of China's electricity spot market accelerates, the participation of renewable energy sources (RES) in the spot market has become an emerging trend. Thus, integrated electricity producers, encompassing thermal power, RES and energy storage systems (ESS), can achieve maximum profit through strategic regulation. Based on the early stage of China's electricity spot market, where the dual-settlement mechanism and deviation assessments co-exist, this study evaluates the bidding revenue in the day-ahead market and the arbitrage opportunities in the real-time market. Considering multiple uncertainties of RES power and market prices, a two-stage optimal bidding and dispatch strategy for integrated energy producers is established, where the day-ahead market bidding strategy and the real-time market rolling self-scheduling strategy are considered. The proposed model optimizes the dispatch schedules of thermal units, maintenance plans for RES units, and bidding strategies in the market, to maximize electricity producers' profitability. A case study based on real data from a certain region in East China is provided, and the numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-time scale scheduling optimization of port integrated energy system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A multi-time scale optimization scheduling strategy for a multi-region integrated energy system in a port is proposed, aiming to improve energy efficiency and the economy of system operation. The strategy includes two stages: day-ahead planning and intraday rolling scheduling, to coordinate adjustable resources with different adjustment rates and reduce the impact of forecast errors and system disturbances. Day-ahead scheduling aims to minimize the total operating cost and make plans for the next 24 hours, whereas intraday scheduling is updated every 5 minutes to adapt to the randomness of renewable energy generation. Simulation analysis shows that the strategy can reduce operating costs by about 4.07%, increase the proportion of renewable energy such as wind and solar energy, and promote their effective utilization.

articleTitle: An Efficiency Optimization Method of DLCC Compensated IPT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) with higher-order compensation circuit is an effective way to improve system transmission performance. However, due to the relevant large number of circuit parameters, optimizing circuit parameters to achieve maximum transmission efficiency remains a challenge. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes an analytical parameter design method to enhance the system efficiency. The power loss of the whole system is first analyzed and modeled, and their relationship with the circuit parameters is analyzed. According to the characteristics of the loss, an analytical parameter optimization design method is proposed. Based on which, the multi-variable optimization problem that maximizes system efficiency can be transformed into multiple single-variable optimization problems, and the analytical solution of the optimal circuit parameters can be derived. This method greatly reduces the design complexity of the circuit parameters, and the analytical solution of the optimal circuit parameters of the IPT system is obtained for the first time. Simulation and experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The prototype can transmit 10 kW of power over a distance of 175 mm with a DCDC efficiency of 97%.

articleTitle: Storage Planning for High Penetration of Renewable Energy Sources Considering Battery Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The extensive application of energy storage batteries has raised concerns regarding their operational properties. It is crucial to consider not only the battery life measured by charge and discharge cycles but also the loss of capacity that occurs as they are used. To prevent situations where the actual operational capacity falls short of the intended capacity, this study integrates a storage capacity degradation model into operational simulations to investigate the impact of storage capacity degradation in practical operational scenarios. Initially, this paper introduces the full equivalent cycles (FEC) model for characterizing energy storage capacity degradation, subsequently integrating it into a conventional operational simulation model. Based on a specific municipal-level power grid, the study analyzes the impact of storage capacity degradation on the decision-making of the operational simulation model. The operational simulation method, which includes energy storage life constraints, is shown to be adaptable to different operational demands and supports the comprehensive management of energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Research on Electric Vehicle Charging Load Forecasting Method Based on Variable Mode Decomposition and one Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the popularity of electric vehicles(EVs), the demand for charging infrastructure is also increasing. To enhance the precision of short-term load forecasting for EVs, a hybrid model has been developed that integrates a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN) with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). This model uses channel fusion to extract time series features from different dimensional directions for model learning and fusion. At the same time, the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is used to optimize the model hyperparameters to avoid the inaccuracy of artificially set hyperparameters. This model’s performance is further enhanced by utilizing the Variable Mode Decomposition (VMD) technique to decompose the experimental data. Our proposed WOA-1DCNN-GRU model is then trained on these decomposed modal components, with the final predictions being reconstructed from them. Utilizing real-world charging pile data from a specific region, our simulation experiments confirm that the WOA-1DCNN-GRU model, which leverages VMD, demonstrates superior forecasting accuracy and stability compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: An Aggregated Model for Wind Power Frequency Regulation Considering Variability in Wind Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The aggregation of wind power into the electrical grid for frequency regulation necessitates the calculation of the collective contribution of wind farms to the grid’s stability. Traditionally, the effect of wind speed on the frequency regulation ability of wind power has not been fully studied. This paper introduces an approach to dynamically calculate the contribution of wind power clusters to the grid’s frequency regulation. Initially, the paper analyses the differences in frequency regulation capabilities of wind turbines at various wind speeds. Subsequently, stochastic differential equation is adpoted to generate multiple time series of wind speed that maintain the correlation between wind farms and conform to statistical characteristic. By applying these two methods, the adjustable capacity of the aggregated wind power clusters can be effectively measured, allowing for an assessment of their frequency regulation potential. The proposed method is validated using actual parameters from the Guangdong province power grid in China, confirming its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research and Practice on Primary and Secondary Fusion Identification Technology for Tree-Line Grounding Faults in Smart Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper focuses on the primary and secondary fusion identification technology for tree-line grounding faults in smart distribution networks. It deeply analyzes the serious threats of tree-line grounding faults to the safe and stable operation of distribution networks and elaborates on the crucial significance of accurately identifying such faults and fusing line environment perception information. The high-precision digital transformer technology, various fault feature analysis algorithms, and multi-source signal fusion strategies for line environment are introduced in detail. Through the development of fault identification devices and pilot applications, the remarkable effectiveness of this technology in improving the fault detection and prevention level of distribution networks is demonstrated, providing strong support for ensuring the safe and stable operation of power systems.

articleTitle: A Method for Photovoltaic Power Prediction Utilizing LSTM Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As global interest in renewable energy escalates, photovoltaic (PV) power generation has emerged as a significant energy source. Nonetheless, accurately predicting PV power remains a formidable challenge, primarily due to the unpredictability of factors like weather conditions. In this study, we introduce a PV power prediction model utilizing the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. This model seeks to enhance prediction accuracy by identifying and learning from patterns and trends within historical data.

articleTitle: Co-Optimization of Active Support Capability for DER in Active Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of large-scale distributed energy resources (DER) brings more operational flexibilities to the distribution network. These flexible resources can provide active support services, including both the frequency and voltage control, to enhance the power system regulation capabilities. This paper proposes a collaborative optimization method of the active support capability for DER in active distribution network (ADN). The frequency and voltage control parameters of DERs are collaboratively optimized with their PQ power setpoints to meet the support requirements from the upper control center, while ensuring the nodal voltage security of the ADN. Case studies conducted on a modified IEEE 69-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting for Virtual Power Plants Based on Improved Laguerre Orthogonal Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, a method for offline analysis of the short-term load method of virtual power plant based on the combination of AR-GARCH model and improved Laguerre neural network combination algorithm (LOBNN) is proposed. Firstly, the combination modelling of optimal AR-GARCH model and improved Laguerre neural network is established. The trained correlation matrix is screened to get the strong correlation factors affecting the load changes, and data preprocessing and correlation analysis are performed. Secondly, the LOBNN model is improved by improving the weights solving algorithm, which is used to enhance the flexibility of the model. Then, a new iterative algorithm is designed to further improve the prediction accuracy of the model, and the new LOBNN model is obtained. Finally, the data are adjusted by substituting the AR-GARCH model and the improved LOBNN model, obtaining two sets of predicted values for the input data, comparing the output multivariate load prediction results with the real values and calculating the loss function, and adjusting the network parameters according to the loss function generation by generation.

articleTitle: Impact of Hybrid Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Converters on Post-Fault Overvoltage in Renewable Energy Base
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the integration of renewable energy and power electronic devices, the dynamic characteristics of the power system have become increasingly complex. In order to reveal the post-fault overvoltage mechanism of hybrid grid-following converter (GFL) and grid-forming converter (GFM) systems, this paper analyzes the terminal voltage characteristics among different systems using phasor diagram. Firstly, this paper introduces GFL model and analyzes the terminal voltage in GFL grid-connected system. Next, this paper analyzes hybrid GFL and GFM system, pointing out that GFM can provide voltage support during short-circuit faults, and reduce post-fault overvoltage. Then, the paper discusses the impact of the capacity ratio of GFL to GFM on terminal voltage. Finally, the theoretical analysis in this paper has been verified in different systems.

articleTitle: The Control Approach of Energy Storage Batteries Joining in Primary Frequency tuning Grounded in Adaptable Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The extensive introduction of new energy sources like wind and solar has gone up markedly the frequency fluctuations in the power system, placing higher demands on the frequency tuning capability of thermal power units. Energy storage batteries have become an ideal frequency tuning auxiliary resource due to fast response and flexible output. Especially in the early stages of frequency fluctuations, the fast response of energy storage batteries reduces frequency fluctuations, thereby improving the frequency performance of the system. At present, the main control strategies for energy storage apparatus joining in primary frequency tuning include virtual inertia control and virtual droop control. However, these two control strategies have unsatisfactory frequency modulation effects when the energy storage condition of charge is low or high. In response to this situation, the paper proposes an adaptable control approach that coordinates virtual positive inertia, negative inertia, and droop control to achieve flexible response of the energy storage apparatus to different frequency changes and reduce frequency variance

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Renewable Energy-Based Hydrogen Production Systems Considering Equipment Lifespan Degradation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The generation of renewable energy from sources such as wind and solar exhibits characteristics of volatility and intermittency. To address the issue of renewable energy integration and reduce the financial burden associated with the degradation of equipment lifespan caused by fluctuations in input power, this paper presents an operational optimization model for renewable energy-based hydrogen production systems that considers equipment lifespan degradation. A proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis system is constructed initially, comprising an electrolytic cell, a dryer, and a compressor. The piecewise linearization method is employed to linearize the relationship between the hydrogen production efficiency and the operating current of the system. Furthermore, an energy storage device is employed to reduce the curtailment of wind and solar energy. To reduce the cost of system lifespan degradation, a cost-sharing mechanism for lifespan degradation due to input power fluctuations is proposed, and its effectiveness is validated using a case study.

articleTitle: Steel load prediction based on SSA-LSTM algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, Pearson method was used to screen highly correlated factors and input them into the prediction model for training. Based on the LSTM model, this paper added the optimization of SSA search algorithm, and used the steel load data of a region in Gansu Province to verify the proposed model. Compared with the original model, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> increased by 8.15% and MAPE decreased by 1.67%, indicating that the prediction effect of SSA-LSTM model was better.

articleTitle: Converter Energy Based Droop ADRC Control with Enhanced Dynamic Performance and Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The cascaded multi-converter system that constitutes a power electronic transformer has input, intermediate and output stages, and the converters at all levels need to switch operating modes frequently under different operating conditions, which determines that a single, fixed PI control strategy and parameters cannot realize global optimization control under all operating conditions. A converter energy-based droop control strategy for multiple converters is proposed, which provides better steady state and dynamic performance and enhances the stability of interconnected converters compared with the traditional droop control method. Modeling simulations are carried out in the PLECS simulation platform to verify the feasibility and superiority of the control strategy.

articleTitle: An Annual Maintenance Scheduling Model for Multiple-type Units Based on Cluster Unit Combinations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the advancement of renewable energy, the formulation of effective maintenance plans for generator sets has become increasingly important for the normal operation of power systems. Historically, maintenance models have typically focused on a single type of unit, while the scale of binary variables and constraint conditions has increased significantly, presenting substantial challenges for solving these optimization issues. This paper integrates the maintenance model with annual production simulations of the power system, proposing a multi-type unit maintenance scheduling model with a minimum time resolution of one hour. The maintenance unit types considered include thermal generator (TG), annual adjustment hydro units, and pumped storage (PS). Furthermore, to tackle the complexity and efficiency issues, this paper introduces clustered unit combinations (CUC) to transform binary variables in basic unit combinations (BUC) into continuous variables. Finally, based on the simulation study of modified IEEE RTS-79 system, validation of models and methods is assured.

articleTitle: Wind Power Forecasting Method Under Extreme Weather Conditions Based on Meta-Learning and Multi-Head Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wind power drops sharply under extreme weather conditions, which will lead to severe imbalances between power supply and demand, posing a significant threat to the safe and stable operation of new power system. Accurate forecasting of wind power under extreme weather conditions is crucial. However, extreme weather conditions are small probability events and only have limited representative samples, resulting in poor forecasting accuracy of traditional statistical models that rely on big data. Therefore, a wind power forecasting method under extreme weather conditions based on meta-learning and multi-head attention mechanisms is proposed in this paper. A base learner based on CNN-Attention-GRU is constructed at first. The samples under extreme weather conditions from nearby wind farms are used to pre-train the forecasting model to make up the lack of representative samples. Then, a meta-learner based on XGBoost is developed to perform targeted training using extreme weather data from the target wind farm to improve forecasting accuracy. Furthermore, the multi-head attention mechanism is used to enhance the learning capabilities of base learner and meta-learner. Operational data of eight wind farms affected by cold wave / typhoon weather conditions is used to verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. The results show that, when root mean square error is used as the evaluation index, the forecasting error can be reduced by 0.13%-4.29% under cold wave conditions, 0.35%-9.84% under typhoon conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Techniques for Identification of Dual AD Inconsistencies Based on Analysis of Differences in Sampling Values
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The current identification method for dual AD inconsistency in protective devices is summarized, and the adaptability of existing method based on field cases is analyzed. The current identification methods have poor ability to identify dual AD inconsistency under low current amplitude conditions. Based on the analysis of the characteristic differences between dual AD data under normal and abnormal operating conditions, a processing approach based on the degree of difference in sampling values is proposed, which includes two methods: sampling value comparison method and correlation coefficient method. The effectiveness of both methods was verified through cases of single channel signal abnormality and dual channel signal abnormality that occurred actually. The verification results show that these two identification methods can effectively improve the identification ability of the protection device for dual AD inconsistent faults under low current amplitude such as less than 0.1A. Among them, the correlation coefficient method is more suitable for situations where single signal is abnormal, and the sampling value comparison method is more suitable for situations where both signals are abnormal. This study provides useful references for supplementing and improving the dual AD inconsistency recognition scheme for protective devices.

articleTitle: A Graph Cut Approach for Coherency Identification with Wind-Integrated Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presented a graph cut approach to detect coherent groups. By calculating the cosine similarity, an undirected graph and normalized Laplacian matrix are created. The graph cut for the formed undirected graph was carried out by using spectral clustering, and the coherent groups were separated by inverse mapping the solved subgraphs into the power system. The proposed method is applied to the modified IEEE39 node system for analysis and verification.

articleTitle: Annual Time-Series Operation Simulation and Rapid Solution Method for Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the proportion of renewable energy increases in the new-type power system, the significance of conducting annual time-series operational simulations for renewable energy gradually emerges. The existing panoramic time-series operational simulations for power systems fail to achieve supply-demand balance over a long time scale, and the solution methods cannot balance both speed and accuracy. To address these issues, we first established an annual time-series-coupled unit commitment (UC) model to conduct hourly operational simulations for all 8760 hours of the year. Subsequently, we selected the optimal number of clusters for the time series in the model on a monthly basis, conducted clustering based on these selections, and reconstructed the time series to reduce its dimensionality. By solving the simplified time series, we achieved rapid solution of the model. Finally, we compared the proposed method with some existing methods, demonstrating that our method maintains high accuracy while greatly improving the solving speed.

articleTitle: Power System Evolution with Synergy of Multiple Energy Storage Planning Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Multiple types of long-term storage paves a promising way for the decarbonization of energy systems, by increasing renewable accommodations and providing operational flexibility in power systems. Nevertheless, comprehensive academic research into the power system evolution planning problems can enhance the precision of planning outcomes. However, power system evolution planning problems considering different types of storage technologies are largely unexplored. To this end, this paper proposes a power system evolution planning model considering multiple types of long-term storage technology. First, the influence of operating voltage and power on multiple energy storage is thoroughly considered to model its dynamic characteristics on power systems. Then, a comprehensive operational model of the storage device is established to reflect its multi-state transition dynamics as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problem. Furthermore, the influence of renewable integration and electricity demand of various scenarios in our power system evolution model is also analyzed. Case studies in a modified IEEE 118-bus test system demonstrate: 1) our model can mitigate the overestimation in capacity planning of the multiple types of storage devices, and 2) more renewable energy and less load will result in less investment in long-term storage and the load has a more significant influence.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Drainage Cabinet on DC Current Flowing into the Neutral Point of the Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To study the impact of the drainage cabinet on the DC current flowing into the neutral point of the power transformer, a simulation model was built using CDEGS. The case study includes one 500kV substation, seven 220kV substations, and a subway system with a total length of 13.5 km and nine traction substations. The potential, primary stray current, and secondary stray current were compared before and after the commissioning of the drainage cabinet. Additionally, the effect of the train's position was analyzed. The results show that after the commissioning of the drainage cabinet, when the train reaches position 23, both the potentials of the grounding grid and the DC current at the substation decrease. The impact of the train's position varies across different substations. In most cases, the DC current decreases after the commissioning of the drainage cabinet.

articleTitle: Rreseach on Optimal Scheduling Strategy of CHP Microgrid Based on Combined Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the face of the impact of renewable energy uncertainty, traditional scheduling methods will be difficult to ensure the stable operation of the system. Aiming at the above problems, an optimal scheduling strategy of combined heat and power-microgrid (CHP) microgrid based on combination forecasting model is proposed. Firstly, a combined prediction model based on neural network and bidirectional long short-term memory network is constructed to provide effective prediction data for optimal scheduling. Secondly, the two-stage power prediction of wind power and photovoltaic is carried out by using the combined prediction model. Finally, a day-ahead and intraday two-stage optimal scheduling model is established, and the day-ahead scheduling plan is solved with the goal of minimizing the total operating cost of the system. The intra-day scheduling plan adopts the rolling optimal scheduling strategy of model predictive control to realize the minimum adjustment of the output of each unit. The example verifies that the proposed method can effectively improve the economy and stability of the system operation.

articleTitle: Internal Aggregation Optimization Model of Virtual Power Plant Considering the Uncertainty of New Energy Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous increase of new energy access scale, the supply and demand form of power system is becoming increasingly severe. As an emerging flexible regulator, virtual power plant plays an important role in the security regulation of power grid. In this paper, the uncertainty of virtual power plant aggregate resources is fully considered, and the internal resource aggregation optimization model of virtual power plant is constructed. Through internal resource aggregation optimization, the flexible regulation potential of virtual power plant is stimulated to the maximum extent. The feasibility of the optimization results is verified by the example simulation.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Rural Microgrid Based on Approximate Dynamic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Rural power grid is an important part of smart grid construction. This paper proposes a rural microgrid optimal scheduling method based on approximate dynamic programming (ADP). Firstly, a rural microgrid optimization model with electric vehicles (EV) is established, and the multi-period optimization problem is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP). Then, the piecewise linear function based on EV energy storage is used to approximate the value function to obtain the approximate global optimal solution, so as to avoid the dimensionality curse and optimize the system online. Finally, the operating costs obtained by the simulation are compared with the operating costs without considering the access of EV to the power grid. It can be obtained that the operating cost of microgrid is smaller than that without considering electric vehicles. At the same time, the ADP online optimization results are better than the myopic strategy results.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation Method for Regulation Capability of Grid-Forming Controlled Photovoltaic-Energy Storage Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the extensive integration of distributed generation, there have been significant changes in the form and power composition of the distribution network. Among them, the integrated connection of photovoltaics and energy storage to distribution network substations is a typical application scenario for the high proportion integration of distributed generation. The stochastics and fluctuation of the distributed generation take significant challenges to the operation and control of distribution networks. However, with the gradual maturity of grid-forming control technology, the power control of photovoltaic and energy storage substations has become a feasible possibility. Accordingly, an equivalent power response model for photovoltaic and energy storage substations is constructed in this paper first. The active regulation characteristics of photovoltaics and energy storage were analyzed separately. Considering different operating states of photovoltaic and energy storage substations and different power commands, a quantitative calculation method for the regulation range and regulation speed of photovoltaic and energy storage substations is provided. At last, the proposed calculation method is validated through simulations on the PSCAD/EMTDC experimental platform.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Accounting Method for Power Transmission Channel Clearing Engineering Based on Binocular Visual Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of complex engineering quantity accounting process and low standardization level in the clearance work of transmission channels, this paper proposes an intelligent accounting method for transmission channel clearance engineering based on binocular visual perception. Firstly, the RGB image and depth image features are extracted separately through convolutional networks, and the RGB image features and depth features are fused using cross modal feature fusion module(CMF) and compact pyramid module (CPM) to achieve automatic recognition and contour extraction of tree stumps on the job site; Subsequently, a tree diameter measurement module based on 3D information reconstruction was constructed to achieve automatic calculation of tree diameter. Experiments have shown that the mAP for identifying tree stumps in transmission channel clearing sites reaches 0.972, and the relative error of tree diameter measurement is less than 5%, verifying the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper and providing technical support for intelligent engineering quantity accounting in transmission channel clearing sites.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Dispatch of Distribution Networks Considering Demand Response and Photovoltaic Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of low-carbon electricity, the low-carbon operation of the distribution network significantly impacts the reduction of carbon emissions in the power system. Addressing how to achieve coordinated low-carbon economic operation at the distribution network level is an urgent issue that requires resolution. This paper proposes a low-carbon scheduling model that considers carbon emissions and demand response within the distribution network. First, we introduce an improved dynamic carbon emission factor for the distribution network, which serves as a guiding signal to provide reference for users' low-carbon electricity consumption. Next, we develop two distinct demand response models: one for industrial users aimed at minimizing scheduling costs while reducing carbon emissions, and another for residential users focused on electricity satisfaction and low-carbon satisfaction. Finally, simulations are conducted using an improved IEEE-33 node distribution system. The results indicate that the proposed scheduling model effectively reduces carbon emissions in the distribution network and enhances the integration of photovoltaic resources.

articleTitle: Research on Early Warning Methods for Electrical Safety Risks in AC and DC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of renewable energy and urbanization, the risk of electrical fires has increased. This paper constructs a three-layer fault disaster risk warning model through multi-sensor information fusion technology. Firstly, system signals are obtained through different types of electrical and physical sensors at the information layer. Next, fault features are extracted to determine the type of fault at the feature layer. Then Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) algorithms are applied to establish the electrical safety risk evaluation model at the decision layer. Finally, the risk evaluation model is applied to warn the electrical safety risks in AC/DC power supply systems separately. The model calculation results show that AHP is suitable for simple and linear problems while DNN is suitable for complex and nonlinear problems.

articleTitle: Multi-agent Scheduling with Multi-stage Training for Mutual Assistance between Distributed Sustainable Energy and Flexible Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of large-scale distributed renewable energy sources has brought tremendous operational pressure on the power grid. Coordinating these distributed renewable energy sources with adjustable resources in distribution grids will become an important means to enhance grid resilience. Addressing the challenges of modeling massive flexible resources and dealing with large decision spaces, this paper proposes a multi-agent scheduling method with multi-stage training algorithm. Firstly, a mathematical model for coordinated regulation of distributed sustainable energy and flexible loads is established. Secondly, a multi-objective phased learning framework is designed. Finally, through training and simulation on a power grid, it is verified that the proposed method can achieve power mutual assistance among distributed resources and improve the level of intelligent collaborative autonomy in distribution power grids.

articleTitle: Study on the Impact of Carbon Emission Right Trading on Energy and Electricity Trading Based on CGE Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As a key field for realizing low-carbon development of the society, the effective control of carbon emissions in the electric power industry is of great significance for coping with global climate change. In order to deeply explore the impact of carbon emission rights trading on the power industry, optimize the energy structure and achieve sustainable development. This paper first analyses the basic concepts and mechanisms of carbon emissions trading, and then establishes the basic framework and equation system of the CGE model, including the modules of production, income and expenditure, market, carbon emissions trading and dynamic mechanism. Through arithmetic analyses, this paper evaluates the responses of the macroeconomy and the energy industry under different carbon emission reduction scenarios. The results show that stricter carbon emission reduction targets have a more significant impact on the economy and energy industry. It provides systematic theoretical support for the low-carbon development strategy of the power industry, and has important reference value for the formulation of related policies.

articleTitle: A Novel Five-level LLC Resonant Converter and Its Modulation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For the DC-DC link following the on-board charger of electric vehicles, as well as in applications such as electric vehicle charging, rail transit power supply systems, and medical equipment power supplies, this paper proposes a novel five-level LLC resonant converter based on switched capacitors. This converter achieves a five-level output through a switched capacitor circuit, offering a simple structure and high efficiency. Research indicates that employing LLC resonant technology effectively reduces switching losses and enhances system efficiency. Additionally, the integration of the switched capacitor circuit allows for a wide-ranging output voltage adjustment, accommodating the charging needs of various battery types. To further improve performance, the converter employs level-shifted sinusoidal PWM (LS-PWM) modulation, which optimizes switching operations and minimizes harmonic distortion. In order to verify the accuracy of the proposed resonant converter, a converter with a switching frequency of 100 KHz and an input of 220 V was built in the PSIM simulation for validation.

articleTitle: Reserve Capacity Optimization of Power System Connected to Large-Scale Wind Farm Based on Chance Constrained Objective Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the access of large-scale wind power, the new power system faces multiple uncertainties (including wind power output and load uncertainties, generator and link fault, etc.), and the total amount of newly added wind power output uncertainties is large, and the time-space correlation is strong, so the traditional reserve capacity demand criteria are no longer applicable. This paper takes the opportunity constraint goal programming as the mathematical theory and method support, and considers the situation of large-scale wind power generation integration. It models the uncertain factors such as the failure shutdown of generating units, load forecast error, and wind power generation error, and uses a genetic algorithm based on the Monte-Carlo random simulation method for solution. It takes the IEEE-9 node system as an example, and the results verify that the spare determination method proposed in this paper can ensure the system's safe and stable operation under the premise of reducing the system's overall operating cost, alleviating the pressure of providing spare capacity on the generation side, and achieving a balance between the system's peak regulation performance and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Multi-time scale optimal scheduling strategy of integrated energy system considering integrated demand response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To further tap the user-side adjustable load resources, improve the economic operation of the system, and reduce the impact of source-load power fluctuations, a multi-time scale optimal scheduling strategy for integrated energy systems considering integrated demand response is proposed. Firstly, a comprehensive demand response model is proposed. In the day-ahead stage, the power load considers the electricity price demand response and the heat load is divided into residential heating heat load and industrial heat load for demand response, respectively. In the intra-day stage, both power and heat load participate in the incentive demand response. At the same time, multi-time scale optimization can suppress source-load power fluctuation and reduce the impact of prediction error on the system. Finally, simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Utilization Benefit Evaluation of Flexible DC Traction Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With rising demands for environmental protection and energy efficiency, integrating photovoltaic (PV) resources into flexible DC traction power systems (TPSs) has become increasingly important. However, PV integration faces two main challenges: the volatility of PV output and traction load uncertainties, as well as the effect of power flow optimization under coordinated control. Current methods, including dynamic simulation, power balance analysis, and power flow analysis, struggle to comprehensively evaluate these factors. To address this, this study proposes a PV Utilization Benefit (PVUB) evaluation model, which quantifies the operational benefits of PV integration by accounting for both PV and traction load uncertainties and power flow optimization effects. Applied to a real-world case on a Beijing Metro Line, the PVUB model effectively analyzes investment benefits and the impact of key factors, providing essential technical support for PV planning and power flow analysis of PV-integrated flexible DC TPSs.

articleTitle: An Improved Bat Algorithm for Load Model Parameter Identification of Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional bat algorithm is easily trapped in the local optimal solution, this paper presents an improved bat optimization algorithm, and uses this algorithm to identify the parameters of the power system load model. The algorithm flow is as follows: Firstly, chaotic mapping traverses the whole solution space and initializes the solution. Secondly, the fitness of each solution is calculated in the application process of the algorithm, and the fitness of the solution near the peak value in the solution space is shared. The more solutions exist in a certain range, the lower the fitness. Moreover, after the algorithm runs a certain number of cycles, the simplex method is used for the second search. This method solves the problem that the traditional bat algorithm is easily limited to the local optimal solution, and makes the parameter identification method of the load model have higher identification accuracy. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has better performance in convergence speed than the traditional bat optimization algorithm, and can be applied to the parameter optimization of load model.

articleTitle: A Numeric Study of the Impact of Renewable’s Penetration in the Energy and Capacity Markets with the Participation of Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of different renewable energy (RE) penetration on the economic and operational outcomes of integrated energy and capacity markets. Using a combined market-clearing model, we analyze the effects of varying RE levels on market dynamics and revenue distribution among generators and RE sources. Our findings indicate that increased RE penetration reduces conventional generators' revenue while enhancing RE profitability due to lower operational costs and priority dispatch. Additionally, this study aims to provide insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders and emphasizes the need for adaptive market designs that maintain system reliability and economic balance during high RE integration.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning-Driven Lifecycle Carbon Footprint Assessment in Electric Vehicle Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which mandates stringent carbon footprint standards for imported Electric Vehicle (EV) batteries, accurate and high-resolution carbon accounting across its lifecycle has become essential. This paper presents a Machine-Learning(ML)-driven methodology for comprehensive carbon footprint accounting designed to precisely capture emissions across material extraction, assembly, logistics, and recycling phases in EV battery production. By employing advanced machine learning techniques, our approach enhances the granularity and accuracy of emissions data, aligning with regulatory requirements and supporting sustainable practices in EV battery manufacturing. The model is validated through empirical analysis, demonstrating its capability to support compliance with evolving global carbon policies.

articleTitle: Calculation Method for Assessing Flexible Ramp-Up Demand in Power Systems with High Proportion of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation method for flexible climbing demand of power systems. Firstly, the flexible climbing demand of the system is described in detail, and based on the flexible climbing products, a joint clearing model of spot electricity energy market and flexible climbing auxiliary service is constructed. By solving the model, it can accurately evaluate and calculate the upward and downward flexible climbing needs of the system in each period, and determine the corresponding flexible climbing capacity provided by the system itself, and further evaluate and calculate the upward and downward flexible climbing capacity and capacity margin of the system in each period. Finally, this paper uses the data of a provincial actual power system for example analysis to verify the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed evaluation calculation method, which provides a strong decision support for the optimal scheduling of the power system, the effective consumption of new energy and the participation in the flexible climbing auxiliary service market trading.

articleTitle: Virtual Phase Sequence Exchange-Based Control for Transient Stability in Virtual Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) controlled isolated power grid has attracted significant attention due to its voltage support capabilities. However, even under small disturbances, the system can experience transient instability risks similar to conventional power grids. To address this issue, various control methods have been explored. Phase sequence exchange (PSE) is one such method, which stabilizes the system without compromising system capacity and inertia, though it introduces additional power electronic components. In response to this, a transient model for VSG-controlled isolated grids is established in this paper, and a novel control strategy called virtual phase sequence exchange (VPSE) is proposed. VPSE enhances transient stability by reducing the power angle of the VSG through power electronic control in the inverter, effectively replicating the stabilizing benefits of PSE without the need for extra devices. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed solution is verified through simulation experiments conducted in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Optimization strategy for monthly green electricity and green certificate transactions for electricity retailer considering renewable energy consumption responsibilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The 3060 goal puts forward new requirements for the consumption of renewable energy. As the entity of the wholesale market, electricity retailer bear corresponding responsibilities. This article explores how electricity retailer can maximize profits by optimizing monthly green electricity and green certificate trading strategies while considering the responsibility of renewable energy consumption. Firstly, the article analyzes the electricity purchase costs of e-sellers in thermal power, hydropower and non-hydropower renewable energy markets, as well as the revenue uncertainty under fixed-price contract and floating-price contract models. Then, a power purchase strategy optimization model based on profit maximization is proposed, which considers the market clearing price, renewable energy consumption quota requirements, non-water renewable energy consumption responsibility and other factors. Through the analysis of numerical examples, the power purchase ratio and green certificate purchase volume of electricity retailer in different energy markets in each month of the next year are analyzed, and the optimal strategy is obtained. The research results show that electricity retailer can set up different types of electricity sales packages in the retail market, by predicting the future clearing price, it can provide a reference for electricity retailer to consider the electricity purchase strategy of renewable energy consumption.

Author Keywords: the responsibility of renewable energy consumption
green electricity and green certificate trading strategies

articleTitle: Access Point Selection for Offshore Wind Farm Transmitted by Fractional Frequency Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Driven by the requirements of the energy transition due to climate change, wind power is developing rapidly. Offshore wind farms are the main trend of future wind power exploitation. In response to the issue of offshore wind farms being connected to the onshore power grid through fractional frequency transmission system, this paper analyzes the factors affecting the selection of access points for offshore wind farms, proposes evaluation indexes for access points and a combination weight model based on the maximum variation coefficient. Simulation results of an offshore wind farm connected to the power grid of an eastern coastal province show that the proposed method enhances the wind power consumption and improves the safety of the power grid.

articleTitle: Wind Deflection Characteristics of Suspension Insulator Strings for 500kV Transmission Lines Based on Realistic 3D Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
