The experimental circuit works well. A lot of data is obtained. Two data processing methods have been compared to estimate the failure rate, and it is found that the overall data fitting method based on the simplified exponential model is suitable for our working scenario.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling of independent microgrid based on multi-objective improved gray wolf algorithmaper
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Microgrids contain a variety of micropower sources and need to meet many constraints, and the traditional gray wolf algorithm is easy to fall into local optimum, so this paper proposes a multi-objective improved gray wolf algorithm (MLGWO) for microgrid economic optimization scheduling. In order to solve the problems of precocious maturity and local convergence, the improved algorithm first uses the tent chaotic map to generate the initial population, and the Levy flight strategy increases the search space to enhance the diversity of followers. Secondly, In order to balance the global search and local development of the algorithm, a nonlinear adjustment is set for the convergence factor. Finally, the adaptive t-distribution variation is used to effectively jump out of the local optimal to improve the solution accuracy. Under the benchmark functions and the microgrid economic optimization scheduling model with the lowest daily operating cost, the improved gray wolf algorithm is compared with the gray wolf algorithm and the particle swarm optimization algorithm. The simulation results show that the improved gray wolf algorithm has certain feasibility and practicability.

articleTitle: Study on the Operation Mode of Electric Vehicle-Based Virtual Power Plants Using TGCN-MPC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The surge in electric vehicles (EVs) necessitates effective load management and scheduling for charging stations. This study introduces an optimized scheduling method for an EV Virtual Power Plant (EVPP) using Temporal Graph Convolution Network (TGCN) and Model Predictive Control (MPC). TGCN predicts charging station load by capturing spatial and temporal dependencies, utilizing historical load data and influencing factors. Combined with MPC, it enables real-time, optimized resource allocation based on forecasted loads. Experimental results indicate substantial improvements in load prediction accuracy and scheduling efficiency, enhancing EVPP operational stability and reducing grid fluctuations compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Method for Evaluating the Benefits of Independent Energy Storage Participation in the Day Ahead Market Based on Ideal Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper introduces a method to evaluate independent energy storage (IES) benefits in the day-ahead market for renewable energy integration in China. By comparing scenarios with and without IES, the approach, validated on the IEEE 30-bus system, shows enhanced grid operation, cost savings, and increased renewable energy usage, offering insights for market design and energy storage.

articleTitle: Transmission Characteristics Analysis of Underwater Three-Coil WPT Systems under Various Misalignment Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper examines the transmission characteristics of underwater three-coil Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems under various misalignment conditions. A circuit model for the three-coil WPT system is established to identify key electrical parameters influencing performance. Through simulation and experimental analyses, the effects of different misalignments on system's transmission characteristics are quantitatively evaluated. The results reveal that horizontal offsets negatively affect the efficiency of the three-coil WPT system, with the adverse impact on system efficiency increasing progressively when the misalignment occurs in the receiving coil, relay coil, and transmitting coil, respectively. The system maintains over 70% efficiency within a horizontal offset of 70 mm. Additionally, it shows strong resilience to coaxial rotational offsets, with efficiency fluctuations kept below 5% under a 30° rotational misalignment. These findings demonstrate the robustness of the underwater three-coil WPT system, highlighting its suitability for practical applications where alignment variations are inevitable.

articleTitle: Cost Calculation for Energy Storage’s Providing Ancillary Services for Frequency and Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The provision of ancillary services by energy storage is becoming increasingly common in power systems. However, the lack of methodology accurately calculating their costs has constrained the development of energy storage. This paper primarily discusses a method for calculating the costs of ancillary services provided by the energy storage alongside the traditional thermal generators. Firstly, models for ancillary services provided by both energy storage and thermal power units are established. Secondly, the system’s demand for ancillary services is reflected through the system frequency regulation model and the system voltage regulation model. Subsequently, a power system dispatch model incorporating multiple ancillary services provided by energy storage is developed. This dispatch model is then solved to obtain the dual multipliers corresponding to the ancillary service constraints, which are utilized to derive the costs of ancillary services provided by energy storage. Finally, the method is applied through simulation to a modified IEEE 14-bus system. This paper provides a reference for the pricing of ancillary services provided by energy storage.

articleTitle: Instantaneous DC Bias Suppression Strategy for Isolated AC/DC Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The isolated AC/DC matrix converter, with its bidirectional power transmission characteristics, demonstrates broad application potential in the field of new energy. However, due to its specific phase-shift modulation requirements, significant DC bias currents may arise during rapid changes in transmitted power, posing a threat to the safe operation of the converter. To address this issue, this paper derives a mathematical relationship between transmitted power and instantaneous DC bias current and proposes a transient control strategy based on adjusting the phase-shift angle and modulation coefficient. This method effectively suppresses DC bias current induced by power fluctuations. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Blockchain-enabled electricity data sharing mechanism using attribute-based encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The current electricity data sharing schemes face challenges such as low encryption efficiency and vulnerability to tampering with user attributes. To address these issues, this paper presents a novel approach that combines blockchain technology with attribute-based encryption (ABE). By integrating ABE with symmetric encryption algorithms, the scheme guarantees confidentiality and provides fine-grained access control over electricity data. An online/offline encryption mode is introduced to improve encryption efficiency, while outsourcing computing technology is employed to reduce the computational burden on users. Attribute sets and data hash values are recorded on the blockchain to guarantee the immutability of user attributes and the correctness of decryption. The analysis demonstrates that this scheme facilitates the secure sharing of electricity data and is well-suited for resource-constrained electricity terminal devices.

articleTitle: Study on a coupled regulation method of distribution network voltage regulation and electric hydrogen generation voltage regulation considering hydrogen demand
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Building a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient energy system has become the main direction of energy industry development. This paper proposes an optimized regulation method based on the idea of multi-objective optimization, it focuses on the impact of user-side electric hydrogen generation devices on the grid side, and investigates how to reasonably utilize user-side small-capacity electric hydrogen generation devices to participate in distribution network voltage regulation and control, in order to improve the effect and economic efficiency of distribution network voltage regulation and control.

articleTitle: A Bi-level Optimization Model for Capacity and Energy Markets Considering the Design of the Capacity Demand Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the acceleration of China's new power system construction and the push towards a unified national electricity market, the focus has shifted to developing an appropriate capacity market mechanism. This mechanism should ensure sufficient system capacity and effectively promote the investment and construction of various capacity resources. This paper proposes a bi-level optimization model for the capacity and energy markets, considering the design of the capacity demand curve. First, different shapes of the capacity demand curve are modeled to establish a reasonable capacity clearing price. Then, a bi-level optimization model is constructed that accounts for the potential operational benefits of the energy market. By iteratively interacting the clearing results from the upper and lower levels, the optimal capacity resource clearing combination can be achieved. Finally, case analysis shows that the proposed model can avoid overinvestment in capacity resources, achieve better economic efficiency, and promote the construction of renewable energy.

articleTitle: An Investigation into Electromagnetic Performance in Novel Reverse-salient Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To solve the problem of the small weak magnetic field range of traditional permanent magnet synchronous motors, a new type of reverse-salient permanent magnet synchronous motor (RSPMSM) is proposed. The direct-axis inductance is greater than the quadrature-axis inductance, so it can obtain a wide speed regulation range. The performance of RSPMSM is analyzed by finite element method and the advantages and disadvantages of two slot-type RSPMSMs are listed by comparative analysis.

articleTitle: A Combined Physics and Data Driven Method for Broadband Impedance Online Estimation of Renewable Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Obtaining the broadband impedance of renewable power plants is a prerequisite for conducting oscillation risk analysis of renewable power integration system. This paper proposed a method for online estimating the broadband impedance of renewable power plants with Kirchhoff's law, based on the topology parameters of collecting power lines and the broadband impedance of renewable power units such as wind turbine under different steady-state conditions. By frequency sweeping of wind farm, it was verified that the proposed method could accurately identify the width-bandwidth impedance of wind farm, which is of great significance to the broadband oscillation risk online assessment of renewable power integration system.

articleTitle: Transient Overvoltage Stability Mechanism of AC-DC Sending-End System with Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the mechanisms underlying transient overvoltage in wind power transmission through VSC-HVDC (Voltage Source Converter based High Voltage Direct Current Transmission) islanding systems. Initially, it presents an overview of the VSC-HVDC system and its applications in wind power transmission. Subsequently, it analyzes the formation mechanisms and influencing factors of transient overvoltage. Finally, practical simulation cases are utilized to validate the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization and Scheduling Strategy of Electric-hydrogen Coupled Island Microgrid Based on Reversible Solid Oxide Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, a novel optimization method for an independent island microgrid based on the balance of plant assisted reversible solid oxide cell is proposed to meet the energy needs of residents on the remote island. Firstly, a refined model of the reversible solid oxide cell which is supported by a high-power balance of plant is established. Secondly, aiming to minimize the daily comprehensive operating cost of the microgrid system, an optimized scheduling strategy is proposed for a hydrogenelectricity coupled isolated microgrid based on the reversible solid oxide cell. Case study analyses confirm the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Anti-Fault Resistance Protection of AC Outgoing Transmission Lines Emanating from Inverter-interfaced Renewable Energy Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The existence of fault resistance can significantly weaken the fault characteristics of AC outgoing transmission lines emanating from inverter-interfaced renewable energy power plants. To solve the problems caused by different types of the faults through fault resistance (FTFR, the faults that the fault point resistance is greater than zero) in AC outgoing transmission lines, a novel anti-fault resistance protection principle based on the energy consumption of fault resistance is proposed in this paper as the backup protection of FTFR. The theoretical analysis show that this protection principle can identify different types of internal FTFR in AC outgoing transmission lines effectively, it can also isolate the FTFR with high reliability and high sensitivity by adopting self-adaptive threshold, and is not affected by the factors such as the fault position, the fault resistance value, and etc. Finally, a model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the validity of the protection principle.

articleTitle: Method for Anomaly Detection in Distributed Photovoltaic Power Generation Based on Kernel Principal Component-OPTICS Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Addressing the lack of professional monitoring in Distributed Photovoltaic Power Generation Systems (DPV), this study proposes a novel method for detecting anomalies in distributed photovoltaic power output. This method leverages the output correlation of adjacent photovoltaic stations and combines Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) with the OPTICS clustering algorithm to perform cluster partitioning and dimensionality reduction on the power output data of photovoltaic power stations. The specific steps are as follows: First, the OPTICS algorithm is used to partition the output data of multiple photovoltaic stations into clusters; then, Kernel Principal Component Analysis is applied to reduce the dimensionality of the clustered data. Based on this, an equal-weighted weighted average method is employed to plot the output curve that reflects the overall output condition of the cluster under different weather conditions. Finally, the output range is fitted using quantile regression, which serves as the basis for anomaly detection in DPV clusters.

articleTitle: Incentive Compatible Trading Mechanism for Double Auction Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of renewable energy, there is an urgent need for flexible resources such as flexible loads to participate in power system dispatch. The goal of power market is to optimize the allocation of electricity resources, but currently the mechanism for demand-side resources to participate in market competition is not yet perfect. The locational marginal price mechanism widely used cannot solve the problems of asymmetric information and strategic bidding, which affect the efficiency of resource optimization. Therefore, on the basis of the VCG design theory, a clearing mechanism for flexible loads participating in the double auction market is proposed. It conforms to incentive compatibility, individual rationality, and social utility maximization simultaneously. Then, a pricing correction strategy based on clearing energy is proposed to address the issue of settlement imbalance caused by the VCG mechanism. Finally, case studies based on the improved IEEE30-bus system are done, validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrating Distributed Generation into Power Flow Calculations: An Improved Newton-Raphson Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the global fossil energy crisis and the pursuit of dual carbon goals, distributed generation (DG) has been increasingly integrated into modern power systems. While DG offers significant benefits in terms of low carbon emissions and sustainable development, its diverse nature complicates traditional power flow calculations, thereby hindering effective system planning and scheduling. This paper presents an enhanced method for power flow calculation that incorporates DG. Initially, we establish mathematical models for various types of DG based on their operational principles, categorizing them into distinct node types. We then provide a comprehensive description of the conversion processes for nodes amenable to the Newton-Raphson method. Finally, we demonstrate the applicability of the improved power flow calculation method by analyzing the impact of DG on the IEEE 33 bus system, focusing on factors such as DG type, location, and capacity.

articleTitle: Simulation of Fast Cascading Failures Considering Voltage Ride Through Capability of Renewable Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable generation, the evolution process of fast cascading failures in the power system with a high proportion of renewable generation turns out to be more complicated. There are few existing fast cascading failure models that take into account the voltage ride through (VRT) capability of renewable generation. The portrayal of the dynamic characteristics of renewable generation still needs to be improved. In response to this, the VRT control model and VRT protection model have been established to comprehensively depict the output characteristics and disturbance tolerance capability of renewable generation in fast cascading failures. Finally, the simulation results of the AC-DC hybrid receiving-end system with a high proportion of renewable generation show that the established models can effectively depict the influence of VRT capability of renewable generation in fast cascading failures, providing a more comprehensive basis for the analysis of fast cascading failures under the access of a high proportion of renewable generation.

articleTitle: Research on the Standard System Construction of Vehicle to Grid and Relevant Suggestions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The rise of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology provides an innovative solution for building a more flexible and efficient new power system. However, the large-scale application of V2G technology requires crossing a series of technical and standard barriers. At present, there is an increasingly urgent need for standardization among the various links of "vehicle-pile-network", including communication protocols, safety standards, charging interface specifications and data interaction formats, which put forward high requirements for the popularization and integration of V2G technology. In this paper, based on the typical scene of V2G, the development status of V2G standards at home and abroad is summarized and analyzed in depth; secondly, the construction method of V2G standard system based on six-dimensional structural model method is proposed, and the V2G standard system is proposed by using the work decomposition method; finally, combined with the development trend of electric vehicle technology, the design thinking and suggestions of V2G standard system in China are put forward.

articleTitle: Wasserstein Distance-Based Renewable Scenario Generation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to address the uncertainty associated with renewable energy sources, this study develops a scenario construction method. An initialization of the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) is achieved through the K-medoids clustering method. Subsequently, a large set of foundational scenarios generated through sampling is subjected to scenario reduction using the Wasserstein distance. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is validated using wind and solar data from the PJM electricity market.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic and Vibration Characteristics of Power Transformer Iron Core under DC Magnetic Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The probability of DC magnetic bias are increasing because of DC transmission projects. Vibration of the iron core will raise under DC magnetic bias. The intense vibration will cause the possibility of the failure of the iron core loosening fault. Therefore, the 3D multi-physical model of the iron core was built in this paper to calculate the electromagentic and vibration characteristics under no-load and DC magnetic bias conditions. The conclusions are as follows: Compared the multi-physical models that directly calculated, the method will save thirty five minutes and also accurate. The excitation current peak, the second harmonic's content, the vibration, the stress and the displacement all increase when the power transformer is subjected to DC magnetic bias. The excitation current peak, the second harmonic's content, the iron core vibration, the stress and displacement all increase when the power transformer is subjected to DC magnetic bias. So measures are taken to prevent the iron core damage under DC magnetic bias. This study provides an effective way to quickly obtain the iron core characteristics of electromagnetic and vibration and provides a theoretical basis for further study of transformer noise characteristics.

articleTitle: Study on Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on SCSSA-CNN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To enhance the accuracy of photovoltaic power generation, this paper integrates the sparrow search optimization algorithm (SCSSA) with convolutional neural networks (CNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory neural networks (BiLSTM). This integration allows the feature data from the CNN to be incorporated into the BiLSTM, while the SCSSA, based on the joint positive cosine and cauchy theorem, creates a new hybrid neural network model for predicting photovoltaic power. Within this model, the BiLSTM establishes the temporal relationships among historical data, leading to improved photovoltaic power prediction outcomes. Ultimately, the SCSSA-CNN-BiLSTM model demonstrates exceptional stability and accuracy in forecasting photovoltaic power, meeting the current accuracy requirements for short-term solar power generation.

articleTitle: Transient Voltage Stability Assessment of Hybrid Power System With Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Generation Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To effectively assess the transient voltage stability (TVS) of hybrid power system, this paper presents an assessment method of TVS based on switching system maximum Lyapunov exponent (SSMLE). First, the voltage differential equations of the system under different operating conditions are established. Next, the SSMLE is calculated and revised to rapidly and accurately assess the system's transient voltage stability. Finally, simulation results investigate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sub-synchronous Oscillation of Wind Farm with MMC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the interaction between the modular multilevel converter (MMC) station and wind farms, various oscillations occur in the offshore wind farm with the modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC). In contrast to two-level converters, the nonlinear dynamics of the arm capacitance and the circulating currents result in the inherent time-periodic characteristic of MMC. Based on the linear time-periodic (LTP) method, this paper presents a small-signal model that preserves the original time-varying dynamics. Then, the effect of generation power, controllers, and their interaction on the sub-synchronous oscillations (SSO) of the system is investigated. Finally, the time-domain responses of the detailed nonlinear model are used to validate the accuracy of the analysis.

articleTitle: Design of Single Frequency Oscillation Suppression Damping Channel for Three-phase Grid-connected Inverter Covering Full Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the design idea of the current oscillation suppression damping channel is not clear and will affect the impedance characteristics of the non-target frequency band, the voltage feedback channel is introduced, and the channel transfer function is designed according to the sequence impedance characteristics of the three-phase grid-connected inverter itself By combining the frequency component selection module composed of digital spike filter and delayer, the voltage feedback channel only passes through the target frequency component. and the single-frequency oscillation suppression of the three-phase grid-connected inverter covering the full frequency band is realized. Verified by an example, the method has good oscillation suppression effect and relatively strong pertinence. Do not increase the risk of oscillation in non-target frequency bands.

articleTitle: Multiple Optimization Method Based on Comprehensive Adjustment Coefficient for Axial Partition Bridge Arm Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of new power systems, low-carbon and high-quality development in China, the proportion of new energy sources such as wind power and photovoltaics is increasing, and flexible DC transmission technology has been widely used in new energy grid-connected, long-distance power transmission and other scenarios because of its advantages of asynchronous interconnection of AC power grids, strong control flexibility and expansibility. The bridge arm reactor is an important equipment in flexible DC transmission project, which runs for a long time in AC and DC amplitude are quite large combined high current conditions, and the temperature caused by the abnormal temperature rise sometimes occurs, which endangers the reactor life and the operation safety of the power grid. The new axial partition bridge arm reactor structure, especially when the split ratio is 45%, can effectively solve the local overheating problem of bridge arm reactors during operation. Further optimization research on axial partition bridge arm reactors can provide a theoretical basis for the design, manufacture, operation and maintenance of large reactors. A multi-optimization method based on the comprehensive adjustment coefficient is proposed. Three comprehensive adjustment coefficients k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> and k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> are set to adjust the proportion of the constant resistance voltage, constant temperature rise and constant current density of the optimization target. The compromise of three optimization strategies is realized. Comparing the temperature field of the traditional structure of the bridge arm reactor, the axial partition structure and the axial partition optimization structure, the axial partition optimization structure effectively reduces the heating capacity of the encapsulation and makes the temperature distribution of the encapsulation more balanced. It also has good temperature rise stability when the transmission power changes. This research not only helps to improve the performance and stability of the bridge arm reactor, but also provides theoretical support for the further development and application of flexible DC transmission technology.

articleTitle: Research on Coordinated Frequency Modulation Control Strategy of Wind-Storage System Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to enhance and ensure the frequency modulation capability of wind turbines, this paper proposes a coordinated frequency modulation control strategy for wind-storage systems based on Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) technology. This approach addresses the high capacity demand and poor economic efficiency associated with traditional energy storage systems that directly compensate for the frequency modulation capability of wind farms. First, a mathematical model of the wind-storage VSG system is established based on its structural framework, and the frequency modulation characteristics of the wind-storage VSG are analyzed. Next, the frequency modulation control methods for the energy storage system VSG are studied according to its mathematical model. Then, considering the output characteristics of both the wind farm and the energy storage system, a coordinated control strategy based on wind turbine inertia release and steady-state support from energy storage is proposed. This strategy optimizes the parallel output control of the wind farm and the energy storage system. Finally, the feasibility of the control strategy is verified through simulation analysis, which demonstrates that it significantly reduces the capacity configuration of the energy storage system while maintaining stable output frequency support, thereby improving the economic efficiency of frequency modulation for the wind farm.

articleTitle: Multiphysics-Constrained Safe Charging Boundary for Lithium-Ion Battery Based on a Coupled Electro-Thermal-Aging Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Fast charging is essential to enhance the practicality of electric vehicles, yet it may accelerate degradation or damage to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). This study introduces a multi-physics constrained safe charging boundary for LIBs within a model predictive control (MPC) framework. This closed-loop charging strategy integrates model-based optimization with rule-based control. Within this control scheme, a coupled electro-thermal-aging model is developed to forecast battery states. Combined the MPC-based control and rule-based control, the proposed charging management can effectively balance the speed, safety, and battery life expectancy without violating the physical constraints. Experimental results compare the proposed MPC-based safe charging boundary with traditional rule-based strategies, highlighting trade-offs between charging speed and battery lifespan.

articleTitle: Application of LSTM Network Combining Global and Local Learning in Power Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Power load forecasting is essential for maintaining the equilibrium between power supply and demand, optimizing resource distribution, enhancing operational efficiency, and minimizing operational costs. The acceleration of industrialization and urbanization, along with the extensive implementation of renewable energy, dramatically heightens the uncertainty and complexity of power load, imposing greater demands on the accuracy and dependability of power load forecasting. Currently, load forecasting research predominantly centers on predicting individual load series, meaning each model is exclusively relevant to a particular load series. This necessitates training various models to forecast varied loads, augmenting the complexity and time expenditure of model training. Moreover, the predictive accuracy of the conventional model will markedly diminish as the user's electricity usage patterns evolve. This research proposes a novel forecasting method that integrates the concepts of a global model with model localization to address the issues mentioned above. A global model is initially trained to manage various load sequences to acquire preliminary forecasting capacity. The prediction accuracy is enhanced by fine-tuning the parameters of the global model to create localized models that conform to the specific characteristics of the various load sequences. The experimental results indicate that the proposed model has markedly enhanced prediction accuracy relative to the standard approach.

articleTitle: Field Tests of Impedance Measurement Using a Megawatt-scale Full-power Grid Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The impedance measurement is becoming widely accepted for characteristic depiction and stability analysis of renewable energy generation. Usually, it is conducted using software or controller hardware-in-the-loop simulations, but rarely in field tests. This work presents the impedance measurements of a voltage source converter and various wind turbines in field tests. The tests were conducted by full-power grid simulators, which have been used in grid adaptability tests in China for years. In this paper, the test setup is introduced. The test procedures are given according to the related standards and documents. The test results are illustrated and compared. These field tests give clear frequency-domain characteristics of the devices under test and validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Power Control and Equalization Strategy for MMC-BESS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper investigates the control strategies for modular multilevel converter-based battery energy storage systems (MMC-BESS). Based on the analysis of topological structure and operational principles of the MMC-BESS, the mathematical model for the AC side is established. A dual-loop control strategy based on feedforward decoupling is adopted to regulate grid-connected power. To improve the battery utilization in the energy storage system, a voltage equalizing control strategy is proposed. Proposed control strategies are verified by simulation models.

articleTitle: SOH Estimation of Energy Storage Batteries Based on ICA and Data-driven Fusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The assessment of the State of Health (SOH) plays a crucial role in diagnosing the condition of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, SOH estimation for large-capacity batteries commonly used in energy storage systems remains insufficiently explored, particularly under conditions of high charge-discharge rates and deep discharge depths. This study proposes a novel approach for estimating the SOH of large-capacity batteries by integrating multi-feature extraction with artificial intelligence techniques. Specifically, various health indicator (HI) sets reflecting reconstructed Incremental Capacity (IC) curve characteristics are extracted from the LIB charging curves. Subsequently, an artificial neural network-based method is introduced to fuse these HIs, enabling precise SOH estimation. The proposed methodology was validated through extensive long-term aging experiments on lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. The results demonstrate the significant advantages of the approach, including high estimation accuracy, reliability, and robustness against cell inconsistencies.

articleTitle: Study on Photovoltaic Uncertainty and Optimal Allocation of Energy Storage in Traction Power Supply System Considering Geographical Differences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale configuration and planning of traction power supply systems (TPSS) combining photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage, current research on PV uncertainty and PV storage capacity allocation needs to be based on large sample PV data. Influenced by geographic differences and climate extremes, it is difficult to converge the PV fluctuation range calculations with a small amount of sample data; in most regions, it is even more difficult to find geographically compatible sample data for capacity allocation planning for supercapacitors (SC). This challenges existing capacity allocation schemes and PV uncertainty resolution methods. In order to solve the PV uncertainty and capacity allocation problem when there is no PV sample data or only short-term sample data, a two-tier optimization model configuration based on PV prediction model is developed. The PSO algorithm embedded in the CPLEX solver is used to solve this optimization model. Finally, the economy and effectiveness of the model are verified by comparing the results with the existing schemes.

articleTitle: Research on the Method for Identifying Abnormal Behavior in the Power Market Using a Subjective and Objective Weighted Fuzzy Petri Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To tackle the difficulties in identifying and regulating manipulation in the electricity market due to growing transaction scales and diverse participants, a multi-level index system for abnormal behavior has been developed. This system includes an adaptive evaluation model that integrates a cloud model with ShuffnetV2 and a fuzzy Petri net, assigning subjective and objective weights. The model's effectiveness has been confirmed using transaction data from a province, offering a practical solution for monitoring abnormal activities in the power market.

articleTitle: The Design and Simulation of the Water Turbine Adjustment System Based on the Matlab
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Hydropower generation, with its fast and stable regulation characteristics, the function in the power grid is gradually changing from power generation to power system regulation, which leads to frequent adjustment of working conditions in the operation of the turbine, no longer being a single power generation function, but more for grid frequency and amplitude regulation. Therefore, the hydraulic turbine regulation control system is required to meet higher requirements. This paper takes the mixed-flow Hydro turbine as the research object and briefly analyzes the basic composition and principles of the turbine regulation system. On this basis, the mathematical model of each part of the hydro turbine governor is established. and the computer simulation model is built using the simulation software MATLAB/SIMULINK. Two models, linear simulation model and nonlinear simulation model, are built, and based on these two models, frequency disturbance experiments under no-load conditions and load disturbance experiments are conducted. The paper focuses on the influence of PID parameter changes on the stability and dynamic response of the regulation system under nonlinear model conditions, and the influence of parameters such as the inertia time constant of the unit and the inertia time constant of the water flow on the dynamic quality of the system, and after the completion of the experiment, the differences and reasons of the simulation results between the linear model and the nonlinear model under the same parameter conditions were compared and analyzed, as well as the influence of system dynamic characteristics such as turbine inertia time constant and water flow inertia time constant on the system dynamic quality. After completing the shed load experiment, the differences and reasons for the simulation results under the same parameter conditions between the linear model and nonlinear model are compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: A Two-Level Trading Strategy for Load Aggregators Considering Grid Flexibility Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the challenge of surging flexible demand and limited resources in power systems, a power market bidding mechanism has emerged as a crucial balancing solution. We have developed a two-tiered optimization framework that integrates load aggregators into the trading of demand-side flexibility resources. This model ensures power supply and new energy consumption while minimizing the cost of demand-side flexibility. The upper tier identifies the required flexibility, while the lower tier maximizes the aggregator's revenue by leveraging curtailable and transferable loads, participating in the power market's centralized bidding and clearing process. Simulations with grids heavily integrated with new energy sources demonstrate that our model not only meets flexibility demands but also enhances the profitability of load aggregators. Finally, based on the simulation analysis using grid data with a high proportion of new energy access, the results show that the proposed two-level optimization model can meet the demand for flexibility resources while increasing the revenue of the load aggregator.

articleTitle: Multi Spectral Detection Technology for Partial Discharge in Oil Based on SiPM Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Compared with conventional partial discharge (PD) detection methods, optical detection technology has a strong anti-interference ability and is more suitable for PD detection in oil-immersed equipment. Among them, silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) have high sensitivity and integration and have broad application prospects. However, existing research on the application of this technology in PD detection has only been conducted in gas-insulated equipment and has not yet been applied in the field of PD detection for oil-immersed equipment. Therefore, this article proposes a multi-spectral detection technology for PD in oil based on SiPM sensing. Firstly, conduct PD detection experiments in oil and compare the proposed technology with a high-frequency current transformer (HFCT). Secondly, considering different detection distances, explore the detection characteristics of SiPM. Finally, a large number of PD multispectral detection experiments in oil were conducted using SiPM sensors. The results indicate that the sensitivity of the SiPM sensor in detecting PD decreases with increasing distance. The number of PD signals in the 350nm~480nm band is much higher than in other visible spectral bands.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization of Power Supply and Demand Balance Considering the Impact of Coal Prices on Coal-Fired Power Generation Willingness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of the construction of new power systems, traditional researches mostly consider the impact of source and load uncertainties such as wind, solar, water, and load on operation risks, while ignoring the impact of coal prices. This work proposes a multi-objective optimization method for power supply and demand balance that considers the impact of coal prices on coal-fired power generation willingness. Firstly, indicators such as the cost factor and efficiency factor of coal-fired power generation are defined. And based on this, a method for constructing the willingness curve of coal-fired power generation is proposed. Furthermore, by combining the construction method of source and load scenario set considering the spatiotemporal correlation, the quantitative analysis of power supply risk is achieved. Then, a multi-objective optimization method for power supply and demand balance is proposed, considering expected daily operating costs, inter-region transmission electricity, and electricity shortage, as well as constraints such as coal-fired power generation willingness and equipment operation. Finally, the method is applied to the test system to analyze the impact of different coal prices on system operational economy, self-balancing degree, and operational risk.

articleTitle: Joint Maintenance Strategy For Urban Integrated Energy Systems Considering Distribution Network Reconfiguration Under Earthquake Disasters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Earthquake disasters could cause power outages and natural gas leaks in urban integrated energy systems, severely impacting residents' normal production and daily life. Enhancing the resilience of urban integrated energy systems can strengthen the system's ability to withstand earthquake disasters. In this paper, a joint maintenance strategy for urban integrated energy systems considering distribution network reconfiguration under earthquake disasters is proposed. The strategy analyzes the effects of distribution network topology reconfiguration on the integrated energy system, focusing on the chain reactions of faults between different subsystems. Case studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in load recovery through an urban integrated energy system composed of the IEEE-13 power system and a 7node natural gas system.

articleTitle: The Influence and Prediction of Carbon Emission Trading Policy on the Asset Efficiency of Enterprises in Power-related industries——Based on the RBF Neural Network Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In achieving the grand goal of carbon neutrality and carbon emission peak in China, carbon emission trading policy is one of the essential means to deal with climate change and promote the transformation of the low-carbon economy. It is also closely related to the efficiency of enterprise assets. In-depth analysis and prediction of the impact of carbon emissions trading policies on enterprise asset efficiency is of great significance for promoting enterprises' sustainable development and green economic transformation. This study is based on the relevant data of China's electric power related industry enterprises to conduct the above research. The results show that, on the one hand, carbon emissions trading policy has a substantial positive impact on improving the asset efficiency of enterprises in power-related industries. On the other hand, the trained RBF neural network model shows commendable prediction ability. These conclusions are of great significance to improving the asset efficiency of power related industry enterprises and realizing national low-carbon sustainable development goals under the background of double carbon.

articleTitle: Pattern Recognition of Partial Discharge using Acoustic Array Data Based on DCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Microphone arrays have the potential to detect partial discharge phenomena in electric equipment non-contact and flexibly. However, the existing methods do not fully consider the data characteristics of microphone arrays, and there is a paucity of research on the identification of local discharge types. to address the varying acoustic characteristics of different fault types, the microphone array data is initially processed to obtain the respective Mel spectrograms. Subsequently, the features are extracted using a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN), and the local discharge types are classified. Based on this approach, a local discharge type recognition model for acoustic array data is proposed, which is founded on the extraction of Mel spectrogram features.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Transmission Characteristics of ±500kV Metal-Enclosed DC Potential Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to obtain the transfer characteristic of DC potential transformer and improve the measurement accuracy, this paper takes the ±500kV metal-enclosed DC potential transformer as the research object and studies the changing rule of the transfer characteristic of ±500kV metal-enclosed DC potential transformer from typical aspects , such as production errors, stray parameters, ambient temperature, and output channel damage. The findings indicate that the errors in resistance production, ambient temperature variations, and the extent of output channel damage contribute to changes in resistance, which subsequently result in measurement errors for DC potential transformers. The relationship among these three factors and their impact on resistance change is as follows: output channel damage>ambient temperature>resistance production error. In the range of 18°C to 32°C, the temperature will not cause the measurement accuracy level of DC potential transformer to decrease. The stray capacitance mainly leads to the measuring error of AC voltage, that is, the measuring error of AC voltage increases about 0.4% when the stray capacitance increases by 5pF. The output channel mainly leads to the measurement error of direct flow, that is, as long as the output channel is damaged, the measurement result will not meet the standard requirements. When the resistance-capacitance matching relationship is destroyed and the system voltage changes, the DC voltage divider measurement results will have a short transition process, and the DC measurement error at the transition moment is seriously deviated from the normal value.

articleTitle: Optimal Control Method for ESS in Transformer Distribution Supply Zone Based on Adaptive Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the development of distributed new energy penetrates deeply into the distribution network, distribution transformer supply zone with high-proportion distributed new energy will face greater problems of power balance and stability. Aiming at the new energy consumption and short-time capacity shortage scenarios in the distribution transformer supply zone, this paper proposes an adaptive operation control method for energy storage system based on the characteristics of photovoltaic power generation and batteries, and verifies through demonstration that this method can take into account the consumption of new energy, preventing power flow reversal and alleviating short-term overload to improve system utilization.

articleTitle: Optimization of Liquid Cooling Double-layer Heatsink for SiC Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The proposal research aims to modify the new structure of the SiC MOSFET power module double-layer heatsink to perform the most appropriate thermal achievement. Liquid cooling has shown to be a better approach for regulating the heat created by the power module, giving increased thermal performance. This work focuses on the geometrical optimization of liquid cooling double-layer heat sinks using the Pareto front method to reduce thermal resistance and achieve an appropriate cooling coefficient of performance. The results reveal the thermal resistance reduction with the increase of geometrical parameters. With the expansion of wall thickness, pin fin diameter and pin fin height of the heat sink, the thermal resistance is reduced by 22.5 percent. At the same condition, optimization showed a decrease in the cooling coefficient of performance by 287.8 percent.

articleTitle: A Bi-Level Charging Station Planning Model Based on the Interaction of Load and Electricity Price
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A good EV charging station plan ensures that it covers the charging demands of the entire region while minimizing the cost. Taking the charging demand of 33 transport nodes in Sydney as reference, combined with local renewable energy parameters and storage battery technology, this paper proposes a Bi-level charging station planning model, which takes into account both transmission and distribution network, to plan the site selection of charging stations in these regions. The upper layer uses IEEE14 bus transmission grid model as the power supply system, and the lower layer uses IEEE33 bus distribution network to connect with the upper layer. The model uses locational marginal price as the power purchase price, constantly iterates the load and price according to the renewable energy of the site selection, forming an interactive iterative system. Finally, the most suitable 15 nodes are selected to build charging stations, and the feasibility is proved by power flow analysis.

articleTitle: A Review of Collaborative Optimization Strategies of Distribution Networks with Electric Vehicle Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the access of electric vehicles to the distribution network, it leads to a large penetration of EV loads with spatio-temporal two-dimensional randomness into the distribution network, which makes the weakness of the distribution network come to the fore gradually. The promotion and application of vehicle to grid technology are of great significance for the satisfaction of charging demand, the alleviation of pressure on distribution grid construction, the utilization of EV flexibility and consumption of new energy. In this paper, we systematically review the existing researches for collaborative optimization strategies of the distribution network taking into account the EVs from the aspects of EV orderly charging/discharging model construction, EV orderly regulation frameworks and application scenarios, and put forward the outlook from the refining the EV load charging/discharging model and demand response incentive mechanism.

articleTitle: Segmented Detection for Wideband Oscillations in Renewable Powered Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Wideband oscillation issues severely impact the secure and stable operation of modern power systems. To achieve rapid and accurate monitoring of wideband oscillations, which is critical for emergency control in practical engineering, a segmented detection method is proposed in this article. Based on requirements for the calculation accuracy and response speed of detecting wideband oscillation, this method analyses the upper and lower limits of the window length corresponding to several frequency components through simulation. Then, the scheme for dividing frequency bands and the appropriate window length for each band are derived. In this article, the traditional windowed discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and interpolation compensation are briefly reviewed, and quantitative indices for the calculation accuracy and response speed of the wideband oscillation detection are defined. The method for segmented detection is introduced in detail, and its effectiveness is verified through case studies.

articleTitle: A Coordinated Dispatch Method for Transmission and Distribution Networks with Multiple Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The energy transition has introduced a variety of small-capacity distributed energy resources (DER) to modern power systems. The concept of virtual power plant (VPP) has emerged as an effective approach to managing them. This paper considers the privacy of the VPP and proposes a hierarchical optimization dispatch method for multi-level power grids. The flexibility of the VPP is aggregated by using the bound shrinking method and its cost function is fitted with a quadratic function. Following this, the VPP is integrated into the system as a virtual generator, enabling it to coordinate with multi-level power grid scheduling. The coordinated economic dispatch (C-ED) of the transmission and distribution (T&D) network is achieved through a heterogeneous decomposition method (HGD).

articleTitle: A PV Hosting Capacity Evaluation Method Considering Source-Load Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Nowadays, owing to the excessive integration of photovoltaic (PV) in distribution network, the system is facing several security problems, thus, it is urgent to accurately evaluate the PV hosting capacity of the system. This paper proposes a PV hosting capacity evaluation method considering the scenario generation. The Gaussian mixture model and Copula theory are adopted in combine with the Monte Carlo sampling as well as the clustering method to generate the typical daily scenarios for the evaluation of the hosting capacity. Furthermore, a successive second-order cone programming (SOCP) method incorporating additional linearized constraints is proposed to reduce the relaxation gap result from the use of the SOCP method in PV hosting capacity problem and obtain the optimal solution of the original problem through multiple iterations. Simulations are performed on an IEEE-33 bus system integrated with PV systems to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A prediction method of relay protection defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: An improved logistic regression model applied to the prediction of relay protection defects is proposed. On the basis of the existing stepwise logistic regression model, by adding additional conditions restricting the training of the logistic regression model to fall into over fitting, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed to improve the existing stepwise regression gradient descent model parameter fitting method, which solves the problem that the multicollinearity characteristics between influencing factors can not be found by the existing indicators caused by the randomness of relay protection defects and insufficient data accuracy, and obtains the regression parameters that follow the reasonable influence direction of independent variables on dependent variables. So as to reasonably predict whether defects occur according to equipment information and provide support for equipment operation and maintenance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Adjustable Potential of Hotel Air Conditioning Load based on Limited Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Air conditioning load is the most important flexible resource for hotel building to participate in power grid supply and demand interaction. This paper proposes a method to evaluate the adjustable potential of air conditioning based on the total load data of hotel users and the air conditioning load data monitored separately during the peak hours of summer electricity consumption. First, electricity load characteristics is analyzed, and the correlation between air conditioning load and total load is obtained. Second, the hierarchical clustering method is applied to extract typical electricity consumption patterns. Finally, based on load clustering and load forecasting results, the adjustable potential of hotel air conditioning system is calculated, which provides a method for adjustable potential evaluation under limited data.

articleTitle: Assessment Method for Minimum Inertia Considering the Differences in Support Characteristics of Various Types of Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper addresses the assessment of minimum inertia demand in large-scale renewable energy systems, considering the dynamic safety constraints of system frequency and the response characteristics of various frequency regulation resources. It establishes frequency response models for different types of regulation resources under typical control methods, accurately representing their behaviors. Additionally, a minimum inertia demand assessment method is proposed, factoring in the initial rate of frequency change as a constraint. This approach effectively accounts for the impacts of renewable energy control elements and parameters, allowing for comprehensive quantification of minimum inertia requirements while ensuring the dynamic safety of system frequency. Validation through simulations.

articleTitle: Identification of Transformer Leakage Inductance Parameters Based on Dynamic Resistance of Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Winding deformation during the operation of power transformers leads to changes in winding leakage inductance, and in order to achieve more accurate on-line identification of leakage inductance parameters, a winding dynamic resistance dependent leakage inductance parameter identification method is proposed. Taking the transformer circuit equation as the reference identification model and the recursive least squares method with forgetting factor as the identification algorithm, a finite element simulation model is established to study the influencing factors of leakage inductance identification. The results show that the change in resistance value has a significant effect on the identification of leakage inductance after excluding disturbance factors such as load and power factor. Based on this, it is proposed to introduce the transformer oil temperature to reflect the dynamic resistance value of the windings, which effectively reduces the error and fluctuation of leakage inductance identification due to the change in resistance value. Finally, the effectiveness of the method in on-line identification of transformer winding deformation is verified by simulated deformation experiments of the winding.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Three-Level Conversion Scheme for Power Router based on ANPC Flexible Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power router (PR) is becoming an indispensable part of building energy Internet. However, due to the variety of power conversions in PR, it is difficult to unify the converters, which significantly limits the wide production and application of PR. Therefore, a reconfigurable three-level (3L) conversion scheme for PR based on active neutral-point clamped (ANPC) flexible modules is proposed in this paper. The 3L-ANPC can be used as DC/AC or AC/DC port in PR due to its superior harmonic performance and high efficiency. In addition, with the rich power switches in 3L-ANPC, it can be reconfigured as a 3L-buck/boost converter for the DC/DC port of PR. One side of the ANPC module is connected to the DC bus of PR, and the other side is connected to different sources or loads through a flexible switch. Various operation modes can be obtained by switching flexible switch and adopting different control strategies. Meanwhile, when a module fails, fault tolerance can be realized by accessing redundant modules. By using the proposed scheme, the utilization rate of hardware resources can be maximized under various conditions, thus greatly improving the flexibility and reliability of PR. Simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Fault line selection of distribution networks based on sparse coefficient Hamming distance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The small current grounding systems have weak ground fault characteristics when a high-impedance grounding fault occurs, making fault line selection a challenging task. To address this problem, a fault line selection method based on the combination of sparse representation and Hamming distance algorithm is proposed. The zero-sequence current of each feeder is decomposed using the sparse representation theory to obtain the sparse coefficient vector of zero-sequence current, the comparison reveals that the sparsity coefficient of the fault line is greater than that of the non-fault line. Then, using the Hamming distance algorithm, calculate the distance of sparse coefficients between the fault line and the non-fault line, and using the Hamming distance correlation coefficient to established a line selection criterion. Through MATLAB simulation, it was verified that the method of this paper is not affected by transition resistance, noise interference, fault location and has a high sensitivity.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Evaluation of Nuclear Power External Grid and Plant Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The development of power reliability research in China is relatively mature, but due to historical reasons, it started relatively late in the field of nuclear power plant electricity consumption. This paper is based on the actual electricity demand of a nuclear power plant in Fujian, China, and conducts reliability evaluation research on its external power grid and plant electricity. The research mainly includes four aspects: probabilistic evaluation of the reliability of the external power grid, evaluation of the reliability of the power plant's main connection, consideration of maintenance and accidents causing all connection lines between the external power system and the nuclear power plant to be unavailable, estimation of the failure rate and repair time caused by adverse weather conditions resulting in the simultaneous loss of the nuclear power plant's outgoing lines, Based on the principle of reliability assessment, the total failure rate and fault recovery time of the nuclear power plant are calculated and analyzed to be 9.23E-03 and 4.91E-01, respectively. Compared with the data from the United States, the reliability indicators have their own advantages and disadvantages. The main wiring failure rate in China is relatively high, which has reference value and guiding significance for engineering construction in China.

articleTitle: Influence of Initial Rotational Speed of Variable-Speed Pump Storage Units on the Hydraulic Interference for Fixed-Speed Units During Pump Power-Off
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Addressing the issue of hydraulic interference caused by variable-speed pumped storage units to individual units with a shared water delivery system, this study conducts numerical simulation research on fixed-variable speed pumped storage units with a shared water delivery system. It explores the patterns of hydraulic interference on fixed-speed units when the pump experience power-off at different initial rotational speeds. The results indicate that within the selected range of initial rotational speed variations (varies from 96% to 104%), the maximum spiral case pressure and the rate of draft tube inlet pressure decrease in the disturbed fixed-speed unit positively correlate with the initial rotational speeds of the variable-speed unit, while the minimum draft tube inlet pressure negatively correlates with it. When the initial rotational speed decreases from 104% to 96%, the input power setting time, overshoot, and amplitude variation rate of the disturbed unit decrease by 3.57 seconds, 6.65%, and 21.51%, respectively. The results demonstrate that the input power stability of the disturbed fixed-speed unit negatively correlates with the initial rotational speed of the disturbing variable-speed unit. The higher the initial rotational speed of the variable-speed unit, the more intense the flow rate and pressure changes. As the initial rotational speed of the variable-speed unit decreases, the stability of the disturbed unit improves.

articleTitle: The cooperative optimization strategy of fault recovery and emergency repair of distribution network after disaster is considered
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Extreme natural disasters can easily trigger large-scale failures in distribution networks, seriously threatening the safety and stability of power systems. To address such challenges, this paper proposes a fault recovery strategy to enhance the resilience of post-disaster distribution networks. First, a hybrid particle swarm optimization algorithm based on a dynamic adaptive mutation strategy (AVPSO) is used for fault reconfiguration. Then, breadth-first search is applied to achieve islanding operation for branches disconnected from the main grid, and combined with fault repair priorities, it aims to minimize network losses and optimize the power restoration process. Finally, simulations of various fault scenarios on the IEEE 69-bus system show that the hybrid particle swarm optimization algorithm significantly improves the fault recovery rate, validating the effectiveness of this strategy.

articleTitle: A novel micro individual behavior characterization method based on trajectory big data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The spatiotemporal trajectory of population is a key factor affecting energy consumption behaviors and levels. Mining micro individual behavior patterns based on trajectory data and finely depicting them is a reliable means of accurately and comprehensively characterizing the flexible energy use potential, spatiotemporal distribution, and response characteristics of the population. Aiming at the problem of insufficient representation of individual behavior by existing methods, a trajectory data hierarchical processing flow and a micro individual behavior representation method based on physical information constraints driven by trajectory big data are proposed. Firstly, due to the presence of a large amount of noise in trajectory data that reduces computational accuracy and redundant data that reduces computational efficiency, a hierarchical processing method for trajectory data is proposed to improve the quality of trajectory data; Secondly, build an OPTICS clustering model based on physical information constraints such as speed to achieve accurate identification of core stationary areas in both moving and stationary states. Finally, a case study was conducted on the Geolife Trajectory 1.3 dataset, and the results showed that the proposed method can achieve trajectory data cleaning. The average error of the processed trajectory data was 16.86 meters, and the trajectory data volume was compressed to 30% of the original data volume. At the same time, the proposed method accurately characterizes the multi temporal and spatial scale activity behavior of microscopic individuals: there are 9 core stationary regions, with the stationary state accounting for 42.6% of all trajectory data and the motion state accounting for 57.4%. This work provides a solid foundation for the analysis and identification of flexible energy consumption patterns.

articleTitle: Optimal Short-term Scheduling of Multiple Small-scale Hydropower Generators based on Water Inflow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The prediction of water inflow plays an vital role in the optimal operation of hydropower stations, and its accuracy is of great significance for the effectiveness of subsequent output distribution schemes. The short-term optimal scheduling is to arrange the day ahead generation plan of the power station and units under the premise of ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power grid, so as to improve the overall operation efficiency and comprehensive benefits of the hydropower stations. Based on the mined meteorological forecast data and forecast solar term data, this paper uses different neural networks to effectively predict the daily inflow of multiple units of XieCunYuan (XCY) cascade hydropower station system which is located in Songyang County, Lishui City, Zhejiang Province in the next 7 days. At the same time, the output distribution is carried out in combination with the turbine efficiency model constructed by PSO-BP and the short-term optimal scheduling model of "output determines water". Based on the operation data of XCY hydropower station in recent years, the proposed solution is evaluated experimentally. The experimental results show that Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) neural network has high accuracy in the prediction of water inflow, and the test set error is the lowest. The short-term optimal scheduling first optimizes the water inflow of the power station, and then optimizes the allocation of the water inflow of the units, which realizes the improvement of the total daily power generation and daily power generation revenue of the hydropower station.

articleTitle: Development of Loop Closure Current Calculation and Auxiliary Discrimination System for 10 kV Urban Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous development of society, people's demand for electricity is increasing, which leads to a greater demand for the service quality of power supply enterprises. The closed-loop power supply significantly enhances the reliability of the distribution network. The closed-loop operation of the power grid enables uninterrupted power supply, though it involves certain security risks. Currently, there is no reliable method with detailed criteria for determining closed-loop operations for distribution network dispatchers. Often, they rely on personal experience. Therefore, this paper begins with the calculation method for loop closure current, considering constraints like bearing capacity, and integrates theoretical analysis with power flow calculation to develop an auxiliary discrimination system for loop closure operations. In the "new generation of distribution automation master station system," real-time SCADA data acquisition allows the calculation and verification of impact and steady-state currents during loop closure operations, facilitating early warning analysis. Test results indicate that the system offers a theoretical basis and decision support for loop closure operations in 10 kV urban networks.

articleTitle: Investigation of Near-Fundamental-Frequency Oscillation in a Renewable Power Integrated System with MMC-HVDC Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Near-fundamental-frequency oscillations (NFFOs) have been observed in practical renewable power integrated system via MMC-HVDC, of which the mechanism is not fully revealed yet. Therefore, in this paper, potential dominant influencing factors of the NFFO are explored based on a general renewable power integrated system at first. Then the equivalent circuit model of the system is built. By calculating the total resistance, the physical mechanism of the NFFO is revealed.

Author Keywords: renewable power integrated system via MMC-HVDC

articleTitle: Dual-Objective Optimization of Integrated Energy System Dispatch with Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To improve the integrated energy efficiency of Integrated Energy Systems (IES), a multi-objective optimization model is proposed. First, the energy efficiency of the IES is analyzed across five stages: energy supply, conversion, transmission, storage, and demand. Then, a multi-objective optimization model for the electric-gas-heat-storage IES is established, with the objective functions of minimizing system economic costs and maximizing integrated energy efficiency. Furthermore, to address the non-convex objective function, a linearization transformation is applied, and the ε-constraint method is used to obtain the Pareto front. Finally, the case study is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model and approach.

articleTitle: Modeling and Characteristic Analysis of Building PV Array Under the Influence of Multiple Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Compared with conventional PV systems, building-integrated photovoltaic systems (BIPV) have more complex operating conditions, with more intricate influencing factors and constraints. A model of building PV arrays is built under multiple influencing factors, like partial shading, azimuth, tilt angle, and aging attenuation. Using a rooftop PV system as an example, the output characteristics of the PV array under the influence of multiple factors are analyzed through simulation.

articleTitle: Distributed Detection and Isolation of False Data Injection Attacks in Islanded AC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The problem of vulnerability of secondary control of AC microgrids to cyber-attack has received much attention. However, there is still no suitable method for detecting and localizing attacks in different locations. In this paper, a set of detection methods for the attack locations and attack methods of False Data Injection Attack (FDIA) is designed using Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) method based on the differences in power grid operation brought by FDIA in different locations. Combined with the trigger signal each neighboring node sends and the change in the set amount of features, the source of the attack can be confirmed and the attack can be detected and localized.
