Different from the measured data in the traditional power system, the data measured in the distribution power system with highly proportional renewable energy integration shows highly related with time and presents random and intermittent in one day, which brings the opportunity of false data injection attack (FDIA) by manipulating the measurement data in the power monitoring system that causing the no response or wrong response of power devices. In order to solve these challenges, many machine learning-based methods are proposed. However, the characteristics of these methods, such as precision, are different and present different potential applications in FDIA detection. In order to assess the performance of typical machine learning-based FDIA detection methods used in distribution power system with highly proportional renewable energy integration, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Autoencoder (AE) is analyzed and the decisive indexes, such as F1-score, precision and recall, are compared to show their potential application scenarios. The actual current data measured from a real distribution power system in northern of China is used for the FDIA methods comparison. The experiment results indicate that CNN and SVM outperformed RNN and AE in detecting FDIA, suggesting that they are better suited for time series data analysis in power system.

articleTitle: A New Electrical Distribution Systems Uniform Scale Model-ing Approach Based on Improved Empirical Modal Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The construction of New Electrical Distribution Systems is the key to achieve the goal of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality in China, which will bring great changes and challenges to the electric power industry. New electrical distribution systems, as an important part of new electrical distribution systems, the modeling and simulation of new electrical distribution systems need more accurate and efficient simulation methods to verify. Therefore, this paper proposes a unified scale modeling method for New Electrical Distribution Systems based on Improved empirical mode decomposition (IEMD) for the problems of inconsistency in time scale, high complexity, and lack of accuracy in the traditional modeling methods for electrical distribution systems. In this paper, we firstly analyze the operation characteristics of the New Electrical Distribution Systems, clarify the transformation mechanism of different time scales under the New Electrical Distribution Systems, and then construct the unified scale modeling framework of the New Electrical Distribution Systems; secondly, taking into account the different time scales, we use IEMD to decompose, transform and reorganize the signals of the different time scales, and then complete the unified scale modeling of the New Electrical Distribution Systems; Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified through the analysis of practical examples, which provides more effective theoretical and technical support for the subsequent stability analysis and control of New Electrical Distribution Systems.

articleTitle: Multiphysics-Coupled Stress Analysis of Hydrogen Storage Filling Using Diverse Composite Layer Winding Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Hydrogen storage technology, as one of the core technologies in the hydrogen energy industry chain, is directly related to the efficient utilization and safe transportation of hydrogen energy. Currently, existing literature overlooks the impact of the wrapping patterns of composite layers, which can cause hydrogen storage containers to exhibit different stress characteristics. In this paper, a Type III hydrogen storage tank model is established to analyze the flow field during the filling process, obtaining the internal pressure load distribution. Subsequently, three different wrapping patterns are modeled to comparatively analyze the stress conditions of the hydrogen storage tank under these patterns. Case studies based on ANSYS reveal that when the wrapping angle tends more towards 90° or 0°, the stress conditions on the composite layers tend to be more extreme, while the stress conditions on the inner liner improve, resulting in a higher maximum stress. This trend gradually diminishes from the inner layers to the outer layers. Moreover, the stress distribution in each layer is related to the wrapping direction of that layer, i.e., the fiber direction, and the position of the layer within the stack, and is almost unaffected by other layers.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Energy Internet with VPP and Energy Distributor under Master-Slave Game
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the reform of the electricity market, the coupling relationship between sources and loads has gradually transformed into a complex competitive structure in which sources and loads interact with each other. The change of energy price will change the usage of load side, and the load usage will in turn affect the energy price. In order to better study the interaction between sources and loads, this paper introduces an energy distributor between the virtual power plant (VPP) and the user group, whose pricing strategy, which is higher than the feed-in tariff and lower than the time-of-use tariff, makes the energy distributor the first choice for the VPP to sell and the user group to buy. First, the revenues of the energy distributor and the VPP are modeled separately with the user groups' spending on purchasing energy as the objective function. Second, the game relationship between the revenues of energy distributors and VPPs and the spending of user groups is analyzed, and the Stackelberg game model is proposed to prove the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium solution. Finally, the solution is carried out on Matlab by combining heuristic algorithm and solver. The results show that the game model proposed in this paper can not only effectively weigh the interests of energy distributors, VPPs and user groups, but also realize the win-win situation of energy distributors, VPPs and user groups, and provide an effective solution for comprehensive energy utilization.

articleTitle: Chance-Constrained Dispatch of Suburban Railway Smart Grids Considering EVs Charging Behaviors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Integration of park and ride (P&R) systems with electrified railways has been demonstrated to effectively reduce traffic congestion and the usage of private vehicles. To reduce operation costs and carbon emissions, this paper investigates suburban railway smart grids (SRSGs) incorporated electric vehicle (EV) charging management and railway energy dispatch. A stochastic optimization model is established, in which EV charging power flow scheduling and the charging/discharging strategies of ultracapacitors (UC) are scheduled. Meanwhile, the uncertainties of EV charging behaviours, such as arrival and departure times and initial states of charge, are captured by chance-constrained programming. The effectiveness of the power flow dispatch approach is demonstrated by the numerical simulation, it is shown that the proposed stochastic dispatch approach can reduce the overall cost by up to 10%.

articleTitle: Coordinated Cyber Attack on Coupled Power and Transportation Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing adoption of electric vehicles, the deepening coupling between transportation network (TN) and power network (PN) allows cyber attacks to propagate across networks, posing a significant threat to the stable operation of such coupled power-transportation network (CPTN). This paper proposes an innovative coordinated cyber attack strategy, where the attacker not only implements load redistribution attacks within the PN but also manipulates traffic demand data to simulate similar demand redistribution attacks in the TN. We first establishe a mathematical model of the CPTN, detailing the coupling mechanism, and then formulate the coordinated cyber attack problem as a bilevel nonlinear optimization problem. The upper-level model simulates the attacker's strategy, aiming to maximize the operation costs of the CPTN, while the lower-level model represents the system's scheduling response, seeking to minimize operation costs. To solve this complex bilevel model, the study applies the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions to transform it into a single-level optimization problem and uses the big-M method and piecewise linearization to handle nonlinear constraints, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed cyber attack strategy significantly increases system operation costs, revealing the serious threat it poses to secure and economic network operations.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Leaning-based Data Driven Method for Fast Solution of Stability Constrained Optimal Power Flow in Isolated Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: An increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources has introduced significant uncertainties and instability issues into microgrids. To rapidly and economically respond to the changes in isolated microgrids operating state, this manuscript introduces a deep reinforcement leaning (DRL)-based data-driven approach for quickly solving the stability-constrained optimal power flow (SC-OPF) in microgrids. The method in question frames the SC-OPF as a task of constraint adherence within the training regimen of a DRL agent, with the agent’s action-value function being enhanced by the incorporation of small signal stability constraints. Numerical evaluations were conducted on modified IEEE 33-bus systems. The outcomes demonstrate that the proposed agent is capable of swiftly (in real-time) securing high-quality SC-OPF solutions that adhere to stability constraints.

articleTitle: LMDI-ARIMA Model for Carbon Emissions Analysis and Prediction in High Energy Consuming Industries with Emission Reduction Measures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, starting from the specific perspective of enterprises, the carbon emission calculation model is first used to calculate and organize the carbon emission data of three typical high energy consuming industries. Secondly, the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition analysis method is used to calculate the contribution of fossil fuels in the carbon emissions of enterprise fuel combustion. After comparison, it is found that steel enterprises are most affected by this factor. At the same time, time series analysis is used to predict the future carbon emissions of different enterprises by Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model. Finally, with the help of the established LMDI-ARIMA model, hypothetical adjustments were made to the proportion of fossil fuels in steel enterprises and carbon emissions predictions were made, obtaining the expected carbon reduction that the steel industry can achieve by changing the proportion of clean energy use.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability in Three-Phase Unbalanced Networks: A Pseudo-Measurement Modeling Based Dynamic State Estimation Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of distributed generation (DG) units, such as photovoltaic systems, poses significant challenges for state estimation and voltage stability analysis in unbalanced three-phase distribution networks. Traditional state estimation methods are often limited by the lack of real-time measurements and the unbalanced nature of distribution networks. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dynamic state estimation framework that utilizes pseudo-measurements derived from a Back Propagation (BP) neural network. The framework is applied to the IEEE 37-node test system, where it performs state estimation at 15-minute intervals over a 24-hour period. The results indicate that nodes close to the DG injection point experience the highest voltage fluctuations, highlighting the impact of DG variability on voltage stability in unbalanced networks. Additionally, the voltage at all nodes tends to peak at specific times following the integration of photovoltaic generation. This study provides valuable insights into the influence of DG variability on voltage stability and demonstrates the effectiveness of using data-driven pseudo-measurements for state estimation in unbalanced distribution networks.

articleTitle: A Nash-Stackelberg Game-Based Peer-to-Peer Joint Energy and Carbon Market Among Local Prosumers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading among emerging prosumers with considerable renewables is a promising pathway to facilitate the low-carbon operation of the distribution network. Influenced by sharing economy principles, carbon allowances, which are the commodity of prosumers, can be traded under the P2P framework integrating with the energy market. This paper proposes to establish a P2P joint energy and carbon market among local prosumers. A Nash-Stackelberg game model is constructed to analyze the interaction characteristics among energy sellers and buyers. The competition in pricing among the sellers can be modeled as a generalized Nash equilibrium problem and the price-demand interaction between energy sellers and energy buyers can be described as a Stackelberg game. The proposed solution method replaces the lower-level model with its optimality condition. The best response algorithm is employed to solve the market equilibrium. Case studies show the effectiveness of the proposed market model in increasing social welfare and reducing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Real-time Regional Auxiliary Service Market Trading Strategies under High Renewable Energy Penetration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The development of regional auxiliary service market (RASM) has allowed neighboring provinces in the same area to provide each other with supports in terms of peak-shaving and reserve capacities, which could greatly promote the system flexibility. This paper introduces the practice of RASM in northwestern region of China and proposes a data-driven trading strategies model for provincial electricity companies who act as the RASM participants. The objective of this model is to maximize the renewable energy utilization rate while reducing the purchase cost of peak-shaving capacities by rolling optimization of the offers/bids and prices in real-time scale. A human experience embedded proximal policy algorithm is adopted to solve the model. Numerical case studies adapted from real-world data proves the advantage of the proposed method and shows the potential of RASM in promoting the integration of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Remote Wind-Storage Power Plants Using Wasserstein-Based Distributionally Robust Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The geographic mismatch between renewable energy generation and consumption centers necessitates long-distance power transmission, introducing complexities in planning and operation. This study addresses the planning of wind-storage hybrid power plants (WSPPs) in remote areas, considering the uncertainty of wind power and the fixed capacity of long-distance transmission lines. This paper develops a two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model with a Wasserstein metric to optimize WSPP investment under risk. The model is simplified into a linear programming problem by deriving a Lipschitz constant, facilitating practical application. The research offers a framework for balancing investment return and risk in the context of renewable energy integration, accounting for stakeholder interactions. The effectiveness of DRO is verified, and the planning results are compared with those of its stochastic and robust counterparts.

articleTitle: Real-Time Simulation Method for Security and Stability Control System Based on Actual Device Code Encapsulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the incorporation of massive heterogeneous control resources on the power supply side and the load side of the new power system into stability control, the traditional hardware in-loop real-time simulation method of the power grid security and stability control system (hereinafter referred to as the "stability control system") cannot adapt to the growing scale of the stability control system and the strong coupling of the action characteristics of multiple stability control systems. Therefore, a real-time simulation method of the security and stability control system based on the actual stability control device code encapsulation is proposed. By adopting code-level transplantation and actual device code encapsulation dynamic link library and other means, the mirror real-time simulation operation of the onsite stability control device software on a general-purpose computer is realized; a visual virtual operation environment of the stability control system is developed, a high-speed field programmable gate array(FPGA) interface for simulating master-slave communication is developed , and a callback function mechanism for simulating inter -station communication is proposed , realizing the full-function virtual operation and simulation of the stability control system; finally, the simulation effect comparison and verification is carried out in combination with the actual stability control system.

articleTitle: Rolling Optimization for VPP in Spot or Ancillary Service Markets Based on Deep Learning Forecasts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for Virtual Power Plant (VPP) participation in spot and ancillary service markets, integrating deep learning-based forecasting with rolling optimization strategies. The proposed approach combines Transformer-GRU hybrid architecture for renewable energy forecasting and LSTM networks for electricity price prediction, achieving forecast accuracies exceeding 96%. A three-stage optimization framework is developed: day-ahead forecast declaration, intra-day rolling optimization, and intra-day dispatch order optimization. The rolling optimization strategy maximizes VPP profitability by coordinating various distributed energy resources, including renewable generation, energy storage systems, and flexible loads. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach improves VPP profitability by 16.25% compared to non-optimized operations, while maintaining rapid response capabilities to grid dispatch orders within 0.1 seconds. The results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enhancing both economic performance and operational efficiency of VPPs in modern electricity markets.

articleTitle: Short-term prediction of PV power by coupling QPSO-LSTM and improved mechanism modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The intermittency and stochasticity of solar energy leads to the strong uncertainty of its output. In the context of carbon neutrality, the photovoltaic (PV) power forecast has become the key technical bottleneck restricting its rapid deployment and connection with the power grid. This paper proposes a combination forecasting model for short-term PV power by coupling data-driven and mechanism modeling methods to improve the accuracy and reliability of PV power prediction. First, based on historical data, QPSO-LSTM and improved mechanism prediction model are established, respectively. Secondly, the minimum error sum method and entropy weight method are used to determine the weight of a single prediction model, and the combined prediction model is constructed. Thirdly, the cumulative prediction error and root mean square error are used as indicators to compare the accuracy and reliability of different prediction models. Finally, a photovoltaic power station in Zhangjiakou is taken as a case study. The results show that the combination forecasting model can effectively improve the accuracy.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Control of Photovoltaic Grid-Connected Inverters Based on Unfolding Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents a reactive power control technique for photovoltaic grid-connected inverters utilizing an unfolding inverter topology. Traditional grid-frequency unfolding inverters and certain DC/DC circuits with unidirectional energy transfer paths face challenges in effectively injecting reactive power into the grid. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a novel method that adjusts the output current waveform, enabling reactive power injection without requiring modifications to the inverter circuit structure. The proposed technique outperforms conventional methods by reducing total harmonic distortion and expanding the power factor adjustment range, making it suitable for a wide range of grid-connected inverters based on the unfolding inverter configuration. Additionally, the operating principles are thoroughly explained, accompanied by a comprehensive mathematical derivation of the grid current reference waveform. The effectiveness and feasibility of this approach are verified through theoretical analysis and detailed simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on the Calculation Method of Arc Sag in Overhead Transmission Lines under Wildfire Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: When wildfires occur under overhead power lines, the high temperatures caused by the fire increase the sag of the lines, decreasing the safe distance between the lines and the ground, and increasing the likelihood of power line trips due to wildfires. Existing methods for calculating line sag under wildfire conditions consider too few factors, making it difficult to accurately assess the degree of line sag under wildfire conditions. Based on the theory of fire burning zone division, this paper establishes a multi-physical field heat transfer model for wildfires, calculates and studies the effects of wildfire burning area, burning temperature, height above the ground, and horizontal distance from the center of wildfire burning on the spatial temperature distribution, and constructs a wildfire temperature distribution function model. Finally, combining the wildfire temperature distribution function with the principles of mass conservation and isothermal expansion, a method for calculating line sag is proposed. Taking a span of 200 meters as an example, the influence of the line's distance from the center of wildfire burning, height above the ground, temperature at the base of the fire, and burning area on the maximum sag of the line is analyzed. The results show that when wildfires occur directly under transmission lines and burn intensely, the higher the burning temperature and the larger the burning area, the lower the line height, the corresponding high temperatures will significantly increase the maximum sag of the line, reducing the ground clearance of the line. Even at distances more than 100 meters from the center of the wildfire, the high temperatures can also slightly increase the line sag.

articleTitle: An End-to-end Prediction Method for Energy Storage System Arbitrage with Battery Degradation Costs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy storage system (ESS) can achieve arbitrage by charging at low electricity prices and discharging at high prices, thus electricity price prediction is important in ESS arbitrage optimization problem. Traditional methods follow "Predict then Optimize" framework, which divides prediction and optimization into two independent processes and focuses on prediction accuracy. However, these methods ignore the inconsistency between prediction error and decision error, and a lower average prediction error may not necessarily generate a better decision. In addition, the battery will suffer degradation during ESS operation, which needs to be considered in arbitrage process. To achieve better modeling of ESS arbitrage and further improve arbitrage benefits, this paper realizes an end-to-end closed-loop method for ESS arbitrage considering battery degradation costs. The electricity price model and ESS arbitrage optimization model are built and simplified to fit into the end-to-end prediction framework. Then the prediction and optimization stages are combined to form a complete closed-loop algorithm. Finally, the proposed method is evaluated by an experiment on a real electricity price dataset, and the results show an enhancement in ESS arbitrage benefit.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning for PV-EV Integrated Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Due to the high volatility of photovoltaic energy and the flexible consumption characteristics of electric vehicles (EVs), the integration of EVs and photovoltaic systems into the existing grid presents both opportunities and challenges. This paper proposes a new two-layer integrated energy management framework to solve the difficulty of priority consumption of photovoltaic energy and improve the economic benefits of the power system. The framework optimizes power procurement and EV charging scheduling through a two-layer reinforcement learning approach. The first layer uses a deep Q-network (DQN) to make power purchasing decisions, giving priority to self-produced photovoltaic power and obtaining additional grid power only when necessary; The second layer uses a multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) approach with multiple DQN to manage service pricing and charging plans for various EV users. In addition, the weighted aggregation approach combines multiple Q values into a single policy to balance different user needs. Experimental results show that the framework significantly reduces operating costs, improves the efficiency of energy procurement and EV charging programs, and provides substantial economic incentives for renewable energy adoption and more efficient energy management.

articleTitle: Estimating Behind-the-Meter Storage Capacity: A Data-Driven Approach Facing Time-of-Use Pricing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the deployment of distributed generators accelerates, the newly installed capacity of behind-the-meter (BTM) storage installations has experienced a significant upsurge. The energy storage economy gains momentum further catalyzing this trend. Nevertheless, the majority of BTM storage systems function autonomously from public utilities, primarily serving as private assets for energy arbitrage, thereby presenting regulatory challenges for the grid operators. The literature has endeavored to tackle these challenges, with a predominant focus on operational strategies. However, the inference of storage capacities to obtain direct insights remains relatively unexplored. This study aims to bridge this research gap by devising a data-driven methodology for estimating storage capacity, with a particular focus on the Time-of-Use pricing schemes commonly utilized by small-scale BTM storage systems. Additionally, the grid operators may face challenges in obtaining sufficient data for estimation. To this end, we examine the theoretical minimum sample size necessary for accurate capacity estimation. Our comprehensive evaluation validates the efficacy of the proposed approach and elucidates the associated complexities of sample size.

articleTitle: Traffic Modeling of Typical Key Power Grid Information Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, information systems are increasingly applied in critical sectors like power grids. The traffic characteristics of these systems significantly impact their performance, stability, and security, making it vital to understand and model these characteristics as a key area of research for system performance. Traffic modeling not only reveals traffic patterns but also helps identify performance bottlenecks and security risks. This paper aims to analyze the traffic characteristics of typical power grid information systems, summarize various traffic modeling methods, outline their applicable scenarios and strengths and weaknesses, and evaluate their effectiveness to enhance the performance and reliability of power grid information systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multi-Objective Electric Vehicle Charging and Discharging Scheduling Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The rapid expansion of electric vehicles (EVs) challenges charging and discharging scheduling. This paper introduces a multi-objective EV scheduling method using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). We build an optimization model considering user satisfaction, grid load fluctuation, and renewable energy integration. Using Q-learning and Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithms, simulations based on Japanese travel data show that when renewable energy integration is prioritized, EVs tend to swap batteries more, increasing renewable energy matching by over 200% with DQN. Compared to Q-learning, DQN offers better renewable energy matching and lower user costs. This study offers valuable insights into multi-objective EV scheduling, aiding renewable energy integration and grid stability.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network Reinforcement Learning Based Coordinated Charging Optimization of Multiple Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing number of electric vehicles (EVs) and the widespread establishment of EV charging stations (EVCSs), the grid faces significant challenges, drawing attention to the system’s economy and safety. To reduce charging costs while ensuring safety and meeting user demands, we have established a coordinated optimization charging scheduling system for multiple EVCSs based on graph neural network reinforcement learning. The scheduling problem is modeled as a markov decision process, and EVCS decisions are solved using multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO), with the final charging and discharging plan generated based on the urgency of user demand. A graph attention network (GAT) is introduced to extract coupling information between EVCSs, enhancing the feature representation of reinforcement learning and improving the accuracy of system scheduling. Experimental results show that this method achieves greater cost reductions while ensuring the safe operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Fault response strategy for high proportion distributed energy resources distribution area based on whale optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The proportion of distributed energy resources in the distribution area is increasing, and its output is uncertain. Therefore, considering the uncertainty, a fault recovery strategy combining island division and recovery and reconstruction is proposed. Firstly, a distributed energy resources output model and a load characteristic model are established, and a combination of breadth-first traversal and depth-first traversal is used to divide the islands according to the faults occurring at different time periods. Then, the network reconstruction model is established with the goal of minimum switching operation times and minimum network loss, and the improved whale optimization algorithm is used to solve it, and the residual power loss load in the distribution area is restored. Finally, the simulation analysis of IEEE33 nodes is carried out, and the experimental results show that the proposed method can restore power supply quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: A Review of the Reinforcement Learning for Wind Farm Operation and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapidly increasing penetration of wind power in power systems, large-scale wind farm control faces not only the cooperation among heterogeneous wind turbines, but also connections to grids, which complicate the control process. Recently, optimization and model predictive control have effectively handled the complexity of wind farm control. However, the above methods rely heavily on accurate system models, making it difficult to describe uncertainties in wind farms through models. Reinforcement learning (RL) is considered an ideal algorithm for handling uncertainties and dynamics in environments, because RL can learn optimal strategies without prior knowledge of models by interactions with the environment. Giving a comprehensive review of RL applications in wind farm control is essential for advancing intelligent control technologies and providing valuable references for academia and industry. This paper first introduces model-free RL algorithms and then reviews RL applications in wind farm control, covering advancements in layout optimization, power maximization, fatigue load minimization, and power reference tracking. Finally, it discusses future developments, aiming to provide comprehensive guidance on RL technology for wind farm control.

articleTitle: MEF-YOLOv8-Based Foreign Object Detection Method in Transmission Lines Under Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The steady operation of transmission lines is crucial for maintaining the stability of power systems. Addressing the issue of low accuracy in identifying common foreign objects such as nests, garbage, kites, and balloons on transmission lines under sophisticated environments, this paper presents a MEF-YOLOv8 model based on the YOLOv8n baseline. Firstly, the Mosaic-9 data augmentation method is adopted at the input stage of the training phase to improve the network's generalization capability. Secondly, the Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA) module is integrated into the backbone of the YOLOv8 network enabling pixel-level attention in feature maps and enhancing the model's ability to capture feature information of foreign objects of different scales. Lastly, to boost the accuracy of foreign object detection in intricate environments, the Focal-EIOU loss function has been introduced to supersede the initial CIOU loss function. The empirical findings indicate that the proposed approach has achieved a 99% mPA@0.5 score in identifying typical foreign bodies on transmission lines, representing a 4.9% enhancement compared to the original YOLOv8 algorithm.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation Method for Grid-Side Hybrid Energy Storage Considering Bidding and Operation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the hybrid electricity trading mode where the market mode coexists with the planned mode, the different allocation of resources for various types of energy storage power stations (ESSs) such as pumped storage station (PSSs), electrochemical storage station (ECS), and hydrogen storage station (HSS), can lead to different bidding and operation strategies. The power grid and various ESSs achieve bidding and operational strategy interaction in a hybrid trading mode through resource allocation. A series of models and the resource allocation method are proposed to solve the strategic interaction problem. Firstly, based on the market clearing model, a electricity and capacity market model involving multiple ESSs is constructed. Based on the goal of maximizing the revenue of each ESS, the formation of ESSs market trading strategies is described. Secondly, by combining the two-part electricity pricing system, a power grid scheduling model is constructed. This model can effectively describe the trading process of different trading modes and the operational characteristics of different ESSs. Thirdly, according to the Stackelberg game model and strong duality theory, an interactive model of bidding and operation strategies between the power grid and various ESSs is proposed, which combines the market transaction model with the unified purchase and sale process. Finally, based on the ESS construction and operation data in eastern China, the effectiveness of the model and method is verified, and the bidding and operation strategies interaction between the power grid and various ESSs is demonstrated. The results indicate that under the dominance of the power grid, by utilizing the resource allocation method, the optimized strategies for resource allocation and operation can be derived, which can reduce the operating costs of the power grid with the conditions of high renewable energy consumption rate.

articleTitle: Application Prospect of New Power System Based on Generative Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AIGC) is an artificial intelligence technology based on generative models, which has powerful capabilities to process and generate video, text, audio, and other content, and can understand and generate interactive information of multimodal complex content. This article focuses on the construction needs of new power systems. Firstly, it introduces the basic principle architecture, underlying models, and application advantages of AIGC. Secondly, based on this, it summarizes the application principles and implementation process of AIGC in four major scenarios: power system prediction, new power system analysis and planning, fault diagnosis and recovery, and power trading assistance. Compared with traditional artificial intelligence technology, it has significant advantages in small sample and multimodal task processing. Finally, the article proposes six solutions from the perspectives of dataset, computing power, and algorithm, taking into account the risks faced in the application of AIGC. These solutions provide a reference for promoting the practical application of AIGC in the power system.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Physics-Informed Gaussian Process Regression Under Multi-Phase Degradation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The widespread adoption of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles and energy storage systems has made accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction increasingly critical for system reliability and maintenance planning. This paper presents a novel physics-informed Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) framework for battery RUL prediction, specifically addressing the challenges of multi-phase degradation patterns. The proposed approach integrates a physics-informed mean function with an adaptive cross-scale kernel structure to enable robust prediction across different degradation phases. The framework combines a phase-aware mean function that explicitly models transition behaviors, an adaptive kernel design for temporal dependencies, and a covariance modulation mechanism that automatically adapts to local degradation characteristics. Experimental validation on both NASA and TOYOTA battery datasets demonstrates the framework's effectiveness across diverse aging patterns. Experimental validation demonstrates the framework's effectiveness across diverse aging patterns, achieving RMSE reductions of up to 75% on the TOYOTA dataset compared to traditional GPR approaches, while maintaining robust regeneration tracking capabilities on the NASA dataset despite its complex capacity fluctuations.

articleTitle: An Optimal Operation Control Method Considering Multiple Operating States Of New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To realize the absorption of distribution generators and electric vehicles, the traditional power system needs to be transformed into a new power system with flexible regulation and control capabilities. AC/DC hybrid power grid (ADHPG) based on flexible DC technology will be an important part of the new power system in the future. In this paper, the optimal operation strategy is proposed for the three operating states of ADHPG, and build different optimization models for various operational scenarios . The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively enhance the operational efficiency of the new power system.

articleTitle: Review of Technical Analysis and Application Status of Hydrogen Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of "dual carbon" goal, the development of hydrogen energy storage technology is helpful to slow down carbon emissions and promote the large-scale utilization of renewable energy. Through in-depth summary of the development status of hydrogen and hydrogen energy, key technologies of hydrogen energy storage system and their application status, three hydrogen production methods including wind power hydrogen production, photoelectric hydrogen production and electrolytic water hydrogen production are analyzed. Four hydrogen storage methods, including high pressure gaseous hydrogen storage, low temperature liquid hydrogen storage, metallic organic hydrogen storage and organic liquid hydrogen storage, and hydrogen power generation technology, and the application status of hydrogen storage system in renewable energy, natural gas, hydrogen fuel cells, and clean utilization of fossil energy are described, in order to provide reference for related research in the field of hydrogen energy storage.

articleTitle: Research on Regulation Capacity Mining and Regulation Technology of Park Considering Multi-Form Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, in the case of vigorously building new energy systems in China, the insufficient absorption capacity of regional power grids has become increasingly prominent. In order to alleviate this phenomenon, this paper studies the scheduling capacity estimation and mining methods of large-scale integrated energy parks, and the benefit interaction mechanism between park users and regional distribution networks. Based on the economic dispatching of the park under the framework of time-of-price, an estimation method of the dispatchability of the integrated energy system based on energy path tracking is proposed to obtain the conservative evaluation of the dispatchability of the integrated energy system. Then, a simplified model of the efficiency function of the integrated energy park is established, and an interaction method between the distribution network and the integrated energy park is formed. On this basis, a Stackelberg game model of "distribution network and park" is established. An improved differential evolution algorithm is proposed to optimize and solve the problem, and the equilibrium solution of the distribution network’s electricity price to the park is obtained.

articleTitle: Exploring Federated Learning for Energy Consumption Forecasting in Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing deployment of smart meters in homes, there is a growing need to enhance privacy in the management of energy consumption data. This paper investigates the application of Federated Learning (FL) as a decentralised approach to energy consumption prediction. Unlike centralised models that require the collection of data from multiple house-holds, FL preserves privacy by keeping data localised while aggregating learning parameters across households. Utilising the "Smart Meters in London" dataset, we compare the performance of locally trained Long Short-Term Memory models, a FL model, and a centralised model using all data from each household. To better reflect real-world applications, we adopt a sliding window approach to training, which requires fewer rounds of communication and only one model update per iteration, in contrast to traditional FL methods that involve multiple training rounds within each iteration. Contrary to expectation, our results show that the FL model outperforms both the local and centralised models in terms of prediction accuracy and generalisation. The study highlights the advantages of FL in balancing privacy with predictive performance, providing insights into its practical implementation in smart home energy management. These results provide valuable guidance for energy companies and stakeholders seeking to adopt FL approaches, particularly in scenarios where both privacy and accurate prediction are required.

articleTitle: Research on the Responsiveness of Residential Electricity Users to the Electricity Accumulation Points Strategy Based on Data Mining and Profiling Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This study constructs a selective ensemble clustering model based on evidence reasoning, following a comprehensive evaluation of various clustering methods. The model is tested using electricity consumption data from residential users in a provincial capital city to ensure the accuracy of the analysis results. Based on this data, a comprehensive system of segmentation indicators for residential electricity consumption behavior is established, covering multiple dimensions such as basic user information, general statistics, and behavioral information. The analysis explores various factors, including electricity consumption, long-term fluctuation trends, seasonal patterns, fluctuation stability, tiered factors, peak-valley differences, and changes in accumulation points. By analyzing the characteristics of residential electricity consumption groups in the city, the study develops detailed profiling for different user groups. Based on the profiling analysis, an application is proposed to assess the responsiveness of different residential user groups to the electricity accumulation points strategy. Effective and reliable differentiated recommendations are provided.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fault Ride-through Control Parameters of Renewable Energy Generators for Frequency Stability Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing integration of power electronic devices, transient frequency stability has become a prominent challenge in power systems. Although the low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control of renewable energy generators (REGs) supports voltage stability, it can negatively impact system frequency stability. Specifically, during fault and post-fault recovery periods, REGs can exacerbate low-frequency issues in the receiving end of a hybrid AC-DC power system due to the reactive power priority setting in their LVRT control strategy. A sudden drop in transient frequency may trigger unnecessary emergency control actions, posing a serious threat to system stability. To address this issue, this paper proposes an optimization method for the LVRT control parameters of REGs in receiving-end systems. The approach begins by establishing the quasi-steady-state model of the system immediately after the fault. By linearizing this nonlinear algebraic model, we derive the sensitivity of REGs’ control parameters with respect to the total unbalanced power of the system. Based on this sensitivity, the LVRT control parameters of REGs are optimized using a gradient descent algorithm. The proposed method is validated on the CSEE-VS test system, showing an improvement in the system frequency nadir from 48.5 Hz to 49.6 Hz, thereby preventing load shedding that could lead to cascading failures and blackouts.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Power Prediction of Photovoltaic based on CNN-AM-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The power of photovoltaic power generation is affected by a variety of factors such as weather, radiation and temperature, exhibit a high degree of randomness and uncertainty. To address this problem, this paper proposes a ultra-short-term photovoltaic power prediction model based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and attention mechanism and bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM). Firstly, Pearson's correlation coefficient was used to filter out the meteorological factors which have significant influence on the historical power. Subsequently, in order to capture the spatial features of the input data, a convolutional neural network is utilized for feature extraction and an attention mechanism is introduced to strengthen the model's ability to discriminate key features. Meanwhile, the Bi-LSTM network is utilized to capture the temporal dependencies in the time series data, and finally the PV power prediction value is obtained. Finally, the validation is based on data from actual PV power plants, and the results show that the proposed Convolutional Neural Networks and attention mechanism (CA) and Bi-LSTM Ultra-short-term PV power prediction model outperforms the single model in terms of prediction accuracy, reflecting the effectiveness and superiority of the hybrid model.

Author Keywords: Bidirectional Long and Short-Term Memory Networks

articleTitle: Real-time Crew Scheduling for Post-Disaster Restoration of Integrated Power and Gas Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Urban energy systems face increasing challenges in maintaining reliable operation during extreme events. Most existing restoration models assume complete information, which is unrealistic under real-world uncertainties like unpredictable repair times. Effective restoration strategies should enable quick decisions and can dynamically adapt to uncertain environments and leverage real-time information efficiently. This paper proposes an online restoration strategy for integrated electricity and gas distribution systems (IEGDS), focusing on repair crew dispatch under uncertainty. Using a Markov decision process (MDP) framework, the method dynamically adjusts restoration actions based on real-time system states. A rollout algorithm is proposed to estimate the Q-function of candidate actions through Monte Carlo simulations, enabling online decision-making without relying on model training or complex mathematical programming. Tested on a 13-bus power system and a 7-node natural gas system, the proposed algorithm achieves performance comparable to offline optimization methods while demonstrating high efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch of Hydropower Plants Considering the Vibration Zone of the Unit and Price-Guided Pumped Storage Hydropower Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy and large load fluctuations, the intraday net load curve fluctuates sharply, which brings a heavy burden to power dispatching. As flexible resources that can be adjusted quickly, hydropower plants and pumped storage hydropower plants (PSH) have great advantages in regulating the peak-valley difference and reducing the climbing demand of traditional thermal power units. However, due to the existence of the vibration zone of the hydropower unit, the stable generating interval is discontinuous, and the pumped storage unit is difficult to model to adapt to various practical conditions due to too many restrictions on actual operation. Therefore, this paper studies the method of continuous power regulation formed by the combination of hydropower unit groups from the actual situation, and carries out a detailed modeling of the PSH. Finally, a case study is carried out to prove the effectiveness of the proposed model and improve the system's absorption ability.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Accelerating Unit Commitment Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Unit commitment (UC) is a critical issue in the optimal scheduling of power systems. As the number of units increases, the scale of the problem expands rapidly, making it a significant challenge to solve the UC problem quickly. This paper addresses the inefficiency of UC model solving by innovatively combining power systems with Graph Neural Networks and Reinforcement Learning. First, a Markov decision chain model is established for the unit commitment problem. Then, an Edge-Conditioned Convolution Network - Long Short-Term Memory - Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (ECT-TD3) model is constructed to quickly obtain an initial solution for the unit commitment problem. Finally, a feasibility recovery verification is performed, followed by the use of a solver to obtain the final solution rapidly. System case studies conducted on data generated from real-world load scenario characteristics demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively accelerates the solution of the UC problem, increasing the solving speed by about three times.

articleTitle: Scenario Generation of Annual PV and Load Correlated Time Series Considering Meteorological Influences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: An accurate annual photovoltaic (PV) and load time series is essential for the assessment of PV accommodation capacity. This paper proposes a scenario generation model for annual correlated time series of PV output and load, incorporating meteorological factors. First, weather types are classified based on the clearness index and solar irradiance fluctuation indicators, and daily PV output time series models are constructed for different weather types. Second, based on load decomposition, temperature-sensitive load components are analyzed in terms of temperature characteristics, and a daily load time series model is developed based on temperature characteristic coefficients. Next, a joint probability distribution model of meteorological factors, based on the clearness index and temperature, is constructed using Copula function. On the basis of a weather-type Markov chain, an annual meteorological scenario is generated, considering meteorological correlations, and corresponding annual PV and load time series are produced. Case study results demonstrate that the series generated by the proposed model accurately simulate the statistical and temporal characteristics of PV output and load, while correctly capturing the correlation between the series.

articleTitle: Multi-population Cooperative Evolutionary Algorithm for Electric Vehicles and Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the issues of significant renewable energy output fluctuations and high electric vehicles (EVs) user benefits in the coordinated scheduling of EVs and renewable energy systems, this paper proposes an innovative multi-objective coordinated scheduling algorithm aimed at simultaneously reducing the impact of renewable energy output fluctuations on the grid and accelerating the adoption of EVs. To achieve these objectives, a multi-objective scheduling model has been developed that integrates EVs, wind power, and photovoltaic systems. This model includes key constraints such as battery storage capacity, charging and discharging power limits, and charging/discharging cycle constraints. To solve this model, this paper proposes a constraint multi-objective evolutionary optimization algorithm based on multi-population collaboration(MCEA), which incorporates the ϵ method for handling constraints within the algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved algorithm shows significant advantages in mitigating renewable energy output fluctuations and enhancing EV user benefits.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Information Physical Fusion in New Distribution Systems Based on Unified Formal Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Information-physical fusion of distribution network refers to: in the process of coupling the physical system and information system of distribution network CPS with each other, using the communication network as the transmission medium, the physical network system and the information system form a series of coupling events with close, complex and diverse interdependence. The new distribution system information-physical fusion modeling and simulation helps to improve the efficiency and accuracy of distribution system modeling, solves the problems of information dispersion and difficult integration of physics and information in traditional modeling, and is of great significance for improving the reliability, safety and efficiency of distribution systems. In this paper, a new information-physical fusion modeling and simulation method of distribution system based on unified formal matrix is proposed, which analyzes the information-physical fusion characteristics of the new distribution network, and considers the information-physical multi-flow fusion process at the same time, and finally completes the information-physical system simulation modeling of distribution network based on the unified formal matrix method of the information-physical fusion model of the new distribution network. Through the analysis of actual cases, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified, which can provide more effective theoretical and technical support for the optimal operation and management of distribution network information-physical system.

articleTitle: Statistically Feasible Mixed-Integer Programming for Integrated Energy System Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Integrated energy systems coordinate multiple energy flows to enhance energy efficiency and reduce costs. However, the uncertain and volatile availability of emerging renewable energy generation poses significant challenges to traditional scheduling paradigms of integrated energy systems. To address this issue, we propose a robust sample-driven approach to ensure the statistical feasibility of operational constraints – a notion that is mild conservative and requires no prior knowledge of randomness. We formulate the scheduling problem of an integrated energy system as a statistically feasible mixed-integer program with discrete control characteristics of combined heat and power. To handle the non-linearities from chance constraints, we use shape learning and shape calibration to construct an uncertainty set with a statistical feasibility guarantee. The approach finally employs Benders decomposition to handle the resulting deterministic linear model, offering a rigorous solution to scheduling an integrated energy system under vast uncertainty. We validate our analysis through extensive numerical studies.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Scene Generation via Self-Attention Augmented Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the gradual spread of renewable energy sources such as photovoltaics, accurate modeling of PV output with uncertainty becomes critical. As a key method to solve this challenge, scenario generation has received a lot of attention. This paper studies the application of generation model based on generative adversarial network (GAN) and its improved version WGAN-GP in generating renewable energy power scenarios. In order to deal with the complexity of dynamic weather and nonlinear power conversion, self-attention mechanism is introduced to improve the ability of the model to capture long-distance dependencies, and enhance the modeling ability of the generator and discriminator. Through experiments, the model shows a good generation effect, can efficiently capture the complex characteristics of renewable energy output, and provides reliable data support for probabilistic prediction and risk assessment of power system. The experimental results show that the model has high diversity and authenticity in the generation of photovoltaic power generation scenes, demonstrating its potential and effectiveness in practical applications.

articleTitle: Typical Key Technologies and Application Analysis in the Field of Integrated Energy Services
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of accelerating global energy transformation and the goal of " double carbon, " to meet the diversified energy production and consumption needs of terminal customers and improve energy efficiency, integrated energy services have emerged as the times require, becoming a typical representative of multi-technology integration and having a profound impact on the field of traditional energy services. This paper focuses on the core technology of integrated energy services and elaborates on the practical application scenarios and successful cases of the four technologies of air conditioning system optimization control, power monitoring and power response, intelligent building management, and energy-saving services in integrated energy services. On this basis, the paper further looks forward to the application prospect and development trend of integrated energy services in the future.

articleTitle: An ADP-Based Optimal Control Strategy for Virtual Synchronous Generators towards "Dual Carbon" Goals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of achieving "dual carbon" goals, enhancing grid frequency stability is crucial to ensuring the efficient utilization of clean energy. This paper proposes an event-triggered optimal control strategy for Virtual Synchronous Generators (VSG) based on adaptive dynamic programming (ADP), aimed at improving frequency stability in AC microgrids to facilitate the integration and optimal use of renewable energy. Unlike traditional model-dependent algorithms, this approach utilizes a model-free algorithm that achieves optimal frequency control through event triggering, thereby reducing communication and computational burdens. The frequency dynamics are modeled as nonlinear state-space equations, with the inverse of inertia as the control input. An optimized cost function that considers angle deviation, frequency deviation, Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF), and control cost is used to effectively balance energy control and frequency deviation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed optimal control strategy significantly improves frequency response under load disturbances while maintaining effective DC-side energy management, providing technical support for green, low-carbon grid operation.

articleTitle: Research on the DC Power Supply Mode Under Safe Voltage for Civil Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing of DC links in civil buildings, the advantage of low-voltage DC power supply systems over traditional AC forms is more significant. However, currently, there is no unified standard for the power supply voltage and mode of low-voltage DC. To consider both electrical safety and power supply capacity, this paper first analyzes the dangerousness of different DC voltage levels in civil scenarios. Further, combined with civil building scenarios, the requirement of power supply capacity for DC voltage levels is discussed, and then a range of DC voltage levels which can simultaneously satisfy safety and power demand is proposed. Finally, based on the obtained determination principle of voltage level, a reasonable power supply scheme is constructed for typical residential building scenarios, which verifies the feasibility of DC power supply with the safe voltage in civil buildings.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Prediction Regions of Wind Power for Robust Economic Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The dramatic increase in non-dispatchable wind power generation poses a significant challenge to power system operations. In this context, probabilistic forecasting becomes increasingly crucial for power systems, as it quantifies the uncertainty of volatile energy sources and supports various decisionmaking processes. This paper proposes a novel nonparametric probabilistic forecasting-based robust economic dispatch (NPF-RED) paradigm aimed at enhancing power system reliability and efficiency. The proposed NPF-RED methodology captures probabilistic information regarding uncertainties by evaluating the feature similarity between prediction targets and historical observations. A minimum volume uncertainty set in the form of multidimensional prediction regions (MPRs) based on similar samples is constructed using similar samples and optimized as a mixed integer programming (MIP). The proposed MPRs serve as inputs of subsequential operation decisions, which can maintain solution robustness while reducing conservativeness simultaneously. Comprehensive experiments conducted on IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus test systems using actual wind power data demonstrate that at a similar risk level, the NPF-RED approach effectively reduces the total cost by 2.56% and 0.50% in the 14-bus and 118-bus systems, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Bidding Strategies for Load Aggregators Considering Multiple Risks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to delve into the optimization of bidding strategies for load aggregators in the face of multiple risks. Initially, the study establishes resource aggregation models and subsequently analyzes the sources of revenue and cost for load aggregators when they participate in day-ahead main energy market bidding, thereby deriving the net profit value for these entities. Following this, the paper takes into account the relevant operational constraints associated with distributed photovoltaics, distributed wind power, adjustable load aggregation bodies, and energy storage devices. Considering the net profit of load aggregators in the day-ahead main energy market is susceptible to various uncertain factors, the paper proposes a Worst-Case Conditional Value at Risk (WCVaR) model that incorporates multiple risks. Ultimately, a case study analysis is performed to ascertain the bidding strategies for load aggregators in the day-ahead main energy market under diverse scenarios. Additionally, the WCVaR model, developed under conditions of multiple risks, is subjected to a sensitivity analysis to validate its feasibility and effectiveness as a decision-making tool.

articleTitle: Network Partition-Based Multi-Timescale Coordinated Voltage Regulation of Distribution Networks with High-Penetration Distributed PVs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Large scale integration of distributed photovoltaics (DPVs) into distribution networks is leading to issues of reverse power flow and voltage rise, which challenges the secure operation of distribution systems. This article focuses on the multi-timescale coordinated voltage regulation of distribution networks with large-scale DPVs and energy storage units. A comprehensive index that includes electrical distance, voltage autonomy, and comprehensive correlation index is established to partition the whole network into several independent regions, which can facilitate coordinated voltage regulation. On top of that, a multi-timescale coordinated distributed voltage control scheme is proposed by integrating the ADMM algorithm and global sensitivity-based fast voltage control approach. The ADMM is employed to coordinate different regions on a longer timescale in a distributed manner, while the global sensitivity-based fully distributed voltage control is used to achieve fast control of devices within a single region. Case studies on a modified IEEE 33-bus test system verify that the proposed voltage control scheme can coordinate multiple regions to achieve optimal voltage regulation and is able to mitigate voltage violations caused by fluctuations in DPV generation.

articleTitle: Impact of Time Synchronization Attacks on State Estimation of Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The time synchronization attack on the Micro Phasor Measurement Units of the distribution networks causes the measurement data error of operation. In this paper, the mechanism of time synchronization attack of a Micro Phasor Measurement Unit is analyzed. According to the influenced measurement data and state estimation method, the effects of time synchronization attacks on state estimation of unbalanced distribution network are studied. Then, considering the effect of bad data, the deviation of state estimation caused by attacks and the range of time synchronization attacks are established. Finally, a power equipment time synchronization attack platform is set up, and a 14-node distribution networks with the three-phase unbalance topology is established for simulation analysis. The results indicate that a time synchronization attack can evade Bad Data Detection and successfully impact the state estimation values of the entire distribution system by tampering with the Pulse Per Second timing of Micro Phasor Measurement Units, thereby posing a threat to system security.

articleTitle: Coordinated Planning of Electricity Lines and Energy Storage Systems Based on Time Series Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The coordinated planning of long-term and short- term energy storage systems is significant to enhance the regulation capability of power systems. However, it’s difficult to balance the time scale and time resolution in the solving process. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a coordinated planning method of electricity lines and energy storage systems based on time series aggregation. Specifically, the electricity line and long- term and short-term energy storage systems are all taken into consideration. Firstly, the yearly long-term operation model is simplified and approximated based on time series aggregation. The optimal number of clusters every month is identified based on the elbow method and the silhouette method. It composes a reconstructed time series. Then, A coordinated planning model for electricity lines and energy storage systems is established. Finally, the planning method is carried out by taking a typical provincial power system in the east of China as an example. The results show that the collaborative planning of long-term, short-term energy storage systems and electricity lines can be solved effectively and strike a balance between the time scale and time resolution. It also improves the new energy utilization and economy.

articleTitle: Multi-time Scale Low-Carbon Optimal Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants Considering Stepped Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to improve energy utilization efficiency and achieve low-carbon emissions, a multi-time scale optimal scheduling method for virtual power plants in a low-carbon environment has been proposed. Firstly, this paper constructs a virtual power plant containing CCPP-P2G-HFC (Carbon capture power plant, power to gas and hydrogen fuel cell), establishes the mathematical model of CCPP-P2G-HFC, and introduces the stepped carbon trading mechanism. Then, based on the multi-time scale regulation and control architecture of virtual power plants, a multi-time scale scheduling method with the objective functions of minimizing the operating cost and carbon trading cost is put forward. The analysis results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the operating cost of virtual power plants while cutting down carbon emissions, thus realizing the coordinated optimization of economy and low-carbon.

articleTitle: Cost Allocation Method Of Auxiliary Service Considering Environmental Value Of Green Energy Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous advancement of green energy transformation and the accelerated development of the green power consumption market, how green electricity transactions can be integrated into the traditional electricity market has become a research hotspot. This paper establishes a market clearing model for electricity that considers green electricity transactions and calculates the indirect carbon emissions between nodes using a carbon flow tracking method. The environmental value of green electricity transaction is represented by the carbon emission reduction coefficient. Additionally, a cost allocation method for ancillary services that takes into account the carbon emission reduction coefficient is proposed. The results of the case analysis indicate that green electricity transactions can effectively reduce the indirect carbon emissions of load nodes, demonstrating significant environmental benefits. The proposed cost allocation method for ancillary services, which considers the carbon emission reduction coefficient, can effectively alleviate the pressure on green electricity units in sharing ancillary service costs, thereby promoting the consumption of green electricity and the development of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Computational Modeling and Solution Methods for power Flow in Multilevel Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Based on the basic structure of transmission and distribution network, this chapter analyzes the output characteristics of dispatchable resources such as renewable energy, conventional generator set, interruptible load and energy storage device in detail, and establishes the basic model of each dispatchable resource participating in grid dispatching. A global model for the calculation of power flow of transmission and distribution collaboration is established. When calculating power flow of transmission network, the equivalent load of distribution network is processed as constant value; when power flow calculation of distribution network is required, the power grid is often processed as equivalent voltage source [1]-[2]. After the distributed power is injected into the distribution system, the distributed model is used to describe the transmission and distribution cooperative system, and the global power flow is calculated by alternating iteration between the transmission and distribution system. Finally, two kinds of solving algorithms are analyzed through a numerical example to verify that when the distributed power supply is connected to the distribution network, the appropriate A-node serial number is selected, which makes the power flow calculation convergence performance of the transmission and distribution collaborative system better, effectively meets the power flow calculation requirements of the transmission and distribution network in practical applications, and provides theoretical and model basis for the subsequent research on the collaborative optimization of transmission and distribution network.

articleTitle: Short-term Power Prediction of Wind Power Cluster Based on KOA-PLE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the gradual acceleration of the world's energy transformation, the construction of new energy is becoming more and more large-scale. At the same time, the proportion of new energy in the power grid is increasing, and the high volatility of wind power poses certain challenges to the stability and reliability of the power system. Therefore, accurate large-scale wind power prediction is very necessary. This paper presents a multi-task learning predicting method for wind power clusters. Firstly, the wind power cluster is divided into subgroups with similar output characteristics, and then the different subgroup power is used to predict the multi-task targets. Meanwhile, the Kepler optimization algorithm (KOA) is used to optimize the model parameters. When the method is applied to a wind power cluster in China, RMSE and MAE are reduced by 2.07% and 1.92% compared with the traditional multi-task learning method, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Transformer Approach to Identifying False Data Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The smart grid is vulnerable to multiple cyberattacks, with false data injection attacks (FDIA) being particularly concerning, as they can evade conventional bad data detection (BDD) systems and disrupt power grid operations. Given the nonlinear nature of state estimation and grid data, along with the temporal continuity of state data, this study introduces a Transformer-based model for detecting FDIA. It utilizes the Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT) to capture precise time-frequency characteristics from power system time-series data. These features are input into the Transformer, where multi-head attention captures long-range dependencies and improves recognition of complex grid patterns. The application of this technique on the IEEE 14-bus system demonstrates its capability to effectively recognize abnormal patterns with high accuracy. In addition, a basic sensitivity analysis of the control parameters was undertaken.
