articleTitle: Real-time Bidding and Dispatch Strategies for Electric Vehicle Aggregator in Joint Energy and Reserve Markets Considering EV User’s Preference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we propose real-time bidding and dispatch strategies for an electric vehicle aggregator (EVA) in joint energy-reserve markets, considering the preferences of EV users in offering flexibility. First, a real-time EVA bidding model in joint markets is formulated, integrating the quantification and pricing of the EV users’ flexibility contribution. The stochastic model predictive control technique (sMPC) is employed to solve the bidding problem online and address the uncertainties from the electricity markets and the EV users. Second, based on minimizing flexibility compensation and power re-adjustment costs, we propose a power dispatch protocol that ensures a profitable and feasible allocation. Numerical results verified the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Study on Optimal Scheduling of Industrial Parks Considering Fire Extinguishing Reserve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the small degree of participation of industrial enterprises in the field of new energy consumption, the problem of poor returns, while taking into account the industrial park fire standby load, this paper puts forward a comprehensive scheduling strategy for the participation of industrial loads in the wind and light energy consumption. Firstly, we construct the production process constraint structure of magnesium industry and analyse the composition of fire fighting loads; then we analyse the composition and time distribution of each type of loads in the park, and determine the load scheduling method; finally, through the data of industrial loads ‘working hours, energy storage capacity, and the time distribution of wind and light, we put forward the multi-objective optimization method considering the cost of regulating and fire fighting loads’ standby, and achieve the reasonable allocation of each dispatch resource in each time period. The results show that this method can provide scheduling economic benefits for industrial enterprise operation under the premise of ensuring sufficient fire load backup in the park, effectively improving the comprehensive economic benefits of industrial enterprises and the comprehensive consumption rate of new energy, which has good engineering value in actual projects.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Optimization of Energy Internet System for Low-Carbon Parks Accounting for V2G and Dynamic Electricity Tariffs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The low-carbon park energy internet (PEI) system utilizes various renewable energy sources and efficient energy utilization technologies to integrate multiple forms of energy, thereby reducing reliance on fossil fuels. This approach aims to achieve low carbon emissions, improve energy efficiency, and promote sustainable development. However, the existing energy market mechanisms may struggle to meet the demands of low-carbon parks, particularly in terms of renewable energy trading and subsidies, necessitating new market models for support. Moreover, the success of low-carbon parks heavily relies on active participation and collaboration from users; however, users’ awareness and acceptance of low-carbon technologies may impact their willingness to engage. Additionally, the tight supply of electricity resources affects the normal operation of the system. This paper addresses the trading mechanisms and optimization issues of the low-carbon PEI system, focusing on day-ahead optimization that accounts for vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interactions and dynamic electricity tariffs. It analyzes the economically driven electric vehicle (EV)-PEI interaction, constructs a V2G trading mechanism based on dynamic pricing, and considers constraints such as energy conservation, energy storage, and EV limitations. A model of the low-carbon PEI system is established, taking into account dual uncertainties of source and load, and solved using the CPLEX solver. The results indicate that the proposed method effectively reduces carbon emissions, minimizes the energy gap, and lowers the total cost of the system.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch for Power Systems Amidst Typhoon Events
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Enhancing the resilience of power systems against the threats posed by typhoon events has become increasingly critical. Evaluating the potential damage to specific transmission lines prior to a typhoon’s arrival and implementing targeted reinforcement measures, along with achieving optimal economic dispatch during the typhoon, are essential challenges that must be addressed. To tackle these issues, this paper presents a novel economic dispatch strategy tailored for typhoon scenarios. This strategy utilizes Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to construct a power generation model for wind farms under typhoon scenarios and evaluates the power line fault conditions in the system at various time intervals during these scenarios. Furthermore, it incorporates an economic dispatch model that operates post-fault to schedule the power output of generation resources at different times. Finally, the efficacy of this strategy is demonstrated through an enhanced IEEE 14-node case study, showcasing its significant potential for improving the system’s adaptability to typhoon-related challenges.

articleTitle: Research on Investment and Construction Strategies for Grid-Side Energy Storage Based on Multi-Scenario Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy storage, as a flexible resource, plays a supporting role in multiple scenarios on the grid side. Based on the theory of externalities, a comprehensive review of the application scenarios of energy storage on the grid side is conducted. A full evaluation cycle cost model for grid-side energy storage is constructed, and a specific case analysis is carried out to explore scenarios suitable for constructing energy storage on the grid side, with the aim of providing a reference for power grid companies to invest in and construct energy storage.

articleTitle: Decentralized Low-carbon Economic Dispatching Model for Distribution Networks Considering Source-grid-load-storage Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Coordinated operation of source-grid-load-storage (SGLS) is crucial for improving the operational performance of the active distribution network (ADN). Concurrently, with the expansion of interconnection networks, the traditional centralized optimization method faces challenges. This paper thus proposes a novel decentralized coordinated low-carbon economic dispatching strategy for soft open point (SOP)-based multiregional ADNs by local model decoupling. By using the analytical target cascading (ATC) method, the original centralized optimization model is divided into several subproblems, in which the local problems of SOP and ADNs are solved in the upper-level and lower-level of hierarchy, respectively. With after, to improve the computational efficiency, a diagonal quadratic approximation is introduced to ATC, i.e., DATC, enabling all local problems are solved in a fully parallel manner. Then, a better initial value of DATC is obtained to conduct the procedure with hot start mode. Such improvements significantly accelerate the iterative process of decentralized model. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated using a modified IEEE 123-bus interconnection system.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Comparison of Long Duration Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Ever-increasing penetration of intermittent solar PV and wind power in power system requires more flexibility to address volatility. Long duration energy storage(LDES) plays an important role in this aspect. This paper surveys and summarizes the state-of-art and on-going development for main LDES technologies, including pumped hydro storage(PHS), compressed air energy storage (CAES), redox flow battery (RFB), hydrogen storage and so on. By collecting investment data of dozens of real-world storage projects in China and relevant documents, this paper investigates the levelized cost of storage (LCOS) for 4 hours, 6 hours, 8 hours 12 hours duration LDES solutions in 2024, 2030, 2045 and 2060. Techno-economic comparison is thus provided. The results show that LCOS ranking varies in different scenarios and LDES should be chosen accordingly.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Driving Force and Mechanism of the New Type Power System Industry Transformation: based on Socio-technological Transformation Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Based on the social technology transformation theory, this paper extracts the four factors that drive the New Type Power System, namely, policy, ecology, technology and market, and forms a "dynamic analysis model for the development and transformation of the new power system industry". The research shows that the staggered influence of the four elements and the transformation power brought by them have promoted the industrial transformation.

articleTitle: Characteristics and Prospects of the New Power System in the Western Inner Mongolia Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of global climate change, this study analyzes the characteristics of the Western Inner Mongolia power system in terms of being clean and low-carbon, safe and controllable, flexible and efficient, intelligent and friendly, and open and interactive, in line with the national dual carbon goals. In response to the flexibility demands brought about by the high proportion of renewable energy integration, this research examines the challenges faced by current flexible resources across four aspects: generation, grid, load, and storage. Based on the development objectives of the Western Inner Mongolia power system in areas such as renewable energy development, promotion of new energy storage, grid structure construction, layout of transmission corridors, and institutional reform, a new modeling approach for power system planning is proposed using power balance theory and the MESSAGEix modeling framework. The results indicate that the Western Inner Mongolia power system will significantly enhance the installed capacity of wind and solar energy, while gradually decreasing the capacity of coal-fired power. Additionally, the scale of electrochemical storage and pumped hydro storage will see significant growth. This study provides theoretical support and practical guidance for the low-carbon transformation of the power system in the Western Inner Mongolia region and even nationwide, which is of great significance for achieving the dual carbon goals.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Prediction of Solar Power Generation in Various Provinces of China
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This study pioneers a forecasting model for solar power generation tailored specifically for the provinces of China, employing a multi-modal data fusion strategy. Diverging from conventional models that rely solely on single-source data, this approach integrates a diverse array of data types including time-series power generation, stock market prices, and textual information from policy documents. This integration enhances the predictive capabilities of our model by leveraging the unique information provided by each data type. We propose a novel approach called Multi-modal Information Fusion (Multiformer), which utilizes an encoder-decoder architecture augmented with a self-attention layer to effectively capture and synthesize the interdependencies among the varied data inputs. This architectural innovation significantly reduces error propagation and improves model accuracy. Empirical validation of our model was conducted through monthly forecasts of solar power generation across various provinces, revealing that Multiformer outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, including ITransformer and Informer, with a substantial 35% improvement in performance for a six-month forecast period. The success of Multiformer underscores its potential to generate accurate predictions that are crucial for energy policy-making and strategic planning.

articleTitle: A quantum-classical hybrid optimization method for restoration of active distribution networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper establishes an optimal restoration model for active distribution networks to rapidly recover from extreme weather events. The optimal restoration problem is defined as a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model, which is non-deterministic polynomial hard (NP-hard). This paper proposes a quantum-classical hybrid optimization method to solve this model. First, the optimal restoration model is split into a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) subproblem and a second-order cone programming (SOCP) subproblem, wherein the MILP subproblem is converted to a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. A decentralized optimization architecture based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is then developed, where quantum computing is used to solve the MILP subproblem (i.e., the QUBO model), and classical computing is employed to solve the SOCP subproblem. Numerical simulations validate that the proposed hybrid optimization method fully leverages the advantages of quantum computing for integer problems and classical computing for continuous problems.

articleTitle: A Distributed Resource Aggregator Pricing Strategy and Energy Optimization of Consumers Considering Thermal Inertia of Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy generations and distribution flexible resources, the aggregator will play an increasingly important role in power management of urban distribution networks. This paper proposes a bilevel optimization model of the aggregator and users' Stackelberg game considering thermal inertia of buildings. The objective of the upper level is to maximize the aggregator's benefit based on the distribution flexible resources operating strategies given by the lower levels and pricing strategies for the customers in the urban grids. The lower level of the proposed model is to minimize electricity cost by optimizing the power consumption strategy of the electric thermal storages. To address the nonlinearity of the proposed model, the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) condition is applied to convert the proposed model into a mixed integer linear programming model to solve. Finally, an urban grid in Jilin Province is taken as an example to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: Wind-Storage Cooperative Frequency Control Strategy Based on Wind Turbine Frequency Regulation Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As renewable energy, particularly wind power, continues to make up a larger share of power generation, the variability and intermittency of these sources pose significant challenges to maintaining grid frequency stability. Traditional methods of frequency regulation struggle to adapt to the fluctuating output of wind turbine generators (WTG), which can lead to inefficiencies and increased mechanical wear on equipment. This paper addresses these issues by proposing a novel cooperative control strategy for frequency regulation based on a combined wind-storage system model. The proposed strategy maximizes the frequency regulation potential of wind power while ensuring that the battery energy storage system (BESS) seamlessly takes over frequency regulation responsibilities during periods of low wind power output. This approach follows relevant national standards and provides a more flexible, efficient solution for handling the dynamic nature of renewable energy. Simulation results under varying load conditions demonstrate the superiority of this method over conventional approaches. The strategy effectively stabilizes grid frequency, reduces mechanical stress on WTG, and optimizes BESS utilization. Overall, this cooperative control strategy offers a robust solution for enhancing the stability of power systems with a high penetration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Research on Electricity Price Volatility Risk Modeling and Early Warning Considering Market Supply-Demand Equilibrium Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper conducts an in-depth study on the modeling and early warning of electricity price volatility risk in the electricity market. Firstly, by analyzing the current state of electricity price forecasting research both domestically and internationally, the paper identifies the limitations of existing methods and highlights the necessity for research on electricity price volatility risk modeling and early warning that considers market supply-demand equilibrium forecasting. The article provides a detailed introduction to the three main steps of electricity price forecasting: denoising of electricity price data, construction of electricity price models, and solution of electricity price models. On this basis, the importance of electricity price forecasting in a certain electricity market is discussed, and the internal and external factors affecting electricity prices are analyzed. The paper focuses on the application of ARIMA and SARIMAX models in monthly electricity price forecasting and compares the forecasting performance of these two models. Furthermore, this paper proposes two methods for analyzing electricity price volatility based on the characteristics of electricity price distribution and electricity price volatility risk indicators, and constructs corresponding early warning schemes. Finally, through case analysis, the effectiveness of the proposed models and methods is verified. The research in this paper provides scientific basis for electricity price risk early warning for electricity market participants, which helps to optimize resource allocation and improve economic benefits.

articleTitle: Zero- and Low-Carbon Energy Transition Policy System for Industrial Parks under Dual Carbon Goals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying global climate change, China has put forward the "dual carbon" goal, that is, striving to achieve carbon peak by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. As a concentrated area of economic activities, the energy consumption and carbon emissions of industrial parks occupy an important position in the country, and their low-carbon transformation is of key significance to achieve the "dual carbon" goal. This study systematically discusses the background, current situation analysis, transition path and policy research of the low-carbon transition of the park, and provides a comprehensive theoretical basis and policy suggestions for the low-carbon transition of the park. This study proposes a variety of low-carbon transition pathways, including supply-side pathways, demand-side pathways, integrated energy system pathways, and full life cycle pathways. The supply-side pathway focuses on optimizing the structure of energy production and supply, and promoting the development of renewable energy sources such as solar, wind and hydropower. The demand-side path focuses on improving energy efficiency, promoting energy-saving equipment, promoting energy-saving equipment and clean energy vehicles, and reducing energy consumption in the industrial and building sectors. In terms of integrated energy systems, the study emphasizes the integrated use of multiple renewable energy sources to improve energy efficiency through smart grids and energy storage technologies. In addition, a full life cycle management path from carbon screening, carbon planning, carbon construction, carbon optimization to carbon trading is proposed, which comprehensively covers all aspects of carbon emissions in the park.

articleTitle: Static Security Analysis Method Considering Source-Load Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The high proportion of uncertain source-load will infiltrate multiple uncertainties into the novel power system, and traditional deterministic static security analysis cannot meet this challenge. It is urgent to propose a static security analysis method that can consider multiple uncertainties in the power grid to effectively handle the uncertainty of the power grid. Therefore, this article proposes a static security analysis method based on probabilistic power flow. Firstly, this method uses polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) instead of Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) to calculate the probability power flow of a single scenario. Then, partial refactorization method, reuse of core data, and parallel computing strategies are proposed to accelerate the probability power flow considering the expected fault scenario. Finally, a complete static security analysis process based on probability power flow is proposed; In addition, a multi uncertainty simulation dataset was established that comprehensively considers wind power, photovoltaics, loads, and their correlations. Combined with the multi uncertainty dataset and the standard IEEE-39 node system, a calculation example was established to verify that the method proposed in this paper can quickly and accurately solve the probability density function of the voltage of each node in the power grid under various expected fault scenarios. The proposed method has significant advantages over traditional deterministic static security analysis methods.

articleTitle: A two-layer optimization method with distributed energy stations based on demand response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Considering the cleanliness characteristics of distributed energy under dual-carbon background, this paper proposes a two-layer optimization method with distributed energy stations based on demand response. Firstly, in the upper level planning model, the optimal allocation scheme of distributed energy is determined with the aim of minimizing the comprehensive cost of the station area. Based on the optimal configuration scheme of the upper layer, the lower operating model optimizes the TOU price with the aim of minimizing the operating cost of the station area. Then, aiming at the problem of insufficient accuracy of gull search algorithm, an improved gull search algorithm is proposed to solve it. Levy flight strategy is introduced to enhance the search direction diversity of the algorithm and the ability to jump out of local optimal. Finally, based on the simulation results and comparative analysis of IEEE33-node system, the rationality and effectiveness of the model and solution method are verified.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Distributed Photovoltaics on Traditional Protection of Distribution Networks under Different Grid-Connection Conditions and Optimization Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the continuous growth of distributed generation (DG) grid-connected capacity, the proportion of distributed photovoltaic (PV) is gradually increasing. Its impact on the safe and stable operation of the distribution network is becoming more and more significant. The traditional distribution network was originally a unidirectional power flow with a single-source radiation structure, but the connection of distributed PV power sources has transformed the distribution network into a complex multi-source system with bidirectional power flow characteristics. This has led to an increase in the uncertainty of the direction and magnitude of current during a fault, making it difficult for the original overcurrent protection scheme to adapt. To address this challenge, this study uses the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform to establish an equivalent photovoltaic model with low voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability. By simulating scenarios with different fault locations and types, the impact of distributed photovoltaic grid-connected capacity on the short-circuit current of protection devices is analysed in depth, and the impact on the performance of protection actions is assessed. Finally, this paper proposes a new criterion for coordinating three-stage current protection with grid-connected capacity based on the output characteristics of reactive current, to ensure that distribution networks with distributed photovoltaics can maintain safe and stable operation.

articleTitle: A Study of Regional Electricity Market System Dynamics Under Policy Factor Considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This study aims to explore the dynamic influence mechanism of policy factors on the green co-evolution system of regional power market, focusing on the role and effect of key policy tools such as carbon quota policy, renewable energy consumption responsibility weighting policy and China's Certified Voluntary Emission reduction (CCER) policy in the development of this system. By constructing a system dynamic model based on policy factors, this paper conducts basic scenario setting and sensitivity analysis, comprehensively evaluates the role and influence of policy factors in the green co-evolution of the regional power market, and reveals the development trend and evolution law of the regional power market under policy regulation.The research results show that the change of policy variables directly affects the key data indicators in the market, and then acts on the market structure and the direction of technological innovation, and has a significant impact on the market ecosystem. The research in this paper provides a scientific basis for the government departments to formulate more accurate and effective policies, has important guiding significance for promoting the sustainable development and green co-evolution of the regional power market, and provides a forward-looking and operational cooperation scheme for relevant parties in the power industry in practice.

articleTitle: Zonotope-Based Aggregation and Control Method for Distributed Energy Storage in Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The widespread adoption of distributed energy storage resources on the distribution network side has increasingly underscored the importance of harnessing their substantial flexibility potential. Given this background, a zonotope-based aggregation and control method for distributed energy storage in networks is proposed. First, an individual operational model of distributed energy storage resources was established, and their feasible region space was characterized. Second, an approximation and efficient aggregation method for the feasible region of distributed energy storage resources based on zonotope was proposed. Then, the aggregated clusters of distributed energy storage resources were applied to the optimal regulation of distribution networks, and a power decomposition method based on the water-filling algorithm was presented. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed aggregation and regulation method for distributed energy storage resource clusters was validated through case studies on the revised 33-bus distribution network.

articleTitle: A Pricing Mechanism and a Cost Diversion Optimization Method for Designing a Standalone New Energy Storage Power Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: New energy storage is both an important technology and a piece of critical equipment supporting new power systems. A reasonable and effective pricing mechanism is the key to the development of new energy storage. In this paper, research is conducted on the pricing mechanism of a standalone new energy storage power station, and the exploration into the pricing mechanism of energy storage power stations in China is discussed, finding that, for energy storage power stations, neither the regulated pricing model nor the standalone participation in the electricity market can support the large-scale commercialized application of such power stations. Based on equal responsibility, power, and interest of all stakeholders, a pricing mechanism and a cost diversion optimization method for designing energy storage power stations, based on the transfer factor, are proposed and explained by case study. The result shows that the transfer factor can effectively distribute the incomes from energy storage capacity and the electricity market, thus guaranteeing a balance of income among the stakeholders.

articleTitle: Artificial neural network-based distributed optimal control for building HVAC systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems are the major contributors to energy consumption in buildings, significantly impacting energy efficiency and occupants’ thermal comfort. In this context, this paper presents a data-driven distributed control framework that utilizes artificial neural networks (ANNs) to model the multi-time-step thermal dynamics of buildings. Each building has a local controller to minimize electricity generation costs in the microgrid while maintaining individual thermal comfort. To coordinate these local controllers, a distributed strategy is adopted to manage HVAC operations. Although conflicting objectives may arise during the iterative distributed coordination process, the framework effectively balances energy usage among the buildings and achieves convergence in total power consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the ANN-based approach optimizes HVAC operations, achieving the aims of temperature regulation and optimal energy management.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cascading Failures in Power Cyber-Physical Systems Under Typhoon Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Given the high coupling of cyber-physical systems in modern power grids, cascading failures are susceptible to natural disasters like typhoons, often leading to widespread blackouts. This study establishes a cascading failure analysis model tailored to typhoon scenarios to assess power CPS vulnerability under extreme weather. First, a typhoon disaster model, based on the Batts model, is constructed to evaluate impacts on transmission lines and initiate failure scenarios. Next, a cascading failure model for power CPS is proposed to simulate failure propagation, followed by simulations analyzing CPS vulnerability under typhoon conditions and assessing physical factors in failure spread. Results underscore the importance of dynamic typhoon path modeling and transmission line vulnerability in failure scenarios. Simulating external forces such as typhoons can improve CPS resilience and potentially mitigate large-scale blackouts during disasters.

articleTitle: Securing Energy Internet Construction: An Optical Fiber Fence Intrusion Monitoring Method Based on Improved Spatial Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Given the complexity and various potential risks present at construction sites of energy internet, particularly the issue of illegal intrusions during the suspension phase of energy internet construction, this paper proposes an optical fiber fence intrusion monitoring method based on an improved spatial attention mechanism. Our method is based on a widely used optical fiber fence intrusion monitoring systems across various industrial sectors. First, endpoint detection is applied to the vibration signals, and noise is removed before transforming the one-dimensional sequences into two-dimensional graphs using Gramian Angular Field (GAF) encoding. Then, an improved Spatial Attention Mechanism (ISAM) module is added to the ResNet50 network, combined with Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) Loss and Center Loss to enhance classification performance. Test results show that the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 98.58% for illegal intrusion detection during the suspension phase of energy internet construction, significantly outperforming traditional methods in terms of both accuracy and real-time, while reducing the false alarm rate and missed detection rates.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Co-optimization of Regulation Resources for Flexible Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that the existing flexible distribution network planning does not fully take the collaboration between flexible resources and traditional regulation equipment into account, which is mainly based on symmetric networks without fine modelling of the three-phase imbalance characteristics of the distribution network, a distributional robust optimization method is proposed for the collaborative planning of SOPs, ESSs and SVCs. Firstly, considering the source-load output uncertainty, a mixed probability distribution uncertainty model based on 1-parameter and ∞-parameter is constructed using the data of historical output scenarios. Secondly, considering the investment cost and operation cost of SOPs, ESSs, and SVCs, a scenario probability-driven collaborative planning model is established. Then, a main problem-subproblem iterative algorithm based on the generation of columns and constraints is adopted to achieve the solution by a commercial solver. Finally, the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method in the paper are verified by the IEEE 33-node arithmetic example.

articleTitle: Power quality improvement control strategy based on active disturbance rejection control based on modified particle swarm optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of the energy revolution, which resolutely implements the core elements of the carbon peak and carbon neutrality tasks, the national power system will develop from high carbon to deep low-carbon or even zero carbon. However, due to the grid connection of a large number of distributed power sources such as wind power and photovoltaic and the extensive access of power electronic equipment, the power quality such as voltage fluctuation and reactive power of active distribution network is becoming more and more prominent. Voltage is an important index of safety and economy of distribution system, and its stability is closely related to reactive power. For cutting, distributed power supply in the operation of the power distribution network load and node voltage caused by the volatility of rise/fall beyond the lower limit of problem,this paper proposes a self immunity (active disturbance rejection control, ADRC) double loop control of the distribution network reactive power control strategy. In view of the fast reactive power regulation ability of the energy storage system and the good performance of the active disturbance rejection control, this paper designs a reactive power support double loop controller based on the lithium battery energy storage system model, combines the ADRC with the voltage and current double closed-loop control, and optimizes the parameters of the ADRC by improving the particle swarm optimization algorithm, so that the voltage at the junction point is kept stable in the limit range. Simulation results show that the strategy is feasible.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation Method of New Power System Industry Chain Autonomy Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, the global energy transformation is accelerating, and China's new energy security strategy is being advanced. The international competition in the power industry and related technologies is becoming increasingly prominent. The autonomy of core technologies is an inevitable choice to ensure national energy security and construct new power system. In this paper, the disadvantages of industry comprehensive analysis, simple calculation methods, low accuracy are considered. The comprehensive autonomy level assessment indices for the new power system industry chain autonomy level are constructed, which helps to accurately judge the foundation of the power industry chain and key equipment. It provides a scientific reference for the implementation of scientific and technological research on new power systems and to accelerate the realization of a high level of autonomy.

articleTitle: Offshore Wind Power Transmission Capacity and Uncertainty Assessment Based on VSC-LCC Hybrid HVDC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The offshore wind power is delivered through a hybrid high-voltage direct current line based on Voltage Source Converter and Line Commutated Converter (VSC-LCC), which can retain the advantages of Flexible High Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC) while saving engineering costs, showing promising application prospects. However, the Line Commutated Converter High Voltage Direct Current (LCC-HVDC) requires a significant absorption of reactive power during operation, which deteriorates the voltage level of the receiving end grid, thus limiting the transmission of wind power. To address this issue, this paper proposes a transmission capacity analysis method for offshore wind power delivered through a multi-terminal hybrid HVDC based on AC-DC continuous power flow. Firstly, an AC system-multi-terminal HVDC power flow model considering VSC and LCC converter stations is established. Then, based on single-parameter continuous power flow and multi-parameter continuous power flow, calculation methods for the transmission capacity of a single wind farm and the joint transmission capacity of multiple wind farms are proposed. Next, considering the randomness of the receiving end grid load, a quantification method for the uncertainty of wind power transmission capacity is proposed. Finally, the validity of the proposed method is verified through a modified IEEE 30-node AC-DC system. The simulation results indicate that the transmission capacity of offshore wind power is closely related to the control strategy of LCC-HVDC and is significantly affected by the volatility of the receiving end grid load.

articleTitle: Multi-Scenario and Multi-Entity Interaction of Village-Level Microgrids Considering Solar-Storage-Charging-Network-Load Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-scenario and multi-entity interaction method for village-level microgrids with solar-storage-charging-network-load coupling. First, considering the deep coupling relationship of solar-storage-charging-network-load within village-level microgrids, this study constructs a collaborative interaction model for solar-storage-charging-network-load based on different resource characteristics. It explores the flexible interaction potential, enabling efficient utilization of large-scale distributed resources and ensuring self-consistent operation of village-level microgrids under various fluctuating source-load scenarios. Then, considering diverse supply-demand relationships among multiple stakeholders within village-level microgrids, a complete information dynamic game behavior model involving different stakeholders is developed. It achieves collaborative energy complementarity, allowing all parties to profit, thereby enhancing the overall social benefits of the village-level microgrid. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model and method are verified in case studies.

articleTitle: Intelligent Approval and Safety Verification in Distribution Network Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Distribution network maintenance is essential to ensure regular operation, reliability, and safety of power supply systems. Traditional maintenance processes rely heavily on manual operations and telephone communications, leading to inefficiencies, poor information transmission, and increased operational risks. This paper proposes designing an intelligent application system for distribution network maintenance to enhance dispatching tasks' efficiency and management level. By integrating artificial intelligence and graphical visualization technologies, the system optimizes existing systems such as the Distribution Management System, Distribution Automation System, and Network Command System. Key features include an intelligent maintenance process monitoring interface, intelligent approval processes for maintenance orders, improved safety error prevention mechanisms, and dispatch business statistical analysis functions. The system enables real-time monitoring of maintenance plan execution, automates the approval and execution of operational tickets, and ensures operational safety through comprehensive error prevention checks. Implementing this intelligent system significantly reduces manual intervention, enhances the intelligence level of dispatching operations, and improves the efficiency and safety of distribution network maintenance.

articleTitle: Bi-level Optimization for Dispatching Grid-Interactive Electric Vehicles in an Urban Community
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents a bi-level optimization model aimed at enhancing the operational efficiency and economic viability of electric vehicles (EVs) interacting with urban community power grids. The proposed model particularly examines the intricate relationships among EV charging and discharging characteristics, urban transmission systems, and distribution networks. The upper-level optimization model focuses on the overall integrity and economic efficiency of the urban power grid, with the objective of minimizing operational costs, which include the start-up and generation costs of thermal power units, environmental costs, penalties for wind and PV generation reductions, as well as the charging costs incurred by EV users. Conversely, the lower-level optimization model determines the optimal charging and discharging locations for EVs through optimal power flow (OPF) calculations to enhance the resilience of the distribution network. Through case studies, this paper validates the effectiveness of the proposed model and demonstrates the impact of varying electricity pricing structures on upper-level optimization. The findings reveal that the bi-level optimization model can adeptly manage EV charging and discharging, fostering a mutually beneficial scenario among the urban grid, charging network operators, and EV owners.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of dynamic characteristics of heating networks on operation characteristics of integrated electricity and heating systems considering the refined heat network model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integrated electricity and heating system(IEHS) consists of electricity, heating systems, and energy coupling equipment. The complex topology and heterogeneous energy flow transmission characteristics make it challenging to establish a universal model. This article conducts research on modeling and solving methods for IEHS. A steady-state hydraulic model considering pipelines, pumps, and adjustable valves was established and combined with a dynamic heating system model to form a quasi dynamic heating system model. Furthermore, a comprehensive energy system model for IEHS was constructed, and a general model solving method was established. Finally, the effectiveness of the method was validated in a case study of an IEHS.

articleTitle: Resilience Enhancement of Polar Electric-Thermal Integrated Energy Systems with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the issue of energy supply interruptions caused by extreme events in Antarctic scientific expeditions, an innovative resilience enhancement strategy for polar electric-thermal integrated energy system (ETIES) with energy storage is proposed. The fault propagation mechanism between ETIES is expounded, and the importance of the real-time compensation ability of energy storage (ES) in the service recovery stage to ensure the stability of system energy supply is discussed. The results show that this method can be applied to the formulation of post-disaster resilience improvement strategies for the ETIES of Zhongshan Station in Antarctica to ensure the continuous energy supply of the system in extreme environments.

articleTitle: A Profit-Oriented FDI Attack Strategy in Real-Time Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The emergence of peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading market brings both benefits and risks to modern power system. Relying on information and communication technology (ICT), transaction in P2P energy trading market is vulnerable to false data injection attacks (FDIAs). Specifically, the malicious redistribution of short-term forecasting load data will mislead the economic dispatch (ED) in the ex-ante real-time (RT) market. Hence, the actual generation outputs deviate from the schedule, and the corrupt result of ED can affect the trading volume in RT market through a P2P framework. Accordingly, targeting on a specific agent in P2P market, we propose a strategy to inject a malicious forecasting data in order to maximize the trading profits for this agent. Moreover, since the P2P model often solved in a distributed way, which brings heavy computational burden, we conduct a preferred locational marginal price (LMP) to give a one-time solution. Eventually, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our attacking strategy based on the IEEE 9-bus test system.

articleTitle: Modeling and Regulating Electric Vehicles Carbon Flow in Coupled Transportation-Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Controlling indirect carbon emissions from electric vehicles (EVs) is essential to achieving a carbon-neutral future for the transportation sector, given the long-term goal of attaining 100% clean electricity. However, the interdependence between power and traffic flows, along with the differing time scales of power system dispatch and traffic flow variation, makes the analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics of indirect carbon emissions within the coupled transportation-power network challenging. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel spatio-temporal dynamic traffic flow model (STDT) that is synchronized with the time scales of power system dispatch and captures the interdependence between EV route choices in the transportation network and charging power from the power network. Then, by combining the time-varying local marginal carbon emissions at each charging station with STDT, a new concept called EV-CF (carbon flow of EVs) can be introduced to analyze the spatio-temporal variation in indirect carbon emissions caused by EV charging and transportation. The spatio-temporal EV-CF can be regulated to minimize indirect carbon emissions of a coupled transportation-power network while ensuring transportation requirements. The proposed model and regulation method are verified through case studies.

articleTitle: Virtual Power Plant Energy Coordination: A Global Solution to Three-Level Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In robust energy scheduling for virtual power plants (VPPs), uncertainty sets (USs) have been used to capture the uncertainty in renewable energy source (RES) outputs. However, for VPP energy scheduling models that employ methods such as the convex hull US (CHUS), which involves a large number of integer variables, traditional column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithms often converge to local optima, posing significant challenges for practical scheduling. This necessitates the development of algorithms capable of escaping local optima. To balance security and economic efficiency, this study adopts a confidence level-based CHUS, which improves scheduling economics by setting a specified confidence level. Subsequently, a vertex-based column-and-constraint generation algorithm is designed to avoid local optima, enabling the confidence level-based CHUS to solve the robust VPP energy scheduling model effectively. Finally, based on an actual VPP system in South China, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed US method and algorithm are validated.

articleTitle: Collaborative Planning Method of Multi-Regional Integrated Electrical and Natural Gas Systems for Low-Carbon Economic Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to the growing shortage of fossil fuels, this paper presents a collaborative planning method for multi-regional integrated electrical and natural gas systems (IENGS), aimed at low-carbon economic development. First, the paper proposes environmental costs under a joint carbon-green certificate trading mechanism. Then, a low-carbon configuration model for IENGS is developed, which accounts for full life cycle costs. Finally, the problem is broken down into three solvable sub-problems for the transmission, distribution, and natural gas networks based on the ATC algorithm, to minimize economic and environmental costs for optimal system configuration. Numerical tests on a 23-node power grid and a 30-node natural gas network verify the effectiveness of the multi-regional planning model in a low-carbon environment.

articleTitle: Analysis and Application of Non-contact Wide-frequency Voltage Measurement Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the continuous development and increasing complexity of power systems have imposed higher demands on voltage measurement technologies. This paper first provides a comprehensive analysis of several typical non-contact wide-frequency voltage measurement methods, focusing on their principles, methodologies, and applications. Following this, the application of non-contact wide-frequency voltage measurement technology in power system monitoring and protection is discussed. The analysis reveals that non-contact voltage measurement technology significantly enhances the safety and reliability of power systems and demonstrates broad prospects in practical applications.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Benefits Assessment Framework for Orderly Integration of Electric Vehicles in Three-phase Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the focus on carbon neutrality intensifies, the rapid expansion of electric vehicles (EVs) presents both opportunities and challenges for distribution networks. Accurately quantifying the benefits of orderly EV integration is essential for ensuring the safe and stable operation of distribution networks while maximizing their overall advantages. To address this, this paper conducts a thorough cost-benefit analysis and introduces a comprehensive benefit assessment framework designed to evaluate the impact of orderly EV integration on system performance. The framework offers a systematic definition and qualitative methods for various benefits, encompassing both operational and investment perspectives. Additionally, a multi-objective optimization model is developed to balance transaction costs, power quality, and reserve provision of EVs. This model incorporates refined three-phase distribution network models that address three-phase unbalance and grid losses, alongside a novel reserve provision model for EVs, enabling precise quantification of related benefits. Case studies validate the framework's effectiveness in highlighting the comprehensive benefits of orderly EV integration.

articleTitle: An Integrated Optimization Approach for Operational and Maintenance Planning of Highway Transportation Self-Sustained Multi-Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Renewable energy sources such as wind and solar power are abundant along highways. To enhance the utilization rate of energy within service areas, self-sustained energy systems for highway service zones have been developed. These systems aim to achieve self-sufficiency in energy by producing, converting, storing, and using energy locally, thereby reducing the losses associated with long-distance energy transportation and improving the overall efficiency of the system. However, maintenance and repair can lead to system downtime, posing challenges to the self-sustained operation of these energy systems. This paper proposes an innovative maintenance scheduling plan tailored for self-sustained energy systems in highway service areas to address these challenges. We have established a multi-energy system that integrates various renewable sources, including cold, heat, electricity, and hydrogen, and set up a joint optimization objective. Compared to traditional sequential maintenance methods, our approach not only reduces operational and maintenance costs but also enhances the system's self-sufficiency and efficiency. The queuing time for electric vehicle charging within the service area is substantially reduced, leading to an overall improvement in the operational efficiency of the service zone.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Smart Grids: A Comprehensive Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The research field of artificial intelligence applications for smart grids has been a rapidly growing hotspot over the past 20 years. This paper conducts a bibliometric analysis of research trends and hotspots in this field based on 12,282 related publications from the Web of Science Core Collection published from 2004 to 2024. First, publication trends and major funding agencies are identified. Then, using CiteSpace software, collaboration network analysis among countries, institutions, and authors is performed to identify active research entities; keywords co-occurrence analysis and literature co-citation analysis are conducted; and scientific knowledge mappings are drawn. Based on the burst analysis, emerging references are presented to indicate future trends in the field. These results can guide researchers studying the fundamental research and frontiers in this field.

articleTitle: Dynamic Route Optimization for Energy Storage and Exchange Vessels in Oceanic Island Groups Based on an Improved Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Oceanic-island groups are crucial to national marine strategy. To address mismatches between energy demand and renewable supply, where traditional energy solutions fall short, this paper introduces a multi-island cooperative model using shared inter-island electric vessels (SIEVs). By classifying islands into resource-rich and load-center types, SIEVs optimize energy transfer and collection across islands while also providing passenger transport, thus enhancing overall energy and transportation efficiency. An inter-island spatiotemporal optimization model, driven by an improved particle swarm algorithm, maximizes energy collection. Simulation results highlight the model's economic and sustainable benefits, offering a practical solution for optimized energy supply within island groups.

articleTitle: New principle of distance protection for asymmetric short circuit of the transmission line of inverter renewable energy station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Because the output current of the renewable energy grid-connected inverter has the traits of weak amplitude feed and controlled phase angle, compared with the traditional AC system, the ability of the distance protection to withstand the transition resistance in the renewable energy access AC power grid is reduced, and the risk of incorrect protection action is aggravated. Therefore, in order to solve the problem of adaptability decline of backup protection, this paper proposes a new principle of distance protection based on the method of solving the additional impedance phase. Firstly, in accordance with the well-known impedance model, combined with the boundary conditions of the sequence network after the asymmetric fault of the AC line, and then using the nature of the new energy side open circuit in the negative sequence network, an additional impedance phase solution method based on the normalization of the negative sequence network is proposed. On this basis, the sine theorem is used to calculate the fault distance, and finally a new protection principle is constructed. Compared with the traditional ratio amplitude distance protection, this principle has a strong ability to withstand transition resistance, and can withstand a maximum of 200 Ω transition resistance when single-phase grounding, which addresses the issue where the proposed distance protection principle is negatively impacted by transition resistance as a result of renewable energy's weak feed characteristics.

articleTitle: Research on the Decision-making of Power-type Virtual Power Plant Participating in Medium and Long-term Market Transactions Considering the Uncertainty of Wind and Solar Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: At present, the development of virtual power plants is moving from the invitation stage to the market stage. The power market includes the electric energy market, the auxiliary service market and the capacity market. This paper studies and establishes a transaction decision-making model for power-type virtual power plants to participate in the medium and long-term electricity market considering the uncertainty of wind and solar output. The model takes the maximum profit of the virtual power plant in the medium and long term electric energy market and the green certificate market in one cycle as the objective function, and considers the market constraints and the virtual power plant aggregation resource constraints. In particular, the influence of the uncertainty of wind and light output of aggregated resources on the deviation assessment cost of virtual power plants participating in medium and long-term market transactions is analyzed. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the model and method established in this paper are verified by an example analysis. By calculating and analyzing the results of virtual power plants participating in the transaction in three scenarios, the trading strategy of power-type virtual power plants participating in the medium and long-term market is given.

articleTitle: Source-load scenario generation method based on conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The historical measurement data of renewable energy and loads can be processed in various ways to generate grid operation scenarios. However, with the continuous development of advanced forecasting technologies, a large amount of valuable prediction data accumulated during the scenario generation process is often overlooked. To address this issue, we propose a new scenario generation paradigm that fully considers the uncertainty of renewable energy generation, enabling multi-scenario generation for grid operations. This method models the uncertainty of renewable energy based on discrete probability distributions and employs the Wasserstein distance with gradient penalty as the objective function for the discriminator. It designs a network structure suitable for short-term source-load scenario generation. Through adversarial training of the conditional generative adversarial network, the generator gradually learns the mapping relationship between the noise distribution under forecasting conditions and the day-ahead scenario set. The proposed method is validated using IEEE 118-bus data, and the results demonstrate that the model can accurately capture the short-term uncertainty of renewable energy generation.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Scheduling Strategy of Virtual Power Plants Based on Conditional Value at Risk and Random Scenario Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Virtual Power Plant (VPP) has become an effective way to improve the stability of power grid and the utilization rate of renewable energy because of its ability to aggregate various distributed energy sources into a whole. However, significant risk losses are faced by the VPP as it seeks to maximize income, owing to the fluctuations in wind power generation and photovoltaic output. A multi-source joint optimal scheduling model of virtual power plant based on Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and stochastic optimization is proposed. CVaR risk control is used to reduce the risk caused by fluctuation, and Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) and K-medoids clustering algorithm are combined to optimize the scene with uncertain wind and scenery, so as to improve the scheduling accuracy. The outcomes of the simulation indicate that an effective balance between benefits and risks can be achieved by the model under varying risk preferences, and improve the economy of VPP and the wind power consumption rate.

articleTitle: Study on Simulation Model of Synergistic Reduction of Pollution and Carbon Emissions in Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The research on synergistic reduction of pollution and carbon emissions is of great significance for cities to improve atmospheric environment quality and realize low-carbon transition. In this paper, Tianjin is used as an example to build an energy-economy-environment-carbon emission simulation and analysis model. Analysis is made on the synergistic reduction effects on atmospheric pollutants and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in Tianjin under measures of adjusting industrial structure, improving energy efficiency, enhancing electrification level, and increasing external electricity proportion. The results show that the measures for increasing energy efficiency have the best synergistic reduction effect, followed by adjusting industrial structure. The synergistic reduction effect between NOx and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is better than that between SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Research on Biomass Energy High-Resolution Prediction Methods Driven by Multi-Source Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-resolution prediction method for biomass energy resources driven by multi-source data and applies it to Sichuan Province as a case study. By integrating biomass resource potential data such as agricultural residues, forestry residues, and energy crops, along with multi-source environmental and socio-economic data, the XGBoost algorithm is used to accurately predict biomass resources. The results show that the model's coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) exceeds 0.9, and the root mean square error (RMSE) is as low as 0.1, demonstrating superior prediction performance under complex spatiotemporal distribution variations. The study indicates significant regional differences in the spatial distribution of biomass resources in Sichuan Province, with higher development potential in the central and southeastern regions and relatively lower potential in the northwest. Temporal analysis reveals a fluctuating trend in biomass resources after 2018, which may be related to environmental policy adjustments, climate change, and market demand fluctuations. This study provides new insights and scientific evidence for the efficient management and sustainable development of biomass energy resources, with important application value and development prospects.

articleTitle: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach Towards Fast Gas Flow Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Natural gas systems (NGS) and electric power systems are increasingly interconnected to enhance flexibility. However, the bidirectional energy flow problem, represented by partial differential algebraic equations (PDAE), remains a challenge for model-based solvers. Achieving feasible solutions with complete parameter availability in a large-scale system can take several minutes to hours. To address this, we propose a Physics-Informed Gas Flow Neural Network (PIGFNN) for gas flow calculations in NGS, effectively mitigating the time-consuming aspects of PDAE. The PIGFNN accurately captures heterogeneous gas states while ensuring a privacy-preserving interface. Additionally, we introduce a physics-informed loss function, NGSPILoss, which quantifies violations of dynamic constraints in NGS, ensuring that PDAE constraints are satisfied in gas flow calculations. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Lane Detection Method for Advancing Sustainable Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology plays a key role in driving the development of a green and smart Energy Internet. As one of the application areas of the Energy Internet, lane detection in intelligent transportation systems can provide accurate real-time traffic data, thus supporting intelligent scheduling and resource optimization, reducing congestion, energy consumption, and emissions, and improving overall energy efficiency. Therefore, deep learning-based lane detection methods can further enhance the intelligence level of the Energy Internet and promote its efficient operation. However, current methods often rely on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which excel at local feature extraction but struggle to capture global information in complex conditions. In varying light, shadows, and obstacles, CNNs struggle to integrate information, leading to inaccuracies, particularly in dense traffic or complex road structures, where diverse local features result in identification errors and hinder lane continuity. This reduces decision-making efficiency and increases energy consumption. Consequently, we present LFKNet, a lane detection framework designed for the fusion of the Lane Focus Mechanism (LFM) and Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) to enhance accuracy and robustness. It consists of two key components: the Lane Focus Mechanism , which utilizes the geometrical topology of lanes for improved global fea ture extraction in complex scenarios, and the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network, which employs a learnable nonlinear activation function to optimize performance on complex and nonlinear features. The experiments demonstrate that LFKNet achieves 97.00% accuracy with a 97.76% F1-score on the Tusimple dataset. It also achieves a 79.43% F1-score on the CULane dataset. Overall, LFKNet’s performance validates its effectiveness in lane detection, enabling accurate traffic monitoring and analysis while providing reliable data support for the Energy Internet.

articleTitle: An improved three-phase unbalanced power flow calculation algorithm of microgrids based on the enhanced loop incidence matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Most distributed generation sources (DGs) are connected to the microgrid in the form of power electronics. The line parameters and loads are asymmetrical, and single phase of DGs, which cause the power flow distribution of the system has the characteristics of three-phase imbalance. According to the operation characteristics of DGs and their interfaces with microgrid system, distributed load flow calculation models of DGs and electric vehicle (EV) charging loads are established in this paper. In order to solve the problem of three-phase unbalance in power flow calculation of the microgrid, the reactance matrix of the power flow calculation node containing the self-impedance and mutual impedance of each line is established by using the method of enhanced loop incidence matrix. To solve the problem of weak processing capability of regulated-voltage (PV) nodes in power flow calculation using the forward backward sweep method, the reactive power is compensated and corrected by using voltage deviation of PV nodes in the iterative process. Finally, the method proposed in this paper is verified by IEEE13 test system and a microgrid system, and the results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Icing thickness prediction model of transmission line based on KPCA-INGO-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A transmission line icing prediction model based on an optimised bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) and the enhanced northern Goshawk algorithm (INGO) is developed in an effort to increase the prediction accuracy of transmission line icing. The classic northern Goshawk algorithm (NGO) is enhanced by employing a hybrid sine cosine algorithm approach and a random opposition-based learning strategy in order to increase the optimisation performance of the INGO method. Based on this, the icing properties of the wire are extracted using the kernel principal component analysis (KPCA), which serves as the input for the icing prediction. Simultaneously, a two-way long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) is utilised to build an icing prediction model that takes into consideration the time-varying nature of icing and thoroughly takes into account the past and future climate features of various times. The bidirectional long short-term memory network's hyperparameter selection is optimised using the INGO method, and a transmission line icing prediction model based on INGO-BiLSTM is created. From the perspective of MAPE, MAE and RMSE, the MAPE, MAE and RMSE of the INGO-BiLSTM model are smaller than those of several other commonly used icing prediction models. The simulation results show that the INGO-BiLSTM model effectively improves the prediction accuracy compared with the BiLSTM icing prediction model, GWO-SVR icing prediction model and NGO-BiLSTM icing prediction model.

articleTitle: Robust Scheduling of a Charging Station Considering Uncertain Charging Demand and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With advancements in increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), the potential for Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) to contribute to a more sustainable energy ecosystem is substantial. However, fluctuations in real-time electricity prices on the grid may cause the overall cost of EVs during continuous charging and discharging processes to exceed that of the pure charging mode. At the same time, the random arrivals of EVs will exacerbate the uncertainty of charging demand at EV stations. Therefore, the paper first introduces a demand response (DR) mechanism that combines the pricing factors of EVs and charging stations, ensuring that neither party incurs increased cost due to participating in the V2G. Additionally, to address the uncertainty of charging demands, this paper develops a distributed robust optimization scheduling scheme (DRO) based on moment information. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A Channel-Wise Cross Attention Mechanism Based Aggregated Distributed Photovoltaic Power Day-ahead Forecasting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To enhance the safety, stability, and economic efficiency of distribution networks, improving the day-ahead forecasting accuracy of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power plants is of significant importance. Given that PV output is influenced by complex factors such as weather, climate, and seasons, traditional forecasting methods based on irradiance forecasts and single-channel historical data struggle to handle the diverse operational scenarios of PV plants. This paper proposes a forecasting method for distributed PV clusters based on a channel-wise cross-attention mechanism. First, the cross-attention mechanism adaptively learns the pattern correlations among different channels of distributed PV data. Building on this, a forecasting model with a time-series Transformer backbone is employed to achieve spatially complementary pattern matching for distributed PV predictions and to reduce overall model prediction errors. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through test cases, demonstrating the substantial potential of spatio-temporal correlations in distributed PV for improving forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: A Control Strategy for VSC under Unbalanced Conditions in AC Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the integration of renewable energy sources and complex loads increases, modern distribution networks face significant challenges related to unbalanced operation. This paper investigates control strategies for two-level voltage source converters (VSCs) operating under unbalanced conditions in AC distribution networks. A novel dual synchronous reference frame (DDSRF)-based phase-locked loop (PLL) method is proposed to mitigate the adverse effects of double-frequency components introduced by unbalanced conditions. Additionally, a negative sequence current control loop is designed to suppress the impact of negative sequence currents on the safe operation of the VSC. Furthermore, an outer-loop power control strategy that accounts for unbalanced factors is introduced to reduce power fluctuations. Through PSCAD simulations results demonstrate that the proposed strategies significantly enhance VSC control performance and system stability under unbalanced conditions.

articleTitle: Reliability assessment method for distribution system with distributed generations in anti-islanding operation mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Large-scale distributed generation (DG) based on photovoltaic power is increasingly integrated into the distribution system, posing a significant threat to its power supply reliability due to its fluctuating output power influenced by weather conditions. Evaluating the reliability of the distribution system following the grid connection of DGs is crucial for guiding the planning of the distribution system and formulating protection strategies. This paper proposes a hybrid analysis method to assist in assessing the reliability of the distribution system under the anti-islanding operation mode of DGs. The reliability model of DGs is established using historical data and stochastic scenario generation techniques, considering the failures of system components. The reliability indicators of load points in the distribution system change based on the assessment of system adequacy, and the limitation of DG output power in the anti-islanding operation mode necessitates the removal of a fixed capacity of loads from the system. A detailed case study is presented in the end.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Indicator Evaluation Method for Integrated Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The development of integrated energy system(IES) echoes the theme of the times of sustainable development, and the multi-index evaluation of IES has become a research hotspot. Based on the three dimensions of economy, environment and energy consumption, this paper establishes three indicators, namely environmental, thermal and economic, by analyzing the overall and local indicators of the system. Then, TOPSIS-entropy weight method is used to rank the indicators and evaluate IESs with different topologies. Finally, the best scheme of the IES can be obtained, In this paper, an real-world IES of the Hongfeng Lake in Guizhou Province, China, is taken as a case study for analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Behavior Modeling in Coupled Electricity and Carbon Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In response to global efforts toward carbon neutrality and the pressing need for sustainable energy systems, the coupled electricity and carbon markets have become critical for optimizing both economic and environmental objectives. This paper proposes a deep learning-based behavior modeling framework to analyze the interactions between these two interconnected markets. By integrating real-world data and hybrid experimental learning, we simulate strategic offering behaviors using generative models, particularly Variational Autoencoders (VAE).
