Our proposed hybrid model synergizes these components, achieving multi-level feature extraction and robust noise suppression, which significantly improves prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on real-world battery datasets demonstrate that the hybrid model outperforms traditional machine learning techniques and standalone deep learning approaches, showcasing its generalization capability across different battery chemistries and operational conditions. Our approach provides a promising solution for real-time battery health monitoring and management.

articleTitle: Transformer fault diagnosis method based on multi-classification logistic regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Transformer is the core equipment in power system, its running state directly affects the safety and economy of power grid. Traditional transformer fault diagnosis methods often rely on experience and regular detection, it is difficult to realize real-time monitoring and early warning. With the development of big data technology, combined with machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms, the operation data of transformers can be deeply analyzed, so as to achieve rapid identification and positioning of potential faults. Taking transformer equipment as the specific research object, a fault diagnosis method based on big data fusion is proposed. After the data preprocessing of the equipment, the fault diagnosis model of the equipment is established from the bottom up through data level fusion (data association fusion), feature level fusion (preliminary diagnosis of multi-classification logistic regression) and decision level fusion (synthesis diagnosis of D-S evidence theory), and specific case analysis and method comparison are carried out. Take a typical transformer equipment as an example for experimental analysis, the results show that this method is superior to some traditional fault diagnosis algorithms and has better diagnostic capability.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Regenerative Electric Heating for Improving Distribution Network Carrying Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The large-scale integration of regenerative electric heating poses higher requirements for the carrying capacity of the distribution network. How to improve the carrying capacity of the distribution network through rational planning of regenerative electric heating capacity has become a key issue for the future development of the power grid. Therefore, a regenerative electric heating optimal configuration method for improving the carrying capacity of distribution network is proposed. Firstly, the regenerative electric heating model is established and the thermal comfort elasticity is analyzed in relation to the regenerative electric heating capacity. Secondly, a multi-objective optimal configuration model for regenerative electric heating is established with the objectives of maximum carrying capacity of the distribution network and minimum annualized cost of the system, combined with constraints such as thermal comfort elasticity constraints and equipment operation constraints. Finally, an arithmetic simulation based on a heating project in a region in northern China verifies that the proposed scheme can improve the regenerative electric heating carrying capacity of the distribution network under the premise of ensuring the economic benefits of the distribution network and the comfort of users.

articleTitle: The small signal stability margin prediction model for grid-connected hybrid renewable power station based on the GCN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale access of high-proportion renewable power and power electronic equipment, power system obviously shows a trend of decreasing inertia and weakening system strength, and the stability problem is becoming more and more serious. In addition to system operation status data, the topology in the hybrid renewable power station also affects the small signal stability of the grid-connected system. However, existing data driven prediction model of grid-connected stability margin of renewable power stations cannot characterize the effect of its topology. Therefore, if the topology in the station changes, its prediction accuracy will be difficult to guarantee. Considering the influence of topology, the grid-connected stability margin prediction model of grid-forming/grid-following hybrid renewable power station based on Graph Convolution Networks (GCN) and Bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) , namely GCN-BiLSTM, is proposed. GCN is used to realize the perception of the topology structure in the renewable power station, so as to be adapt to the change of its topology and improve the topology generalization ability of the model. BiLSTM is used to deeply fit the nonlinear relationship between renewable power station topology, system operation status and stability margin, so as to further improve the prediction accuracy of GCN-BiLSTM model. The information of power grid strength, the configuration ratio and distribution location of grid-forming/grid-following power generation equipment, type of energy storage device and topology of the station are input into the GCN-BiLSTM prediction model. And the prediction results of small signal stability margin in low frequency band and sub/super-synchronous band are output online. Taking a demo grid-forming/grid-following hybrid renewable power station with energy storage device as an example, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed grid-connected renewable power station stability margin prediction model based on the GCN-BiLSTM are verified. The experimental results show that compared with the prediction model based on the BiLSTM, GCN-BiLSTM has better topological generalization ability, and higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on the Comprehensive Evaluation index System for Assessing the Development Level of New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A comprehensive and objective evaluation of the construction level of the new power system in Northern Hebei is essential for its effective planning and implementation. This paper responds to the specific needs of the new power system in Northern Hebei by developing a detailed evaluation framework that incorporates five primary indicators: low-carbon random coupling power sources, resilient and flexible smart grids, and diverse collaborative interactive loads. Each indicator is clearly defined, with corresponding calculation methods provided. Additionally, a hierarchical evaluation system based on these indicators is proposed. This framework serves as a valuable decision-making tool for future planning and key construction initiatives of the new power system in Northern Hebei, promoting the efficient development of the regional power system.

articleTitle: Simulation of Airflow Field for 252kV Eco-Gas GIS Fast Earthing Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Research on the gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is widely used in the power industry. Although SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> as its gas insulation medium has good insulation and arc extinguishing performance, SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> is a strong greenhouse gas. Under the background of "double carbon", the research on environmental friendly C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N mixed gas and its feasibility in switchgear is one of the hot spots in the field of electrical engineering in recent years. In this paper, the physical parameters of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixed gas are calculated. Aiming at the opening process of 252kV GIS fast earthing switch, a two-dimensional dynamic calculation model of 252kV GIS fast earthing switch is established based on the fluid dynamics theory. The arc simulation of the model is carried out by using the finite element method, and the changes of gas pressure, temperature and density in the gas chamber of the fast earthing switch are calculated and obtained. articleTitle: Interpretable Transient Frequency Stability Prediction Based on Graph Convolutional Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To optimize China’s energy structure and improve energy utilization efficiency, an increasing number of large-capacity HVDC along with high-proportion renewable energy sources are being integrated into the power systems. This makes the power systems gradually gain a low-inertia nature. Low-inertia power systems exhibit weak inertia support, high uncertainty in power output, and poor frequency regulation capabilities, leading to high risk of encountering transient frequency stability issues after large disturbances. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to predict the transient frequency stability of a specific system in a reliable and efficient manner. To cope with the limitations of existing data-driven transient frequency stability prediction (TFSP) methods that simply learn from temporal information without sufficient consideration other valuable data like spatial information, this paper proposes an interpretable TFSP approach based on a Graph Convolutional Network via Initial residual and Identity mapping (GCNII). By incorporating the power network spatial information with temporal responsive data acquired from individual buses into the GCNII model, the proposed approach enables the model to comprehensively capture and learn the complex mapping relationships between system spatial-temporal dynamics and transient frequency stability status. Furthermore, the interpretable SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method is used to interpret the stability prediction results for better understanding. Finally, numerical tests on a realistic regional power grid in China demonstrate the efficacy of proposed method as well as its desirable interpretability.

Author Keywords: Graph Convolutional Network via Initial Residual and Identity Mapping

articleTitle: Comprehensive Approaches to a Low-Carbon Transition of the Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As the largest source of carbon emissions, the power grid has garnered significant attention for its decarbonization from academia, government, and industry. This transition is complex due to the involvement of various stakeholders, including power generation, transmission networks, and active customers. The purpose of this paper is to present a framework aimed at facilitating the low-carbon transition, focusing on emission reduction strategies across four components of the power system. On the generation side, retiring coal-fired generators and deploying renewable energy sources coupled with energy storage systems can significantly lower overall system emissions. Correspondingly, on the consumer side, the electrification of transportation offers a viable alternative to internal combustion engine vehicles, thereby reducing societal emissions. Furthermore, in terms of system control, planning methodologies such as gas-electric coupling optimization can expedite emission reduction efforts. For market design, effective policies like carbon taxes and carbon emission allowance trading incentivize power companies to actively lower emissions. Besides the above, advanced AI-based prediction methods, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs) and large language models (LLMs), enhance the accuracy of forecasting uncertainty including electricity prices and loads, improving the efficiency of transition. These evolving policies and grid technologies will enable us to decarbonize the grid and better mitigate the impacts of climate change driven by electricity consumption.

articleTitle: Capacity Enhancement Method for Distribution Network Considering Multi-Power Charging Pile Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the rapid increase in the number of electric vehicles (EVs), the carrying capacity of distribution networks is facing immense pressure. This paper proposes a method for enhancing the carrying capacity of distribution networks based on multi-power charging pile planning. First, an electric vehicle charging load model is constructed, and a set of assessment indicators for the carrying capacity of the distribution network is designed, encompassing multiple dimensions such as safety, stability, and quality, to ensure the comprehensiveness and scientific validity of the evaluation. Based on these assessment indicators, a multi-objective enhancement model is proposed, which takes into account both economic factors and carrying capacity. This model aims to optimize the layout and capacity of charging piles, thereby improving the overall carrying capacity of the distribution network while ensuring the safety and stability of the system. In the comparative analysis of three different schemes, the results indicate that the proposed method effectively balances economic efficiency with the safety and stability of the distribution network, significantly enhancing its capacity to accommodate EVs.

articleTitle: Collaborative planning method for independent microgrids under the integrated energy consumption mode of electricity, heat, and oxygen
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Independent microgrids are an effective solution to the problem of power supply in remote areas that cannot be covered by large power grids such as polar scientific research stations and isolated islands. However, the planning of independent microgrids faces a contradiction between power supply safety and the consumption of new energy. Especially, the planning of microgrids under the condition of integrated energy consumption of electricity, heat, and oxygen involves more factors to consider and more complex constraints. This article focuses on the significant seasonal differences in energy demand under the electricity heat oxygen integrated energy consumption mode of an independent operating microgrid system. While ensuring the reliability of heating, oxygen supply, and important load power supply, the work efficiency and benefits of the microgrid are improved. Combining the time delay characteristics of the thermal storage system and the adjustable characteristics of the oxygen load, a suitable power balance strategy for source load storage coordinated control is formulated. Finally, the particle swarm algorithm was used to calculate and analyze the optimal configurations for four scenarios: light storage, light storage with additional oxygen production, light storage of firewood, and light storage of firewood with additional oxygen production. The planning results showed that the configuration scheme considering oxygen production load had a lower overall cost.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Voltage Control for Power Systems with Static Var Generator Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Voltage stability is a critical aspect of power system operation, where sudden load or generation fluctuations can lead to voltage instability, impacting end-user equipment and potentially triggering cascading failures. This paper presents a novel approach for voltage control using Static Var Generators (SVGs) optimized through Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm. The proposed method integrates Lyapunov stability constraints within the RL training process to ensure stability, addressing a key challenge where conventional RL policies lack formal guarantees for system stability. The results validate the method’s effectiveness in maintaining voltage within acceptable ranges under dynamic conditions, offering a viable solution for real-world power system applications.

articleTitle: Interpretable Deep Learning for Strategic Behavior Analysis in Joint Electricity and Carbon Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of carbon markets with the electricity sector represents a crucial development in aligning economic activities with environmental goals, particularly in China. Generation companies (GenCos) navigate these coupled markets through strategic bidding behaviors influenced by various carbon emission allowance (CEA) allocation methods. This study explores how different market conditions and regulatory policies shape GenCo bidding strategies, employing deep learning models like GAN to model these behaviors. To enhance interpretability, we utilize Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and introduce a Bayesian extension (BayLIME), which leverages empirical data and prior knowledge for a more robust analysis. The results demonstrate significant correlations between operational features and strategic dimensions, providing insights that could aid in optimizing market performance and ensuring compliance. The application of BayLIME particularly enhances the reliability and consistency of model explanations, offering a clearer understanding of market dynamics for stakeholders. The findings contribute to both strategic planning and policy-making efforts aimed at fostering a sustainable energy market.

articleTitle: Review of Lithium-Ion Battery Energy Storage Systems: Topology, Power Allocation, and SOC Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As increasement of the clean energy capacity, lithium-ion battery energy storage systems (BESS) play a crucial role in addressing the volatility of renewable energy sources. However, the efficient operation of these systems relies on optimized system topology, effective power allocation strategies, and accurate state of charge (SOC) estimation. This review aims to clarify the current state of these key technologies and provide a theoretical foundation for enhancing the reliability of energy storage systems. The paper summarizes the topology and power allocation strategies of lithium-ion BESS and reviews various SOC estimation models and methods.

articleTitle: An Integrated "Electricity-GEC-Carbon" Market Clearing Model on Urban-level Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the adoption of carbon reduction policies, the power market is becoming more and more interfered by the carbon emission and green electricity certificate (GEC) markets. This paper investigates an integrated "electricity-GEC-carbon" market clearing model on the urban power grid in order to analyze the market interaction among the three markets. Case studies show that the market behaviors of generation units and the total carbon emission amount are deeply influenced by the market interaction.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Capacity and Line Configuration Based on Operation Economy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the challenges of enhancing system reliability and reducing operational costs through energy storage, a two-phase energy storage optimization configuration method is proposed. This method comprehensively considers the reliability and operational economy of the distribution network. Firstly, the planning focuses on a single-point access model for the energy storage system (ESS), establishing a dual-layer multi-objective planning operation model. The upper layer aims to minimize the sum of energy storage investment costs, system outage penalty costs, and overall operational costs. In contrast, the lower layer seeks to minimize the sum of comprehensive operational costs, including network losses, power quality, and load fluctuation operational costs, to devise an energy storage planning and operation scheme. Then, the method examines a multi-point access model for ESS following the addition of new power supply cables, with the optimization goal of maximizing reliability improvement benefits, resulting in a new cable planning scheme. Finally, employing a modified IEEE 33-node system as a case study, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated across different scenarios.

articleTitle: A Reliability Evaluation Method for Integrated Energy System with Hydrogen Considering Gas Inertia and Delay of Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper proposes a reliability evaluation method for electricity-gas integrated energy system (IEGS) with hydrogen considering gas inertia and delay of flow. Firstly, based on the mathematical models of coupled components and new energy sources of wind, solar and hydrogen in IEGS, the multi-energy flow calculation method and load shedding model are proposed. Secondly, the effects of gas inertia and delay of flow on the failure and recovery process of IEGS are demonstrated, and the model for modified IEGS timing process and load point reliability indices is derived. Thirdly, reliability indices and improved reliability evaluation methods applicable to IEGS with hydrogen are proposed. Finally, the effects of considering gas inertia and delay of flow, independent and coupled operation of the system, the addition of wind and solar units, and the utilization of hydrogen energy on the reliability of the IEGS are verified by combining with practical cases to prove the validity of the adopted method.

articleTitle: Coupling Electricity Market with Emission Allowance Market: Problems and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper explores the frameworks for renewable electricity in China, focusing on market-based mechanisms that integrate renewable energy generation with the evolving electricity market and carbon trading systems. It examines Guaranteed Purchase (GP) obligations, participation in the regular electricity market, and the Renewable Electricity Market (REM), which reflect distinct methods for renewable power plants (RPPs) to engage in electricity sales and achieve economic gains. Additionally, the paper delves into the coupling of the electricity and emission allowance markets, identifying critical issues related to the use of green certificates (GECs), the risk of double counting emissions reductions, and the calculation of emission factors for embedded electricity. By proposing a dynamic method for calculating emission factors, the study offers a pathway for more precise carbon accounting, promoting environmental integrity in China's transition toward a low-carbon energy system. The paper concludes with policy recommendations to enhance GEC credibility, address double-counting risks, and align China's renewable energy systems with international best practices.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Load Recovery Method for Power-Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To improve the load recovery effect in post-disaster cities, a collaborative load recovery method for power-transportation system is proposed. First, based on the building envelope and the power-transportation network, a collaborative load recovery model is established. Then, considering the auxiliary role of road repair and electric buses, a three-stage collaborative load recovery strategy is proposed. Finally, a typical failure scenario is used to verify the superiority of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation Method of Multi-element Electric Hydrogen Fusion System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The comprehensive modeling and simulation method of multi-element electric hydrogen fusion system, are proposed in this paper. The corresponding control strategy for all the power electronic converters are designed to adapt the condition of power fluctuation and bi-directional energy flow. The typical energy and power flow mode of the system and the efficiency of the hydrogen production component are analyzed, which can be applied for the preliminary planning and design for this sort of integrated offshore clean energy system.

articleTitle: Study on the Aging Characteristics of Retired O-Ring Seals in Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Transformers are integral to the functionality of power systems. Yet, they are susceptible to the deteriorative impacts of persistent exposure to adverse environmental conditions, including moisture, elevated temperatures, mechanical stress, and salt fog, which can cause the O-ring seals within these transformers to degrade over time. The advanced aging of these seals can culminate in their failure, potentially resulting in critical safety incidents, such as the leakage of transformer oil. Nitrile rubber has become a prevalent material in transformer sealing systems, largely due to its extended service life, economic efficiency, and favorable elastic properties. Currently, artificial accelerated aging methodologies are frequently employed to examine the aging characteristics of seals; however, these methods often fail to account for the full spectrum of environmental aging factors. In contrast, the direct assessment of the performance of O-ring seals that have naturally aged over an extended period presents a more accurate approach to studying their aging characteristics. This study focuses on O-ring seals from a transformer involved in an oil leakage incident within a power grid in southern China, scrutinizing the aging characteristics of these retired nitrile rubber O-ring seals, which have been in service for a duration of 15 years. A suite of tests and characterization techniques, including hardness, mass, dimensional analysis, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), macroscopic examination, microscopic analysis, and elemental composition assessment, have been utilized to elucidate their aging properties. The findings from this research are instrumental in enhancing the materials and design of seals, thereby reducing the incidence of oil leakage incidents. This contributes significantly to the safety and stability of the power system, ensuring its reliable operation.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Integration and Development of Energy Network, Transportation Network, and Information Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Amid the rapid development of modern society and the growing demands of daily life, the integration of energy, transportation, and information networks is becoming an inevitable trend. This article examines the advantages, necessity, methods, and system architecture of integrating these three networks and summarizes their system structure, detailing the main functions of each layer. Additionally, examples of the integration, including smart energy, smart transportation, and smart cities, are provided. Finally, this article concludes by identifying current challenges and forecasting future development trends.

Author Keywords: the integration of the three networks

articleTitle: A Bi-level Economic Dispatch considering Battery Degradation Prediction Model for Microgrids with Hybrid Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources (RES) and energy storage systems (ESS) offers significant potential benefits to users. However, the intermittency of RES introduces volatility and uncertainty to power systems. To address the limitation of traditional models, which often focus solely on short-term economic benefits and fail to effectively integrate long- and short-term energy management, we propose a two-layer microgrid economic dispatch model based on a hybrid energy storage system (HESS-TEM) comprising battery energy storage (BESS) and compressed air energy storage (CAES). In this model, CAES is leveraged for long-term energy management, while BESS provides short-term power compensation to minimize prediction errors. Additionally, a neural network-based battery degradation cost prediction model (NN-BDC) is incorporated to capture the nonlinear degradation dynamics of batteries by factoring in key indicators, including environmental temperature, charge-discharge rate, state of charge, state of health, and depth of discharge. Experimental results demonstrate that HESS-TEM achieves strong economic performance and stability under various pricing schemes, with NN-BDC showing a notable advantage in accurately capturing complex battery degradation behaviors. This model provides an effective solution to enhance the economic viability and stability of microgrids with high RES penetration.

articleTitle: Transient stability assessment of power system based on Bayesian deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The gradual development of China's power grid has formed the current pattern of cross regional interconnected power grid with ultra-high/ultra-high voltage AC/DC hybrid connection, which has effectively promoted the optimized allocation and utilization of primary energy nationwide. However, with the rapid growth of model dimensions in the power system, traditional model driven power grid stability analysis and control decision-making techniques are difficult to achieve real-time perception of power grid safety and stability, and are prone to missing opportunities for power grid regulation. Therefore, there is an urgent need for a more effective power system transient stability assessment technology. This article proposes a transient stability assessment method for power systems based on Bayesian deep learning. Using Bayesian deep neural networks to learn and extract the data distribution of transient stability boundaries; Based on variational inference method, Bayesian deep neural network parameters are trained on big data to obtain an artificial intelligence based stability evaluation model for power grid faults. This model can more accurately predict the transient stability of power grid operation mode and objectively measure the reliability of artificial intelligence model prediction results, overcoming the shortcomings of traditional deterministic neural networks in easily misjudging stability in system critical states.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Control Strategy for Distribution Networks Considering Active Support of Distributed Photovoltaic Power Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasing scale of distributed photovoltaic grid-connectedness will inevitably bring a lot of pressure on the traditional distribution network, and will also have a direct impact on the topology and operation mode of the distribution network. Therefore, the study of reactive power optimization for this has been urgently needed. This paper analyzes the impact on network current distribution, node voltage phasors, and network losses. In order to solve the voltage quality problem, a mathematical model for reactive power optimization with the objective of minimizing active network loss and voltage deviation is developed. In order to improve the solving ability of the model, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is used. The arithmetic example is verified in the IEEE-33 node distribution system, and the results show the correctness of the model and the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Design and Temperature Field Analysis of hybrid Excitation Alternating pole Permanent Magnet Linear Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid-excitation alternating-pole permanent magnet linear motor is proposed. The structure integrates the topology of two kinds of alternating pole permanent magnet linear motors. The flux linkage intersection of the permanent magnets between the primary and secondary in the same direction further improves the thrust density of the motor and increases the flux utilization rate of the internal space of the motor. By analyzing the magnetic circuit direction of the motor, the network topology of the motor is established, and the space air gap permeance of the motor is calculated. Through the finite element analysis of the motor, the electromagnetic characteristics of the motor under no-load and load conditions are obtained and the structure of the motor is optimized. Finally, the temperature rise analysis of the motor is carried out, and the temperature rise curve and temperature field distribution cloud diagram of each part of the motor under the working condition are obtained, which further illustrates the rationality of the motor in this state.

articleTitle: Energy Cooperation Optimization Strategy Of Multipark Integrated Energy System Considering Electrical and Heating Power Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low energy efficiency and high carbon emission, an energy cooperation optimization strategy for multi-park integrated energy system (IES) considering electrical and heating power interaction was proposed. Firstly, the cooperative operation framework and model of multi-park IES based on electrical and heating power interaction are constructed. Secondly, the energy cooperation optimization model based on Nash negotiation is constructed, and distributed solution is completed by alternate direction multiplier method(ADMM). Finally the contribution factors of electrical and heating energy are considered to redistribute the benefits of the multi-park IES alliance. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the strategy in economy, low carbon and environmental protection.

articleTitle: Research on Voltage Sag Suppression Method Based on Improved Sparrow Optimization Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In view of the increasing proportion of sensitive loads (SL) such as high-speed computers and frequency converters in the power system, in order to effectively improve power quality, a hybrid configuration and optimization method of Shunt Capacitor Bank and Distribution Generator (DG) considering the severity of voltage sag of sensitive loads is proposed, while taking into account the effect of system voltage sag management. Firstly, considering the impact of voltage sag amplitude and duration on sensitive loads, the effects of both amplitude and duration are integrated to quantify the severity of the consequences of sensitive loads being affected by voltage sag; Next, with the goal of reducing the active power loss and the severity of sensitive load voltage in the power system, a joint optimization configuration model for SCB and DG is constructed, and an enhanced swarm intelligence optimization algorithm that improves the sparrow search algorithm is proposed to optimize the joint model; Finally, the proposed optimization method was validated by selecting the IEEE 33-node distribution network system for simulation, results show that the method proposed in the paper can provide effective reference for modern power grid energy quality management.

articleTitle: A Review on Two-stage Robust Optimal Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants Containing Wind Power Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of my country's power industry and the needs of economic growth, the consumption of fossil energy by the power system is increasing. Natural fossil energy reserves such as coal are declining year by year and the burning of a lot of fossil energy will cause air pollution. As a clean and renewable energy source, wind power is occupying an increasingly important position in China, however, the integration of wind power will have a bad affect to the power system. The operation mode of the virtual power plant can provide good operating conditions for the grid connection of wind turbines, realize the efficient use of wind energy, and reduce the wind curtailment rate caused by grid connection. Due to the strong randomness and intermittence of wind power [1], it is a problem that needs to be studied to optimize the scheduling of virtual power plants with grid-connected wind power. This paper first constructs the structure of the virtual power plant, including thermal power and hydropower units, interruptible loads, energy storage equipment and wind power units, establishes objective functions and constraints, and builds a two-stage robust optimal dispatch model. In response to the uncertainty of wind power output and load supply, the formulated dispatching plan has better operating economy. In order to solve the min-max-min two-stage robust model, a column constraint generation algorithm is used to divide the model into a main problem and a sub-problem, then use strong duality theory to convert the subproblem into a single-layer solution to the maximum value problem, and use the big-M algorithm to linearize the subproblem. Finally, an example is given to verify the economics of the two-stage robust optimization scheduling model scheduling scheme, which can greatly reduce the scheduling operating cost compared with the deterministic optimal scheduling scheme. Then the effects of different robust adjustment parameters and wind power output fluctuation values on the scheduling results are analyzed, and the effectiveness of the algorithm is proved by simulating the scheduling results in different operating scenarios.

articleTitle: A Variational Inequality Approach for Modeling Bounded Rationality in Electric Vehicle User Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicle ownership will inevitably impact the operational state of coupled power-transportation networks. It is crucial to study how to effectively incorporate the rational behavior of users and guide them in the cooperative scheduling and interaction of the coupled network. In this context, this paper proposes a coupled network model that accounts for the bounded rational behavior of electric vehicle users. First, we construct a second-order cone optimization model of the distribution network that incorporates electric vehicle charging demand. Second, we establish a transportation user equilibrium model that considers bounded rationality, which is equivalently described by variational inequalities. Based on this framework, we design an algorithm that combines immobile point iteration and projection-contraction to solve the coupled network. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and method through arithmetic simulation, and the results demonstrate the necessity of considering bounded rationality in the decision-making processes of user behavior within coupled networks.

articleTitle: Enhanced Photovoltaic Power Forecasting: An iTransformer and LSTM-Based Model Integrating Temporal and Covariate Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is critical for integrating renewable energy sources into the grid, optimizing real-time energy management, and ensuring energy reliability amidst increasing demand. However, existing models often struggle with effectively capturing the complex relationships between target variables and covariates, as well as the interactions between temporal dynamics and multivariate data, leading to suboptimal forecasting accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a novel model architecture that leverages the iTransformer for feature extraction from target variables and employs long short-term memory (LSTM) to extract features from covariates. A cross-attention mechanism is integrated to fuse the outputs of both models, followed by a Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) mapping for enhanced representation. The effectiveness of the proposed model is validated using publicly available datasets from Australia, with experiments conducted across four seasons. Results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively capture seasonal variations in PV power generation and improve forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Energy Scheduling of VPPs with Renewable Generation: A Hybrid Data-Driven Convex Hull Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of energy scheduling under uncertainty for virtual power plants (VPPs) with renewable energy sources. While existing robust scheduling methods using uncertainty sets offer solutions to handle renewable generation variability, they often struggle to balance between conservatism and computational efficiency. We propose a novel data-driven approach that combines ellipsoidal uncertainty sets (EUS) with a hybrid convex hull uncertainty set (HCHUS) to overcome these limitations. First, we develop a minimum-volume ellipsoid method to construct an EUS that comprehensively covers potential renewable energy outputs while minimizing over-conservatism. To enhance computational efficiency, we then approximate the non-linear EUS using an HCHUS composed of rectangular and diamond convex hulls. Results demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves an effective balance between solution accuracy and computational tractability, offering a practical tool for VPP energy scheduling in both day-ahead and real-time markets.

articleTitle: Research on the Multi-User Behavior Modeling Methods Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing integration of flexible resources, such as a high percentage of new energy sources connected to the grid, distributed power generation, and controllable loads, significant uncertainty arises regarding sources, loads, and grid operation trends. Consequently, the behavioral modeling of this new class of electric loads is essential. In this paper, a collection of meteorological statistical features closely related to multivariate user behavior is developed. The fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm is then applied to group the load features, resulting in clusters that align with user behavior patterns. To thoroughly capture the mapping relationships within these multivariate user behavior clusters, the XGBoost algorithm for integrated learning is introduced, enabling adaptive classification and prediction of multivariate user behavior, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the modeling process. A multivariate load dataset from a province in Southwest China is utilized, resulting in significant improvements in prediction accuracy and model generalization compared to traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Disturbance Factor Measurement and Whole Process Control Technology for Grid Infrastructure Project Investment Balance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As China's power grid continues to develop and power system reforms advance, investment projects in power grid infrastructure are increasingly facing diversified disturbances and challenges in supervision. This paper proposes a disturbance measurement and whole-process control technology designed to ensure balanced investment in power grid infrastructure projects. Firstly, based on historical and key project databases, a project progress diagram representing both expected and actual execution of each project is established, allowing for statistical analysis of deviation sources and ranges. Secondly, using the PESTR analysis model and the deviation source statistical set, internal and external disturbances affecting the project execution process are identified from both the internal and external environments of the power grid. Key disturbances are refined through the grey correlation analysis method. Simultaneously, for different stages of project execution, a project control index set is established based on the Triple Rate Integration and the deviation range statistical set. Key indicators are screened using the minimum mean method and the maximum extreme difference method, with the relative weights of each indicator level determined through subjective and objective weighting methods. A whole-process control model is established to assess the risks of projects across various voltage levels. Finally, the explanation structure model is used to analyze the transmission chain of multi-dimensional disturbances, and the influence path between disturbances and control indicators is mapped through a quantitative analysis model, thereby constructing a quantitative analysis model for balanced power grid investment under multiple disturbances.

articleTitle: Cost-Benefit Analysis Method for Disaster Prevention and Restoration Resource Investment in Power Systems Based on Resilience Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A resilient power system is crucial for ensuring the power stability and safety. Pre-allocating flexible resources ensures of power system’s reliable supply. This article studies an analysis method for resource investment from an angle of cost-effectiveness. A probabilistic resilience assessment method is used to evaluate performance during the disaster. The life cycle cost model is also applied to analysis. The proposed framework offers guidance to power system in resource investment planning.

articleTitle: GPU-Accelerated Power Flow Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In recent years, the increasing complexity of modern power systems has made power flow analysis increasingly important. The matrix-vectorized model for power flow analysis based on the Newton-Raphson framework involves numerous complex operations during computation, such as indexing operations, which significantly degrade performance in a GPU environment. This paper presents a novel GPU-accelerated method for power flow computation aimed at improving computational efficiency and memory management. To further improve the efficiency of sparse matrix indexing on GPUs, we introduce two novel indexing techniques: spGEMM and kernel indexing. The spGEMM method achieves slicing of sparse matrices by utilizing matrix multiplication in place of indexing operations. The kernel indexing approach employs a kernel function in combination with the storage principles of the compressed sparse row (CSR) format to perform matrix indexing, thereby enabling the slicing operation. Simulation results conducted with varying numbers of buses demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms traditional CPU-based approaches in terms of computation speed and scalability. The findings indicate that the proposed indexing techniques effectively improve the speed of power flow analysis and optimize its memory management.

articleTitle: Uncovering Temperature-Load Sensitivity via Structure Modeling and IVGMM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurately capturing the temperature sensitivity of electricity demand contributes to efficiently managing power system operation. Conventional approaches typically attempt to reduce uncertainties by incorporating temperature as a feature within forecasting models to improve load forecasting accuracy. However, such models often fail to quantify the degree of temperature sensitivity at each time point. In this paper, we leverage structure modeling and Instrument Variable Generalized Method of Moments (IVGMM) to estimate the dynamic temperature sensitivity of electricity demand. Structure modeling explores the relationship between actual load value, time series forecasting results, and external weather factors through multivariate statistical analysis and Structure Equation Modeling (SEM). The time series forecasting results, representing expected electricity demand at each time point, are generated by a deep learning module including a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU). Based on the uncovered relationships between variables, IVGMM provides robust parameter estimates to the model. In the case study, the proposed process is validated to achieve accurate quantification of temperature impact on load and well capture irregular patterns of fluctuations in load.

articleTitle: Research on Unit Combination Optimization Model Considering the Change of Climbing Rate under Deep Adjustment of Coal fired Power Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the growth of global energy demand and the intensification of environmental problems, the development and utilization of new energy are facing challenges, and the comprehensive regulation and system optimization of coal-fired power and new energy have become hot topics. How to solve the coordination and integration problem between coal-fired power and new energy, and achieve stable operation and efficient utilization of the system, has become an urgent problem to be solved. The power structure in China is mainly composed of coal-fired power units, and improving the flexibility and deep peak shaving capability of coal-fired power units is the key. Traditional optimization scheduling generally takes minimizing system energy consumption or power generation costs as the optimization objective. Based on this, research has further extended the objective to new energy consumption and low-carbon environmental protection, proposing more comprehensive and balanced optimization models. However, there is still a lack of research on the changes in climbing rate of coal-fired power units after flexibility transformation. This article constructs a segmented climbing rate optimization model for coal-fired power units on AIMMS software, studies the unit combination optimization method considering changes in climbing rate, and verifies the effectiveness of the model based on provincial power grid data.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Joint Chance-Constrained Scheduling for Integrated Energy System Considering Symmetric-Unimodality Information of Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, their unpredictable characteristics bring remarkable challenges to the stable operation of integrated heat and electricity systems. In this paper, we propose a distributionally robust (DR) joint chance-constrained scheduling model considering renewable energy uncertainties. Firstly, an optimal scheduling model of integrated energy system including conventional generators, wind power plants, combined heat and power units and electric boilers is developed taking into account system operational constraints such as heat transfer time-delay comprehensively. A moment-based ambiguity is established to characterize the uncertainty whose symmetric and unimodality information is taken into consideration. The adopted ambiguity notably reduces conservatism compared to single-moment metrics. By introducing optimized Bonferroni approximation (OBA), the DR joint chance constraints are transformed into DR individual chance constraints. Due to the intractability of OBA formulation, we employ convex approximations to convert it into tractable forms. Case studies performed on the test system demonstrate that the proposed methodology can effectively reduce system costs and conservatism.

articleTitle: Research on Tree Line Grounding Fault Identification Technology Based on Improved YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Aiming at the frequently occurring tree line ground fault recognition challenges in power systems, the article uses the improved YOLOv8 model for the study. By integrating the KAN neural network architecture and adopting the EIoU loss function to improve the bounding box prediction accuracy, the accuracy of the model is improved, which makes up for the accuracy limitation problem faced by the traditional YOLOv8 model in the power system image recognition task. The experimental results show that a significant increase of 1.7% in precision, 9% in recall, and 6.9% in average precision (mAP_0.5) is achieved while maintaining the original processing speed, which verifies the effectiveness of the method in improving the power system image data processing precision and fault feature recognition effectiveness.

articleTitle: Active Islanding Strategy for Distribution Networks Containing Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the increasing share of distributed generation in the power market, the intelligent operation of power grids, operation costs, and fault-based repair strategies of distribution networks are all affected. For the challenges brought by this new situation, an in-depth study of the island partition strategy for distribution networks containing distributed generation sources is crucial for improving the operational stability, power supply reliability, and power supply quality of distribution networks. After introducing some basic concepts of island partition, this paper proposes that in order to realize islanding, the principles of network topology, matching degree of distributed generation output and load demand must be satisfied. Then for the inadequacy of the current island partition strategy in the optimization degree, a more reasonable and efficient optimization scheme is provided after analysis and comparison. The scheme takes into account the core elements of distributed generation output characteristics, network structure and load demand, and combines the constraints of voltage, current and load classification, and finally selects the depth-first search algorithm for island partition. Finally, in order to verify the rationality and feasibility of the algorithm, simulation is carried out with the help of the IEEE 33-node system, and compared and analyzed with the actual operation data. The results show that the strategy has significant advantages in improving power supply reliability, reducing network loss and optimizing resource allocation.

articleTitle: The Model and Outlook of Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the growing global demand for clean energy, hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) are increasingly becoming a key solution to address energy shortages and reduce carbon emissions. This paper evaluates the major renewable energy sources (RES), including wind, solar, hydropower, geothermal, and biomass, and their integration into hybrid systems. It also explores various energy storage solutions, such as batteries, pumped hydroelectric storage, and hydrogen storage. Future research directions are discussed, focusing on emerging energy storage technologies to promote the development of energy sustainability.

articleTitle: Exploration of New Power System Protection Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the proposal of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, the construction of a new power system dominated by new energy generation has become a key issue in the current energy structure transformation. With the introduction of new energy and power electronic equipment, power systems, fault diagnosis, and protection systems have become increasingly complex. The design of future protection urgently requires clear guidance on protection architecture. This article defines protection architecture as a series of abstract patterns aimed at achieving protection objectives. The significance of protection architecture lies in providing guidance for protection design in increasingly complex scenarios, while maintaining the rationality of the protection system's own design while clarifying the achievement of protection goals. The traditional power system protection architecture essentially protects the system by protecting equipment, utilizing three-phase electrical information and switch values to achieve pattern recognition-based assessment goals. The new power system has introduced new energy generation and power electronic equipment marked by converters, changing the operating characteristics of the system and proposing new protection requirements. Power electronic devices are quickly controlled and fragile. Rapid and controlled changes have altered the operational and fault characteristics of the protected equipment, blurred the boundary between faults and non-faults, and increased fault chain paths. Based on the protection requirements of the new power system, this article proposes that the new power system protection architecture should protect the system through protection equipment, while blocking fault chain and optimizing equipment protection through the protection system. By collecting and communicating electrical information and control status across all frequency bands, conducting fault analysis based on pattern recognition of modified electrical quantities, implementing coordinated protection between primary and backup protection, optimizing multi-interval control and electrical information interaction, the top-level goal of the protection architecture is achieved. Finally, this article proposes a typical protection scheme based on a new power system protection architecture, which adopts a control coordination method to expand the adaptability range of traditional protection. It provides a reference for the design of protection schemes and the integration of control and protection in future new power systems.

articleTitle: Research on a Short-Term Electricity Price Forecasting Model Based on SSA-ESN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Against the backdrop of the increasing integration of renewable energy sources, the dynamic characteristics of the electricity market have become more complex, with a significant increase in electricity price volatility, posing higher demands for the accuracy of electricity price forecasting. Current neural network models all have certain limitations. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a hybrid model based on Echo State Networks (ESN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) for electricity market price forecasting. The model first uses ESN for feature extraction to capture the deep structure and complex patterns of the data. Then, a Bi-directional LSTM network model is designed, which utilizes its sequential learning ability for electricity price prediction. Additionally, the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) is employed for parameter optimization. Through empirical analysis and comparative experiments, the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid model in enhancing the accuracy of electricity price forecasts has been validated, particularly when dealing with highly volatile datasets, demonstrating good robustness and predictive performance. Moreover, the model is adaptable to different market conditions, providing more precise decision support for participants in the electricity market.

articleTitle: Integrated Planning and Operation Optimization of Distributed Integrated Energy Systems Synergizing the Multiple Distributed Power Sources and Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Along with the rapid development of renewable energy, the application of distributed power sources in the distribution network is becoming increasingly popular, and the equipping of energy storage systems is indispensable. This paper proposes a collaborative planning methodology aimed at accomplishing the holistic planning of distributed power sources and energy storage in order to improve the economy and reliability of distribution network operation. An economical and reliable planning scheme is developed by constructing a holistic optimization model that takes into account a variety of factors, including load fluctuations, renewable energy output characteristics, voltage smoothness and economics of the distribution network. The results of the study show that the voltage stability is improved by 9.6% and the total planning and operating cost is reduced by 2.9% after adding the energy storage system for collaborative planning, which has better safety, reliability, and economy. Finally, the validation based on actual cases proves the effectiveness and feasibility of the planning method, and the research results of this thesis provide theoretical guidance for the intelligent development of distribution networks and further promote the reform of energy structure.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Method of Medium and Low Voltage AC / DC Distribution System for Distributed Resource Access
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Given many problems caused by large-scale distributed power access, such as power reverse transmission, equipment/line overload, voltage over-limit, and so on, they are essentially caused by the inability of distributed power to absorb. With the rise of distributed energy and the deepening of the research on power electronic power systems, the flexible use of electric energy in the form of DC has been widely discussed. Distributed power supply and energy storage devices can be integrated into the system from the DC side, which reduces the inverter link of power electronic equipment, reduces the cost and loss, and improves the reliability of the power supply. To adapt to different types of power sources and loads, the distribution network is gradually developing into an AC/DC hybrid distribution network model. In this paper, the medium and low voltage AC/DC distribution network (M&L-V AC/DC DN) with distributed power supply, energy storage, and electric vehicle access is taken as the research object. A centralized-distributed coordinated medium and low voltage double-layer control architecture is established. The medium and low voltage control model and the model-solving algorithm based on the particle swarm optimization algorithm are established. The power flow calculation method of the AC / DC system is proposed. Several working conditions are set up to verify the effectiveness and applicability of the control architecture and model proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Evaluating Multi-dimensional Response Capability of Adjustable Resources in New Urban Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of low-carbon energy, the overall regulation capacity of the power system is gradually declining. It is necessary to explore new regulatory resources within the modern urban power grid (NUPG) to support this. This article proposes a method for assessing the response capacity of adjustable resources in modern urban power grids, quantitatively evaluating their response capabilities. First, a method for assessing the response capacity of individual resources is proposed. This involves evaluating the online response capability of individual electric buses and central air conditioning loads, as well as their response capabilities under different scheduling instructions. Next, a multidimensional response capacity assessment method for adjustable resources based on BP neural networks is proposed. This method evaluates the multidimensional response capabilities of the aggregated units of electric bus load (EBL) and central air conditioning loads (CACL), including rapid response capability, sustainable response capability, and continuous response capability. Finally, a multi-dimensional response capability assessment method for the new urban power grid is proposed, which considers the consumption of load-side resources due to the internal operations of NUPG and presents the capability of regulating the net load for external purposes. The results indicate that the proposed model can effectively improve the accuracy of the aggregate unit response capability assessment, and quantitatively provide rapid, continuous, and sustained network-level response capabilities.

articleTitle: Scenario Generation Method for Provincial Summer Load Based on Load Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The provincial summer load scenario is of significance for the adequacy assessment and the planning of the power resource. In this regard, a summer load scenario generation method based on the load decomposition idea is proposed. Firstly, the power consumption curve is constructed by considering the impact of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power on the original grid load. The power consumption curve is decomposed into two components, namely the basic load and the temperature-related load. Secondly, the basic load is a partial load component determined by the law of social production development. The improved multivariate grey system is used to establish the correlation model between key indicators of social development and basic load, which is used to realize the future scenario of basic load. Then, the temperature-related load is a load component affected by meteorological factors. And the TCN-Transformer model that considering the spatiotemporal characteristics of temperature factors and classification of summer weather processes is established to realize the scenario generation of temperature-related load. Finally, given the social development indicators, summer meteorological data and distributed PV power installed capacity of the planning target year, the above model can be used to generate summer load scenario. And the load data of the provincial power grid are analyzed as an example to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A BERT-Based Method for Residential Behind-the-Meter PV Monitoring with NILM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) has become a key technique for enhancing residential energy awareness, efficiency, and management. However, many existing NILM approaches aim to disaggregate explicit load profiles based on the smart meter data, neglecting the impact of behind-the-meter Photovoltaic (PV) systems. As most standard smart meters only record the net household load, these methods may not perform well in scenarios where PV generation is present. The absence of dedicated devices to accurately capture PV output further limits the real-world applicability of such methods. To address this, we propose a BERT-based NILM method that utilizes only hourly meter data and weather information to simultaneously disaggregate appliance-level loads and PV export. Compared to other conventional approaches, our method incorporates an embedding module to learn latent variables representing the context of the residence. Experimental results using real-world hourly data from Texas show that our method can reduce the root-mean-square error by 34.6%, lower the normalized disaggregation error and mean-absolute error 43.8%, 38.7% separately, and improve disaggregation accuracy by 2.7% compared to vanilla BERT model.

articleTitle: GRU-ATT high-precision short-term PV power combination prediction model combining improved MVMD and INFO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The objective of this study is to address the issue of inadequate prediction accuracy in short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. To this end, we propose a novel combined prediction model that integrates the gated recurrent unit (GRU) with an enhanced multivariate variational modal decomposition (MVMD) and a vector-weighted averaging algorithm (INFO), along with an attention mechanism (ATT). Initially, the improved multivariate variational mode decomposition (iMVMD), or iMVMD, is employed to decompose the original data, thereby reducing the volatility of historical photovoltaic (PV) power generation data. Secondly, the improved INFO (imINFO) is employed to optimize the GRU and ascertain its optimal parameters, thereby enhancing the performance of the GRU model. Additionally, the attention mechanism is integrated to accentuate the more pivotal influencing factors, thereby enabling the GRU neural network to render more precise assessments. Ultimately, the dataset of photovoltaic power plants in the Ningxia region of China is selected for predictive analysis. The findings demonstrate that the combined prediction model proposed in this paper can markedly enhance the prediction accuracy of PV power.

articleTitle: Graph-Based Electricity Carbon Sensitivity Analysis for Distribution Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the intensification of global climate change, achieving carbon peak and carbon neutrality has become a key objective for many nations. As one of the major sources of carbon emissions, the power system’s carbon emission characteristics are closely tied to power flow within the grid. This paper proposed a graph-based algorithm for analyzing the electricity carbon sensitivity of generating units in a distribution network, aiming to identify the impact of various generating units on the carbon emissions of the target substation based on the network’s topology and power flow estimation results. First, the paper constructed a graph model of the distribution network, defining its topological connections and employing graph computation to obtain power flow estimations. Then, a graph parallel supply path search algorithm and a recursive supply percentage calculation for a distribution substation were developed. Finally, an electricity carbon sensitivity analysis method was proposed by integrating the carbon emissions of different types of units to achieve the rapid carbon flow trace. Using a provincial distribution network in Southwest China as a case study, the proposed method was validated for its rationality and feasibility. Results showed that the algorithm efficiently and accurately calculated the carbon sensitivity of units, which contributed to the optimization of carbon emissions in the power grid and promoted the adoption of clean energy.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Strategy of Distribution Network with Distributed Photovoltaic Based on Optimization Search Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The widespread adoption of distributed solar photovoltaic technology has enabled distribution networks to manage the voltage levels at critical nodes through precise control of the reactive power supplied to the grid. This study has developed an adaptive voltage control scheme specifically designed for distribution networks integrated with large-scale photovoltaic resources. The scheme employs an advanced optimization search algorithm to automatically adjust the PI parameters of the voltage controller, ensuring flexible adaptation to real-time system fluctuations. The PI gain of the voltage controller minimizes the cost function that reflects the performance of the voltage controller through online updating. A distribution network model containing a 5MW PV system is constructed in MATLAB/Simulink to test the proposed self-adaptive voltage controller. The simulation results show that the proposed voltage controller can adapt well to load variations and grid faults, and improves the reliability and voltage stability of a power system, compared with the traditional PI controller.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Optimal Configuration for Renewable Energy to Hydrogen to Ammonia System Considering Multiple Operating Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Renewable Energy to Hydrogen to Ammonia (RtHtA) is an innovative approach to alleviate renewable energy consumption issues. It also helps heavy chemical industries transition to a green electricity and hydrogen supply model, significantly reducing carbon emissions. At present, there is no mature solution for the operation mode of the RtHtA system, and exploring low-carbon optimization configuration solutions has become a key research focus. This paper proposes a low-carbon optimization configuration method for the RtHtA system and designs four typical operating modes. And a comparative analysis of the optimal configuration results under these different modes is conducted. The case study verifies the effectiveness of the proposed low-carbon optimal configuration method, which achieves a balance between economic efficiency and low carbon emissions. The results of the case study indicate that, under different operating modes, the RtHtA system has distinct advantages and disadvantages in terms of economics and carbon emissions.

articleTitle: An Improved ARIMA Based Anomaly Detection Method for Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, IoT data processing standards in China are somewhat vague, and monitoring data is typically used in subsequent stages for analysis, prediction modeling, and applications. However, monitoring and control data are often affected by various factors that can introduce anomalies, which in turn impacts intelligent control systems. To improve the quality of monitoring data, this paper addresses the limitations of traditional anomaly detection methods, which often require high similarity in data and face challenges with highly diverse monitoring data. Additionally, traditional ARIMA models are limited by difficulties in parameter selection, threshold determination, and high false-positive rates. Thus, we propose an improved ARIMA-based anomaly detection method for time-series data. This approach encompasses the complete process of monitoring data fitting and prediction, anomaly detection, and anomaly validation. The method has three main features:1.Optimized Parameter Selection: For varied batches of monitoring data, this method combines ACF and PACF plots with AIC and BIC heatmaps to determine optimal ARIMA parameters for each data batch.2.Incorporation of a Sliding Window: A sliding window is used to analyze residual data characteristics within the window, enabling precise anomaly detection for individual data points.3.Anomaly Validation: A K-means clustering algorithm is incorporated to validate initial anomaly detection results.The method was verified in a real-world cigar leaf curing barn, and experimental results demonstrate that it effectively detects anomalies in the IoT monitoring system data, contributing to improved IoT data quality.

articleTitle: Aggregating the data value of multiple application scenarios: a case from electricity market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Electricity market data has diverse application scenarios, making it essential to aggregate value across these scenarios for accurate data evaluation. This paper establishes a multidimensional data value evaluation and aggregation model for data samples, incorporating carbon emission reduction and price forecasting scenarios. These values are based on load forecasting for emissions reduction and electricity price forecasting for power sales company profits. TMC algorithm is used to quickly compute the aggregated value, which is represented by the Shapley value, of data samples. A case study of 183 data samples of electricity market from April to October 2023 in Hebei Province, China, was conducted. The analysis considered three weighting situations, showing that the aggregated value of a single sample ranged from [-300, 300] thousand yuan. Under different situations, the weight allocation strongly influences the distribution of values, with samples from mid-June to late July showing higher aggregated values.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation and Reactive Power Sharing in AC Microgrids: A Non-cooperative Game Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a non-cooperative game (NCG) approach for trade-offs between voltage regulation and reactive power sharing in market-driven AC microgrids. Firstly, the NCG model is constructed, which contains both voltage regulation error and reactive power sharing error. Secondly, a power estimation algorithm is designed to obtain non-neighbor power information in the NCG model. Distributed renewable energy generators (DREGs) only need to share the estimated power values with neighbors. Then, a distributed Nash equilibrium search algorithm is introduced. This approach is proved to be stable under the NCG via the Lyapunov method. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed NCG-based approach for voltage regulation and reactive power sharing is validated through simulations on a 4-DG test microgrid.

articleTitle: Research on the Development Path of New Energy Industry in Qinghai Province from the Perspective of Macro - Electricity – Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Developing new energy industry is the key to accelerating the construction of a new power system and ensuring that China achieves its carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals as scheduled.
