To clarify the progress of new energy industry construction in Qinghai Province (Qinghai), eliminate a series of problems faced in the process of industrial development and clarify the path of industrial development, first, combined with the economic and industrial development situation of Qinghai, the definition and research perspective of Qinghai’s new energy industry are clarified. Secondly, the development status of Qinghai’s new energy industry is analyzed by industry scale and industry chain construction. Thirdly, the problems faced in the actual operation of the new energy industry in Qinghai and the deep-seated reasons are deeply analyzed in terms of macro development, power system and industrial construction. Finally, based on the above research conclusions, relevant suggestions are put forward on how to further promote the development of new energy industry in Qinghai.

articleTitle: A Multi-indicator Multi-objective and Multi-scenario Evaluation Scheme of Energy Storage Applicability Based on Analytic Hierarchy Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Energy storage systems have multiple types of medium, and their application scenarios are diverse and scattered. The evaluation of the energy storage system is a complex evaluation problem with various indicators, objectives, and scenarios. Currently, there is no objective evaluation scheme for the applicability of energy storage systems under different scenarios. This paper proposes a multi-indicator, multi-objective, and multi-scenario applicability evaluation scheme for energy storage systems using the Analytic Hierarchy Process-Entropy Weight Method. The application scenarios and requirements of energy storage were analyzed at first. Then, multiple electrochemical energy storage systems are studied, and evaluation indicators are designed based on four main hierarchies of technical, economic, environmental, and safety. The relative weights of evaluation indicators in multiple scenarios are solved by using weight judgment matrixes to obtain the comprehensive evaluation results of energy storage system applicability. Finally, a case study was conducted on semi-solid lithium-ion batteries, and the evaluation results with the highest applicability in the mobile energy storage for emergency power supply were obtained. The effectiveness and rationality of the above schemes were verified, which is of great significance for promoting the large-scale application of energy storage technology.

articleTitle: Domestic and foreign energy storage participation in electricity market trading: practical analysis and prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Under the background of the "dual carbon" target, the proportion of new energy is gradually increasing, and the rapid development of new energy will bring huge challenges to the stable operation of the power system. In the system of large-scale integration of new energy, energy storage can effectively solve the problems of insufficient grid regulation capacity and increased difficulty in frequency stability caused by a high proportion of renewable energy.This article first analyzes the types, operational characteristics, and cost characteristics of energy storage, and then explores the development of energy storage marketization at home and abroad from the perspective of market practice. Finally, based on the current situation of China's new round of electricity reform and foreign experience, corresponding prospects are proposed for the participation of energy storage in the development of the electricity market in China.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient SOH Estimation for Lithium-ion Batteries via Structural Re-parameterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Online state of health (SOH) estimation is critical for the safety and performance of lithium-ion batteries, especially in dynamic environments like electric vehicles and grid energy storage systems, where accurate monitoring prevents failures and enhances reliability. Convolutional Neural Networks have shown great potentials in SOH estimation. To improve the estimation accuracy, traditional methods focus on increasing the depth and width of the network. The resulting network structure is often complex and difficult to deploy on resource limited mobile devices. Based on the structure reparameterization technique, this paper simplifies the network structure from the training stage to the inference stage. Tuning the hyperparameters of a complex network is not an easy task. In this paper, an advanced hyperparameter optimization engine is used to automatically search for the optimal hyperparameters of the network structure. Finally, in the inference stage, the FLOPs of the model after structure reparameterization are reduced by 16.799% as least. The SOH estimation results on two battery aging datasets demonstrate the superiority and robustness of the proposed model, with a maximum average performance improvement of 21.92%.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Load Forecasting Method Based on Improved iTransformer of Decomposition-Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is crucial for the safe and stable operation of power systems. In order to further improve the accuracy of load forecasting, an improved iTransformer ultra-short-term load forecasting method based on decomposition-reconstruction is proposed. Firstly, the load data is decomposed using time varying filtering-empirical mode decomposition (TVF-EMD) to obtain several intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). The IMF components are then reorganized based on their entropy values using sample entropy (SE). Secondly, the iTransformer neural network is improved by introducing a stand alone attention (SAA) mechanism to replace the self-attention mechanism in the iTransformer encoder, which effectively enhances the model's ability to capture the dependencies of different variables. Finally, the restructured components are input into the improved iTransformer for prediction, and the obtained results are superimposed to obtain the final prediction value. The actual active load dataset of 220kV substations in a region of China is taken as an example for validation and comparison with the existing mainstream models, and the results show that the prediction method adopted in this paper has better prediction performance.

articleTitle: Review of Virtual Power Plants with Multi-source Distributed Resources: Concepts, Applications and Outlook
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to standardize the power curve of the power system, optimize efficiency, reduce costs, and achieve reasonable allocation of power resources, the concept of virtual power plant (VPP) was raised to realize the management and scheduling of distributed power resources. With its light-asset and structured characteristics, VPP can play a key role in scenarios such as the power market. In recent years, there has been a dense research trend on VPP and related topics in academia. This paper summarizes and investigates the research field of VPP with multi-source distributed resources (MDER), gives the definition of VPP, summarizes the common architecture, operation mode and corresponding functions of VPP, and gives the current application status of VPP combined with several specific project cases. In addition, we also collate the evaluation indicators for VPP and propose new evaluation perspectives. Finally, we offer an outlook of future research and application prospects of this field.

articleTitle: Research on Cascading Fault Path Analysis of Power System Based on GPU Parallel Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Recently, the frequency of extreme disasters has increased, leading to higher risk of cascading failures in power system. To solve the problems faced by the overload-dominant cascading fault analysis, this paper proposes a cascading fault path evolution analysis method based on GPU parallel. Case studies confirmed that the overall computation time is reduced by about 50%. This method provides a scientific basis for defense strategies after disaster warnings, thus reducing disaster losses.

articleTitle: Comparison and Testing of Equivalent Modeling Methods for Wind Farm Composed of Doubly-Fed Induction Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: For analyzing the power system with high penetration of wind power, it is important to establish accurate models of wind turbines and wind farms, which is a basic and important work. In the analysis of wind power grid integration, it is necessary to aggregate the equivalent value of the wind farm into one or a few wind turbines. At present, there are two commonly used equivalence methods: current source multiplication (commonly used in commercial software) and full dynamic aggregation method. The former achieves wind farm equivalence by multiplying the output current of a single wind turbine generator, while the latter dynamically aggregates the wind farm into one or several large wind turbine generators. There is still a lack of research on the differences between the two. Based on the actual wind farm structure, this paper studies the electrical characteristics of steady-state operation and transient fault ride through operation using single machine dynamic aggregation method and current source multiplication method separately, and compares the equivalent simulation results with the detailed wind farm simulation results. The equivalent accuracy of the single machine aggregation method and the current source multiplication method is calculated to provide a reference for method selection in wind farm equivalent modeling.

articleTitle: Ultra-Short-term Load Forecasting Using TCN-LSTM with Photovoltaic Penetration Rate and Temporal Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To enhance the accuracy of ultra-short-term load forecasting while accounting for the impact of distributed energy resources, this paper presents a novel TCN-LSTM cascaded model that integrates photovoltaic penetration rates and multi-level temporal feature extraction for distribution transformer area load prediction. The proposed methodology first establishes a relationship model between PV generation and load consumption to quantify the influence of distributed PV systems on local power demand. Subsequently, a multi-level temporal feature extraction framework is introduced to capture multi-scale temporal patterns within load data. The correlation between load and temporal features is quantified using Mutual Information, with strongly correlated features selected as inputs for the Temporal Convolutional Network model. The architecture culminates in a TCN-LSTM cascade model, where TCN predictions and load data serve as inputs to the Long Short-Term Memory network. This design leverages TCN’s advantages in parallel processing and multi-scale feature extraction, while harnessing LSTM’s capability in capturing long-term dependencies. The empirical validation is conducted using load data from a distribution network in a city in southern China. Comparative analyses against standalone machine learning models demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior load forecasting accuracy, robust stability, and enhanced dynamic response capabilities.

articleTitle: Offshore Wind Power Forecasting Method Based on Hybrid Model Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The accurate and real-time offshore wind power forecasting can effectively mitigate the impact of offshore wind power integration on the power system, enhancing its safety, stability, economy, and controllability. However, offshore wind power forecasting currently faces three major challenges: difficulty in identifying anomalous data, high dimensionality of input vectors, and instability in multi-step forecasting. To address these issues, this paper optimizes existing wind power forecasting technologies from three aspects: "data", "feature" and "model", proposing an ultra-short-term power forecasting method for offshore wind power based on DBSCAN-Pearson-Informer. First, a wind power data preprocessing method based on the adaptive DBSCAN algorithm for different wind speed intervals is proposed, which effectively identifies various types of abnormal wind power data and corrects them. Second, a feature selection method for wind power forecasting based on Pearson correlation analysis is proposed, which selects factors highly correlated with wind power as input data for the forecasting model. Finally, an ultra-short-term offshore wind power forecasting model based on Informer is constructed, and the trained model is used to carry out offshore wind power forecasting work. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to classical time-series forecasting models such as LSTM, TCN, and Transformer, the proposed method achieves average percentage improvements in MAE, RMSE, and MBE of 66.11%, 63.02%, and 90.73%, respectively, while also exhibiting higher forecasting stability and faster execution efficiency.

articleTitle: Operating Model Study of Micro Energy Network Considering Economy and Security of Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the development of new energy technology and the growth of rural power demand, the construction of a safe and economic rural distribution network operation mode has become an important research direction. This paper proposes a rural distribution network operation model based on a micro-energy network. Through the " PV self-generation and self-consumption " , " all on-grid " , " energy storage sharing " and " energy mutualisation " , a reasonable combination of operation types is aimed at maximizing the benefits of multiple subjects. This paper analyzes the economics and safety of different mode of operation. A rural distribution network operation strategy that can optimize resource allocation and enhance economic efficiency under the premise of ensuring system stability is proposed. The effectiveness of this operation model in improving system stability and economic efficiency is demonstrated through Case Analysis simulations.

articleTitle: Optimization of Port Integrated Energy Systems Considering the Dissatisfaction of Port Operators with Hydrogen Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Hydrogen energy, as a clean energy source, is increasingly being applied to port operations. However, previous studies on hydrogen energy applications have largely overlooked the impact of hydrogen energy safety on system design. This paper introduces prospect theory in the context of hydrogen-containing ports and proposes a safety dissatisfaction model for port operators based on this theory, which innovatively incorporates their considerations of hydrogen energy safety into the analytical framework. An optimization model of port integrated energy system based on hydrogen safety is developed and formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming problem. The optimization model effectively reduces the operation cost and operator dissatisfaction level of the port through the simulation of a large port example, which validates the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Fault Current Analysis Method for IIRES Considering the Transient Processes of both the PLL and the Current Inner Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the high proportion of renewable energy integration in new type power systems on protection, it is essential to analyze the fault characteristics of renewable energy sources. Renewable energy is often integrated into the grid in the form of inverter-interfaced renewable energy sources (IIRES), and the phase-locked loop (PLL), as a crucial control component for grid integration, directly affects the fault characteristics of these inverters. This paper proposes a fault current analysis method for IIRES that accounts for the transient processes of both the PLL and the current inner loop. By examining the impact of the PLL on the Park transformation, the paper clarifies the influence path of the PLL on the fault current of IIRES. Additionally, it simplifies the effect of the PLL on the transient process of the current inner loop, deriving fault current analytical expressions related to the parameters of both the PLL and the current inner loop. The results are validated through comparison with simulation waveforms.

articleTitle: Pixelization of Steady-state Variables Based Power System Transient Stability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Rapid and accurate implementation of transient stability assessment (TSA) in power systems can improve grid perception capabilities and reduce the likelihood of stability disruptions, making it crucial for the safe operation of power systems. In order to further enhance the speed and accuracy of transient stability assessment, this paper proposes a method for power system transient stability assessment based on pixelization of steady-state characteristic variables and deep machine learning. Firstly, the steady-state power flow data and electrical topology connection information are mapped to a multi-dimensional pixel feature map of active power-reactive power-voltage by using the proposed transfer mechanism, fully utilizing the advantages of convolutional neural networks (CNN) in feature map processing. Multiple deep convolutional neural networks are then used to extract the operating state features of the power grid for transient stability assessment. Finally, the proposed method is validated by using the New England 10-machine 39-bus standard system, and the results show that the data-model fusion optimization model, which fully retains the system topology and the magnitude and direction information of each electrical quantity, improves the performance of transient stability assessment compared to other machine learning methods, providing a new approach for online assessment and analysis of power systems.

articleTitle: A Lightweight MBConv-Based Model for Real-Time Load Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) disaggregates household power consumption into appliance-level data, offering economic and privacy-preserving solution for energy management. However, many SOTA models such as transformers require high computational power and large datasets, posing practical and privacy challenges. Inspired by lightweight CNN advancements, this paper proposes a real-time MBConv-based model that reduces parameters while maintaining strong performance.

articleTitle: Research on the design method of 61850 client for monitoring system of large-capacity wind and solar storage power station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we address the monitoring system requirements for large-capacity wind and solar energy storage power stations by discussing a client design method based on the IEC 61850 standard. Initially, we employed a flow method to analyze the SCD (Substation Configuration Description) model, facilitating data modeling tailored to various device types. Building upon a distributed architecture, we implemented task allocation technology to enhance the efficiency of real-time data acquisition and control command execution. Furthermore, a load balancing strategy was introduced to optimize data processing and alleviate server load. For typical EMS (Energy Management System) applications, two group control strategies were developed: one allows a single control command to be simultaneously applied to multiple PCS (Power Conversion System) units, streamlining operations; while the other maintains precise control over individual PCS units in conventional mode. This dual-mode approach not only accelerates the system's overall response but also ensures high control precision, providing a robust technical foundation for managing and operating large-capacity renewable energy storage facilities.

articleTitle: Coordination optimization of multi-micro-network and distribution network based on multi-agent reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: A distributed coordination method based on hybrid multi-agent reinforcement learning is proposed to solve the problem that the multi-micro-network and distribution network cooperative optimization with discrete devices makes it difficult to solve the problem of efficient computation of non-convex models. By constructing an optimal scheduling model that considers the constraints of regulating resource operation and system security, and introducing multi-agent technology, two agent groups of the distribution micro-network are designed respectively, and the centralized scheduling model is transformed into a distributed optimization problem between cooperative and competitive mixed multi-agents. Then, an improved multi-actor-attention-critic algorithm is proposed to train discrete and continuous action agents at the multi-microgrid-distribution network level to avoid dimension explosion caused by too high state action dimension and realize extensible learning.

Author Keywords: multi-micro-network and distribution network cooperative optimization

articleTitle: Bi-level Optimization of Mobile Energy Storage System Allocation and Scheduling for Grid Stability and Peak Load Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This research examines Mobile Energy Storage Systems (MESS) for improving grid stability and peak shaving in electrical networks. It employs a bi-level optimization approach based on different optimization methods to determine optimal MESS location and operation strategies. Tested across various monthly/seasonal scenarios, this approach is applied to the IEEE 33 bus and 141 bus test systems, considering real data for the consumption behavior of the nodes.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Simulation and Fault Analyses of Photovoltaic Modules from Electronic Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: photovoltaic (PV) power station has become one of the most important energy sources and an indispensable component of the new power system, the traditional PV simulation where the whole station is represented by a single power output formula no longer satisfies the necessity of applicative researches. Ideally, a simulation of PV station is constructed in a bottom-up manner, and the mathematical model at each layer is built from integration of simulations of power electronics, and the hierarchical model of the whole station is verified by realistic reactions of electronic components to replicate real power plants. In this study, a simulation of PV modules is constructed by power electronics, and the simulated individual and combined module reactions are compared with experiments on commercial products. The modules under four most common fault conditions are analyzed down to the electronic level to prepare for precise control strategies of individual modules. The research is supported by abundant experimental data, to enable practical virtual trials and parameter tuning of further fault detection and protection development on the simulation, such that costly experiments are avoided and mechanisms of each layer can be studied extensively.

articleTitle: A Nash Bargaining Approach for TSO-DSO Flexibility Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of large-scale distributed energy resources (DERs) requires the coordination of transmission and distribution systems to guarantee system balance. In this paper, we construct a Nash bargaining game to investigate the flexibility coordination between transmission system operator (TSO) and distribution system operators (DSOs). To resolve the anticipated system imbalances, TSO and DSOs aim to determine their energy exchange and dispatch level through bargaining to minimize the operational costs. It is challenging to solve the Nash bargaining solution due to the non-convex optimization problem. To address the computational complexity, we decompose the original Nash bargaining game into two sub-problems: the social cost mini-mization problem and the benefits sharing problem. To ensure privacy during the bargaining process, we adopt the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) algorithm to obtain the optimal flexibility trading amount and resource sharing payment. Numerical results show that TSO and DSOs are better off by participating in the Nash bargaining game, demonstrating the benefit of sharing.

articleTitle: Congestion Management in Distribution Systems Based on Decentralized and Finite Flexibility Offers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Flexibility platforms help DSOs manage electricity demand and supply fluctuations, avoiding congestion—crucial as grids integrate renewables. This paper introduces FPM, a flexibility platform acting as a parallel market to aid DSOs in congestion management. It minimizes DSOs’ procurement costs while maximizing CSPs’ comfort. Efficient, scalable algorithms are employed, and results show that FPM is a promising and good alternative to be implemented.

articleTitle: Deep learning model analysis for hybrid PV-TEG maximum power extraction and GMP estimation: A step toward cleaner energy generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The hybrid of a photovoltaic-thermoelectric generating (PV-TEG) system offers great potential for solar energy harvesting, but its efficiency is limited by both sources components. This study proposes an evolutionary neural network (NN)-based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques using an arithmetic optimization (AO) technique for enhancing the performance of the deep neural network (DNN) for real-time global maximum power (GMP) tracking. To further improve the control resilience, a Proportional-Integral (PI) regulator is employed, with gains optimized by the AO algorithm. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of this approach, showing a median efficiency of 99.98%, minimal power oscillations, and a tracking time under 5 ms. Comparative analysis with other MPPT methods such as particle swarm optimizer (PSO), grasshopper optimization (GHO), and gray wolf optimization (GWO), validate the superior performance, stability, and real-time capabilities of the DNN-AO and AO-PI controllers for enhancing the PV-TEG system's energy generation.

articleTitle: Carbon-aware Coordination of Active Distribution Network and Large-scale Electric Vehicles under Source-load Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the popularity of electric vehicles (EVs) in the context of carbon neutrality, the effective utilization of their charging flexibility in active distribution networks (ADNs) has drawn wide attentions. This paper proposes a carbon-aware bilevel model for the ADNs with multiple charging stations (CSs) with consideration of multiple source-load uncertainties. In the upper level, the distribution system operator (DSO) minimizes the carbon-related operation cost of the ADN with uncertainties of renewable energy. In the lower level, the EV aggregator (EVA) optimizes EV charging based on the carbon intensity released from the DSO and sets optimal incentives for EV drivers under their responsivity uncertainties. The source-load uncertainties are modeled by distributionally robust chance constraints (DRCCs) and their tractable reformulations are derived. Moreover, a heuristic iterative algorithm is designed to solve the established bilevel model efficiently. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness and computational efficiency of the proposed model and algorithm for improving the system economy and reducing carbon emission.

articleTitle: Distributed Photovoltaic Consumption Capacity Enhancement Methods for Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In order to effectively solve the problems of voltage crossing, line overloading and bidirectional flow of distribution network caused by new energy photovoltaic (PV) connected to the distribution network, a distribution network optimization method based on the coordination of demand response (DR) and smart soft-open switch (SOP) with energy storage is proposed. Firstly, the DR and SOP distribution network optimization model is constructed based on energy storage, and the multi-temporal optimization model is constructed after PV is connected to the distribution network with the optimization objective function of maximizing the power of new energy PVs, minimizing the loss of SOPs, and minimizing the cost of ESS operation and maintenance. Then, the second-order cone optimization algorithm is used to solve the problem with the CPLEX solver. Finally, Simulations on the IEEE33 bus system show that the method enhances voltage quality, reduces peak-to-valley load differences, and improves PV accommodation capacity, ensuring network security.

articleTitle: A Joint Planning Method for Wind-Solar-Storage Capacity Allocation in New Energy Transmission Bases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: China needs to build a massive new energy transmission infrastructure if it hopes to meet its carbon peaking and carbon neutrality targets as well as promote coordinated development in both its eastern and western regions. Ensuring the transmission base operates economically and reliably requires the efficient allocation of diverse new energy sources and energy storage capacity. This paper proposes a capacity allocation method for new energy transmission based on the confidence probability of wind and solar resources. First, an improved K-means clustering method is introduced to optimize the transmission power of the DC channel, taking into account the load curve at the receiving end. Next, a transmission confidence probability index is suggested, which evaluates whether the transmission base's output power can satisfy the DC channel's transmission requirements. The ideal model for the distribution of wind energy and energy storage capacities is constructed with this confidence probability index as a constraint, and it is solved using a stochastic planning technique. In order to verify the efficacy of the suggested allocation model, we lastly examine a case study involving a resource supplier in western China and a recipient region in eastern China.

articleTitle: Pilot Protection Based on Time-domain Model Recognition for Low-frequency Transmission Lines of Offshore wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Traditional current differential protection and time-domain model recognition pilot protection designed for onshore wind power transmission systems are not applicable to offshore wind farm low-frequency transmission systems. This paper summarizes the requirements of the new system. Based on the original time-domain model recognition pilot protection, the shunt reactor current compensation algorithm is proposed, combining with the Bergeron model formulation, a new protection principle and criterion which do not require remote-end voltage are introduced. The components suitable for the model are also designed. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to verify the correctness of the proposed protection principle and to test the performance of the protection criterias.

Author Keywords: Low-frequency transmission lines of offshore wind farm
suitable frequency band of transmission line model

articleTitle: Application of Large Language Models to Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: By discussing the application of large language models (LLMs) in the power market, their potential and challenges in assisting quotation decision-making, risk monitoring, intelligent customer service, transaction management, and retail package generation are analyzed. Based on the basic principles and development process of large models, combined with current technical requirements, the development direction of large model applications in the power market in the future is proposed, and multiple power market application functions based on large models are designed to improve the decision-making efficiency and risk management capabilities of the power market.

articleTitle: Pumped Storage Power Station Participation in Electricity Market Bidding Optimization Strategy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the swift advancement of fluctuating renewable energy production, the demand for flexible adjustment resources such as pumped storage has significantly increased. To enhance the enthusiasm for constructing pumped storage power stations and ensure their revenue levels, China's electricity pricing system is transitioning from a two-part tariff to a spot market pricing model. Due to its early development stage, the spot market system is not yet mature, and the participation in the ancillary services market is insufficient, making it difficult to reflect the flexibility value of pumped storage power stations. To this end, we firstly analyse the forecast of the tariff mechanism of pumped storage power plants under the market environment, determine the possible risks of tariff fluctuations in the current and future development stages of the tariff mechanism, and establish a risk- return model for power plants based on the CVaR value. Combined with the analysis of the example, we compare the two cases of only participating in the electric energy market and participating in the market of electric energy auxiliary services, highlighting the criticality of the development and improvement of auxiliary services to the income of pumped storage power stations. And at the same time, using the established risk-reward model, we compare returns that include risk considerations with conventional returns to assess the model’s practicality in reducing risk.

articleTitle: Research on a new county power distribution system based on metric hierarchical coordinated control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Currently, the research on power distribution automation in China mainly focuses on urban centres, while the research on county distribution networks is relatively small. In this paper, we aim to solve the problem of unbalanced active power distribution in traditional county distribution systems, and innovatively propose a "meta-meta-sharing" strategy for metacell-level energy units in new county distribution networks. First, we explored and designed the metacell structure in the distribution system, which laid a solid foundation for the subsequent work. Subsequently, under the constructed multi-level and multi-cell grid-connected control framework, we cleverly integrate the multi-intelligent body system technology, consider each cell as an independent intelligent entity, and through precise regulatory commands, we achieve the efficient and coordinated operation among cells while keeping the power fluctuation of the whole group of cells at a minimum. Finally, to verify the effectiveness and superiority of this coordination strategy, we designed and implemented a series of simulation experiments from three key dimensions of power distribution system operation stability, reliability and efficiency, and the results fully proved the feasibility and potential value of the proposed strategy in practical applications.

articleTitle: Energy Community Resilience: A Multi-Objective Approach with Shared Battery Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The introduction of shared battery storage in the energy community (EC) grid provides a unique solution to grid congestion issues. This paper presents an energy management strategy for ECs, leveraging shared communal battery storage (CBS) integrated with community resources to optimize energy distribution. The proposed hierarchical optimization framework is used to minimize costs and CO2 emissions while maximizing self-consumption, using CBS as a modular Virtual Battery Storage (VBS) adapted to community needs. Each VBS module within the CBS is used to optimize different objective functions in the energy management framework. This study demonstrates how the VBS concept can be incorporated into community energy systems for sustainable management and grid stability. The proposed approach is tested on the Aardehuizen community model based on a real EC located in Olst, the Netherlands.

articleTitle: TSO-DSO-Consumers Coordination for Flexibility Procurement: A Tri-level Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Demand-side flexible resources are essential for transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs) to manage the intermittency and uncertainty of distributed renewable energy. We investigate the strategic interactions of TSO, DSO, and consumers for flexibility procurement, through a tri-level optimization problem. In the upper-level (UL) problem, TSO aims to address system imbalances with minimal operating costs by procuring its own flexible resources and incentivizing its DSOs to provide flexible resources. In the middle level (ML), given the upward and downward flexibility prices set by the TSO, DSOs maximize their profit by procuring local resources, including their own flexible resources and the consumers’ flexible resources. In the lower level (LL), consumers make demand response decisions to maximize their utility based on the flexible prices set by their DSOs. Despite the challenges in solving the tri-level problem, we propose a modified Column-and-Cut Generation (C&CG) algorithm that can efficiently solve the proposed problem. Numerical studies show that the consumers’ participation is beneficial for all market participants, including TSO, DSO, and consumers.

articleTitle: Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Method for Active Distribution Network Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy generation and distributed energy resources (DERs), modern power systems face numerous new challenges, such as the intermittency of renewable energy output and the non-convex characteristic of alternating current power flow constraints. Currently, the standard method for coordinating distributed generation under network constraints is to solve the optimal power flow (OPF) problem. This paper proposes a distributed OPF method for active distribution networks (ADNs) based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL). First, the centralized OPF problem of ADNs, constrained by the network and containing a significant amount of renewable energy, is decoupled into a distributed OPF problem and modeled as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP). Then, the objective is to minimize the main grid's purchasing cost and network losses, with voltage limits imposed as constraints, leading to the derivation of the optimal control strategy. Subsequently, the proposed approach integrates a prioritized experience replay (PER) mechanism with a multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3) algorithm to enhance the scalability of the algorithm by sharing effective information and efficiently utilizing experience samples. Finally, numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms the latest deep reinforcement learning algorithms and model-based solving methods, enhancing both control response speed and control strategies' quality.

articleTitle: Simulation-based Online Operating Policy for Wind-storage Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The integration of battery energy storage systems is popularized in wind farms to mitigate generation volatility. For a integrated wind-storage plant, selling energy to a power market is a typical application scenario at the generation side. The revenue maximization problem is challenging as the operation policy has to be settled under generation and price uncertainty. This paper presents a novel online operation policy for wind-storage systems through a simulation-based optimization method. The Lyapunov optimization model is introduced first to construct a base policy that can be expressed explicitly. Then, in the online stage, the state-action value is estimated by sampling the action values and conducting scenario-based simulations for future operation periods based on the Lyapunov policy. The computational complexity of the simulation is alleviated by sampling the output power instead of the multi-dimensional control variables. Finally, the economic efficiency is validated with numerical tests over a yearly horizon.

articleTitle: Learning-Enabled Optimization for Security-Constrained Unit Commitment with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Fast and intelligent scheduling is essential for the safe and stable operation of modern renewable energy power systems. To address the complex Security-Constrained Unit Commitment (SCUC) problem, this paper introduces a rapid solution algorithm based on the learning-enabled optimization. Using the SCUC model that incorporates energy storage, we integrate machine learning techniques within a mixed-integer programming framework, proposing a "prediction + decision" approach. Turing statistics are employed to build a confidence-based training set, and a multi-layer neural network classifier is used to predict logical strategies in real time, enabling fast online decisions. Simulation results on the IEEE 9-bus system demonstrate that this method outperforms traditional solvers and other data-driven algorithms in terms of speed, success rate, and optimal value. The learning-enabled decision-making algorithm provides high-quality approximate solutions, improving decision-making speed by more than an order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Research on Technical Route of AI Large Models for Electric Power Knowledge Services
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) large language models have shown great potential and value in various vertical fields. In response to the demand for the intelligent development of new power systems, this paper summarizes the difficulties faced in the application of AI large language models in the field of power such as large language model illusions. To address these difficulties, starting from the two dimensions of large language model response enhancement and knowledge enhancement, combined with technologies such as fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and retrieval-enhanced generation, this paper proposes an engineering framework for the implementation of AI large models for electric power knowledge services, providing support for empowering the construction of new power systems in China with AI large models. Finally, this paper gives the corresponding solutions to the challenges faced in building large language models for power systems, including difficulties in data acquisition, data security, low interpretability, and high research and development cost.

articleTitle: A Semi-Supervised Learning-Based Method for Classifying the Status of DC Charging Piles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Latent faults in DC charging piles are difficult to reproduce, and manual fault diagnosis is time-consuming, hindering efficient operation and maintenance. This paper proposes a semi-supervised learning-based approach for classifying the operational status of DC charging piles. A comprehensive status assessment framework is developed, integrating electrical, operational, and safety data. Key health factors are selected through correlation analysis, and a semi-supervised learning method is employed to train a classification model, combining multi-feature extraction with artificial intelligence techniques. Specifically, statistical features derived from weekly data are used to construct health factors, which are then fused using an artificial neural network for accurate classification of the charging pile's status. Extensive validation on real-world data demonstrates that the proposed method achieves a classification accuracy exceeding 91%.

articleTitle: Discharge Streamer Development Mmorphology in Multi-element Mixed Insulation Oil Considering Ionization Energy Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this study, considering the influence of oil chemical composition on oil ionization energy and the variation law of oil ionization energy with electric field intensity, an improved discharge streamer simulation model was established to reveal the influence mechanism of lightning impact breakdown characteristics of multi-element mixed insulating oil. The simulation results show that the larger the applied positive voltage, the earlier the surge time of the multi-element mixed insulation oil discharge stream appears. With the decrease of the oil gap distance between the pin-plate electrode, the discharge stream of the multi-element mixed insulation oil develops more violently under the same voltage. Compared with the development characteristics of mineral oil, soya-based natural ester, palm-based natural ester and isooctyl stearate, the mixed-balance effect of oil composition dominated the development of multi-element insulating oil discharge stream.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Empowered Voltage Control for Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Emerging digital twin technology has the potential to revolutionize voltage control in power systems. However, the state-of-the-art digital twin method suffers from low computational and sampling efficiency, which hinders its applications. To address this issue, we propose a Gumbel-Consistency Digital Twin (GC-DT) method that enhances voltage control with improved computational and sampling efficiency. First, the proposed method incorporates a Gumbel-based strategy improvement that leverages the Gumbel-top trick to enhance non-repetitive sampling actions and reduce the reliance on Monte Carlo Tree Search simulations, thereby improving computational efficiency. Second, a consistency loss function aligns predicted hidden states with actual hidden states in the latent space, which increases both prediction accuracy and sampling efficiency. Experiments on IEEE 123-bus, 34-bus, and 13-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed GC-DT outperforms the state-of-the-art DT method in both computational and sampling efficiency.

articleTitle: Application of virtual power plant technology in facility agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) is an innovative technology that integrates distributed energy sources (such as photovoltaic and wind power) and energy storage systems through information and communication technology to achieve intelligent energy dispatch. With climate change and the world's growing population, agricultural production, especially facility agriculture, faces challenges of high energy consumption and unstable power supply. Traditional centralized power grids are difficult to cope with the fluctuations in agricultural facilities' electricity consumption and the instability of renewable energy sources. Virtual power plants provide facility agriculture with a flexible and efficient energy management solution. This article starts from the components, functions, and roles of virtual power plants and analyzes their application in facility agriculture in detail, including the integration of photovoltaic and wind power generation, the introduction of energy storage systems, and the implementation of intelligent dispatching and demand response mechanisms. Through case studies, this article explores the actual application of virtual power plant technology in agricultural production in countries such as the Netherlands, Japan, and China, demonstrating its advantages in peak shaving, filling valleys, energy optimization management, and reducing energy costs. In addition, the article discusses the technical challenges faced by virtual power plant applications, including the integration of distributed energy sources with the grid, the stability of data collection and communication networks, the complexity of intelligent dispatching algorithms, and the high cost of energy storage technology. Finally, the article proposes the future development direction of virtual power plants, including the enhancement of intelligent level, breakthroughs in energy storage technology, policy support, and reform of the power market. The widespread application of virtual power plants in facility agriculture is expected to drive agriculture towards a green and intelligent transformation and achieve sustainable development.

articleTitle: Research on photovoltaic power combination model prediction based on 5G+ technology and irradiance correction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate prediction of photovoltaic power is crucial for the dispatch and operation of power systems. Aiming at the problem of poor photovoltaic power prediction due to the deviation of irradiance forecast and the low prediction accuracy of a single model, a combined model of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and the Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) based on 5G+ technology and irradiance correction is proposed for photovoltaic power prediction. Firstly, the global horizontal total irradiance is updated in real time by using the high-speed data transmission and low-latency characteristics of 5G+ technology, and a slope irradiance correction model is established by the slope conversion method to ensure the accuracy of the slope irradiance on the photovoltaic panel. Then, important features are selected as the input of the combined prediction model according to their contribution to the output power. Finally, a comparative experiment is carried out on a high-performance computing platform supported by 5G+ network using real operating data. The results show that compared with other methods, the proposed method reduces the MAE by at least 17.56% and the RMSE by at least 14.19%.

articleTitle: Construction Method of Power Grid Dispatching Operation Index System Considering Distributed New Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed new energy brings subversive challenges to the operation and control of power system. It is of great significance to construct the operation index system of power grid considering distributed new energy to guide the safe and stable operation of large power grid. Firstly, the influence of distributed new energy output fluctuation on the active power balance of power grid, the partition power balance and reactive power exchange between main and distribution network is analyzed. Then, considering the displacement of conventional units and the weak immunity of new energy units, the instability mechanism of transient voltage and frequency after the permeability increase of distributed new energy is revealed. On this basis, a risk assessment index system covering balance risk, security and stability risk, steady-state regulation ability and stability control ability is established. The risk control level of various regulatory resources in multiple time scales is described by risk control ability index. The operation mode probability is incorporated into the risk index evaluation model. The deterministic control strategies are provided for dispatching operation through probabilistic discrete scenarios. Finally, the effectiveness of the operation index system and evaluation method is verified by the standard test system and actual power grid system.

articleTitle: Enhanced Day-ahead Dispatch of the Integrated Energy System in Wastewater Treatment Plants: Refining Treatment Process Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the high energy consumption issues in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), improving energy management is an effective approach. Therefore, accurately modeling the energy utilization and conversion across various stages of wastewater treatment is crucial. However, existing studies often overlook the tertiary treatment or simplify the modeling of its energy consumption. This paper proposes an enhanced day-ahead dispatch model for the integrated energy system in WWTPs, featuring a detailed model of the tertiary treatment based on reverse osmosis (RO) and the incorporation of energy recovery systems. Simulations conducted on a sample ROWWTP validate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Reviews on the Capacity Market Bidding Strategy of Virtual Power Plants with Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In the context of building a new power system, incentivizing electric vehicles to participate in the capacity market not only helps to fully leverage their capacity value, but also ensures the long-term reliable operation of the power system. In recent years, with the rapid increase in the number of electric vehicles and the gradual maturity of V2G technology, electric vehicles, as a special mobile energy storage system, have received increasing attention for their ability to provide auxiliary services such as frequency regulation and peak shaving for the power grid. However, in the existing electricity market mechanism, the capacity value and physical characteristics of EV resources have not been fully reflected, resulting in insufficient long-term profitability. In view of this, this article conducts research and analysis on the current development status and profitability of virtual power plants considering electric vehicles at home and abroad, and introduces the importance of virtual power plants considering electric vehicles entering the capacity market. On this basis, the challenges faced by China in considering virtual power plants for electric vehicles and the construction route of China's capacity market were discussed.

articleTitle: Study on the Synergistic Operation of Pumped Storage and Electrochemical Energy Storage under High Percentage New Energy Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The amount of renewable energy included into the power system has increased significantly in light of the "dual-carbon" targets, and the inherent stochasticity and intermittency of renewable energy outputs have posed significant issues pertaining to power system stability and security. This necessitates the integration and coordination of various energy storage technologies to enhance the system’s flexibility in scheduling and regulation. This paper presents a day-ahead and intra-day rolling optimal dispatch strategy that incorporates the coordinated participation of pumped storage and electrochemical energy storage. It quantitatively evaluates the system support capabilities and economic benefits of their coordinated operation across four key dimensions: smoothing renewable energy output fluctuations, promoting renewable energy absorption, improving generation reliability, and reducing the burden of system peak shaving. Utilizing data from the Xinjiang provincial power grid, a case study is carried out to evaluate the support capacities of various energy storage coordination solutions within each dimension, confirming the benefits and efficacy of the suggested methodology.

articleTitle: Offshore Wind Farms-Photovoltaic-Energy Storage Systems Planning Based on Kernel Copula
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The increasing global demand for renewable energy has positioned offshore wind as a key component of energy strategies due to its low environmental impact. Scaling up offshore wind power and achieving efficient grid integration are critical to meeting future energy needs. However, the integration process is challenged by the inherent unpredictability and variability of wind power output. This paper proposes a comprehensive planning method combining kernel density estimation and copula functions to model offshore wind farms (OWF) and generate output power curves. The method also incorporates the synergy relationship between photovoltaic (PV) and OWF, along with multi-timescale energy storage systems (ESS), to optimize energy consumption. Case studies and sensitivity analyses reveal that this approach enhances the consumption capacity of OWF and PV while effectively mitigating output fluctuations, with the optimization results demonstrating a degree of robustness.

articleTitle: Information Security Technology and Defense Measures for Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: As a key infrastructure of a modern nation, the power grid is inextricably linked to the livelihoods of its citizens and the development of the economy. The advent of the smart grid has significantly promoted socioeconomic development by optimizing issues inherent in the traditional power grid through intelligent power distribution, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and achieving rational allocation of electrical energy. Due to the power grid's heavy reliance on information and communication technology, it is susceptible to information security issues, necessitating robust enhancements in information security defenses. Considering that the smart grid represents the future trajectory of power grid development, and given that the power system is a technologyintensive industry, the development of the smart grid relies on secure and stable data interactions. This paper proposes technologies and protective frameworks related to smart grid information security, aiming to provide insights for the current secure and stable operation of the power grid and the integration of information security technologies. Ultimately, it seeks to leverage modern information technology to facilitate the transition from the traditional power grid to the smart grid.

articleTitle: Leveraging Explainable AI and Reinforcement Learning for Enhanced Transparency in Adaptive Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The rapid evolution of digital financial services has significantly increased the vulnerability of financial systems to fraudulent activities. Traditional machine learning models have offered substantial progress in detecting fraudulent transactions; however, they often lack adaptability and transparency, critical for dynamic financial environments and regulatory compliance. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance fraud detection capabilities in cloud-based financial platforms. Our model, tested on the synthetic PaySim mobile money transaction dataset, leverages the adaptive nature of DRL to continuously learn and update its fraud detection strategies based on evolving transaction patterns. Concurrently, the integration of XAI provides clear, interpretable insights into the decision-making process, thus ensuring transparency and building trust. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance with an achieved accuracy of 99.5% and an F1-score of 99.0%, significantly outperforming traditional fraud detection systems. These results not only underscore the efficacy of our model in improving the accuracy of fraud detection but also highlight its capability in offering significant improvements in understanding the underlying reasons for each decision, thereby aiding compliance with financial regulations. The practical implications of this research highlight its potential to provide a robust, scalable, and transparent solution for real-time fraud detection, which is essential for safeguarding the integrity of modern financial systems.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling and Optimization Scheduling of Electrochemical Energy Storage System under Multi Resource Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: The new energy installed capacity in China is growing rapidly, and it is expected to exceed 1.2 billion kilowatts by 2030, which accounts for 50% of the total installed capacity. The increasing proportion brings intermittent and fluctuating challenges, and energy storage has become the key to solving the fluctuations in new energy output and improving system regulation capabilities. China has already achieved its goal of installing new energy storage capacity ahead of schedule, but the current issue is how to scientifically utilize large-scale energy storage. This article explores the research on electrochemical energy storage technology and creates a modeling and optimization framework for systems that manage electrochemical energy storage in coordination with various resources. The model's effectiveness and practicality are confirmed using real information from a regional electricity network, and the impact of electrochemical modeling accuracy on system performance is studied. The applicability of different modeling methods is analyzed. The outcomes of the simulation indicate that the unit combination optimization model of electrochemical energy storage considering multiple constraints can support the secure and consistent functioning of the system, and coordinate with coal-fired power and adjustable loads to absorb more new energy.

articleTitle: Attack-Resilient Communication-Efficient Economic Dispatch Algorithm Design for Virtual Power Plants and Parameter Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the development of economic dispatch algorithms using communication-censoring strategy, applied to distributed generators (DGs) in virtual power plants (VPPs). Virtual power plants contain a large number of distributed generators, which offer many advantages compared to traditional power systems. However, this also makes them extremely susceptible to network-attacks. Additionally, under the condition of limited communication resources, there are issues such as communication congestion caused by excessive communication times. In order to improve the communication efficiency in virtual power plants economic dispatch, we first implement a distributed, communication-efficient dispatch algorithm called Co-DRA. However, Co-DRA cannot work properly under network attack. Therefore, taking into account the communication cost and security issues, we implement a communication-efficient attack-resilient economic dispatch algorithm called Co-BREDA. The feature of Co-BREDA is that if the local information an agent needs to transmit differs little from the last transmission, then this agent will not perform iteration in this round, and by means of this communication-censoring strategy, it reduces the number of communication times between agents. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments on the IEEE-118 bus power system show that, with the reasonable selection of the threshold function, compared with the existing algorithm, Co-BREDA can significantly improve communication efficiency while maintaining comparable accuracy to the original algorithm, thus having strong practical significance.

Author Keywords: Economic Dispatch of Virtual Power Plants

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Behind-the-Meter PV-Load Disaggregation via Prior Knowledge Constrained Blind Source Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Accurate disaggregation of behind-the-meter (BTM) photovoltaic (PV) generation and load demand (PV-load) is essential for utility operators to make informed decisions (e.g., demand response). Existing methods for BTM PV-load disaggregation commonly rely on the availability of detailed information, such as observations of neighboring end users’ PV generation or load demand and geographical location, physical parameters of the PV panel and weather conditions, or labeled historical disaggregated observations. However, such information is often unavailable in practice due to privacy concerns or high economic costs for monitoring devices. Instead, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving BTM PV-load disaggregation algorithm that only requires the observed net load data based on prior knowledge constrained blind source separation. Specifically, ensemble empirical mode decomposition is first used to enhance the signal dimension of the observed net load, and then prior knowledge constrained independent component analysis is applied to disaggregate PV generation and load demand from the enhanced mixed signal. Furthermore, the demand response potential of the BTM PV-load unit is evaluated based on the disaggregation results. Numerical experiments on a real-world dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Non-instrusive Load Identification Method based on FHMM in a New Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: Load disaggregation aims to obtain a detailed indoor electricity usage based on comprehensive data monitored by smart meters. Real-time load disaggregation can help users make reasonable electricity-using plans under the time-of-use policy in smart grid and power IoT. It can also be used as the basis for load forecasting, and it is conducive to energy conservation in energy use terminal. This paper presents an energy management system to manage electricity process from power generation to load terminal, among which the smart meters are the core devices. The five components of this system (smart meters, communication networks, servers, dispatching automation system and energy services system) and their relationships with power IoT are described. The proposed method in this paper considers load disaggregation to be a factorial hidden Markov model (FHMM) which can be trained by the method using in the generalized additive models (GAMs). Numerical simulations indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method for energy disaggregation. Through the application of advanced metering infrastructure and integrated information system, this method can make a promotion for the use of intelligent electricity.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Economic Dispatch for Distributed Energy System Using Quasi-Potential Game
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: In this study, an innovative distributed energy system (DES) is proposed, which integrates carbon capture power plants (CCPPs), supercritical carbon dioxide (SCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) power plant, organic rankine cycle (ORC) technology and low-carbon demand response (LCDR). Carbon capture technology effectively captures and stores carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), SCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> power plant improves energy utilization efficiency, and ORC further improves the overall efficiency of the system by using waste heat. LCDR can promote the efficient utilization of renewable energy and the load balance of the DES by dynamically adjusting the power consumption pattern of users. Through this complementary optimization strategy, the system can reduce the carbon footprint, improve the flexibility and reliability of energy utilization, and promote the realization of sustainable development goals. Finally, testing was conducted on the modified IEEE39 node, effectively verifying the effectiveness of our system.

articleTitle: Research on Microwave Wireless Power Transfer Applications for Moving Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the issues of limited battery capacity, short endurance, and challenging charging processes for moving targets, microwave wireless power transfer technology provides an effective solution to the limitations of traditional power supply technologies in such applications. This paper examines the principles of microwave wireless power transfer technology, reviews and compares international dynamic microwave wireless power supply systems and their performance indicators in recent years, highlights the key technologies and challenges present in current applications, and concludes with a summary and perspective on future development trends.

articleTitle: Optimized Joint Configuration Strategy of Independent Grid-Side Energy Storage for System Value
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: This paper presents an optimized configuration strategy for independent grid-side energy storage systems aimed at maximizing system value and improving grid performance. A system value evaluation model is developed to assess key benefits including reducing line losses, smoothing renewable energy output, enhancing system reliability, and deferring grid upgrades. By utilizing an adaptive mutation particle swarm optimization (AMPSO) algorithm, the study optimizes the configuration and operation of grid-side energy storage. Case studies demonstrate the strategy’s effectiveness in balancing investment costs with operational benefits.

articleTitle: A study on the coordinated optimization and economic dispatch of hybrid energy storage systems based on carbon trading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th Conference on Energy Internet and Energy System Integration (EI2)
abstract: To address the stability and reliability challenges posed by the increasing share of renewable energy in the Xinjiang power grid, this paper introduces a collaborative optimization model for the economic dispatch of pumped hydro storage and new energy storage systems, grounded in carbon trading principles. The study emphasizes the volatility and unpredictability of renewable energy generation, focusing on how coordinated operation of energy storage systems can mitigate peak shaving pressures in the Xinjiang grid, thus enhancing its capacity to absorb renewable energy. The proposed model coordinates pumped hydro storage with new energy storage and incorporates a tiered carbon trading mechanism to effectively manage total carbon emissions. The objective is to improve both economic efficiency and environmental sustainability within the power system. The case study using a real 220kV power system from a specific region in Xinjiang illustrates that the hybrid storage operation proposed in this model successfully smooths renewable energy output fluctuations, decreases wind and solar curtailment, and achieves effective peak load shifting. These results contribute to reduced generation costs and enhanced low-carbon characteristics for the system. Future scenario analysis suggests that as renewable energy penetration increases, the optimized configuration outperforms in terms of operational costs and carbon emissions, confirming the model's capability in fostering low-carbon economic operation and power system stability.
